## Restriction to the slice commutes with big-site localization

[Open item](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-localization) · level 8

### Statement
With the sites and conventions of [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site), there is a canonical natural equivalence $j^*L_{\mathcal C}P\simeq L_{\mathcal C/U}(j^*P)$ for every complex-valued presheaf $P$. It identifies the restriction of the ambient localization unit with the slice localization unit. The same argument works for hyperdescent localization if that convention is chosen on both sites; no equivalence between ordinary and hypercomplete localization is needed here.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site) gives the actual sites and preservation of sheaves by $j^*,j_*$.

[F2] Sheafification is the reflective localization of presheaves into sheaves: a map is a local equivalence precisely when mapping it into every sheaf gives an equivalence of mapping spaces.

### Proof
**Given:** $P$ on $\mathcal C$.

**Goal:** Prove localization compatibility, including the actual units.

1.1 The formulas in [F1] give an adjunction $j^*\dashv j_*$. Explicitly, a map $j^*P\to Q$ yields $P(V)\to P(V\times_SU)\to Q(V\times_SU\to U)$. In the other direction, evaluate $P\to j_*Q$ at $V$ and restrict $Q$ along the graph $(\operatorname{id},f):V\to V\times_SU$ for each $(V,f)$. Naturality and the projection–graph identities make these constructions inverse, coherently; equivalently the forgetful functor on scheme categories has right adjoint $V\mapsto V\times_SU$, and the functor-category adjunction is the induced one. Hence this is an adjunction of mapping spaces, not just of isomorphism classes. [F1, construct]

2.1 If $v:P\to P^{\prime}$ is a local equivalence on $\mathcal C$ and $Q$ is any slice sheaf, then $j_*Q$ is a sheaf by [F1]. The adjunction gives $\operatorname{Map}(j^*P^{\prime},Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(P^{\prime},j_*Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(P,j_*Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(j^*P,Q)$. Thus $j^*v$ is a local equivalence. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply this to the localization unit $P\to L_{\mathcal C}P$. Its restriction is a local equivalence, and its target is a slice sheaf by [F1]. The universal property in [F2] identifies it with the slice localization unit. The resulting equivalence is canonical and natural in $P$, so it transports natural maps as well as objects. For hyperdescent, pullback preserves hypercovers and the same descent/adjunction argument applies verbatim. [F1, F2, step 2.1] ∎


## A chosen root trivializes the actual Tate coefficient on the slice

[Open item](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-chosen-root) · level 8

### Statement
Let $k$ be a field, $p$ invertible in $k$, and $\zeta\in k$ of multiplicative order $p$. On every small étale site of a qcqs $k$-scheme $V$ the map $t_{\zeta,V}:\mathbb Z/p\to\mu_p$, $a\mapsto\zeta^a$, is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\mathbb Z/p$-modules. Its tensor cube gives $t^{(3)}_{\zeta,V}:\mathbb Z/p\to\mu_p^{\otimes3}$, $1\mapsto\zeta^{\otimes3}$, naturally in $V$. This natural transformation is on $\mathcal C/U$; no such chosen-root map is asserted on all of $\mathcal C$.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] [def-etale-tate-coefficients](item-def-etale-tate-coefficients) supplies the coefficient sheaves, tensor powers and factorization argument. [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site) fixes precisely the slice category. The constant coefficient is the constant étale sheaf, not a claim that its section group equals $\mathbb Z/p$ on a disconnected scheme.

### Proof
**Given:** $k,p,\zeta,V$ as stated.

**Goal:** Construct the coefficient isomorphism with its exact naturality domain.

1.1 The factorization $T^p-1=\prod_{a=0}^{p-1}(T-\zeta^a)$ has pairwise unit differences on every $k$-scheme. A root on an affine étale object therefore gives a finite disjoint open decomposition on which it equals a unique $\zeta^a$. Thus the constant-sheaf map is locally bijective, and hence is a sheaf isomorphism, as in [F1]. [F1, given]

2.1 Tensor this map three times over the constant ring sheaf $\mathbb Z/p$ and identify $(\mathbb Z/p)^{\otimes3}$ with $\mathbb Z/p$ using multiplication. Tensoring the inverse gives its inverse. Every $k$-morphism carries $\zeta$ to the same chosen base-field section, so these isomorphisms commute with pullback. The root need not exist over an arbitrary object of the ambient site, and none is used there. [F1, step 1.1] ∎


## Restriction of hyperdescent and arbitrary abstract blowup squares

[Open item](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-cdh-hyperdescent) · level 8


### Statement
Let $F=\mathbb Q$ or $F=\mathbb F_p$ for a prime $p$, let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and put $E_\Lambda(X)=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\underline\Lambda_X)$, with its actual derived pullback maps and the constant coefficient sheaf in degree zero. On the entire site of quasi-compact quasi-separated $F$-schemes, with the specified small-skeleton universe convention, $E_\Lambda$ satisfies cdh hyperdescent and Nisnevich descent. Here the cdh topology is generated by Nisnevich covers and abstract blowup families $\{Z\to X,Y\to X\}$ with $Z\to X$ a finitely presented closed immersion and $Y\to X$ finitely presented proper, inducing an isomorphism away from $Z$. The functor sends every such abstract blowup square to a cartesian square in $D(\Lambda)$ and takes the empty scheme to zero. No invertibility assumption on the order of $\Lambda$ is imposed.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The prime field $F$, finite commutative ring $\Lambda$, actual étale cohomology functor $E_\Lambda$, and exact qcqs site in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish hyperdescent, Nisnevich descent, abstract blowup square descent and the zero empty-scheme value for this functor.

[F1] The universe convention and the exact qcqs prime-field site are fixed in [lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site).

[F2] Every specified cdh generator is an arc cover, so the source cdh topology is coarser than the arc topology. [lem-author-7113c087ecba-generators-arc](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-generators-arc)

[F3] For finite commutative $\Lambda$, the actual complex $E_\Lambda$ with its derived pullbacks satisfies arc hyperdescent on all qcqs schemes. [lem-author-7113c087ecba-endomorphism-hyperdescent](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-endomorphism-hyperdescent)

[F4] The EM qcqs-square criterion, with the necessary zero value on the empty scheme, is imported in [thm-author-7113c087ecba-arc-input](item-thm-author-7113c087ecba-arc-input). This criterion concerns ordinary sheaves and is used after hyperdescent has been established.

### Proof
1.1 The source category of qcqs $F$-schemes is stable under the fiber products in its covers and hypercovers. In a cdh hypercover each matching map is locally surjective for the cdh topology. By the generator comparison the same map is locally surjective for the finer arc topology. Thus it is an arc hypercover; apply the endomorphism-hyperdescent supplier to this diagram of underlying schemes, with the finite ring $\Lambda$ fixed above. This proves cdh hyperdescent for the actual functor and its pullback maps, and in particular Nisnevich descent. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 In particular the functor is an ordinary cdh sheaf. The étale topos of the empty scheme has only the zero sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules, so $E_\Lambda(\varnothing)=0$. The qcqs-square criterion therefore applies to its underlying $D(\mathbb Z)$-valued functor and makes every specified abstract blowup square cartesian. Restriction of scalars $D(\Lambda)\to D(\mathbb Z)$ preserves limits, being a right adjoint, and detects equivalences on cohomology, so the square is also cartesian in $D(\Lambda)$. This supplies all the source abstract squares with both finite-presentation conventions; no finite-type or separatedness hypothesis on the schemes, or restriction to ordinary ideal blowups, has been introduced. [F1, F4, step 1.1] ∎

## Finite valuative dimension for noetherian and finite type schemes

[Open item](item-thm-author-14463ef2f4e5-finite-valuative-dimension) · level 8

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. A noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension has finite valuative dimension, bounded above by its Krull dimension. Every scheme of finite type over a field has finite valuative dimension. A noetherian scheme here is one covered by finitely many affine spectra of noetherian rings. Its Krull dimension is the supremum of the lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets; the empty scheme has dimension $-1$. A scheme of finite type over a field has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated algebras over that field.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** Choice, and either a noetherian scheme $X$ of finite Krull dimension $d$, or a scheme $X$ of finite type over a field $k$.

**Goal:** Prove finite valuative dimension in both cases and the bound in the first case.

[F1] For a noetherian domain, valuative dimension equals Krull dimension. [thm-author-14463ef2f4e5-noetherian-valuative-input](item-thm-author-14463ef2f4e5-noetherian-valuative-input)

[F2] A prime quotient of a noetherian ring is a noetherian domain and has dimension at most that of the ring. [lem-author-14463ef2f4e5-noetherian-quotient](item-lem-author-14463ef2f4e5-noetherian-quotient)

[F3] Under Choice a finitely generated algebra over a field is noetherian and has finite Krull dimension. [lem-author-14463ef2f4e5-finite-type-dimension](item-lem-author-14463ef2f4e5-finite-type-dimension) [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F4] The valuative dimension of a scheme is the supremum of the valuative dimensions of the rings in any affine open cover. [lem-author-14463ef2f4e5-affine-cover](item-lem-author-14463ef2f4e5-affine-cover)

### Proof
1.1 Let $A$ be a noetherian ring. For each prime $\mathfrak p$, [F2] makes $A/\mathfrak p$ a noetherian domain of dimension at most $\dim A$. By [F1], its valuative dimension equals its Krull dimension. Taking the supremum over prime quotients gives $\dim_v A\leq\dim A$, including the zero-ring convention. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of a scheme $X$ of dimension $d$, a strict chain of primes in $A$ gives a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $U$ in reverse order. Taking their closures in $X$ gives a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets: intersecting each closure with the open set $U$ recovers the original closed subset. Therefore $\dim A\leq d$. If $X$ is noetherian, choose its finite noetherian affine cover. Step 1.1 bounds each cover member's valuative dimension by $d$, and [F4] gives $\dim_v X\leq d$. The empty scheme satisfies the same assertion by convention. [F4, given, step 1.1]

3.1 If $X$ is finite type over $k$, choose a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. By [F3] each coordinate ring is noetherian of finite dimension, so step 1.1 gives a finite bound for its valuative dimension. The maximum of these finitely many bounds is finite, and [F4] gives the result. The empty cover gives dimension $-1$. [F3, F4, given, step 1.1, choose] ∎

## Completely decomposed proper maps are abstract-blowup covers

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-57a7caabd963-cdp-abstract-generation) · level 8


### Statement
Let $k$ be a field. On the category of separated finite-type $k$-schemes let $J$ be the topology generated by Nisnevich covering families and abstract blowup families whose proper map is an actual isomorphism on the open complement of the closed center. Every completely decomposed proper morphism is a $J$-cover. Consequently $J$ is the cdh topology generated by Nisnevich covering families and singleton completely decomposed proper morphisms. No reducedness hypothesis on the schemes is imposed.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The field, category and generated topology in the statement, and a completely decomposed proper morphism $p:Y\to X$.

**Goal:** Prove the reverse generation implication with actual open-complement isomorphisms.

[F1] The meanings of complete decomposition, properness, abstract blowup family and generated topology, and the fact that every actual abstract blowup family is a Nisnevich-plus-cdp cover, are supplied by [def-cdh-topology-interface](item-def-cdh-topology-interface), including its disjoint-union sieve justification.

[F2] A proper birational map of integral finite-type $k$-schemes is an isomorphism over a dense open of its target, with its entire inverse image. [thm-adjudicate-57a7caabd963-birational-dense-open-input](item-thm-adjudicate-57a7caabd963-birational-dense-open-input)

[F3] Finite-type schemes over a field are noetherian of finite dimension, with finitely many irreducible components. A closed subset missing all generic points has smaller dimension. A reduced zero-dimensional such scheme is a finite disjoint union of spectra of fields. These follow from the affine noetherian dimension statements; all closed immersions and finite-type maps here are finitely presented.

### Proof

1.1 For every $X$, the reduction $X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ is a $J$-cover: take the abstract blowup family with closed center $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ and proper member $\varnothing$. Both open complements are empty, so the required actual isomorphism holds. Properness and complete decomposition survive base change. For the latter, a residue-field lift over $x$ base changes along $x'\to x$ to a $\kappa(x')$-valued lift. Thus, once the assertion is proved for reduced targets, apply it to $Y\times_X X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X_{\mathrm{red}}$ and then use local character along the reduction cover. It suffices to treat reduced targets. [F1, F3, construct]

1.2 Prove the assertion for reduced targets by induction on $d=\dim X$. The empty case is immediate. If $d=0$, each of the finitely many field components of $X$ has a residue-field-preserving lift in $Y$. These lifts define a section of $p$ over each component and hence over $X$. A map with a section generates the maximal sieve and covers. This proves the base case. [F1, F3, given]

1.3 For the induction step, for each generic point $\eta_i$ of the reduced $X$ choose a lift $y_i\in Y$ with $\kappa(y_i)=\kappa(\eta_i)$. Let $X_i$ be the corresponding reduced irreducible component and $Y_i$ the reduced closure of $y_i$ in $Y$. The map $Y_i\to X$ factors through $X_i$, since $Y_i$ is reduced and its image lies in that closed component. The induced map $Y_i\to X_i$ is proper and birational: the closure is integral with generic residue field $\kappa(y_i)$, and it is closed in the proper $X$-scheme $Y$. Apply [F2] to each such map. After deleting component intersections and the finitely many closed complements of the resulting dense opens, there is an open $U\subseteq X$ meeting every component such that $Y'=\coprod_iY_i\to X$ is an actual isomorphism over $U$. Let $Z$ be the reduced closed complement of $U$. Then $\dim Z<d$ and $\{Y'\to X,Z\to X\}$ is an actual abstract blowup family. [F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 The base change $Y\times_XZ\to Z$ is completely decomposed proper and therefore covers by the induction hypothesis, since $Z$ is reduced and has smaller dimension. For the sieve $R$ generated by $p$, its pullback to $Y'$ is maximal because $Y'\to X$ factors through $Y$. Its pullback to $Z$ is covering because it contains the covering sieve generated by $Y\times_XZ\to Z$. Local character along the abstract blowup family in step 1.3 makes $R$ covering. This proves the induction, and step 1.1 then supplies all nonreduced targets. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3]

3.1 Every generator of $J$ covers for the Nisnevich-plus-cdp topology by [F1]; conversely every cdp generator covers for $J$ by step 2.1, and the Nisnevich generators are common. Minimality of the two generated topologies proves equality. Only finitely many lifts and dense opens were selected in each finite-dimensional induction, so the local argument adds no arbitrary-index choice assumption. [F1, step 2.1] ∎


## Nonconnective K theory of perfect complexes

[Open item](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) · level 9

### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice. A **qcqs scheme** is a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme. For such X, realize the full sheaf-derived stable idempotent-complete category Perf(X) of [def-scheme-perfect-complexes](item-def-scheme-perfect-complexes) by the full perfect fiber widehat Perf(X) in the single localized K-flat family of [lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-kflat-enhancement-comparison](item-lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-kflat-enhancement-comparison). Each fiber is identified with the supplied Perf(X) by the actual exact inclusion-induced equivalence. The supplier has specified no prior scheme-indexed tensor/pullback diagram; here its coherent interface is, by definition, the one produced by that common family. Its tensor and pullbacks are those of [lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-derived-tensor-pullback](item-lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-derived-tensor-pullback). By [lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-perfect-essential-smallness](item-lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-perfect-essential-smallness) these fibers are essentially small. Extend 𝕂 once to the equivalent domain of essentially small stable idempotent-complete infinity-categories, rather than selecting independent skeletons for separate maps. Let 𝕂 be the nonconnective functor of [thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-nonconnective-multiplicative-input](item-thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-nonconnective-multiplicative-input), and define

$$K(X)=\mathbb K(\operatorname{Perf}(X)),\qquad K_i(X)=\pi_iK(X)\quad(i\in\mathbb Z).$$

All groups use the indexing of [def-stable-spectra-interface](item-def-stable-spectra-interface); negative i are allowed and are not set to zero by a connective truncation. In the displayed formulas Perf and its supported categories mean these common-family realizations of the supplied enhanced categories. Equivalent coherent small presentations give naturally equivalent spectra and diagrams.

For every subset T⊆X define

$$K_T(X)=\mathbb K(\operatorname{Perf}_T(X)),\qquad K_{i,T}(X)=\pi_iK_T(X)\quad(i\in\mathbb Z).$$

The supported category consists of perfect complexes whose cohomology stalks vanish off T. For closed T this is equivalently acyclicity on the open complement. Its exact inclusion in Perf(X) supplies $K_T$(X)→K(X). Here $K_T$(X) is defined by that category, without presupposing a fiber identification with K(X)→K(X∖T).

For every morphism f:X→Y of qcqs schemes, exact derived pullback gives f*:K(Y)→K(X). On pairs it gives f*:$K_T$(Y)→$K_{f^{-1}T}$(X). These are coherent contravariant operations; on affine finite-projective representatives they are derived extension of scalars. No flatness, regularity or finite Tor-dimension assumption on f is imposed.

Derived tensor and the lax symmetric monoidal 𝕂 give the coherent E∞ multiplication K(X)∧K(X)→K(X), with unit induced by $O_X$. Thus K(X) is a commutative ring spectrum. Each $K_T$(X) is a module over K(X), and there are coherent support pairings $K_T$(X)∧$K_S$(X)→$K_{T\cap S}$(X). They induce $K_{i,T}$(X)⊗$K_{j,S}$(X)→$K_{i+j,T\cap S}$(X) for all integers i,j. Pullback respects the products and module actions. For proper T no distinguished ring unit on $K_T$(X) is asserted; its specified structure is the ambient module and supported pairings.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** qcqs schemes, arbitrary support subsets, morphisms as above, AC and the chosen universes.

**Goal:** Define the nonconnective spectrum and justify its domain, all-integer groups, contravariance and products.

[F1] [lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-kflat-enhancement-comparison](item-lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-kflat-enhancement-comparison) constructs the single coherently localized scheme/tensor family and identifies its fibers with the supplied enhancement; [lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-perfect-essential-smallness](item-lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-perfect-essential-smallness) supplies its essentially small stable idempotent-complete domain.

[F2] [lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-derived-tensor-pullback](item-lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-derived-tensor-pullback) and [lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-supported-tensor-ideal](item-lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-supported-tensor-ideal) supply the actual enhanced operations and support control.

[F3] [thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-nonconnective-multiplicative-input](item-thm-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-nonconnective-multiplicative-input) supplies nonconnective 𝕂 and its lax symmetric monoidal structure; [def-stable-spectra-interface](item-def-stable-spectra-interface) supplies π_i for all integers.

[F4] [lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-nonconnective-functor-products](item-lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-nonconnective-functor-products) applies these inputs and establishes presentation independence and multiplicative contravariance.

### Justification
1.1 Use the common-family model of [F1] and apply [F3] to its whole coherent diagram and to each full support subfamily. This defines the displayed spectra, inclusion maps and all-integer groups independently of equivalent small presentations, as proved in [F4]. [F1, F3, F4]

2.1 Apply [F3] to the exact pullbacks and coherent separately exact pairings in [F2]. The functorial, ring, module and support-product assertions are precisely those of [F4]; smash of shifted sphere maps gives the degree i+j formula. The unit belongs to the ambient Perf(X), so it does not create a unit in a proper support category. This proves the interface. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1] ∎

### Scope of separate inputs
A degree-zero comparison with a Grothendieck group, comparison with a particular classical nonconnective model, and a scheme localization theorem identifying a support category as the fiber are separate results with their own hypotheses. No such theorem is inferred from this definition. No identification with coherent-sheaf G-theory on a singular scheme is made.


## Reported alternative argument in arbitrary dimension

[Open item](item-rem-morrow-general-dimensional-comparison) · level 9

### Remark
The article reports that Matthew Morrow communicated an alternative proof of its Theorem 6.7, working in arbitrary dimension $d$ without the normality assumption. Theorem 6.7 is the article's comparison between the indicated motivic filtration subgroup of $K_0$ and the subgroup generated by classes of smooth closed points, in its stated normal affine threefold setting.

The reported argument identifies the motivic cohomology group $H^{2d,d}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ with the Nisnevich cohomology group $H^d_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,\mathcal K_d^M)$ and invokes a result of Kato and Saito that the latter group is generated by cycle classes of smooth closed points. Motivic cohomology here is the Elmanto–Morrow cohomology described in [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology); Nisnevich cohomology is sheaf cohomology on the Nisnevich site, and $\mathcal K_d^M$ denotes the Milnor $K$-theory sheaf intended in the communication. The article says that the argument will appear in ongoing work of Elden Elmanto and Matthew Morrow.

The article's authors also express the belief that the ideas in their proof of Theorem 6.7 might generalize to higher dimensions under a stronger restriction on singularities, giving normality as an example. This is reported as their expectation, not as a proved generalization.

### Reading limits
Remark 6.8 does not give complete hypotheses for the communicated comparison, a precise Kato–Saito locator, or the convention for the Milnor $K$-sheaf. In particular, [def-milnor-k-sheaf-interface](item-def-milnor-k-sheaf-interface) defines a naive convention but does not identify it with the convention intended in the report. This item records the communication as reported; it supplies neither a proof nor an independently established arbitrary-dimensional comparison and is not a logical premise for that comparison.

## The diagonal of a finite subintegral map is a cdh cover

[Open item](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-subintegral-diagonal-cover) · level 9

### Statement
For a finite subintegral morphism $p:T\to X$ of separated finite-type schemes over a field, its diagonal $\Delta:T\to T\times_X T$ is a finite subintegral morphism and a cdh covering singleton. The diagonal is the unique map whose composites with both projections are the identity of $T$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Such a morphism $p$.

**Goal:** Prove the assertion about $\Delta$.

[F1] A subintegral morphism is a universal homeomorphism and induces residue-field isomorphisms. [def-seminormal-scheme-interface](item-def-seminormal-scheme-interface)

[F2] A finite morphism is separated, so its diagonal is a closed immersion; a closed immersion is finite and induces isomorphisms on residue fields at its image points.

[F3] A finite subintegral morphism in this category is a cdh covering singleton. [lem-author-60d95bfb692a-finite-subintegral-cdh-cover](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-finite-subintegral-cdh-cover)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Use the base change of the universal homeomorphism.

1.1 The first projection $q:T\times_X T\to T$ is a base change of $p$ and is therefore a homeomorphism on underlying spaces by [F1]. Since $q\Delta=\operatorname{id}_T$, the diagonal is bijective on points. [F1, given]

2.1 By [F2], $\Delta$ is finite and induces residue-field isomorphisms at image points. Together with step 1.1, it is subintegral. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 The fibre product is again separated and of finite type over the field. Apply [F3] to $\Delta$ to obtain the stated cdh cover. [F3, step 2.1] ∎

## A finite-family basis for the generated cdh topology

[Open item](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-generated-topology-basis) · level 9

### Statement
Let $B$ consist of finite families obtained from finite Nisnevich families and singleton cdp maps by finitely many covering-family compositions, including identities and the empty family over the empty scheme. A sieve is cdh covering exactly when it contains a family in $B$. In particular every covering sieve contains a finite covering family of arrows individually belonging to it. A sieve is closed under precomposition; it is not assumed closed under taking coproducts of arrows.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The site and its topology generated by the two kinds of families, as in [def-cdh-topology-interface](item-def-cdh-topology-interface).

**Goal:** Identify its covering sieves by an explicitly finite basis.

[F1] [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-nisnevich-subfamily](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-nisnevich-subfamily) reduces every generating Nisnevich family to a finite subfamily.

[F2] [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-cdh-generators-pullback-composition](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-cdh-generators-pullback-composition) proves the base-change/composition closure of $B$; composites of finite families are finite.

[F3] The sieve axioms for a topology and the meaning of least generated topology are those of [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification).

### Proof
1.1 Define $J_B(X)$ to be the sieves containing a $B$-family. The identity family proves maximality, and pulling back the contained family proves pullback stability by [F2]. For transitivity, let $S$ contain a finite $B$-family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}$ and let $R$ be a sieve such that $f^*R$ is in $J_B$ for every $f\in S$. For each of these finitely many $f_i$ choose a finite $B$-family $\{g_{ij}\}$ in $f_i^*R$. The finite composite family $\{f_ig_{ij}\}$ belongs to $B$ and to $R$. Hence $R\in J_B$. Thus $J_B$ is a topology. [F2, F3]

2.1 It contains every generating cdp sieve and every generating Nisnevich sieve by [F1]. Therefore the least generated cdh topology is contained in $J_B$. Conversely any topology containing the generators contains every $B$-family sieve by repeated transitivity, and hence every sieve containing such a family by upward closure (itself an immediate consequence of transitivity). Apply this to the cdh topology to get the reverse inclusion. The equivalence and finiteness assertion follow. Only individual family arrows have been placed in the sieve. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## Prime-field evaluation and compatibility with the standing theory

[Open item](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-general-interface) · level 9

### Statement
For any prime field $F\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb F_p\}$ and $j\geq0$, define the general EM groups on qcqs $F$-schemes by
$$\widehat H^{i,j}_{F}(X,\mathbb Z)=H^i(M_{j,F}(X)).$$
For a field $k$ with prime subfield $F$, restriction of this interface to qcqs $k$-schemes is exactly the standing $H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}$ functor, including its pullbacks. Thus the same notation can be used for the general prime-field evaluation and its fixed-field restriction. Write $F_{j,F}$ for the actual fiber of the natural map $M_{j,F}\to C_{j,F}$, with fiber sequence $F_{j,F}(X)\to M_{j,F}(X)\to C_{j,F}(X)$ at every $X$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The completed prime-field motivic sheaves, the standing fixed-field definition and their actual comparison to cdh motivic complexes.

**Goal:** Define the larger-scope interface without substituting a different motivic theory.

[F1] [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) supplies $M_{j,F}$ for every prime field and explicitly obtains the $k$-scheme functor by restriction along forgetting $k$ to $F$.

[F2] [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) defines its groups by objectwise cohomology of exactly that restricted functor; [lem-author-b747b28c359f-derived-cohomology](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-derived-cohomology) supplies functoriality on $D(\mathbb Z)$.

[F3] [thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-cdh-interface-input](item-thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-cdh-interface-input) supplies the actual natural map $\alpha_{j,F}$ to the specified cdh complex.

### Proof
1.1 Apply cohomology to the actual prime-field functor in [F1]. By [F2] this defines the displayed general groups and their pullbacks. On a qcqs $k$-scheme, forgetting its $k$-structure before evaluation gives precisely the complex used by the standing definition, by its stated construction. The underlying complexes and maps are thus the same restricted diagram, so the groups and pullbacks agree without an independently chosen comparison isomorphism. [F1, F2]

2.1 Take the pointwise derived fiber of [F3]. Limits of functor diagrams are computed objectwise, so it gives an actual presheaf and the stated natural fiber sequence at every $X$. On restriction to $k$-schemes this is the same sequence, again by precomposition. Empty schemes give zero complexes by empty-cover Nisnevich descent. The weight range is exactly $j\geq0$ as in [F1]. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎

## External EM affine syntomic filtration and actual obstruction map

[Open item](item-thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-em-syntomic) · level 9

### Statement
For every $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $A$ and $j\geq0$, the complex $\mathbb F_p(j)_{\rm syn}(A)$ has a finite filtration from zero to itself, with graded pieces, in order,
$$L^j[-j-1],L^{j-1}[-j],\ldots,L^0[-1],\quad L^0,L^1[-1],\ldots,L^j[-j],$$
where $L^a=L\Lambda^aL_{A/\mathbb F_p}$. The cotangent complex and its derived exterior powers are cohomologically nonpositive (compute by a simplicial polynomial resolution).
For any qcqs $\mathbb F_p$-scheme $X$ the canonical comparison fits in the actual natural fiber sequence
$$\mathbb Z(j)_{\rm mot}(X)/p\longrightarrow\mathbb F_p(j)_{\rm syn}(X)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{\rm cdh}(X,\widetilde\nu_1(j))[-j-1].$$
Here $\widetilde\nu_1(j)(A)$ is the cokernel of the Artin–Schreier map on differential forms (EM Definition 4.29), and its cdh sheafification is meant. The second arrow is EM (4.7), not an arbitrary map selected from a group isomorphism.

### External input
Import EM Lemma 4.16 and Corollary 4.32 with their stated hypotheses. The finite filtration is proved there by the de Rham/Cartier filtration and left Kan extension; the fiber sequence is proved from the actual motivic pullback square. These are established inputs, not locally reconstructed foundations. In particular, the obstruction formula is the correct primary comparison used to interpret the positive-characteristic part of the next external input. No equivalence between derived syntomic cohomology and ordinary étale logarithmic forms on an arbitrary singular affine is asserted.


## External EM multiplicative motivic complexes and actual Chern map

[Open item](item-thm-author-79117e1d72ed-em-multiplication-c1) · level 9

### Statement
Let $F=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$. The supplied EM complexes $C_b(X)=\mathbb Z(b)_{\rm mot}(X)$ on qcqs $F$-schemes are the shifted graded pieces of the specified multiplicative filtration. In the terminology of EM §2.2, the graded spectra $G_b=C_b[2b]$ form a natural commutative algebra object for graded Day convolution: there are coherent associative symmetric unital products $G_b\wedge G_d\to G_{b+d}$ and unit $\mathbb S\to G_0$, and pullbacks preserve this data. Equivalently these induce the usual motivic cup products, with even weight shifts. The negative graded pieces vanish, so $C_b=0$ for $b<0$.
There is the actual natural map of complex-valued presheaves
$$c_1:R\Gamma_{\rm Nis}(X,\mathbb G_m)[-1]\longrightarrow C_1(X)$$
of Lemma5.1/Definition5.2. Its degree-two source is $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ with tensor-product group law. It agrees with the classical class on smooth $F$-schemes. The maps denoted $c_1(\mathcal O(1))^m\pi^*$ in §5 are defined using this class and the multiplication just specified.
EM writes $P_X^{\rm lin}(V)$ for the projectivization classifying rank-one subbundles of $V$, with tautological subbundle $\mathcal O(-1)$ and its dual $\mathcal O(1)$.

### External input
These are the stated construction and conventions at the exact locators in the source reference, restricted to the completed motivic-complex supplier. Definitions4.9/4.23 take pullbacks in filtered E∞-algebras; §2.2 gives the symmetric monoidal associated-graded construction. Definition5.2 supplies the complex map, rather than a class chosen from group agreement. Import those established foundations. Restriction along the prime-field forgetful functor supplies the same interface on qcqs schemes over any field. No replacement of the supplied motivic theory or K-theory model is made.

## The actual finite-quotient map to cdh-local motivic cohomology

[Open item](item-lem-author-e71ff76fe904-finite-quotient-comparison) · level 9


### Statement
Let $F=\mathbb Q$ or $F=\mathbb F_p$ for a prime $p$, and work on the category of all qcqs $F$-schemes. For $j\geq0$, write $M_j=\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot},F}$ for the supplied Elmanto–Morrow complex-valued presheaf, and $\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{cdh},F}$ for its specified classical-input cdh target. For every integer $n\geq1$ invertible in $F$, the objectwise derived quotient of the canonical motivic-to-cdh comparison is a natural equivalence
$$\alpha_j:M_j/n\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{cdh},F}/n.$$
The slash denotes the objectwise derived quotient $C\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathbb Z/n=\operatorname{cofib}(n:C\to C)$, precisely as in the completed motivic definition. This is an equivalence of actual $D(\mathbb Z)$-valued presheaves on that same category and may be evaluated at every qcqs $F$-scheme. If $k$ is any field with prime subfield $F$, precomposition along the forgetful functor from qcqs $k$-schemes retains this equivalence, with source the standing motivic complex and target the restriction of the specified prime-field cdh complex.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the displayed construction or conclusion with its actual maps.

[F1] [thm-author-e71ff76fe904-cdh-factorization-input](item-thm-author-e71ff76fe904-cdh-factorization-input) imports the actual canonical maps and their stated equivalences on the qcqs prime-field category.

[F2] [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) supplies the prime-field motivic functor and its fixed-field restriction. [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) and [lem-author-b747b28c359f-derived-finite-coefficients](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-derived-finite-coefficients) fix the objectwise derived quotient.

### Proof
1.1 If $F=\mathbb Q$, apply the canonical-map assertion of EM Theorem4.10(4), supplied by [F1], with $m=n$. Its slash is derived quotient, the same construction as [F2]. [F1, F2]

1.2 If $F=\mathbb F_p$, [F1] supplies the equivalence $M_j[1/p]\to\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{cdh},F}[1/p]$. Since $p$ is a unit in $\mathbb Z/n$, localization followed by derived tensor with $\mathbb Z/n$ is just derived tensor with $\mathbb Z/n$: the equality follows from $\mathbb Z[1/p]\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z/n\cong\mathbb Z/n$, with $\mathbb Z[1/p]$ flat. Tensoring that actual comparison thus gives exactly the stated canonical quotient map. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 For each qcqs $F$-scheme $X$, steps 1.1–1.2 give an equivalence upon evaluation at $X$. All constructions are objectwise and functorial, so these maps form the stated natural equivalence. Precomposing that same diagram with the forgetful functor for any field $k/F$ preserves its maps and equivalences; by [F2] its source is precisely the standing motivic quotient. The target remains the restriction of the prime-field cdh complex, without any unproved exchange of restriction and sheafification. This proves both scopes. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Constant cdh sections on the two article sites

[Open item](item-lem-author-a279c89ed6c8-cdh-zero-site-comparison) · level 9


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and choose the site universes specified below. Let $k$ be a field with prime subfield $F$, and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Evaluation at $X$ of the constant integer cdh sheaf on the specified qcqs $F$-scheme site is canonically isomorphic to evaluation at $X$ of the constant integer cdh sheaf on the site of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. The isomorphism is natural for morphisms between such $k$-schemes.

Here qcqs means quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The first site is the small skeleton of qcqs $F$-schemes in the chosen universe, with topology generated by Nisnevich covers and abstract blowup families whose closed immersion and proper map are finitely presented. The second site consists of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with the cdh topology generated by Nisnevich covers and abstract blowup families. An abstract blowup family is $\{Z\to T,T'\to T\}$, where $Z\to T$ is a closed immersion, $T'\to T$ is proper, and $T'\setminus(T'\times_T Z)\to T\setminus Z$ is an isomorphism. The constant integer sheaf is the sheafification of the presheaf with value $\mathbb Z$ and identity restriction maps.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Choice, the two specified sites and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$.

**Goal:** Compare the actual constant-sheaf evaluations and their restriction maps.

[F1] The generators and universe convention of the qcqs prime-field site are fixed by [lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site). The finite-type interface [def-cdh-topology-interface](item-def-cdh-topology-interface) defines cdh using Nisnevich covers and completely decomposed proper maps.

[F4] On separated finite-type $k$-schemes that topology is also generated by Nisnevich covers and actual abstract blowup families, including for nonreduced schemes. [lem-adjudicate-57a7caabd963-cdp-abstract-generation](item-lem-adjudicate-57a7caabd963-cdp-abstract-generation)

[F2] Sheafification is obtained by applying the plus construction twice; plus sections are matching families on covering sieves modulo agreement on a common covering refinement. [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification)

[F3] Every separated finite-type scheme over a field is noetherian. A finite-type morphism between noetherian schemes is finitely presented; an étale morphism is locally of finite presentation. A quasi-compact open subspace of a noetherian scheme is noetherian. These standard finite-presentation facts follow on affine charts from finite generation of ideals in noetherian rings.

### Proof

1.1 By [F4], the finite-type topology is generated equally by Nisnevich covers and actual abstract blowup families. Every generator in this presentation, viewed over $F$, is a cover in the qcqs site: its closed immersion and proper map are finitely presented by [F3], and its Nisnevich family is a Nisnevich cover in the larger site. The same holds for pullbacks and finite composites of generators. Thus this comparison includes the completely decomposed proper generators of the specified finite-type interface. [F1, F3, F4, given]

1.2 Conversely, consider a generating cover of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ in the qcqs site. In an abstract blowup family both members are separated and of finite type over $T$, hence are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. For a Nisnevich cover, refine its members by affine open subschemes and use quasi-compactness of $T$ to choose finitely many of these opens still covering $T$ in the Nisnevich sense: use the assumed Axiom of Choice to select, for each point, a residue-field-preserving lift and an affine neighbourhood of that lift (and representatives in the fixed small skeleton); the resulting Nisnevich family admits a finite subfamily on a noetherian base by noetherian induction on the closed complement of an open over which a chosen étale morphism has a section. Each chosen affine is of finite type over $T$ because it is quasi-compact and étale, hence finitely presented over $T$; it is separated. Thus the refined family belongs to the finite-type site. The same argument applies after each base change to a finite-type object, so finite composites of generating covers in the larger site admit refinements in the smaller site. [F1, F3, construct]

2.1 Consequently, on each separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, finite-type covering families are cofinal among the generating-basis refinements used in the larger topology. This comparison is made in the slices over $T$: every object mapping to $T$ inherits its $k$-structure, and every arrow over $T$ respects that structure. Thus the different base fields introduce no additional arrows in the matching diagrams on these families. Their iterated fiber products over $T$ also belong to the finite-type site. For a presheaf obtained by restricting a larger-site presheaf, matching families and their common-refinement equivalence may therefore be computed using those same families on either site. Applying this observation first to the constant presheaf and then to its plus construction identifies the two double-plus values. The identification respects restriction because pullback and refinement of the same families are used in both constructions. [F2, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 The double-plus values are the stated constant-sheaf sections. Step 2.1 gives the canonical natural isomorphism, including the empty scheme. [F2, step 2.1] ∎


## Flag detection over an arbitrary field by prime-field restriction

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-6cf37231df39-arbitrary-field-flag-detection) · level 9

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site-size and universe bounds of the actual motivic complexes. Let $k$ be any field and $X$ any qcqs $k$-scheme. For finitely many finite locally free sheaves on $X$, the simultaneous line-quotient flag tower $q:Y\to X$, constructed on the finite common clopen rank partition, detects integral motivic cohomology:
$$q^*:H^{a,b}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^{a,b}_{\mathrm{mot}}(Y,\mathbb Z)$$
is injective for every $a\in\mathbb Z$ and $b\geq0$. No algebraic closure, finite-type, noetherian or dimension assumption is required. With the source zero extension in weights $b<0$, detection in those weights is vacuous.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] The prime-field complexes and their restrictions to field-schemes are homotopy-coherent derived Nisnevich sheaves, and cohomology is evaluated on these actual complexes. [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes), [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology)

[F2] The actual projective-bundle equivalence for qcqs prime-field schemes has pullback as its zero summand. Its line-subbundle convention becomes the line-quotient convention by applying it to the dual bundle. [thm-author-ab0a6fc202cb-elmanto-morrow-projective-input](item-thm-author-ab0a6fc202cb-elmanto-morrow-projective-input)

[F3] The simultaneous flag construction is a finite composite of positive-rank projective bundles on each common rank stratum. On qcqs $X$ the partition and its union are finite and qcqs. [lem-flag-tower-line-quotients](item-lem-flag-tower-line-quotients)

[A1] Choice and the stated bounds are inherited through the flag construction and the derived sheaf evaluations. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof
**Given:** $k,X$, the finite bundle family, Choice and the size bounds in the statement.

**Goal:** Supply detection in the arbitrary-field scope used by the actual second-stage comparison.

1.1 Let $F\subseteq k$ be the prime subfield. Forgetting to $F$ changes neither the underlying qcqs scheme, its vector bundles and projective bundles, nor the value of its restricted motivic complex in [F1]. For a positive constant-rank bundle $G$, an invertible quotient of $G$ dualizes to a locally split line subbundle of $G^\vee$, and dualizing again is inverse. Thus the source projective bundle for $G^\vee$ is the required quotient-projective bundle for $G$, with the same tautological $\mathcal O(1)$. Apply [F2] to $G^\vee$. Projection onto the index-zero summand of the inverse equivalence is a left inverse to the actual quotient-projective pullback. Thus that pullback is injective on cohomology in every degree and nonnegative weight. [F1, F2, A1]

2.1 For constant ranks the tower in [F3] is finite. Applying step 1.1 at each stage and composing the injective homomorphisms proves detection for that tower. Rank-zero cases contribute the identity tower. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 For varying ranks write $X=\coprod_\alpha X_\alpha$ for the finite clopen common rank partition and $Y=\coprod_\alpha Y_\alpha$ for its towers. Derived Nisnevich descent in [F1] for this disjoint open cover identifies the complexes on $X$ and $Y$ with the finite products on their pieces; their empty intersections contribute zero, since derived sheaf descent for the empty cover gives the zero complex on the empty scheme. Taking cohomology commutes with these finite products. Therefore $q^*$ is the product of the injective maps of step 2.1 and is injective. The additional negative-weight assertion follows only from the expressly adopted zero extension. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Affine perfect K zero and bundle K zero

[Open item](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge) · level 10


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and suitable universes. For a commutative unital ring A and X=Spec A, there is a canonical isomorphism π₀K(X)≅K⁰(X), where K(X) is the nonconnective spectrum of [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) and K⁰(X) is the vector-bundle Grothendieck group. Under this isomorphism the class of the associated sheaf complex of a bounded complex P of finite projective A-modules maps to Σₙ(−1)ⁿ[P̃ⁿ], and the spectral class of a vector bundle E placed in degree zero maps to [E]. Equivalently, the inverse sends [E] to the class of E[0]. No noetherian or regularity hypothesis is imposed.

A vector bundle is a locally finite free $\mathcal O_X$-module. Its Grothendieck group is generated by isomorphism classes of vector bundles with [E]=[E′]+[E″] for every short exact sequence 0→E′→E→E″→0 of vector bundles. A finite projective A-module is a finitely generated module having the lifting property through surjective module maps; a bounded complex has finitely many nonzero terms. This is a comparison with vector-bundle K zero, not an identification with coherent-sheaf G-theory.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** AC, suitable universes, a commutative unital ring A, and X=Spec A.

**Goal:** Identify the degree-zero group of the specified nonconnective spectrum with the vector-bundle group and establish the stated formulas.

[A1] Choice is assumed for the essentially small perfect-category and K-theory constructions invoked in [F1]; it is not inferred from affineness. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] An affine scheme is qcqs. The supplied interface defines K(X)=𝕂(Perf(X)), with an essentially small stable idempotent-complete perfect category and invariance under an equivalent small presentation. [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface)

[F2] The cofiber Grothendieck group of a small stable infinity-category is canonically the triangle Grothendieck group of its homotopy category. [lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-presentation](item-lem-author-3a003d7b5208-triangle-presentation)

[F3] For a small idempotent-complete stable infinity-category, the object-class map identifies its cofiber Grothendieck group with π₀ of the specified nonconnective K-theory. This is an external input with the source and reading limits recorded there. [thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input](item-thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input)

[F4] The triangle group of Perf(X) identifies with the vector-bundle group; it takes a bounded finite-projective representative to the alternating sum of its associated bundle terms and E[0] to [E]. The exact affine equivalence used there is degreewise associated sheaf. [lem-author-3a003d7b5208-affine-triangle-euler](item-lem-author-3a003d7b5208-affine-triangle-euler), [def-scheme-perfect-complexes](item-def-scheme-perfect-complexes)

### Proof
**Proof technique:** Compose the spectral, triangulated and affine Euler comparisons.

1.1 Choose a small stable idempotent-complete presentation C equivalent to Perf(X), available by [F1]. The equivalence identifies the corresponding K-theory spectra and hence their π₀ groups. Apply [F3] to C and invert its object-class isomorphism; then apply [F2] to obtain an isomorphism from π₀K(X) to the triangle Grothendieck group of hPerf(X). The construction is independent of the presentation by the naturality and equivalence invariance in [F1] and [F3]. [A1, F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 Compose the isomorphism of step 1.1 with the affine Euler isomorphism of [F4]. This gives π₀K(X)≅K⁰(X). By [F3], the spectral class of an object is sent in step 1.1 to its triangle class. Therefore [F4] sends the class represented by P to Σₙ(−1)ⁿ[P̃ⁿ], and sends the class of E[0] to [E]. [F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 The classes [E] generate K⁰(X), so the final formula also describes the inverse on its generators. The hypotheses of all invoked suppliers are satisfied by the given commutative unital ring, AC and affine qcqs scheme; none requires noetherianity or regularity. This proves the bridge and both formulas. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1] ∎


## Rational splitting of the motivic tower

[Open item](item-prop-rational-weight-splitting-input) · level 10


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and use the universes of the supplied perfect-complex $K$-theory interface. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme over $\mathbb Q$ or over $\mathbb F_p$ for a prime $p$, of finite valuative dimension in the supplied convention. Let $F^\bullet_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ be the Elmanto–Morrow motivic filtration on that nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum. Rationalization means smashing each stage with the rational sphere spectrum. There is a natural equivalence of augmented filtered spectra from this rationalized tower to the tail tower

$$q\longmapsto\bigoplus_{j\geq q}\mathbb Q(j)^{\mathrm{mot}}(X)[2j] \quad(q\geq0),$$

extended constantly for $q\leq0$. Here $\mathbb Q(j)^{\mathrm{mot}}(X)$ denotes the rationalization of Elmanto–Morrow's weight-$j$ motivic cohomology spectrum, and $[2j]$ is its $2j$-fold suspension. In particular, the associated motivic spectral sequence has zero differentials after rationalization. The induced image filtration has successive quotients given by the homotopy groups of the corresponding rational weight pieces.

### Statement references

[def-valuative-dimension-and-boundedness](item-def-valuative-dimension-and-boundedness)

[def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface)

### External input
The existence, boundedness and natural rational filtered splitting of the Elmanto–Morrow tower are imported from the cited theorems. Their construction and proof are not reconstructed here. In characteristic zero the cited theorem additionally asserts multiplicativity of its equivalence; no multiplicativity of the splitting is asserted here in positive characteristic. The splitting by itself is not a terminal-edge isomorphism: a particular edge comparison also requires the appropriate graded identification and high-filtration vanishing.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** Choice, the fixed universes, $X$ as in the statement and the cited Elmanto–Morrow motivic filtration.

**Goal:** Obtain the stated splitting and its formal spectral-sequence and image-filtration consequences.

[A1] Choice is inherited from the specified perfect-category and nonconnective $K$-theory interface and is used when invoking that model of $K(X)$. The formal consequences of a supplied split tower introduce no additional selection step. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] The external input in Elmanto–Morrow, Theorems 4.12 and 4.27, supplies the natural rational filtered splitting under the stated respective hypotheses. The decreasing-filtration convention is Section 2.2; the proof of Lemma 7.1 explicitly writes the split stage $q$ as the sum over weights $j\geq q$ (there for affine schemes). This is the stagewise meaning of the filtered splitting in the two theorems, not an affine restriction on those theorems.

[F2] [lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-spectral-cofiber](item-lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-spectral-cofiber) and [lem-author-9f61e4df2141-tail-splitting](item-lem-author-9f61e4df2141-tail-splitting) identify the graded pieces and zero connecting maps of the tail tower.

[F3] [lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-tower-boundaries](item-lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-tower-boundaries) transports those zero boundaries across a tower equivalence, and [lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-couple-degeneration](item-lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-couple-degeneration) gives zero differentials in its tower spectral sequence.

[F4] [lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-image-filtration](item-lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-image-filtration) identifies the successive image-filtration quotients for such a splitting.

### Proof
1.1 If $X$ is a $\mathbb Q$-scheme, apply Theorem 4.12; if it is an $\mathbb F_p$-scheme, apply Theorem 4.27. In either case the qcqs and finite-valuative-dimension hypotheses are exactly those in [F1]. The imported equivalence gives the displayed natural augmented tail splitting, with graded pieces as in [F2]. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 Apply [F3] to the rationalized tower and the equivalence from step 1.1: all differentials in the associated tower spectral sequence vanish. Apply [F4] to the same equivalence to obtain the stated successive image-filtration quotients. These are formal consequences of the imported splitting and do not reconstruct it or supply a separate edge comparison. [F3, F4, step 1.1] ∎


## Detection on a simultaneous flag tower

[Open item](item-lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection) · level 10

### Statement
Assume AC. Let $H^{*,*}$ be an additively oriented bigraded theory with the projective bundle contract on a scheme category $\mathcal C$. For a finite family of vector bundles $E_1,\ldots,E_m$ of constant ranks on an object $X$, the simultaneous flag tower $q:Y\to X$ induces injective pullback $q^*:H^{a,b}(X)\to H^{a,b}(Y)$ for every $(a,b)\in\mathbb Z^2$. Each $[q^*E_i]$ in the Grothendieck group of vector bundles is the sum of the classes of its global line-bundle filtration quotients, with the empty sum for rank zero.

More generally let $X$ be qcqs and the ranks merely locally constant. Suppose the finitely many common rank strata $X_\alpha$, their inclusions, the component flag towers $q_\alpha:Y_\alpha\to X_\alpha$, their finite disjoint union $Y$, its component inclusions, and $q:Y\to X$ all belong to $\mathcal C$. If the joint restriction $H^{a,b}(X)\to\prod_\alpha H^{a,b}(X_\alpha)$ is injective for every bidegree, then $q^*$ is injective in every bidegree. This additional joint-restriction hypothesis is explicit: it is not part of the abstract projective bundle contract.

For the actual Elmanto-Morrow motivic theory of the article, on qcqs schemes over its field $k$ (algebraically closed unless otherwise specified), joint restriction to these strata is an isomorphism. Hence the componentwise flag tower detects $H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(-,R)$ for every $i\in\mathbb Z$, $j\geq0$, and $R=\mathbb Z$ or $\mathbb Z/n$, $n>0$. This uses the actual derived motivic complexes and requires no smoothness, noetherianity, finite-type or dimension assumption. If the source's explicit extension $\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}=0$ for $j<0$ is adopted, the same statement holds for all integer weights, with zero groups in negative weights; the current nonnegative-weight definition alone makes no separate negative-weight assertion.

For varying ranks the line-quotient class equality holds separately on every $Y_\alpha$. Globally it holds after extending those quotient bundles by zero along the clopen inclusions; these extensions are vector bundles of rank one on that component and zero elsewhere, rather than global line bundles. A finite sum of global line-bundle classes is asserted only in the constant-rank situation. Here $K^0_{\mathrm{vb}}$ denotes the group on finite locally free sheaves modulo short-exact-sequence relations. None of these statements asserts injectivity of $q^*$ on that group.

Consequently any equality $u=v$ between classes of the same cohomological bidegree whose two sides pull back naturally can be checked on the appropriate detecting tower: $q^*u=q^*v$ implies $u=v$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the theory and category, and the bundles above; in the abstract varying-rank case also the explicit membership and joint-restriction assumptions. For the actual motivic application use the stated qcqs field, weight and coefficient hypotheses.

**Goal:** Preserve constant-rank detection, prove conditional abstract varying-rank detection, supply its actual motivic application, and state precisely the class equalities used.

[F1] The constant-rank simultaneous tower is a finite composite of positive-constant-rank projective bundles, with locally split line-quotient filtrations; it is qcqs over a qcqs base. [lem-flag-tower-line-quotients](item-lem-flag-tower-line-quotients)

[F2] In the abstract contract, pullback along such a finite composite is injective in every bidegree; pullbacks are contravariantly functorial group homomorphisms. [lem-projective-pullback-detection](item-lem-projective-pullback-detection), [def-bigraded-oriented-theory](item-def-bigraded-oriented-theory)

[F3] The common rank partition and componentwise tower are finite and qcqs, with identity constructions at rank zero. [lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-finite-common-rank-strata](item-lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-finite-common-rank-strata)

[F4] The actual motivic complexes have finite-clopen product decomposition and hence joint cohomological restriction is an isomorphism, integrally and with finite coefficients, in their specified weights. [lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-motivic-rank-restriction](item-lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-motivic-rank-restriction), [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology)

[F5] The exact actual motivic projective-bundle equivalence and its rank/weight/convention hypotheses are imported separately. [thm-author-ab0a6fc202cb-elmanto-morrow-projective-input](item-thm-author-ab0a6fc202cb-elmanto-morrow-projective-input)

[F6] Finite products commute with cohomology and the finite-coefficient cone. [lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-finite-derived-products](item-lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-finite-derived-products)

[F7] Filtration relations give global line sums for constant ranks and componentwise line sums for varying ranks. Extension by zero along finite clopen inclusions gives the valid global vector-bundle class formula. [lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-clopen-line-quotient-classes](item-lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-clopen-line-quotient-classes)

[F8] AC is inherited through the flag construction and is retained throughout. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

1.1 In the constant-rank abstract case, apply [F1] to the finite bundle family and [F2] to every stage. Their finite composite is injective in every integer bidegree; if there are no stages the map is the identity and remains injective. [F1, F2, F8, given]

2.1 Apply [F7] to the global locally split filtrations from [F1]. Telescoping the short-exact-sequence relations gives $[q^*E_i]=\sum_s[L_{i,s}]$, with no summands for rank zero. This uses only those vector-bundle relations and asserts neither a globally split extension nor cohomological detection from a K-group equality. [F1, F7, step 1.1]

3.1 In the abstract varying-rank case, let $\iota_\alpha:X_\alpha\hookrightarrow X$ and $j_\alpha:Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y$ be the inclusions. The construction satisfies $qj_\alpha=\iota_\alpha q_\alpha$. All the bundles on $X_\alpha$ have constant ranks, so step 1.1 gives injectivity of each $q_\alpha^*$. [F3, given, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 If $q^*x=0$, then functoriality gives $q_\alpha^*\iota_\alpha^*x=j_\alpha^*q^*x=0$. Step 3.1 yields $\iota_\alpha^*x=0$ for every $\alpha$. The stated joint-restriction hypothesis then implies $x=0$. This proves conditional varying-rank detection without adding an unproved axiom to the abstract contract. [F2, given, step 3.1]

5.1 For the actual motivic theory, take one positive-constant-rank quotient-projective stage $\pi:\mathbb P(G)\to S$ of a component tower. The source in [F5] uses line subbundles. Dualizing a locally split invertible quotient of the finite locally free $G$ gives a line subbundle of $G^\vee$, and dualizing again recovers the quotient. Hence the represented projective bundles are canonically identified over $S$, with the same projection and the source's dual tautological line equal to the quotient $\mathcal O(1)$. Apply [F5] to $G^\vee$, of the same positive constant rank. Its index-zero summand is $\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}(S)$ and its map is precisely $\pi^*$. The inverse of the derived equivalence followed by projection onto that summand is a retraction. Thus $\pi^*$ is injective on every integral cohomology degree $i$, for $j\geq0$. [F1, F5, F6, construct, step 4.1]

6.1 Applying the finite-coefficient cone to that equivalence and using [F6] gives the same zero-summand retraction and injectivity for $R=\mathbb Z/n$. Compose these injections through every finite component tower; identity stages at rank zero preserve the conclusion. Joint restriction to the common rank strata is injective by [F4]. The functorial argument of step 4.1 therefore proves the asserted actual motivic injectivity for both coefficient choices. The optional negative-weight convention gives zero source and target groups and so extends it trivially when that convention is explicitly used. [F3, F4, F5, F6, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 Finally [F7] gives all stated varying-rank class equalities, with supported extensions in the global formula, and explains why they cannot in general be called sums of global line-bundle classes. If $q^*u=q^*v$ in any of the detecting cases, functorial additive pullback gives $q^*(u-v)=0$, and the relevant injection from step 1.1, step 4.1 or step 6.1 implies $u-v=0$. Naturality identifies pulled-back expressions with those formed from the pulled-back bundles, which proves the final identity-detection assertion and completes the proof. [F2, F7, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 6.1] ∎



## Perfect residue classes at smooth closed points

[Open item](item-lem-koszul-point-support-class) · level 10

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a finite-type scheme over a perfect field $k$, and let $x$ be a closed point at which $X$ is smooth over $k$. Write $i:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ for the closed immersion of the point. There is a smooth affine open neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ on which the ideal of $x$ is generated by a regular sequence whose images in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ form a regular system of parameters. Its Koszul complex is a finite free resolution of $i_*\kappa(x)|_V$. Thus $i$ is a regular immersion, and the residue sheaf $i_*\kappa(x)$, placed in degree zero, is perfect on $X$ and supported on $\{x\}$.

Consequently it has a distinguished class $[i_*\kappa(x)]$ in $K_{0,\{x\}}(X)$, whose image in $K_0(X)$ is its ordinary perfect-complex class. This class is independent of the choice of neighbourhood and parameters. No claim that it generates the supported group is made here; that identification requires a separate purity or dévissage result.

A perfect field is a field whose algebraic extensions are separable. A regular local ring is a noetherian local ring whose dimension equals the dimension of its maximal ideal modulo its square over its residue field. A regular system of parameters is a minimal generating sequence of that maximal ideal of length equal to the dimension. A sequence is regular if each element is a non-zero-divisor modulo its predecessors and the final quotient is nonzero. A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence. The Koszul complex on a sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ has terms $\bigwedge^j A^d$ and differential given by contraction with $(f_1,\ldots,f_d)$; for the empty sequence it is $A$ in degree zero. The residue sheaf $i_*\kappa(x)$ has stalk $\kappa(x)$ at $x$ and zero stalks elsewhere.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, a finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ over a perfect field, and a smooth closed point $x$.

**Goal:** Construct the local Koszul resolution, prove global perfectness and support, and identify the resulting supported class.

[F1] A smooth finite-type scheme over a perfect field has regular local rings under AC. A finite-type algebra over a field is noetherian, being a quotient of a finite-variable polynomial algebra. ([math:thm-regular-equals-smooth-over-perfect-field](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-regular-equals-smooth-over-perfect-field), [math:lem-finite-variable-polynomial-algebras-over-fields-are-noetherian-direct](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-finite-variable-polynomial-algebras-over-fields-are-noetherian-direct))

[F2] Under AC, in a regular local ring every regular system of parameters is a regular sequence, and its Koszul complex is a finite free resolution of the residue field. ([math:thm-regular-local-rings-are-domains-and-cohen-macaulay](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-regular-local-rings-are-domains-and-cohen-macaulay), [math:lem-regular-local-residue-field-koszul-resolution](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-regular-local-residue-field-koszul-resolution), [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice))

[F3] Perfectness is the local condition of being represented by a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. The supported perfect category consists of perfect objects whose cohomology stalks vanish outside the specified subset. ([def-scheme-perfect-complexes](item-def-scheme-perfect-complexes))

[F4] For qcqs schemes the supported K-spectrum is the nonconnective K-theory of the supported perfect category, and its inclusion induces the support-to-global map. For an idempotent-complete stable category, the degree-zero comparison sends each object to its K-theory class and is natural for exact functors. ([def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface), [thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input](item-thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input))

### Proof

1.1 By smoothness at $x$, choose a smooth affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$; it is of finite type over $k$. The point corresponds to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ because it is closed. By [F1], $A$ is noetherian and $R=A_{\mathfrak m}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is regular local. Choose a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $R$. Since $\mathfrak mR$ is generated by images of elements of $\mathfrak m$ and denominators outside $\mathfrak m$ are units, after multiplying each $t_i$ by a unit we may represent it by an element $f_i\in\mathfrak m$; the resulting tuple remains a regular system of parameters. When $d=0$ take the empty tuple. [given, F1, choose]

2.1 The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, and its quotient by $(f_1,\ldots,f_d)$ localizes to zero at $\mathfrak m$. Thus some $h_0\notin\mathfrak m$ kills that quotient: choose an annihilating denominator for each of its finitely many generators and multiply them. For each $j$, let $M_j=A/(f_1,\ldots,f_{j-1})$. The kernel of multiplication by $f_j$ on $M_j$ is a finite $A$-module because $A$ is noetherian. Its localization at $\mathfrak m$ is zero by [F2] and exactness of localization, so some $h_j\notin\mathfrak m$ kills it. Set $h=h_0h_1\cdots h_d$ and $V=D(h)$. On $V$ the $f_i$ generate $\mathfrak mA_h$ and each multiplication by $f_j$ on $A_h/(f_1,\ldots,f_{j-1})$ is injective. The final quotient is $A_h/\mathfrak mA_h\cong A/\mathfrak m\ne0$. Hence the sequence is regular on $A_h$, including the empty-sequence case. [F2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 The closed point $x$ in $V$ is cut out by $\mathfrak mA_h=(f_1,\ldots,f_d)$. Applying the Koszul resolution statement in [F2] locally at $x$ and using the same noetherian denominator argument, or equivalently applying its regular-sequence resolution assertion to the sequence on $A_h$, gives a finite free resolution of $A_h/\mathfrak mA_h$. Its associated complex of finite free sheaves resolves $i_*\kappa(x)|_V$. Since the ideal is generated by a regular sequence on a neighbourhood of the only point of the closed subscheme, $i$ is a regular immersion. [F2, step 2.1]

4.1 The stalks of $i_*\kappa(x)$ vanish away from $x$: because $\{x\}$ is closed, each other point has a neighbourhood disjoint from it. On $V$ step 3.1 gives a bounded finite free resolution; on $X\setminus\{x\}$ the sheaf is zero, represented by the zero complex. These opens cover $X$, so [F3] makes $i_*\kappa(x)$ perfect with support contained in $\{x\}$. Its nonzero stalk at $x$ shows that its support is exactly $\{x\}$. This argument does not extend a locally free resolution by zero: the globally defined object is the residue sheaf itself. [F3, step 3.1, given]

5.1 A finite-type scheme over a field is qcqs, so [F4] applies. The object of step 4.1 gives its object class in $K_{0,\{x\}}(X)$; naturality for the exact inclusion sends it to the class of the same object in $K_0(X)$. Every choice of parameters and neighbourhood in steps 1.1 through 3.1 resolves the same globally defined sheaf, so the supported object and its class are independent of those choices. AC is used through the stated suppliers. [F4, step 4.1, F2] ∎

## Finite-coefficient motivic to cdh comparison

[Open item](item-prop-finite-coefficient-cdh-comparison) · level 10

### Statement
Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, X an affine threefold over k as in Proposition 2.6, and p a prime. The canonical comparison induces an isomorphism

$H^{5,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)\cong H^{5,3}_{\mathrm{cdh}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)$.

Here the left group is $H^5(\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z/p)$, as in [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology). The right group is $H^5(\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{cdh}}(X)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z/p)$, where $\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{cdh}}$ is Elmanto–Morrow's cdh-local motivic complex on qcqs Q-schemes. Finite coefficients are taken after evaluating each complex at X. The isomorphism is induced by the actual canonical comparison map; this statement does not identify the paper's cdh site with a separately chosen small site.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** k, X and p as stated.

**Goal:** Prove the displayed canonical group isomorphism.

[F1] For a qcqs Q-scheme and a nonnegative weight, the canonical motivic-to-cdh map has rational cofiber. [lem-author-4b6f215bcf3b-em-rational-comparison-cofiber](item-lem-author-4b6f215bcf3b-em-rational-comparison-cofiber)

[F2] A map in D(Z) with rational cofiber becomes an isomorphism after derived tensoring with Z/n for every positive n, and therefore induces an isomorphism on every cohomology group. [lem-author-4b6f215bcf3b-rational-cofiber-comparison](item-lem-author-4b6f215bcf3b-rational-cofiber-comparison)

[F3] Derived tensoring with Z/p is represented by the cone of multiplication by p. [lem-derived-coefficient-exact-sequence](item-lem-derived-coefficient-exact-sequence)

### Proof

1.1 Since k has characteristic zero, the unique homomorphism Q → k exists. Composition X → Spec(k) → Spec(Q) makes X a Q-scheme. An affine scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so X satisfies [F1]. [given, F1]

2.1 Apply [F1] with $j = 3$ to obtain the canonical map Z(3)_mot(X) → $\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{cdh}}$(X) with rational cofiber. Since p is positive, [F2] makes its derived tensor with Z/p an isomorphism in D(Z). [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Taking $H^5$ and using the definitions in the statement gives the displayed isomorphism. By [F3] these are derived finite-coefficient groups; the map is induced from the canonical comparison before taking the quotient. This is the characteristic-zero application used on the cited article page. [F2, F3, step 2.1] ∎

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the selected local perfect-complex $K$-theory realization. Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ for a prime $p$. On the opposite of the category of quasi-compact quasi-separated $\mathbb F$-schemes, nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory has a functorial, multiplicative, $\mathbb N$-indexed decreasing motivic filtration whose zeroth stage is naturally equivalent to $K$. In the terminology of coherently multiplicative filtered spectra, the imported multiplicative filtration includes coherent products, unit and transition compatibility; its maps to $K$ are induced through its zeroth stage.

### Statement references

[def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum](item-def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum)

### External input
This is the existence and zeroth-stage part of the cited Elmanto–Morrow results. It is imported as literature, not proved by the local formal lemmas. The source's later boundedness and convergence assertions require additional hypotheses and are not imported here. The nonconnective $K$-theory is used through the perfect-complex interface of [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface), under its stated Choice assumption. This assumption belongs to the selected local realization; it is not an additional geometric hypothesis attributed to Elmanto–Morrow.

**Goal:** Supply the functorial multiplicative filtration and its zeroth-stage equivalence under exactly these hypotheses.

[F2] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) discharges the explicit Choice premise of [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) when its common-family enhanced perfect categories and essentially small nonconnective-functor domain are invoked. Definitions 4.9 and 4.23 construct the imported filtration as a pullback of filtered $E_\infty$-algebras, providing the coherent multiplication specified by [def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum](item-def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum).
