### Proof
1.1 Under the inherited Choice premise in [F2], use the selected $K$-theory realization and apply the characteristic-zero assertion of [F1] when $\mathbb F=\mathbb Q$, and the characteristic-$p$ assertion when $\mathbb F=\mathbb F_p$. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 The qcqs hypothesis is exactly the common hypothesis of those initial assertions. The stated functoriality and coherent multiplicativity are the imported theorem's data, with the filtered-algebra structure in [F2]; no finite-valuative-dimension conclusion is used. [F1, F2, given, step 1.1] ∎


## Sections match across a finite subintegral cover

[Open item](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-subintegral-matching) · level 10

### Statement
Let $p:T\to X$ be a finite subintegral morphism of separated finite-type schemes over a field, and let $F$ be a set-valued cdh sheaf. For every $s\in F(T)$, its pullbacks along the two projections $T\times_X T\rightrightarrows T$ agree. The fibre product represents pairs of maps to $T$ with the same composite to $X$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $p$, $F$ and $s$ as stated.

**Goal:** Prove equality of the two pullbacks.

[F1] The diagonal $\Delta:T\to T\times_X T$ is a cdh covering singleton. [lem-author-60d95bfb692a-subintegral-diagonal-cover](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-subintegral-diagonal-cover)

[F2] Restriction of a sheaf along a covering singleton is injective. [lem-author-60d95bfb692a-cover-restriction-injective](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-cover-restriction-injective)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Compare after restriction to the diagonal.

1.1 Each projection composed with $\Delta$ is $\operatorname{id}_T$. Consequently the two pullbacks of $s$ restrict along $\Delta$ to the same element $s$. [given]

2.1 By [F1] and [F2], restriction along $\Delta$ is injective. The two pullbacks are therefore equal. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎

## Finite coproducts and refinement inside a sieve

[Open item](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-coproduct-sieve-refinement) · level 10

### Statement
Let $S$ be a cdh covering sieve on $X$ and let $\{u_i:U_i\to X\}_{i=1}^m$ be a $B$-family in $S$. Its coproduct $u:W=\coprod_iU_i\to X$ is a cdh covering morphism, and admits a finite word factorization into Nisnevich covering morphisms and cdp morphisms. No assertion that $u\in S$ is made. If a two-stage refinement of $u$ is supplied,
$$V\xrightarrow{q}X'\xrightarrow{p}X,\quad h:V\to W,\quad pq=uh,$$
with $q$ Nisnevich and $p$ cdp, then $V_i=h^{-1}(U_i)$ are finitely many open-and-closed subschemes, $\{V_i\to X'\}$ is a finite Nisnevich family, and every composite $V_i\to X$ is in $S$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The finite $B$-family, and only for the last assertion the displayed refinement as an explicit premise.

**Goal:** Make the cover morphism available for a source refinement theorem while keeping final arrows inside $S$.

[F1] [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-cdh-generators-pullback-composition](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-cdh-generators-pullback-composition) and [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-generated-topology-basis](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-generated-topology-basis) supply the finite generating tree and the closure rules.

[F2] Finite coproducts exist in the site; their summand inclusions are open-and-closed immersions. Such inclusions form a Nisnevich family: they are étale and uniquely lift their component points with unchanged residue fields. [def-nisnevich-covering-interface](item-def-nisnevich-covering-interface)

### Proof
1.1 Realize the construction of the $B$-family by a finite tree of elementary generating-family substitutions. Start with the frontier $X$. When a leaf $A$ is replaced by a generating family over it, take its source coproduct and leave all other leaves unchanged using their identities. The new frontier coproduct maps to the old one. For a Nisnevich substitution this is a Nisnevich covering morphism; for a cdp substitution it is cdp, by [F1] and the disjoint target components. Finitely many substitutions give a finite word with final frontier $W$, and composite $u$. Hence $u$ is cdh covering. This is a consequence of the family construction, not closure of the sieve $S$ under coproducts. [F1]

1.2 Under the stated refinement, preimages of the summands of $W$ give a finite open-and-closed decomposition $V=\coprod_iV_i$. Each $V_i\to X'$ is étale since $q$ is. Every point of $X'$ has a residue-preserving lift in $V$ by the Nisnevich condition on $q$, and that point belongs to a summand $V_i$. Thus these restricted maps form a finite Nisnevich family. Their composites to $X$ factor as $V_i\to U_i\xrightarrow{u_i}X$ and therefore belong to $S$ by sieve closure under precomposition. The schemes $V_i$ remain separated of finite type over $k$. [F2, given]

2.1 For emphasis, the generally invalid implication $u_i\in S$ for all $i\Rightarrow\coprod u_i\in S$ has not been used. For example the sieve on a disconnected $X=A\amalg B$ generated by its two nonempty summand inclusions does not contain $\mathrm{id}_X$, although their coproduct is $\mathrm{id}_X$. It is nonetheless a Nisnevich covering sieve. The split family in step 1.2 is the required correct refinement inside $S$. [F2, step 1.2] ∎


## Constant-sheaf sections have finite local representatives

[Open item](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-constant-sheaf-finite-local-representatives) · level 10

### Statement
For any set $A$, let $P_A$ be the constant presheaf and $aA=aP_A$ its cdh sheafification on the specified site. For every $s\in(aA)(X)$, the sieve of arrows $f:Y\to X$ for which $s|_Y$ is the image of some $a\in A$ is covering. Hence $s$ has a finite cdh covering family of constant representatives $a_1,\ldots,a_m$. For $A=\mathbb Z$, setting $D=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\subset\mathbb Z$ yields a section of the finite constant-set sheaf $aD$ whose image in $a\mathbb Z$ is $s$. This is the precise finite-values assertion; it does not posit an unproved interpretation of arbitrary cdh sections as ordinary point functions.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A constant presheaf and a section of its sheafification.

**Goal:** Produce finitely many constant representatives, and a finite constant-set factorization.

[F1] The completed sheafification contract defines $aP=(P^+)^+$ using matching families on covering sieves modulo common covering refinement. [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification)

[F2] Every covering sieve contains a finite $B$-family. [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-generated-topology-basis](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-generated-topology-basis)

### Proof
1.1 Represent $s$ by a matching $P_A^+$-family on a covering sieve $R$ using [F1]. Each of its entries in turn is represented by a matching $P_A$-family on a covering sieve of its source. On each arrow of this second sieve, the restriction of $s$ is the image of an actual element of $A$. The sieve $L$ of all arrows having such representatives is closed under precomposition because restrictions of constants remain constant. For each arrow of $R$, its pullback of $L$ contains the corresponding second covering sieve, so it covers. Transitivity therefore shows $L$ covers $X$. Apply [F2] to choose a finite family in $L$ and representatives $a_i$ for it. [F1, F2]

2.1 Sheafification preserves a presheaf injection: if two matching families from $P$ become equal in $Q^+$ under an injection $P\hookrightarrow Q$, they agree on a common covering refinement in $Q$, hence there in $P$; thus $P^+\to Q^+$ is injective, and applying this twice proves the assertion. Consequently $aD\to aA$ is a monomorphism for the subset $D=\{a_i\}$. The local sections $a_i$ in $aD$ have equal restrictions on every pairwise overlap, since their images are the restrictions of $s$ and the map is injective. They glue uniquely to a section of $aD$ by the sheaf condition. Its image is $s$ by uniqueness of gluing in $aA$. The empty-scheme case uses the empty family and the unique empty-domain section. This proves the finite-values formulation, in particular for integers. [F1, step 1.1] ∎


## Normalizing the comparison fiber for the dimension criterion

[Open item](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-shifted-hypotheses) · level 10


### Statement
For $j\geq0$ and a prime field $F$, set $W_{j,F}=F_{j,F}[j]$, with cochain shift $H^n(C[j])=H^{n+j}(C)$. Then $W_{j,F}$ satisfies every hypothesis of the dimension criterion over base ring $F$: it is finitary Nisnevich, cdh-acyclic, pro-cdh on Noetherian $F$-schemes, and has nilpotent-relative values in degrees $\leq0$ on every Noetherian local henselian $F$-algebra.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The actual fiber $F_{j,F}$ and the shift convention in the Statement.

**Goal:** Check the precise domain, ideal and degree hypotheses before applying the criterion.

[F1] [thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-relative-package-input](item-thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-relative-package-input) gives finitariness, Nisnevich descent, cdh acyclicity, pro-cdh descent, and the relative bound $\leq j$ for finitely generated nilpotent ideals.

[F2] [thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-dimension-criterion-input](item-thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-dimension-criterion-input) is the criterion requiring relative bound $\leq0$ for Noetherian local henselian algebras. [lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-general-interface](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-general-interface) specifies the actual fiber used here.

### Proof
1.1 Shift by $[j]$ is an equivalence of the stable derived category and commutes with limits and colimits. Thus it preserves the finitary and Nisnevich properties, commutes with pointwise total fibers, and preserves the supplied degreewise pro-cdh condition: for every integer $n$ the shifted total-fiber system has $H^n=H^{n+j}$ of the original system, which is zero as a pro abelian group. This uses the explicit convention of [F1]–[F2], without asserting cartesianness in $\operatorname{Pro}(D(\mathbb Z))$. It also commutes with cdh sheafification: shifting preserves sheaves and its inverse does likewise, so the reflective sheafification universal property identifies the two composites. Hence $W_{j,F}$ retains the first geometric properties of [F1], including $L_{\mathrm{cdh}}W_{j,F}=0$. [F1, F2]

2.1 Let $A$ be any Noetherian local henselian $F$-algebra and $I$ any nilpotent ideal. Every ideal of a Noetherian ring is finitely generated, so [F1] applies without an added ideal hypothesis. For $n>0$, the relative cohomology of $W_{j,F}(A,I)$ in degree $n$ is the relative cohomology of $F_{j,F}(A,I)$ in degree $n+j>j$, hence zero. This is exactly the degree and functor-class hypothesis of [F2]; the source’s stronger arbitrary-algebra package has been used only under its actual finitely-generated-ideal condition. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Affine characteristic-p syntomic amplitude without regularity

[Open item](item-lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-syntomic-bound) · level 10

### Statement
For every $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $A$ and $j\geq0$, $H^i(\mathbb F_p(j)_{\rm syn}(A))=0$ for $i>j+1$. In particular its degree-five group vanishes when $j=3$.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] [thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-em-syntomic](item-thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-em-syntomic) supplies EM Lemma 4.16 and its notation $L^a_{A/\mathbb F_p}=L\Lambda^aL_{A/\mathbb F_p}$. These derived exterior-power complexes lie in $D^{\leq0}$; they are computed by a simplicial polynomial resolution with ordinary differential forms in degree zero.

### Proof
**Given:** Any $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $A$, with no smoothness, reducedness or finite-type hypothesis.

**Goal:** Establish the stated upper bound.

1.1 In [F1] the first block of graded pieces is $L^a[-a-1]$ for $0\leq a\leq j$ and the second block is $L^a[-a]$ for $0\leq a\leq j$. A complex in $D^{\leq0}$ shifted by $-b$ lies in $D^{\leq b}$. Every listed piece therefore lies in $D^{\leq j+1}$. [F1]

2.1 The filtration is finite, starts at zero, and ends at the syntomic complex. The cohomology exact sequence for each successive extension shows inductively that the entire complex lies in $D^{\leq j+1}$. For $j=3$, $5>4$, yielding the assertion. [F1, step 1.1] ∎


## External canonical top-weight motivic-to-syntomic comparison

[Open item](item-thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-topweight-comparison) · level 10


### Statement
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $X$ a finite-type $k$-scheme, $j\geq\dim X$, and $\ell$ any prime. The canonical map of Elmanto–Morrow complexes
$$\mathbb Z(j)_{\rm mot}(X)\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathbb Z/\ell\longrightarrow\mathbb F_\ell(j)_{\rm syn}(X)$$
is an equivalence. If $\ell$ is invertible in $k$, the target is $R\Gamma_{\acute et}(X,\mu_\ell^{\otimes j})$. If $\ell=\operatorname{char}k$, the target is the derived syntomic theory specified in [thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-em-syntomic](item-thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-em-syntomic).

### External input
Import the published report Theorem4, not its application to torsion-freeness. Its proof uses Artin vanishing at invertible primes. In characteristic $p$, it kills the cdh Artin–Schreier obstruction by henselian rigidity and the Kato–Kuzumaki bound for residue fields of transcendence degree at most $j$ over an algebraically closed field. Interpret that obstruction through the precise fiber sequence in [thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-em-syntomic](item-thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-em-syntomic). Thus this input concerns the actual map and specified EM theory, not merely abstractly isomorphic groups. The report's proof, not a purported reconstruction of the deeper field/rigidity results, is imported. Theorem4 has no reducedness hypothesis.

### Source qualification
In the published report, Theorem 3(2), printed p.1994, has an étale lower-right corner; EM v1 Theorem 4.28, printed p.29, has the éh corner, identified there with the cdh localization of the étale presheaf. We retain this as a qualified discrepancy and do not import the report's printed square on arbitrary singular schemes. The precise comparison is supplied by [thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-em-syntomic](item-thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-em-syntomic).

The report's characteristic-$p$ proof of Theorem 4, printed p.1995, describes the cofiber without its shift. With its cited Artin–Schreier obstruction convention, EM v1 Corollary 4.32 gives the cofiber $R\Gamma_{\rm cdh}(X,\widetilde\nu_1(j))[-j-1]$. This is a confirmed nonfatal source-display omission: vanishing of the obstruction also kills its shift. It does not refute Theorem 4, whose full finite-type scope is retained. The reducedness premise of the separate Theorem 1 is not a premise of Theorem 4.


## Natural unital bigraded motivic ring with negative zero extension

[Open item](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-bigraded-ring) · level 10

### Statement
Let $k$ be any field. On qcqs $k$-schemes set $C_b(X)=\mathbb Z(b)_{\rm mot}(X)$ for $b\geq0$, and explicitly set $C_b(X)=0$ for $b<0$. Define $H^{a,b}(X)=H^a(C_b(X))$ for every pair of integers. The direct sum $H^{*,*}(X)$ is naturally an associative unital ring, with products of bidegrees $(a,b)+(c,d)=(a+c,b+d)$, unit in $(0,0)$, and $xy=(-1)^{ac}yx$. Pullbacks are contravariantly functorial unital ring homomorphisms. This extends the supplied groups without modifying their nonnegative weights.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] [thm-author-79117e1d72ed-em-multiplication-c1](item-thm-author-79117e1d72ed-em-multiplication-c1) supplies the natural commutative graded spectrum $G_b(X)=C_b(X)[2b]$, its unit and products; negative pieces are zero.

[F2] [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) fixes the specified complexes and cohomology groups; [def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum](item-def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum) specifies the associated graded products. A cochain complex $C$ has underlying spectrum with $H^a(C)=\pi_{-a}C$; the symmetry on $S^u\wedge S^v$ has sign $(-1)^{uv}$.

### Proof
**Given:** $k,X$ as stated, all integer bidegrees.

**Goal:** Construct and justify the ring and pullbacks.

1.1 For $b\geq0$ identify $H^{a,b}(X)=\pi_{2b-a}G_b(X)$ by [F1]. Multiplying representatives in homotopy groups with the actual graded product $G_b\wedge G_d\to G_{b+d}$ defines the stated bilinear product. If either weight is negative its group is zero; define that product to be zero. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 The unit $\mathbb S\to G_0$ gives $1_X\in H^{0,0}(X)$. Associativity and the unit identities follow by applying homotopy groups to the coherent diagrams in [F1]. Swapping homogeneous classes contributes $(-1)^{(2b-a)(2d-c)}=(-1)^{ac}$; hence the required graded commutativity follows. Cases with a zero negative-weight factor satisfy these identities as well. Finite-support sums define the direct-sum ring. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Each morphism of schemes induces a map of these unital graded algebra objects. Its homotopy-group maps preserve the products, unit, identities and composites. The unique maps on the zero pieces preserve these assertions for negative weights. Restriction from the prime subfield to $k$ is composition of contravariant functors, so all these claims hold for arbitrary $k$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## The actual EM first Chern class is additive and natural

[Open item](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-additive-c1) · level 10

### Statement
For every qcqs scheme $X$ over a field, define $c_1$ to be the degree-two map of EM Definition5.2. Then $c_1:\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to H^{2,1}(X)$ is a natural group homomorphism. In particular $c_1(L\otimes M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M)$, $c_1(\mathcal O_X)=0$, and $c_1(L^\vee)=-c_1(L)$.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] [thm-author-79117e1d72ed-em-multiplication-c1](item-thm-author-79117e1d72ed-em-multiplication-c1) supplies the actual natural map $R\Gamma_{\rm Nis}(X,\mathbb G_m)[-1]\to C_1(X)$, and its source degree two identifies with $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ under tensor product.

[F2] [math:def-picard-group-scheme](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-picard-group-scheme) defines this group and identifies its inverse with duality.

### Proof
**Given:** $X,L,M$ as stated.

**Goal:** Justify this definition, additivity and naturality.

1.1 Apply $H^2$ to the map in [F1]. A map in the derived category induces an abelian-group homomorphism on cohomology, so its Picard map is additive for the tensor-product group law. ## Quotient and line projectivizations agree after dualizing

[Open item](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-dual-conventions) · level 10


### Statement
Assume AC. For a rank-$r>0$ finite locally free sheaf $E$ on $X$, let $Q_X(E)=\operatorname{Proj}_X\operatorname{Sym}(E)$ denote the quotient projectivization, and let $P_X^{\rm lin}(E^\vee)$ denote EM’s projectivization of rank-one subbundles in $E^\vee$. There is a canonical base-change-compatible $X$-isomorphism $\alpha:Q_X(E)\simeq P_X^{\rm lin}(E^\vee)$ identifying the quotient $\mathcal O_Q(1)$ with the dual of the subbundle $\mathcal O_{P^{\rm lin}}(-1)$. In particular $\alpha^*\mathcal O_{P^{\rm lin}}(1)\simeq\mathcal O_Q(1)$, with no sign change of $c_1$. Here subbundle means an inclusion whose cokernel is locally free.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice, as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). It is used in step 2.1 to invoke the AC-qualified line-quotient representation in [F1]; that published supplier uses it to select trivializing affine data.

[F1] [math:thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients) gives the natural representation of quotient lines. [thm-author-79117e1d72ed-em-multiplication-c1](item-thm-author-79117e1d72ed-em-multiplication-c1) records the source line convention and tautological dual.

[F2] Finite locally free sheaves are canonically isomorphic to their double duals, checked on finite free local frames. A surjection onto a free rank-one sheaf locally splits: lift its basis section; elementary row operations show that its kernel is finite free of rank one less.

### Proof
**Given:** AC, $E$ as stated and a test scheme $g:T\to X$.

**Goal:** Construct the isomorphism and identify its actual tautological line.

1.1 Dualizing a quotient $g^*E\twoheadrightarrow L$ gives $L^\vee\hookrightarrow g^*(E^\vee)$ with locally free cokernel by the local splitting in [F2]. Conversely, dualizing a rank-one subbundle $S\hookrightarrow g^*E^\vee$ gives $g^*E\twoheadrightarrow S^\vee$, using the local splitting of its locally free cokernel and double duality. The two operations are inverse on isomorphism classes. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 These bijections commute with pullback, because all sheaves are finite locally free and the sequences locally split. Under [A1], the representing properties in [F1] give inverse morphisms $\alpha$. Applying the construction to the universal quotient identifies $S=L^\vee$, hence $S^\vee=L$; this is exactly the asserted identification of the two bundles named $\mathcal O(1)$. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 For any base change the same correspondence applies, so the isomorphism and tautological identification commute with it. The Chern class is applied to the identical line bundle $S^\vee=L$, not to its inverse, so no negative sign is introduced. [step 2.1] ∎

$$C_{r,F}|_{S_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq z^r(-,\bullet)[-2r].$$
In particular, the restriction to the entire diagram of opens of this fixed $S$ is coherent, and each cycle arrow is actual open restriction. On that open diagram it also identifies $C_{r,F}$ with the derived-section functor of the MVW classical coefficient complex $\mathbb Z(r)$. Homological degree $n$ is cochain degree $-n$ before shifting. The equivalence may depend on $S$ and $r$; no compatibility between choices for different ambients or weights, or multiplicative compatibility, is asserted. There is no finite-generation requirement on $k/F$.

## Determinant descends on the actual perfect K zero

[Open item](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-perfect-determinant) · level 10


### Statement
For every qcqs scheme $X$, the specified perfect-complex group $K_0(X)=\pi_0\mathbb K(\operatorname{Perf}(X))$ has a natural homomorphism $\det_X:K_0(X)\to\operatorname{Pic}(X)$. On a bounded finite locally free complex $P^\bullet$ its line is $\bigotimes_i(\det P^i)^{(-1)^i}$; this formula is local when no global such representative exists. It agrees with the exterior determinant on a bundle, sends a shift to the inverse line, and respects all cofiber relations. This requires no equality with vector-bundle K zero.

Only these data are used here; a map of K-spaces or naturality for arbitrary ordinary triangle diagrams is not a premise.

[F2] [thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input](item-thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input) identifies the cofiber Grothendieck presentation of the supplied essentially small stable idempotent-complete perfect category with its actual spectral $K_0$, naturally by the object-class map. [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) fixes this category and its exact derived pullbacks. [def-scheme-perfect-complexes](item-def-scheme-perfect-complexes) identifies its homotopy category with the full perfect subcategory of the sheaf-derived category, with cofibers represented by mapping cones.

[F3] [def-exterior-determinant-bundles](item-def-exterior-determinant-bundles) fixes exterior determinants and the Picard group law. On a bundle of locally varying rank, apply its constant-rank construction on the disjoint open rank loci.

[A1] AC and the fixed universe bounds are those already assumed in the specified enhanced model in [F2]; [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) states AC. They are used here through that supplied model and its essentially small presentation. The class argument makes no simultaneous choice of bundle representatives or triangle isomorphisms.


**Given:** $X$ qcqs, AC and the fixed universes of the specified perfect-complex model.

**Goal:** Descend the global determinant to its actual $K_0$, with the stated formulas and naturality.

### Proof
1.1 Assign to a perfect object $P$ the Picard class $d(P)$ of the underlying line of its global graded determinant in [F1]. Derived-isomorphism invariance makes $d(P)$ depend only on its object equivalence class, and $d(0)=0$. Forgetting the grading is done only on isomorphism classes, after using the graded determinant data. [F1, F3, A1]

2.1 For any complex representing $P$, the identity mapping cone is acyclic, and the termwise split short-exact complex diagram $0\to P\to\operatorname{Cone}(1_P)\to P[1]\to0$ is a true triangle of perfect complexes. Its determinant additivity gives $d(P)+d(P[1])=d(\operatorname{Cone}(1_P))=d(0)=0$. This proves the inverse-line identity without assuming triangle functoriality in the ordinary derived category. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Given an enhanced cofiber sequence $P\to Q\to R$, pass to its distinguished triangle in the supplied sheaf-derived category. Represent its first morphism by a roof and replace its source by the quasi-isomorphic complex $P'$ in that roof, obtaining an actual complex map $a:P'\to Q$ whose cone represents $R$. All three objects are perfect by [F2], although these representing complexes need not be globally bounded complexes of bundles. The globally defined termwise split short-exact complex diagram $0\to Q\to\operatorname{Cone}(a)\to P'[1]\to0$ is a KM true triangle. Thus [F1] and step 2.1 give $d(R)=d(Q)+d(P'[1])=d(Q)-d(P)$, so every actual cofiber relation is killed. Only existence of these isomorphisms is needed for the equality of Picard classes. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Extend $P\mapsto d(P)$ to the free abelian object-class group. By step 3.1 it descends through all its cofiber relations, and the object-class isomorphism of [F2] gives the homomorphism on the specified spectral $K_0$. For a morphism $f:Y\to X$ of qcqs schemes, [F1] identifies the global determinant of $Lf^*P$ with the pullback determinant of $P$; the naturality of the object-class map in [F2] therefore makes these homomorphisms natural in $X$. Exactness of the supplied derived pullback, rather than flatness of $f$, is what is used. [F1, F2, step 3.1]

5.1 On any open with a bounded finite locally free representative, [F1] gives the alternating tensor formula in the Statement. In degree zero it is the exterior determinant of [F3], and step 2.1 gives the shift formula. These are formulas for restrictions of an already global line: the line and its descent isomorphisms come from [F1]. They do not assert that an arbitrary perfect class is globally a bundle difference or admits a global bounded bundle representative. This proves the full qcqs statement. [F1, F3, step 2.1, step 4.1] ∎



## Derived global sections on a scheme site

[Open item](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites) · level 11


### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fixed universe size bounds. For each $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Nis},\mathrm{cdh},\mathrm{et}\}$, fix a small scheme site $\mathcal C_\tau$ equipped with the indicated Nisnevich, cdh, or étale topology, and an object represented by the scheme $X$. The choice of site and topology is part of the data; these names alone do not identify a big site with a small one.

An abelian sheaf is a contravariant functor from the site to abelian groups whose underlying set-valued presheaf satisfies the sheaf condition. Let $D(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C_\tau))$ be its unbounded derived category: complexes are localized at the chain maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves. For $C$ in this category define $R\Gamma_\tau(X,C)$ as the right derived functor of evaluation at $X$, with value in the derived category $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ of complexes of abelian groups. Concretely, for a representative complex choose a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex $I^\bullet$ and take the derived-category class of $I^\bullet(X)$. K-injective means that every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I^\bullet$ is chain-homotopic to zero. Set $H^n_\tau(X,C)=H^n(R\Gamma_\tau(X,C))$, where $H^n$ is the kernel of the degree-$n$ differential modulo the preceding image.

For an ordinary abelian sheaf $F$ regarded as a complex concentrated in degree zero, $H^n_\tau(X,F)=0$ for $n<0$. This convention does not assert a comparison between the three topologies or an identification between sheafification and derived localization.

### Definition references
[def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification)

[lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input](item-lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input)

### Justification
The already stated Choice premise is inherited by the selected K-injective construction and its derived evaluation. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

The chosen site and object make evaluation meaningful, and the size bounds specify the ambient categories. [lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input](item-lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input) supplies the abelian category, existence and choice-independent derived-functor interpretation of K-injective evaluation, and a nonnegative injective resolution computing the value for $F[0]$. Applying [lem-author-a44f2061570d-nonnegative-resolution](item-lem-author-a44f2061570d-nonnegative-resolution) to that resolution proves the negative-degree assertion. These inputs apply to each chosen topology separately; no comparison among them is used.


## Units split the K one determinant

[Open item](item-lem-unit-section-of-k-one-determinant) · level 11

### Statement
Assume AC and let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, with K(X)=𝕂(Perf(X)) as specified in [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface). There is a natural group homomorphism

$$s_X:\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times\longrightarrow K_1(X),\qquad u\longmapsto[\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal O_X].$$

There is a natural determinant homomorphism det_X:K₁(X)→Γ(X,$O_X$)×, characterized by the usual stable matrix determinant on each affine restriction under the explicit affine comparison. It satisfies det_X∘$s_X$=id; hence determinant is surjective and $s_X$ injective. For a vector-bundle automorphism α, det_X([α]) is the unit inducing the top-exterior-power automorphism det(α) of its determinant line (defined locally on rank loci). Neither a global resolution property nor regularity/noetherian hypotheses are required. This statement makes no identification of a motivic projection with determinant.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** qcqs X, AC, the supplied perfect enhancement and nonconnective K functor; rings below are commutative and unital. The notation [α] is the automorphism loop under the natural core→connective K→nonconnective K construction, not an object class in K₀.

**Goal:** Establish the precise affine π₁ comparison and unit normalization, construct det_X and $s_X$, and prove the splitting.

[F1] [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) supplies the actual sheaf-derived perfect model and exact pullbacks. [lem-author-4f716d60801a-lifted-affine-equivalence](item-lem-author-4f716d60801a-lifted-affine-equivalence) and [lem-author-4f716d60801a-finite-projective-model](item-lem-author-4f716d60801a-finite-projective-model) identify its affine fiber with the enhanced bounded finite-projective model. [lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-derived-tensor-pullback](item-lem-author-c5bc2838d897-kcoherent-derived-tensor-pullback) identifies actual affine pullback with derived extension of scalars on those representatives.

[F2] [thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-classical-comparisons](item-thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-classical-comparisons) supplies the matrix/Quillen/S/Gillet–Waldhausen comparisons, with their automorphism-class normalization.

[F3] [thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-enhanced-comparisons](item-thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-enhanced-comparisons) supplies the actual Waldhausen-to-infinity K comparison, the natural automorphism classes and j inducing an isomorphism on π₁ to the supplied nonconnective functor.

[F4] [lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-stable-matrix-determinant](item-lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-stable-matrix-determinant) constructs determinant on GL(A)_ab; [lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-determinant-base-change](item-lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-determinant-base-change) proves its ring-map naturality.

[F5] [lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-gluing-units](item-lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-gluing-units) and [lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-local-determinant-gluing](item-lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-local-determinant-gluing) supply unit sheaf gluing and the induced homomorphism. [lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-split-surjective-homomorphism](item-lem-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-split-surjective-homomorphism) gives surjectivity and injectivity from a right inverse.

[F6] [def-exterior-determinant-bundles](item-def-exterior-determinant-bundles) supplies the exterior-power determinant line and its local wedge bases and pullback compatibility.

### Proof
1.1 For a ring A, P(A) is split exact: a surjection onto a projective module has a section, so its kernel is a direct summand of the finite projective source and is finite projective. This verifies the kernel-of-surjections hypothesis of Gillet–Waldhausen in [F2]. The Waldhausen category C(A) of bounded finite-projective cochain complexes has mapping cylinders, so every map factors as a degreewise split monomorphism followed by a quasi-isomorphism. Its homotopy category after quasi-isomorphisms is the enhanced perfect category’s homotopy category by [F1]; hence a map is a weak equivalence exactly when it becomes an isomorphism (DHKS-saturation). Indeed the cone of a quasi-isomorphism between bounded projectives is bounded acyclic projective and contractible: apply the K-projective mapping property in [F1] to its identity. Thus the comparison hypotheses in [F3] hold. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Compose the actual maps of [F2], the actual Waldhausen/infinity comparison of [F3], j on π₁ from [F3], and the exact affine enhancement equivalence of [F1]. They give an isomorphism $c_A:GL(A)_{ab}\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_1\mathbb K(\operatorname{Perf}(\operatorname{Spec}A))$. Every step carries an automorphism M of Aⁿ to the class of that same degree-zero automorphism: degree-zero inclusion is literal, the S-construction comparisons use its core loop, and associated sheaf sends it to its matrix acting on $O^n$. Thus $c_A([u])=[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal O]$. This uses π₁ agreement in the positive-degree range of j; no π₀-only comparison is substituted. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 This $c_A$ is natural for unital A→B. Extension of scalars takes finite projectives to finite projectives and preserves split monomorphisms. A bounded projective quasi-isomorphism is a homotopy equivalence by step 1.1, so tensor with B preserves it without a flatness hypothesis. Hence it is weakly exact on C(A). All comparisons are induced by the corresponding actual functors in [F1]–[F3], and on matrix generators they send M to its entrywise image. The resulting π₁ naturality square commutes. Define $d_A=\det_A\circ c_A^{-1}$; [F4] makes these homomorphisms commute with all such ring maps, and $d_A$([u])=u by step 2.1. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Given k∈K₁(X), on each affine open V=Spec(A) take $d_A(k|_V)\in\mathcal O_X(V)^\times$. On an intersection of two affine opens, restrict further to any affine neighbourhood W inside that intersection. Naturality from step 3.1 identifies both restrictions with $d_{\mathcal O(W)}(k|_W)$. They therefore agree as sections on the intersection by the sheaf uniqueness axiom. Apply [F5] to glue a unique global unit det_X(k). The same gluing lemma shows det_X is a homomorphism and independent of the affine cover. [F1, F4, F5, step 3.1]

5.1 A global unit is the automorphism $m_u$ of $O_X$. The natural automorphism map in [F3] defines $s_X$(u)=[$m_u$]. Composition $m_u m_v=m_{uv}$ makes $s_X$ a group homomorphism. It is compatible with scheme pullback by [F1] and [F3]. Restriction to an affine V sends its class to the class [u|_V] of step 2.1. [F1, F3, step 2.1, step 4.1]

6.1 The restriction of det_X($s_X$(u)) to each affine V is u|_V by steps 3.1 and 5.1. Unit sheaf uniqueness in [F5] gives det_X($s_X$(u))=u globally. The right-inverse lemma in [F5] proves surjectivity of determinant and injectivity of $s_X$. For f:Y→X between qcqs schemes, choose an affine V around f(y) and an affine W around y inside f⁻¹(V). Step 3.1 proves determinant naturality on W; sheaf uniqueness then proves it globally. Thus both maps are natural on the stated category. [F1, F5, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 For an automorphism α of a vector bundle E, choose affine opens where E is free of constant rank. Naturality of the automorphism construction restricts [α] to the matrix class of α there. The top-wedge expansion in [F6] says that its action on det(E) is multiplication by that matrix determinant, exactly the local unit used in step 4.1. These local units glue uniquely; a line-bundle automorphism is canonically multiplication by a unit, because that is true on trivializations and scalar multiplication commutes with transition units. Thus det_X([α]) has the asserted exterior determinant interpretation. The empty scheme has only the unique unit and zero K-group, so the same assertion also includes it. This completes the proof. [F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, step 4.1, step 6.1] ∎



## Isomorphism classes of vector bundles

[Open item](item-def-vector-bundle-classes) · level 11

### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the suitable universes used for the supplied perfect K-theory construction. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme and $n$ a nonnegative integer. A **vector bundle** on $X$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module: each point has an open neighbourhood on which it is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_X$. It has **rank $n$** if every point has such a neighbourhood with exactly $n$ copies. An isomorphism of vector bundles is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism. Write $\mathrm{Vect}_n(X)$ for the set of their isomorphism classes and $[E]_{\mathrm{iso}}$ for the class of a rank-$n$ bundle $E$ in that set.

The supplied nonconnective perfect K-theory spectrum is $K(X)=\mathbb K(\operatorname{Perf}(X))$, and $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$. A bundle $E$, regarded as a complex concentrated in degree zero, is perfect. Write $[E]\in K_0(X)$ for its object class in this spectral K-zero group. The unit of the ring $K_0(X)$ is denoted $1=[\mathcal O_X]$. Here $[E]$ denotes a K-zero class, not an isomorphism class in $\mathrm{Vect}_n(X)$.

If $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative unital ring $A$, the supplied affine comparison identifies this $K_0(X)$ with the vector-bundle Grothendieck group: the abelian group generated by bundle isomorphism classes subject to $[E]=[E']+[E'']$ for every short exact sequence $0\to E'\to E\to E''\to0$ of vector bundles. Under the comparison the two meanings of $[E]$ agree. This affine assertion makes no identification of perfect K-theory with coherent-sheaf G-theory.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme $X$, a nonnegative integer $n$, the Axiom of Choice and suitable universes.

**Goal:** Define the set of bundle isomorphism classes and justify the spectral class, unit and stated affine comparison.

[F1] A finite locally free sheaf has well-defined local rank, and a bundle is locally a finite free sheaf. [math:def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank)

[F2] A complex locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves is perfect. The perfect category contains such complexes. [def-scheme-perfect-complexes](item-def-scheme-perfect-complexes)

[F3] For qcqs $X$, the supplied spectrum is defined on the essentially small perfect category; its multiplication has unit induced by $\mathcal O_X$. For a small idempotent-complete stable category, the object-class map identifies the cofiber Grothendieck group with $\pi_0$ of its supplied nonconnective K-theory. [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface), [thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input](item-thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input)

[F4] Assuming AC and suitable universes, for $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ commutative and unital, the spectral degree-zero group is canonically isomorphic to the vector-bundle Grothendieck group and sends the spectral class of $E[0]$ to the bundle class of $E$. [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge)

[F5] The article conventions define qcqs schemes and use finite locally free sheaves as vector bundles. [def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions), [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Justification
1.1 The open subsets of $X$ form a set. For each indexed open cover drawn from that set, rank-$n$ bundles trivialized on the cover are described up to isomorphism by transition matrices in $\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathcal O_X(U\cap V))$ satisfying the identity, inverse and cocycle conditions. These matrices form a set; changing trivializations acts by a set of invertible matrices, and its equivalence classes form a set. Taking the union over covers and identifying data defining isomorphic sheaves gives a set of isomorphism classes. Every rank-$n$ bundle occurs by its local triviality, and an isomorphism preserves local rank. Thus $\mathrm{Vect}_n(X)$ is well-defined, including when $X$ is empty. [F1, F5, construct]

2.1 By local freeness, $E[0]$ is locally a bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves, so it is an object of $\operatorname{Perf}(X)$. The object-class map in [F3] assigns it a well-defined element of $\pi_0K(X)$, invariant under isomorphism. The unit statement in [F3] identifies the multiplicative unit with the class of $\mathcal O_X[0]$. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 If $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ as stated, the hypotheses of [F4] hold; its comparison identifies the spectral and vector-bundle classes on every generator. This establishes the stated notation and affine comparison. No corresponding identification with coherent G-theory is used. [F4, step 2.1] ∎

## Motivic filtration and image groups

[Open item](item-def-motivic-filtration) · level 11


### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix a field $k$, algebraically closed under the article convention unless otherwise specified. Write $\mathrm{Sch}_k$ for the category of quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms, as in [def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions). For $X$ in this category, let $K(X)$ be the nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum of perfect complexes, and let $K_i(X)=\pi_iK(X)$ for every integer $i$, as in [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface).

The **motivic filtration** $F^\bullet_{\mathrm{mot}}K$ is the Elmanto–Morrow functorial multiplicative nonnegative filtration supplied by [thm-author-98a750efd0cc-motivic-filtration-input](item-thm-author-98a750efd0cc-motivic-filtration-input), restricted from the prime field of $k$ to $k$-schemes. Extend it to integer indices by the construction of [lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-extension](item-lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-extension). Thus it is a functor

$$F^\bullet_{\mathrm{mot}}K:\mathrm{Sch}_k^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{FilSp}),$$

where $\operatorname{FilSp}$ is the category of integer-indexed decreasing spectra with coherent transitions and $\operatorname{CAlg}$ denotes its coherently commutative, associative and unital algebra objects, as specified in [def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum](item-def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum). Its zeroth stage is naturally equivalent to $K(X)$; we use that equivalence to write $F^0_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=K(X)$. Its multiplication includes maps

$$F^a_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\wedge F^b_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow F^{a+b}_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$$

for all integers $a,b$, coherently compatible with transitions, pullback and the multiplication on $K(X)$.

For $i\in\mathbb Z$ and $j\geq0$, define the **image filtration group**

$$F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_i(X)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_iF^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow K_i(X)\bigr).$$

The arrow is induced by the transition to stage zero and its identification with $K(X)$. Its image is a subgroup, and the induced map onto that subgroup is surjective. The same formula also makes sense for negative $j$ under the stated extension, in which case it gives all of $K_i(X)$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A field $k$, a qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, the Axiom of Choice, and the integer indices specified above.

**Goal:** Justify the functor, its augmentation and multiplication, and the image-group definition without reconstructing the external filtration.

[F1] [def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions) defines the scheme category; every field contains its prime field, either $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$.

[F2] The assumed Choice premise, [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), discharges the explicit AC hypothesis of [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) when its common-family perfect-complex realization and essentially small nonconnective-functor domain are invoked. That interface supplies contravariant nonconnective $K$, all integer homotopy groups and the ambient ring structure. [thm-author-98a750efd0cc-motivic-filtration-input](item-thm-author-98a750efd0cc-motivic-filtration-input) imports the nonnegative filtration, functoriality, multiplication and zeroth-stage equivalence on qcqs schemes over the prime field.

[F3] [lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-extension](item-lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-extension) supplies the integer-indexed extension; [def-decreasing-filtered-spectrum](item-def-decreasing-filtered-spectrum) and [def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum](item-def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum) specify its augmentation and coherent algebra-object notation.

[F4] [lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-image](item-lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-image), [lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-nesting](item-lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-nesting), [lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-naturality](item-lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-naturality) and [lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-products](item-lem-author-98a750efd0cc-filtration-products) establish, respectively, subgroup and surjectivity, nesting, naturality and compatibility of products for such images.

### Justification
1.1 Invoke the perfect-complex $K$-theory interface in [F2] under the assumed Choice premise. The structure morphism of each $k$-scheme composes with $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb F$ for its prime field $\mathbb F$. Its underlying scheme remains qcqs, and every $k$-morphism is an $\mathbb F$-morphism. Restrict the functor in [F2] along this forgetful functor; no finite-type, regularity or finite-dimensional assumption is needed. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Apply the extension in [F3] to the restricted nonnegative tower. Its stage zero is naturally equivalent to $K$, and its coherent products give the displayed maps. The extension and all maps are functorial because they are built from the original transitions and products. The equality at stage zero is notation for the supplied natural equivalence. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply the image lemma in [F4] to each stage-to-$K$ map. The subgroup and surjectivity statements follow. Nesting, pullback compatibility and product containment follow from the remaining lemmas in [F4]. If $j<0$, the extended stage and its map to $K$ are identified with $K$ and its identity, so the image is the whole group. This justifies the definition and its stated properties. [F3, F4, step 2.1] ∎

### Scope
The external construction is not reconstructed here. No completeness, boundedness, associated-graded identification or injectivity of a stage-to-$K$ map is asserted by this definition.


## Finite refinement for integer cdh sections

[Open item](item-prop-cdh-cover-refinement) · level 11

### Statement
On the specified site of separated finite-type schemes over a field $k$, every cdh covering sieve $S$ on $X$ contains a finite covering family $\{U_i\to X\}$. Its finite coproduct $W=\coprod_iU_i\to X$ is a covering morphism and has an MVW two-stage refinement
$$V\xrightarrow{q}X'\xrightarrow{p}X,$$
where $p$ is completely decomposed proper and $q$ is Nisnevich, with a map $h:V\to W$ over $X$. Splitting $V$ into the finite clopen pieces $V_i=h^{-1}(U_i)$ gives a finite Nisnevich family over $X'$ whose composites to $X$ all belong to $S$. Neither $W\to X$ nor $V\to X$ is asserted to belong to $S$.

Every section of the constant integer cdh sheaf has finitely many constant local representatives on such a finite covering family, and therefore factors through the sheafification of a finite subset of $\mathbb Z$. If desired the above two-stage refinement may be chosen for that representing family, retaining its finitely many representative values on the split pieces. No conclusion for an arbitrary qcqs base outside this site is asserted.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The exact finite-type cdh site, a covering sieve $S$, and, for the last assertion, $s\in H^0_{\mathrm{cdh}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z$ meaning the sheafification of the constant presheaf.

**Goal:** Prove finite refinement and finite local values without a coproduct-in-sieve assumption.

[F1] [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-nisnevich-subfamily](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-nisnevich-subfamily), [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-cdh-generators-pullback-composition](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-cdh-generators-pullback-composition) and [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-generated-topology-basis](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-generated-topology-basis) prove that covering sieves contain finite composite generating families.

[F2] [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-coproduct-sieve-refinement](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-finite-coproduct-sieve-refinement) proves that their coproduct is a covering morphism and explains how any two-stage refinement is split back into arrows of the original sieve.

[F3] [thm-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-mvw-finite-type-cdh-two-stage-input](item-thm-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-mvw-finite-type-cdh-two-stage-input) imports MVW12.26/12.28 and identifies its topology with the specified one, under exactly these hypotheses.

[F4] [lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-constant-sheaf-finite-local-representatives](item-lem-author-5bfbe3ebf14f-constant-sheaf-finite-local-representatives) supplies local representability from the actual two-plus sheafification and the finite constant-set factorization. [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification) fixes that convention.

### Proof
1.1 Apply [F1] to $S$ to obtain a finite $B$-family $\{U_i\to X\}$ whose arrows individually lie in $S$. By [F2] its finite coproduct $W\to X$ is a cdh covering morphism. All schemes remain separated of finite type over $k$. Therefore [F3] applies to this morphism and gives $V\to X'\to X$ and $h:V\to W$ with the claimed proper and Nisnevich conditions. Lemma12.26 in [F3] identifies that proper cover as completely decomposed. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Apply [F2] to $h$: the $V_i$ form a finite clopen decomposition of $V$, their maps to $X'$ are a Nisnevich family, and their composites to $X$ factor through the corresponding $U_i\to X$. Those composites consequently lie in $S$. This proves the sieve-level two-stage refinement in its precise family sense; no coproduct arrow has been added to $S$. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 For an integer section use [F4] to obtain its covering sieve of constant representatives, then a finite $B$-family in that sieve. The finitely many representatives $n_i$ give its factorization through the constant-set sheaf of $D=\{n_i\}$. Apply steps 1.1 and 2.1 to this family if a two-stage form is desired. Since $V_i\to X$ factors through $U_i$, the representative on $V_i$ remains $n_i$; no new values appear. This proves the finite-values assertion and completes the proposition with the original cover-refinement claim preserved. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Characteristic-zero coefficient vanishing and torsion freeness

[Open item](item-lem-characteristic-zero-top-torsion) · level 11


### Statement
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let $X$ be an affine threefold over $k$. For every prime $p$, choosing a primitive $p$th root of unity in $k$ gives an isomorphism
$$H^{5,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)\cong H^5_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)=0.$$
Consequently multiplication by $p$ is injective on $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ for every prime $p$, and this group is torsion-free.

Here affine threefold means $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra and $\dim X=3$, as in [def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions); no smoothness, reducedness, or irreducibility is assumed. The motivic groups are the cohomology of the Elmanto–Morrow weight-three complex, with finite coefficients formed by derived tensor product after evaluation, as defined in [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology). The étale group is the cohomology of the small étale site of $X$ with the constant sheaf $\mathbb Z/p$. Torsion-free means that no nonzero element is annihilated by a positive integer.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An algebraically closed characteristic-zero field $k$, an affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension three, and a prime $p$.

**Goal:** Establish the displayed isomorphism and vanishing, the coefficient-sequence injectivity, and torsion-freeness.

[F1] [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) defines $C=\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)$, $H^{i,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)=H^i(C)$, and $H^{i,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)=H^i(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathbb Z/p)$.

[F2] [thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-topweight-comparison](item-thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-topweight-comparison) gives, for finite-type $X$ over an algebraically closed field and weight $j\geq\dim X$, an equivalence from the actual finite-coefficient motivic complex to $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_p^{\otimes j})$ when $p$ is invertible in the field. Here $\mu_p$ is the étale sheaf of $p$th roots of unity and $\mu_p^{\otimes j}$ is its $j$-fold tensor power over $\mathbb Z/p$.

[F3] [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-chosen-root](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-chosen-root) says that a chosen primitive $p$th root $\zeta\in k$ induces an isomorphism of étale sheaves $\mathbb Z/p\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_p^{\otimes3}$, sending $1$ to $\zeta^{\otimes3}$. [thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-artin-affine](item-thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-artin-affine) gives $H^i_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_p^{\otimes3})=0$ for $i>\dim X$ under the present affine, finite-type and invertibility hypotheses.

[F4] [lem-derived-coefficient-exact-sequence](item-lem-derived-coefficient-exact-sequence) supplies the exact sequence $H^5(C/p)\to H^6(C)\xrightarrow{p}H^6(C)$, where $C/p=C\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathbb Z/p$. [lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-primewise](item-lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-primewise) says an abelian group is torsion-free if multiplication by every prime is injective.

### Proof

1.1 Characteristic zero makes $p$ invertible in $k$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, $T^p-1$ splits in $k$; its roots are distinct because its derivative $pT^{p-1}$ has no common root with it. The group of its $p$ roots has order $p$, so any nonidentity root $\zeta$ has order $p$. Thus the chosen-root hypothesis of [F3] holds. [given, F3, construct]

2.1 Apply [F2] with $j=3=\dim X$. Using [F1] and taking degree-five cohomology gives an isomorphism from $H^{5,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)$ to $H^5_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_p^{\otimes3})$. The inverse of the coefficient isomorphism in [F3] identifies this with $H^5_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)$. The latter identification depends on the choice of $\zeta$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 By affine étale vanishing in [F3], $H^5_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_p^{\otimes3})=0$ because $5>3$. Step 2.1 therefore proves both the displayed isomorphism and the vanishing. [F3, step 2.1]

4.1 The first term of the exact sequence in [F4] is zero by [F1] and step 3.1. Exactness therefore makes multiplication by $p$ injective on $H^6(C)=H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. [F1, F4, step 3.1]

5.1 The argument applies to every prime $p$. The primewise criterion in [F4] now shows that $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is torsion-free. This proves all assertions. [F4, step 4.1] ∎


## Critical-rank representatives of rank-zero classes

[Open item](item-lem-critical-rank-representatives) · level 11


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and suitable universes. Let $X$ be a nonempty affine scheme of finite type over a field, of dimension $d=2$ or $3$. Every class $\alpha$ of pointwise rank zero in $K_0(X)=\pi_0 K(X)$ can be written $\alpha=[E]-[\mathcal O_X^d]$ for a vector bundle $E$ of constant rank $d$. Moreover, any vector bundle $V$ of constant rank $r\geq d$ is isomorphic to $E'\oplus\mathcal O_X^{r-d}$ for a vector bundle $E'$ of rank $d$.

A vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module; its rank at a point is the number of copies of the structure sheaf in a local trivialization there. Constant rank means the same rank at every point. The dimension is the supremum of the lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. The spectrum $K(X)$ is the nonconnective K-theory of perfect complexes in the supplied interface. The class of a vector bundle in $K_0(X)$ is the class of the complex concentrated in degree zero. Pointwise rank on $K_0(X)$ is transported through the affine K-zero isomorphism to the rank homomorphism on the vector-bundle Grothendieck group: a difference $[B]-[C]$ has rank $\operatorname{rank}_x B-\operatorname{rank}_x C$ at $x$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, suitable universes, and $X$ and $d$ as in the statement.

**Goal:** Represent every pointwise rank-zero class by a rank-$d$ bundle minus the trivial rank-$d$ bundle, and split any constant-rank bundle down to rank $d$.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice is used through the assumed contracts of the affine perfect-K-zero bridge and finite-projective-complement suppliers in step 1.1, and of Serre splitting in steps 3.1 and 4.1. Padding in step 2.1 requires no additional choice. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] For an affine scheme, the supplied bridge identifies $K_0(X)$ with the vector-bundle Grothendieck group $K^0(X)$ and sends the spectral class of a bundle to its bundle class. This requires the Axiom of Choice and suitable universes. [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge)

[F2] For a locally noetherian affine scheme, under the Axiom of Choice, each element of $K^0(X)$ is $[B]-[\mathcal O_X^N]$ for some vector bundle $B$ and integer $N\geq0$. Its rank at $x$ is $\operatorname{rank}_x B-N$. The construction uses a finite projective complement to turn the negative bundle into a trivial bundle. [lem-finite-projective-complements](item-lem-finite-projective-complements)

[F3] Under the Axiom of Choice, on a nonempty noetherian affine scheme of dimension $d$, a constant-rank-$r$ vector bundle with $r>d$ is isomorphic to a rank-$d$ bundle plus $r-d$ trivial line summands. [thm-serre-affine-splitting](item-thm-serre-affine-splitting)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** First use a finite projective complement to obtain a single bundle minus a trivial bundle, then pad or split off trivial summands.

1.1 A finite-type algebra over a field is noetherian, so $X$ is noetherian and locally noetherian. By [F1] and [F2], write the given rank-zero class as $\alpha=[B]-[\mathcal O_X^N]$ with $N\geq0$. Since its rank is zero at every point, [F2] gives $\operatorname{rank}_x B=N$ for every $x$; thus $B$ has constant rank $N$. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 If $N\leq d$, put $E=B\oplus\mathcal O_X^{d-N}$. Then $E$ has rank $d$, and the direct-sum relation in $K^0(X)$ gives $[E]-[\mathcal O_X^d]=[B]-[\mathcal O_X^N]=\alpha$. [F1, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 If $N>d$, apply [F3] to $B$ to obtain $B\cong E\oplus\mathcal O_X^{N-d}$ with $E$ of rank $d$. The direct-sum relation gives $[B]-[\mathcal O_X^N]=[E]-[\mathcal O_X^d]$. Together with step 2.1, this proves the representative assertion in all cases. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 For the additional assertion, if $r=d$ take $E'=V$; the trivial rank-zero bundle is the zero bundle. If $r>d$, [F3] directly supplies $V\cong E'\oplus\mathcal O_X^{r-d}$ with $E'$ of rank $d$. This proves the stated splitting as well as the representative claim. [A1, F3, given, step 3.1] ∎


## Cdh sheaves invert finite subintegral maps

[Open item](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-subintegral-sheaf-invariance) · level 11

### Statement
If $p:T\to X$ is a finite subintegral morphism of separated finite-type schemes over a field and $F$ is a set-valued cdh sheaf, then restriction $F(X)\to F(T)$ is a bijection. In particular this applies to the finite seminormalization map when it belongs to this category.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $p$ and $F$ as stated.

**Goal:** Prove bijectivity of restriction.

[F1] The singleton $\{p\}$ is a cdh cover. [lem-author-60d95bfb692a-finite-subintegral-cdh-cover](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-finite-subintegral-cdh-cover)

[F2] Every $s\in F(T)$ has equal pullbacks to $T\times_X T$. [lem-author-60d95bfb692a-subintegral-matching](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-subintegral-matching)

[F3] A sheaf has unique amalgamations for covering sieves; restriction to a covering singleton is injective. [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification), [lem-author-60d95bfb692a-cover-restriction-injective](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-cover-restriction-injective)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Glue the matching section along the generated sieve.

1.1 Given $s\in F(T)$, assign to each arrow $v:V\to X$ in the sieve generated by $p$ the pullback $a^*s$ for any factorization $v=pa$. This does not depend on the factorization: two such maps $a,b:V\to T$ define a map $V\to T\times_X T$, and [F2] identifies $a^*s$ and $b^*s$. These assignments are compatible with precomposition. [F2, construct]

2.1 By [F1] and [F3], this matching family has a unique amalgamation in $F(X)$, whose restriction to $T$ is $s$. Restriction is therefore surjective; [F3] also gives injectivity. Thus it is a bijection. [F1, F3, step 1.1] ∎

## The global dimension bound for the specified comparison fiber

[Open item](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-fiber-bound) · level 11

### Statement
For every prime field $F$, every Noetherian $F$-scheme $X$ of finite dimension $d$, and every $j\geq0$, the actual comparison fiber satisfies
$$F_{j,F}(X)\in D(\mathbb Z)^{\leq j+d}.$$
Equivalently $H^i(F_{j,F}(X))=0$ for $i>j+d$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** $F,X,d,j$ as stated and the actual fiber rather than an abstract object with matching groups.

**Goal:** Apply the geometric criterion and undo the normalization with the correct cochain sign.

[F1] [lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-shifted-hypotheses](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-shifted-hypotheses) checks all the criterion hypotheses for $W_{j,F}=F_{j,F}[j]$.

[F2] [thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-dimension-criterion-input](item-thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-dimension-criterion-input) applies to every finite-dimensional Noetherian scheme over the chosen base ring. [lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-general-interface](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-general-interface) specifies the pointwise fiber.

### Proof
1.1 Take the base ring in [F2] to be $F$. A Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: it has a finite affine cover, and the intersection of two affine opens is a Noetherian open, hence quasi-compact. Thus $X$ belongs to the criterion’s scheme domain. With all sheaf and relative hypotheses supplied by [F1], the criterion gives $W_{j,F}(X)\in D(\mathbb Z)^{\leq d}$. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 If $i>j+d$, then $i-j>d$. The shift convention gives $H^i(F_{j,F}(X))=H^{i-j}(W_{j,F}(X))=0$ by step 1.1. This is the claimed bound on the actual fiber. No conclusion has been extracted from a spectral sequence abutting to total K-groups. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎

## The exact projective bundle map in every integer bidegree

[Open item](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-all-bidegrees) · level 11


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be qcqs over a field, $E$ finite locally free of constant rank $r>0$, $\pi:Q_X(E)\to X$, and $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O_Q(1))$. For all integers $a,b$ the map $\bigoplus_{m=0}^{r-1}H^{a-2m,b-m}(X)\to H^{a,b}(Q_X(E))$ given by $(x_m)\mapsto\sum_m\pi^*(x_m)\xi^m$ is an isomorphism, where $H^{a,b}(T)=0$ for $b<0$.

### Statement references
[lem-author-79117e1d72ed-bigraded-ring](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-bigraded-ring)

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice, as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). In step 1.1 it discharges the explicit AC hypothesis of [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-dual-conventions](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-dual-conventions), inherited from the relative-Proj line-quotient representation. No additional geometric hypothesis is imposed.

[F1] [thm-author-79117e1d72ed-em-complex-pbf](item-thm-author-79117e1d72ed-em-complex-pbf) supplies the complex-level equivalence with components given by the actual pullback and powers of EM’s Definition5.2 class for every nonnegative target weight.

[F2] [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-dual-conventions](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-dual-conventions) identifies the relevant projectivizations and tautological lines. [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-bigraded-ring](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-bigraded-ring) and [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-additive-c1](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-additive-c1) specify precisely the product and Chern class being used.

### Proof
**Given:** AC and $X,E,r,a,b$ as stated.

**Goal:** Obtain the exact contracted map in all bidegrees.

1.1 Regard $X$ as a qcqs scheme over the prime subfield of its base field; this does not change its underlying scheme or the supplied motivic complexes. For $b\geq0$, apply [F1] to $E^\vee$ of rank $r$ and target weight $b$. Using [A1] to discharge the AC hypothesis of the dual-conventions supplier in [F2], transport its target through that identification. Each component remains $\xi^m\pi^*$ for the actual product in [F2]. Taking $H^a$ commutes with this finite direct sum, and $H^a(C_{b-m}[-2m])=H^{a-2m,b-m}(X)$. This gives an isomorphism with those components. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 The degree of $\xi^m$ is $2m$, even. Graded commutativity therefore identifies $\xi^m\pi^*(x_m)$ with $\pi^*(x_m)\xi^m$ without a sign, giving exactly the displayed map. For $m=0$ the power is the unit, so the component is pullback. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 For $b<0$, every $b-m<0$ with $m\geq0$. All source groups and the target vanish by the explicit zero convention. The unique homomorphism between these zero groups is an isomorphism, and its formula is the same sum with zero entries. This covers all $a\in\mathbb Z$, including negative cohomological degrees; no truncation was taken. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

### Reading limits
For this repair, read [Elmanto–Morrow, arXiv:2309.08463v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.08463v1), Definition 5.2 and the convention following (5.2), printed p.34, and the component maps, projectivization convention, Theorem 5.24 and its proof, printed pp.43–44. The complex-level equivalence is imported through the external-input supplier in [F1]. Its cited Annala–Iwasa argument and the earlier trace, syntomic and projective-line foundations were not reconstructed.

## A coherent comparison of the particular open restriction

[Open item](item-lem-author-8a080e7d9445-restriction-diagram) · level 11


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the supplied comparisons. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension three, put $U=X_{\mathrm{smooth}/k}$, and let $T\subset X$ be a closed subset contained in $U$. Use the reduced structure on $T$ when a scheme structure is needed. Put $V=U\setminus T$ and $W=X\setminus T$. For the actual arrow $V\hookrightarrow U$, the weight-three motivic restriction diagram is equivalent to the actual cycle restriction diagram
$$[\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(U)\to\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(V)]\simeq[z^3(U,\bullet)[-6]\to z^3(V,\bullet)[-6]].$$
It follows in particular that its $H^6$ arrow is ordinary Chow restriction. The square is supplied before applying cohomology.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** $k,X,U,T,V,W$ and the choice and size assumptions of the statement.

**Goal:** Construct the stated actual maps and prove their consequence.

[F1] [thm-author-8a080e7d9445-em-regular-input](item-thm-author-8a080e7d9445-em-regular-input) and [lem-author-8a080e7d9445-geometry](item-lem-author-8a080e7d9445-geometry).

Both comparison diagrams use the fixed universe bounds. The composition of diagram equivalences makes no additional choice.

### Proof
1.1 Apply the natural regular comparison of [F1] to the two regular Noetherian objects of the geometry lemma and their open arrow. This gives an equivalence of arrow diagrams from the motivic arrow to the cdh arrow. It applies although $k$ need not be finitely generated over its prime field. [F1]

2.1 Apply the fixed-site classical interface of [F2] with the single smooth ambient $S=U$ over the fixed perfect field $k$, and restrict its equivalence to the two opens $U$ and $V$. Compose the equivalences of diagrams, inverting only natural equivalences. Its bottom arrow is the actual open restriction on cycles. Taking $H^6$ gives its degree-zero cycle homology arrow, which is ordinary Chow restriction by the completed degree-zero cycle supplier. This establishes the arrow identification before inferring any surjectivity. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎

## Full affine K-space comparison and its sheafification

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-10deda40f9da-affine-k-space-sheafification) · level 11


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds. For any commutative unital ring $A$, let $\mathcal P(A)$ be its exact category of finite projective modules and let $\mathcal C(A)=\mathrm{Ch}^b(\mathcal P(A))$ have degreewise split cofibrations and quasi-isomorphisms. The canonical comparisons give natural equivalences of entire pointed spaces
$$\Omega BQ\mathcal P(A)\simeq\Omega^\infty K^W(\mathcal C(A))\simeq\Omega^\infty K_{\mathrm{Perf}}(\operatorname{Spec}A).$$
Here $K^W$ is connective Waldhausen K-theory and $K_{\mathrm{Perf}}$ is the specified nonconnective perfect-complex theory. The equivalences include components, preserve direct sum and carry the actual degree-zero object and automorphism maps to those of the same perfect objects.

For every qcqs scheme $X$, these comparisons identify the local sheaf models of the vector-bundle Q-space presheaf and the perfect K-space presheaf on the small Zariski or Nisnevich site, and on the smooth big site with either topology. Quasi-compact objects and quasi-compact open covering bases suffice. Here the local model uses derived sheafification of spaces; when using the source's stalkwise local homotopy convention, take its hypercomplete replacement consistently on both sides. The perfect K-space has its canonical natural map into derived sections of the chosen common model. No global equality of vector-bundle and perfect $K_0$ is asserted.

### External input
Import the full S/Q, Gillet–Waldhausen and BGT comparisons at the exact frontmatter locators. In particular, import BGT Remark 9.33's degree-zero clause with its idempotent-completeness hypothesis, in addition to the positive-degree comparison already supplied locally. The following proof checks their application and the local sheaf consequence; it does not reconstruct the imported foundations.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Choice and the fixed universes are used for the supplied essentially small enhanced models and small presentations. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] The cited Weibel IV.8.5–8.7 and V.2.2 give the natural entire S/Q and bounded-projective K-space comparisons. The object/automorphism maps are the core maps in IV.8.3.2. The current full Quillen–Waldhausen supplier states this entire comparison, with its degree-zero object map; it is used without modification. [thm-adjudicate-9ead0798f06a-projective-q-w-comparison](item-thm-adjudicate-9ead0798f06a-projective-q-w-comparison)

[F2] The enhanced supplier gives the natural full Waldhausen-to-connective comparison and the canonical positive-degree comparison with the specified nonconnective functor. The additional degree-zero clause of BGT Remark 9.33 applies when the underlying stable category is idempotent complete. [thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-enhanced-comparisons](item-thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-enhanced-comparisons)

[F3] The actual bounded-projective and associated-sheaf enhanced equivalences are supplied here. The specified perfect category is idempotent complete, and its degree-zero object-class comparison is the affine Euler bridge. [lem-author-4f716d60801a-finite-projective-model](item-lem-author-4f716d60801a-finite-projective-model) [lem-author-4f716d60801a-lifted-affine-equivalence](item-lem-author-4f716d60801a-lifted-affine-equivalence) [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge)

[F4] The exact HTT input above supplies derived space-valued sheafification and its left exactness, and separately the further left exact hypercompletion when a stalkwise local model is chosen. These are not inferred from set-valued sheafification. Asakura–Sato Definition 5.1 and Proposition 5.3 specify the formal local Q-space model. The site and size conventions are supplied here. Derived sections of a space-valued local model mean evaluation after the chosen derived local replacement; this is not an extension of the separate definition scoped to Nisnevich, cdh and étale abelian sections. [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification)

### Proof
**Given:** The ring, sites, category models, Choice and size bounds in the Statement.

**Goal:** Establish the full affine comparison and its precise local use.

1.1 Every surjection between finite projective modules splits, and its kernel is finite projective, so the application of Gillet–Waldhausen in [F1] is valid in the ambient module category. The K-projective property in [F3] makes a bounded acyclic projective complex contractible. The mapping cylinder $Q\oplus\operatorname{Cone}(\mathrm{id}_P)$ factors a map $P\to Q$ as a degreewise split cofibration followed by a quasi-isomorphism, within bounded finite projectives. A map invertible in the localization is a quasi-isomorphism because its image in the derived category is invertible. This verifies factorization and DHKS-saturation for [F2]. The actual localization is the full affine perfect category of [F3], which is stable and idempotent complete. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Compose the S/Q equivalence, degree-zero bounded-complex inclusion, enhanced comparison and canonical connective-to-nonconnective map from [F1]–[F3]. The comparison is an isomorphism in all positive homotopy degrees. BGT's additional degree-zero clause applies by step 1.1; the affine Euler bridge also identifies this same degree-zero object-class map. Thus it is an equivalence of full spaces, including components. Naturality for extension of scalars follows from the actual functors: it preserves projectives and split cofibrations, and it preserves quasi-isomorphisms here because their bounded projective cones are contractible. The core maps carry each object and automorphism to itself, and direct sums are preserved. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 On each indicated site every object has an affine open covering, whose affine pieces remain objects of that site. On the small Nisnevich site these are affine étale objects; on the smooth big site these are affine smooth objects. Intersections need not be affine: their affine open covers suffice again. The exact degree-zero bundle-to-perfect functor, with the natural S/Q comparison, gives the Q-space-to-perfect-space arrow on every object, compatibly with pullback; on affines it is the arrow of step 2.1. It is therefore an equivalence on a covering basis, and hence an equivalence after derived space-valued sheafification by [F4]: restriction to the affine basis identifies the presheaves, and covering descent reconstructs their sheafifications on all objects. Left exactness also identifies the looped Q model. Applying the further left exact hypercompletion gives the same comparison in the source's stalkwise local convention, without identifying the two conventions on arbitrary presheaves. For the presheaf $\mathcal K$ of perfect K-spaces, write $L_\tau$ for the chosen derived local replacement. The natural unit $\mathcal K\to L_\tau\mathcal K$, followed by derived evaluation on $X$, supplies its map into sections of that common model. This only uses local comparison and the unit; it neither assumes hyperdescent of the original presheaf nor identifies global vector-bundle $K_0$ with perfect $K_0$. Restrictions and the units commute by naturality. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 2.1] ∎
