## Derived cdh localization

[Open item](item-def-cdh-derived-localization) · level 12


### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe bounds of [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites). Fix the small cdh site $\mathcal C$ of [def-cdh-topology-interface](item-def-cdh-topology-interface). A presheaf of abelian groups is a contravariant functor $\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Ab}$. A complex-valued presheaf means a cochain complex of such presheaves. Its derived category $D(\operatorname{PSh}_{\operatorname{Ab}}(\mathcal C))$ is obtained by inverting objectwise quasi-isomorphisms: maps inducing isomorphisms on cohomology at every object of $\mathcal C$.

Let $a$ be cdh sheafification of abelian presheaves and $i$ the inclusion of abelian sheaves into abelian presheaves. For a complex $C$, apply $a$ degreewise, choose a quasi-isomorphism $aC\to I$ to a K-injective complex of cdh sheaves, and define $L_{\mathrm{cdh}}C$ to be the object represented by the underlying presheaf complex $iI$. A K-injective complex is one for which every chain map from an acyclic complex is chain-homotopic to zero. The unit $C\to L_{\mathrm{cdh}}C$ is induced by $C\to iaC\to iI$ in the derived category of presheaves.

A morphism of complexes is a **cdh local equivalence** if its degreewise sheafification is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of cdh sheaves. An object $E$ of the derived presheaf category is **cdh-local** if, for every cdh local equivalence $u:A\to B$, precomposition with $u$ induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(B,E)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,E)$. Equivalently, $E$ is cdh-local exactly when its unit $E\to L_{\mathrm{cdh}}E$ is an isomorphism. Here equivalence means isomorphism in the indicated derived category, not an objectwise isomorphism of complexes.

For $X$ an object of the chosen site, evaluation of $L_{\mathrm{cdh}}C$ at $X$ is represented by $I(X)$ and hence is $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cdh}}(X,aC)$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ as defined in [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites). This convention uses unbounded derived sheaves and their derived sections; it is the hypercomplete derived-sheaf convention. No assertion is made that ordinary Čech descent alone implies locality. The truncation $\tau^{\leq n}C$ is the objectwise cohomological truncation, with degree $n$ equal to the kernel of $d^n$, degrees below $n$ unchanged and degrees above $n$ zero. Sheafification of cohomology presheaves, derived localization, truncation and evaluation are distinct operations; a proposed interchange or comparison with another topology requires its own hypotheses.

### Justification
The already stated Choice premise is used through the imported K-injective resolution-existence construction in [lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input](item-lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input). [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

The cdh site and its topology are fixed by [def-cdh-topology-interface](item-def-cdh-topology-interface). The plus construction and its universal property in [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification) apply to abelian-group objects: matching families, restrictions and equivalence on a common covering subsieve are compatible with addition. Thus $a$ is left adjoint to $i$ on abelian groups. It is exact. Indeed, at each object the plus construction is a filtered colimit, over covering sieves ordered by refinement, of matching-family groups. Matching families preserve finite limits, and filtered colimits of abelian groups commute with finite limits; hence $a$ preserves kernels. If a map of presheaves is objectwise surjective, every section of the sheafification of its target locally lifts: represent the section locally by a target-presheaf section and lift that section objectwise. A locally surjective map of sheaves is an epimorphism, since two sheaf morphisms agreeing after local lifts agree on a cover and therefore agree globally. Applying this to the objectwise cokernel factorization shows that $a$ also preserves cokernels.

The supplier [lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input](item-lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input) gives K-injective resolutions of unbounded complexes of abelian sheaves under the stated size and choice assumptions. Since $a$ is exact, it sends acyclic presheaf complexes to acyclic sheaf complexes. The ordinary adjunction therefore identifies chain maps from an acyclic presheaf complex to $iI$, up to homotopy, with those from its sheafification to $I$; these vanish. Thus $iI$ is K-injective as a presheaf complex. The adjunction on complexes consequently induces the derived adjunction $a:D(\operatorname{PSh}_{\operatorname{Ab}}(\mathcal C))\rightleftarrows D(\operatorname{Sh}_{\operatorname{Ab}}(\mathcal C)):Ri$, where $Ri$ is represented by $iI$. The counit $aRi\to\mathrm{id}$ is an isomorphism, because $aiI=I$ and $aC\to I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $Ri$ is fully faithful and $Ri\,a$ is a localization, independent up to unique isomorphism of the chosen resolution.

For a local equivalence $u$, the derived adjunction makes precomposition by $u$ bijective on maps into any $RiF$. Conversely, the unit of any object is a local equivalence because applying $a$ identifies it with the resolution map $aC\to I$. If an object is local, applying its defining bijection to its unit produces a retraction; naturality of the unit and the isomorphism of the unit on objects in the image of $Ri$ show that this retraction is also an inverse. This proves the stated characterization. Finally, evaluation of $iI$ at $X$ is $I(X)$, and [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites) identifies it with derived cdh sections. The definition makes no comparison with Čech descent or with another site.


## Top cycles supported on an integral curve

[Open item](item-lem-curve-support-divisor-complex) · level 12

### Statement
Assume AC. Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $U$ a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension three, and $T\subset U$ an integral closed curve. Put $K=k(T)$ and define
$$\operatorname{div}_T(f)=\sum_{x\in T\text{ closed}}\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{T,x}}(f)[x],\qquad \operatorname{ord}_{R}(a/b)=\ell_R(R/aR)-\ell_R(R/bR).$$
For the fixed-support Bloch complex with alternating face differential,
$$\mathrm{CH}^3_T(U)\cong\operatorname{coker}\!\left(K^\times\xrightarrow{\operatorname{div}_T}\bigoplus_{x\in T\text{ closed}}\mathbb Z[x]\right).$$
When $T$ is affine, normalization $\nu:\widetilde T\to T$ induces a surjection
$$\operatorname{Pic}(\widetilde T)=\mathrm{CH}^1(\widetilde T)\twoheadrightarrow\mathrm{CH}^3_T(U),$$
induced on point cycles by $[y]\mapsto[\nu(y)]$. For $f\in K^\times$, $\operatorname{ord}_x(f)=\sum_{y\in\nu^{-1}(x)}\operatorname{ord}_y(f)$, with DVR valuations upstairs and the displayed length orders downstairs. No normality or smoothness of $T$ is assumed.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** AC and $k,U,T$ as stated; for the normalization assertion, also assume $T$ affine.

**Goal:** Identify the supported top Chow group and prove the normalization surjection and divisor compatibility.

[F1] The supported group is degree-zero homology of the fixed-support complex. Its relevant terms are $Z_0(T)$ and $B_1(T)$, and its boundary is the endpoint difference $b[W]=[W_1]-[W_0]$ with local length coefficients. [def-supported-higher-cycle-complex](item-def-supported-higher-cycle-complex), [lem-author-1437578267d2-supported-degrees](item-lem-author-1437578267d2-supported-degrees)

[F2] The displayed length formula defines a divisor homomorphism, and its image is precisely the endpoint-boundary subgroup. [lem-author-1437578267d2-length-orders](item-lem-author-1437578267d2-length-orders), [lem-author-1437578267d2-graph-boundary](item-lem-author-1437578267d2-graph-boundary)

[F3] For affine $T$, normalization induces the stated surjection from $\operatorname{Pic}(\widetilde T)=\mathrm{CH}^1(\widetilde T)$ to the divisor quotient and satisfies the displayed order formula. [lem-author-1437578267d2-normalization-quotient](item-lem-author-1437578267d2-normalization-quotient)

### Proof
1.1 By [F1], the outgoing differential from degree zero is zero and $\mathrm{CH}^3_T(U)=Z_0(T)/bB_1(T)$. The sign is $W_1-W_0$: with $s=t_1$, the zeroth face is $s=1$ and the first is $s=0$. [F1, given]

2.1 By [F2], the divisor map is well defined and its image is exactly $bB_1(T)$, with the stated multiplicities even at singular points. Substitution into step 1.1 proves the cokernel presentation. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 If $T$ is affine, apply [F3] and the identification of step 2.1. This gives the normalization pushforward, its surjectivity and the displayed equality of local orders. [F3, step 2.1] ∎

## Support fibers with explicit cohomological indexing

[Open item](item-def-supported-complex-indexing) · level 12

### Definition
Let $X$ be a scheme, $T\subseteq X$ a closed subset, and $U=X\setminus T$ its open complement. Fix an integer $j$ and a restriction map $f:C_j(X)\to C_j(U)$ of cochain complexes of abelian groups. A cochain complex $A$ consists of abelian groups $A^n$ and homomorphisms $d_A:A^n\to A^{n+1}$ with $d_A^2=0$; its cohomology is $H^n(A)=\ker(d_A:A^n\to A^{n+1})/\operatorname{im}(d_A:A^{n-1}\to A^n)$. A restriction map here means a cochain map: $d f=f d$.

Define the **support complex** $C_{j,T}(X)$ to be the homotopy fiber of $f$. Explicitly, for $A=C_j(X)$ and $B=C_j(U)$, one model has
$$C_{j,T}(X)^n=A^n\oplus B^{n-1},\qquad d(a,b)=(d_Aa,\,f(a)-d_Bb).$$
The projection $(a,b)\mapsto a$ is the support-to-global map. Define the **supported cohomology group** by
$$H_T^{a,j}(X)=H^a(C_{j,T}(X)).$$
For complexes represented only in the derived category, use a cochain-map representative of the restriction morphism and take the resulting derived isomorphism class of this fiber. In particular, derived sections may provide the complexes and restriction map when the site, size and choice hypotheses in [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites) and the required restriction data are supplied.

Write $HC_{j,T}(X)$ for the Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectral realization specified in [lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index](item-lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index), and write $[2j]$ for suspension of a spectrum by $2j$. For every integer $i$ the indexing conventions are
$$\pi_i HC_{j,T}(X)\cong H_T^{-i,j}(X),\qquad \pi_i\bigl(HC_{j,T}(X)[2j]\bigr)\cong H_T^{2j-i,j}(X).$$
The two spectra in these formulas are distinguished: the second is shifted and the first is not. This auxiliary convention does not identify either spectrum with the article's support object without a separately specified comparison. The article's printed Definition 2.7 formula is retained separately in its article item.

### Justification
The displayed differential squares to zero because $d_A^2=d_B^2=0$ and $f d_A=d_B f$; the projection to $A$ commutes with differentials. This complex is the mapping cone of $f$ shifted by $-1$, with the displayed sign convention, and hence models the homotopy fiber. A commutative square of cochain maps induces a map of these models. If both vertical maps in such a square are quasi-isomorphisms, the induced map on fibers is a quasi-isomorphism: the short exact sequence of complexes $0\to B[-1]\to C_{j,T}(X)\to A\to0$ gives a natural long exact cohomology sequence, and the five-lemma applied to its corresponding segments gives the assertion. Thus the construction depends only on the restriction morphism in the derived category up to isomorphism, and cohomology and the support-to-global map are well-defined there. The derived-sections application uses exactly the site, size and choice assumptions of [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites).

Finally, [lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index](item-lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index) applies to the unbounded cochain complex $C_{j,T}(X)$ and gives both displayed natural group isomorphisms. It uses spectral suspension for the second formula; no comparison with the article's separately named object follows from indexing alone.

## Euler class of a regular bundle functional

[Open item](item-lem-regular-zero-koszul-euler-class) · level 12

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the suitable universes used in the supplied K-theory construction. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme, $E$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of constant rank $r\geq 0$, and $s:E\to\mathcal O_X$ a functional. Let $I=\operatorname{im}(s)$ and let $Z=Z(s)$ be the closed subscheme defined by $I$. Suppose that at every point $x\in Z$, the values of $s$ on a local basis of $E_x$ form a regular sequence in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ of length $r$: successively, each value is a non-zero-divisor modulo its predecessors and the final quotient is nonzero. For $r=0$ the sequence is empty and $Z=X$.

The Koszul complex $K(s)$ has $\Lambda^iE$ in cohomological degree $-i$, with differential given by contraction with $s$. It is a perfect complex supported on the underlying closed set of $Z$, and its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism $K(s)\to\mathcal O_Z$. Define the supported Euler class $e_Z(s)\in K_{0,Z}(X)$ to be the K-zero class of this complex. Under the map induced by the inclusion of supported perfect complexes into all perfect complexes, it maps to

$$\lambda_{-1}(E)=\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i[\Lambda^iE]\in K_0(X).$$

For a section $t:\mathcal O_X\to E$, the corresponding functional is $t^\vee:E^\vee\to\mathcal O_X$; under the same regularity hypothesis for its coordinates, the formula uses $E^\vee$ in place of $E$.

### Statement references

[def-exterior-determinant-bundles](item-def-exterior-determinant-bundles)

[def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface)

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** $X$, $E$, $s$ and the regularity hypothesis in the statement, together with choice and the stated universes.

**Goal:** Construct the supported class, prove the resolution and calculate its image in $K_0(X)$, including the section convention.

[F1] Exterior powers of a finite locally free rank-$r$ module are finite locally free, vanish above degree $r$, and have the usual increasing-wedge bases locally. [def-exterior-determinant-bundles](item-def-exterior-determinant-bundles)

[F2] For a finite sequence in a commutative ring, the Koszul differential is the alternating deletion formula. If the sequence is regular, its Koszul complex on the ring is a finite free resolution of the quotient by the sequence. [math:def-koszul-complex-of-a-sequence-with-coefficients](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-koszul-complex-of-a-sequence-with-coefficients) [math:cor-koszul-complex-resolves-a-regular-quotient](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/cor-koszul-complex-resolves-a-regular-quotient)

[F3] A bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves is perfect. A perfect complex is supported on a closed set precisely when its restriction to the complement is acyclic; the supported perfect objects form a stable idempotent-complete category. [def-scheme-perfect-complexes](item-def-scheme-perfect-complexes)

[F4] For qcqs $X$, the supplied K-theory assigns spectra to the perfect and supported perfect categories and a map to the ambient spectrum induced by inclusion. For an essentially small idempotent-complete stable category, its degree-zero group is naturally the group on object classes with the cofiber relations. Bundle classes agree with the object classes of the corresponding degree-zero complexes. [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) [thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input](item-thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input) [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

### Proof
**Proof technique:** Construct the Koszul differential locally, check exactness on stalks, and use the finite filtration by cohomological degree.

1.1 For local sections $v_1,\ldots,v_i$ of $E$, define contraction by $d(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_i)=\sum_{j=1}^i(-1)^{j-1}s(v_j)v_1\wedge\cdots\widehat{v_j}\cdots\wedge v_i$. This formula is alternating and compatible with restriction, so it defines a global map $\Lambda^iE\to\Lambda^{i-1}E$. In a local basis it is the differential in [F2]; hence $d^2=0$ locally and therefore globally. The quotient map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X/I=\mathcal O_Z$ is an augmentation because its composite with $d:E\to\mathcal O_X$ is zero. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 At $x\in Z$, choose a basis of the free stalk $E_x$. The stalk of the complex is the Koszul complex of the corresponding values of $s$; the regularity hypothesis and [F2] give homology only in degree zero, where it is $\mathcal O_{X,x}/I_x$. At $x\notin Z$, some value of $s_x$ is a unit. If $v\in E_x$ satisfies $s_x(v)=1$, exterior multiplication by $v$ is a contracting homotopy: the contraction formula gives $d(v\wedge w)+v\wedge d(w)=w$. The quotient stalk is also zero there. Thus the augmentation induces an isomorphism on every cohomology stalk and is a quasi-isomorphism. For $r=0$ this says $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$ is an isomorphism. [F2, step 1.1, assume-hyp, construct]

3.1 By [F1], $K(s)$ is bounded with finite locally free terms, so it is perfect. Step 2.1 shows it is acyclic away from $Z$; by [F3] it is an object of $\operatorname{Perf}_Z(X)$. Its object class in the degree-zero K-group is therefore well-defined, and this is the stated $e_Z(s)$. The construction uses the underlying closed set for support; it does not identify supported K-theory with coherent-sheaf G-theory. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1]

4.1 In the ambient perfect category, filter $K(s)$ by its subcomplexes consisting of the terms in degrees at least a fixed integer. Each successive quotient is a single term $\Lambda^iE$ placed in degree $-i$, and the short exact sequence of complexes is degreewise split. Its associated cofiber sequence gives the corresponding additive relation in [F4]. A shift changes the sign of an object class: the cofiber sequence $A\to0\to A[1]$ gives $[A[1]]=-[A]$. Iterating the finite filtration yields $[K(s)]=\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i[\Lambda^iE]$. Naturality of the object-class map sends $e_Z(s)$ to $[K(s)]$ under inclusion, proving the displayed formula. [F4, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 A section $t$ gives the dual map $t^\vee:E^\vee\to\mathcal O_X$ by evaluation, and its values in a dual basis are the coordinates of $t$ in the original basis. The dual of a finite locally free module is finite locally free of the same rank. Applying steps 1.1 through 4.1 to $t^\vee$ under the stated regularity hypothesis gives the section formula with $E^\vee$. [F1, step 4.1, assume-hyp] ∎

## Representable cdh sheaves and seminormalization

[Open item](item-prop-cdh-representable-seminormalization) · level 12

### Statement
Let $k$ be a perfect field, and let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Write $h_Y(Z)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(Z,Y)$ and $h_Y^{\mathrm{cdh}}$ for its sheafification on the big cdh site of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Then there is a natural bijection
$$h_Y^{\mathrm{cdh}}(X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(X^{\mathrm{sn}},Y).$$
If $X$ is seminormal, this identifies $h_Y^{\mathrm{cdh}}(X)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_k(X,Y)$.

A perfect field is one for which every algebraic extension is separable. A finite-type $k$-scheme has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras; separatedness means its diagonal is a closed immersion. The cdh topology and sheafification are those in [def-cdh-topology-interface](item-def-cdh-topology-interface), and the seminormalization $X^{\mathrm{sn}}\to X$ is the subintegral map with seminormal source described in [def-seminormal-scheme-interface](item-def-seminormal-scheme-interface). A subintegral map is integral, bijective on points and induces residue-field isomorphisms.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A perfect field $k$ and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$.

**Goal:** Establish the displayed bijection and its seminormal specialization.

[F1] The Huber–Kelly external input gives the displayed natural bijection for separated finite-type schemes over a noetherian Nagata base. It explicitly includes the spectrum of a perfect field among such bases. [thm-author-60d95bfb692a-huber-kelly-representable-input](item-thm-author-60d95bfb692a-huber-kelly-representable-input)

[F2] For a finite-type scheme over a field, its seminormalization is subintegral, has seminormal source and is finite over the reduction. A reduced seminormal scheme admits no nontrivial finite subintegral morphism from a reduced scheme. [def-seminormal-scheme-interface](item-def-seminormal-scheme-interface)

[F3] A set-valued cdh sheaf sends finite subintegral morphisms of separated finite-type schemes to bijections. [lem-author-60d95bfb692a-subintegral-sheaf-invariance](item-lem-author-60d95bfb692a-subintegral-sheaf-invariance)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Apply the imported theorem and then specialize its source.

1.1 The base $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ satisfies the hypotheses of [F1], and $X,Y$ satisfy its separated finite-type hypotheses. Applying [F1] gives the displayed natural bijection. [F1, given]

1.2 Suppose $X$ is seminormal. It is reduced by [F2], so its seminormalization is a finite subintegral map from a reduced scheme to $X$. The finite-morphism criterion in [F2] makes $X^{\mathrm{sn}}\to X$ an isomorphism. Precomposition with its inverse therefore identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_k(X^{\mathrm{sn}},Y)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_k(X,Y)$. [F2, given]

2.1 The map $X^{\mathrm{sn}}\to X$ also induces a bijection on sections of any cdh sheaf by [F3]; this records the descent compatibility used in the specialization. Combining steps 1.1 and 1.2 proves both assertions. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Torsion freeness of top threefold motivic cohomology

[Open item](item-prop-top-motivic-torsion-free) · level 12


### Statement
For an affine threefold $X$ over an algebraically closed field $k$, $H^{6,3}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is torsion-free. Threefold means finite type and dimension three, without any smoothness, reducedness or irreducibility assumption.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) defines $C=\mathbb Z(3)_{\rm mot}(X)$ and its finite coefficients by objectwise derived tensor.

[F2] [lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-invertible-prime](item-lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-invertible-prime) gives $H^5(C/\ell)=0$ for invertible primes. [lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-characteristic-prime](item-lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-characteristic-prime) gives the same for the characteristic prime.

[F3] [lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-bockstein](item-lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-bockstein) turns this vanishing into injectivity; [lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-primewise](item-lem-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-primewise) detects torsion-freeness.

### Proof
**Given:** $X$ and $k$ as stated.

**Goal:** Prove the unrestricted characteristic-independent assertion.

1.1 Fix any prime $\ell$. If $\ell$ is invertible in $k$, apply the first part of [F2]. Otherwise $\operatorname{char}k=\ell>0$, and apply its second part. Hence $H^5(C/\ell)=0$ for every prime, including the characteristic prime. [F1, F2]

2.1 By [F3], multiplication by every prime on $H^6(C)$ is injective. The primewise criterion makes $H^6(C)$ torsion-free. By [F1] this is precisely $H^{6,3}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)$. [F3, step 1.1] ∎

### Source qualifications
The article's Proposition 2.6, pp. 5–6, states the full assertion but supplies only a characteristic-zero proof. This is a nonfatal omission in that source. The current argument uses the separate published report Theorem 4 at weight three and EM v1 Lemma 4.16, rather than treating the article's deferred positive-characteristic proof as a premise. The report's separate reducedness hypothesis in Theorem 1 is not imposed in its Theorem 4.

The report Theorem 3(2) prints an étale lower-right corner, while EM v1 Theorem 4.28 prints the éh corner. The printed discrepancy is verified; a theorem-level error in that square is not established here. The proof above uses the precise EM comparison through its declared suppliers. The report's Theorem 4 proof also omits the shift from its description of the comparison cofiber: EM v1 Corollary 4.32 gives $R\Gamma_{\rm cdh}(X,\widetilde\nu_1(3))[-4]$. This confirmed source omission is nonfatal because the report proves vanishing of the obstruction itself.

The report Remark 5 has a separate incorrect duality exponent. With its stated higher-Chow homological indexing, $X=\mathbb P^1$, $j=1$, $i=0$ and invertible prime coefficients give a nonzero left side and a zero degree-three right side. This display is not used above. In the smooth proper prime-to-characteristic setting the compatible degree is $2d-2j+i$; no replacement for the report's full quasiprojective or syntomic scope is asserted.


## Bertini functional with finite smooth zero locus

[Open item](item-prop-swan-bertini-point-section) · level 12

### Statement
Assume AC. Let $X$ be a normal affine threefold of finite type over an algebraically closed field $k$ of arbitrary characteristic, and let $P$ be a rank-three vector bundle on $X$. There is a functional $s:P\to\mathcal O_X$ whose scheme-theoretic zero locus $S=V(\operatorname{im}s)$ is a finite smooth $k$-scheme contained in $X_{\mathrm{sm}/k}$. Thus $S$ is a finite set of distinct reduced $k$-rational closed points, possibly empty. No Chern-class or determinant hypothesis on $P$ is needed for this assertion; it therefore applies to the particular $P$ in Theorem6.7. Threefold may be read as pure dimension three or, more generally, a normal scheme of dimension three; the construction below treats lower-dimensional clopen components as an additional avoidance locus.

Let $Q=\ker s$. It is coherent, and there is a surjection $\mathcal O_X^m\twoheadrightarrow Q$ for some finite $m$. On $U=X\setminus S$, the restriction $Q|_U$ is a rank-two vector bundle, its displayed generators restrict to a surjection $\mathcal O_U^m\twoheadrightarrow Q|_U$, and
$$0\longrightarrow Q|_U\longrightarrow P|_U\xrightarrow{s|_U}\mathcal O_U\longrightarrow0$$
is exact. Hence $Q|_U$ is generated by global sections on $U$, even though $U$ need not be affine.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** AC, the normal affine finite-type threefold and bundle above. A functional on $P$ is a section of its dual $P^\vee$; its zero ideal is locally generated by its three coefficients.

**Goal:** Produce the actual functional in every characteristic and establish the kernel properties used in the article.

[F1] [lem-author-fc2380accb47-normal-smooth-strata](item-lem-author-fc2380accb47-normal-smooth-strata) provides $W$ and its closed complement $D$ of dimension at most two. [lem-author-fc2380accb47-coordinate-first-jets](item-lem-author-fc2380accb47-coordinate-first-jets) constructs a finite-dimensional dual-section family spanning first jets, using [lem-affine-coherent-global-generation](item-lem-affine-coherent-global-generation).

[F2] [lem-author-fc2380accb47-nontransverse-incidence](item-lem-author-fc2380accb47-nontransverse-incidence) and [lem-author-fc2380accb47-simultaneous-good-parameters](item-lem-author-fc2380accb47-simultaneous-good-parameters) provide a nonempty good parameter open and a $k$-point. [lem-author-fc2380accb47-finite-etale-zero-fibers](item-lem-author-fc2380accb47-finite-etale-zero-fibers) proves the actual selected zero scheme is finite étale and avoids $D$, and identifies its geometric scheme structure.

[F3] [lem-surjection-kernel-bundle](item-lem-surjection-kernel-bundle) gives local freeness and rank for a kernel off the zero locus; [lem-affine-coherent-global-generation](item-lem-affine-coherent-global-generation) gives finite generators for coherent sheaves on the affine scheme and on restrictions. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes) fixes vector-bundle conventions and AC. [lem-regular-section-parameter-family](item-lem-regular-section-parameter-family) fixes actual zero ideals and base-change fibers.

### Proof
1.1 Apply [F1] with $E=P^\vee$. Its coherence and affineness give finite global generators, and multiplying them by a finite list of algebra generators for $\mathcal O_X(X)$ produces the first-jet-spanning family. Apply [F2] to choose a $k$-rational parameter outside the closures of both the nontransverse-zero incidence and the forbidden-locus incidence. The corresponding global section of $P^\vee$ is the desired functional $s$. Its actual zero scheme, not just its underlying set, is finite étale by [F2], and lies in $W\subset X_{\mathrm{sm}/k}$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed it is a finite disjoint union of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. This proves the existence and all-characteristic smoothness/avoidance assertions, including the empty case. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 On the Noetherian scheme $X$, the kernel of a morphism of coherent sheaves is coherent: locally it is a submodule of a finite module over a Noetherian ring, hence finite, with finite relations. Thus $Q$ is coherent. By the completed affine-generation result in [F3] it admits a surjection $\mathcal O_X^m\twoheadrightarrow Q$ with $m$ finite. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 On $U$ at least one coefficient of $s$ is locally a unit, by the definition of its zero ideal. Hence $s|_U$ is surjective. Restriction preserves its kernel, so [F3] makes $Q|_U$ locally free of rank $3-1=2$ and gives the asserted exact sequence. Restricting the surjection of step 2.1 preserves surjectivity on stalks and gives $\mathcal O_U^m\twoheadrightarrow Q|_U$. Its images of the standard basis are global sections on $U$, proving global generation. Together with step 1.1 this completes every asserted part. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

### Source/application note
The article cites Swan's Bertini form through KM82 section3. The authored proof here instead gives the characteristic-free finite-first-jet incidence argument, following the bad-locus method actually read in Stacks Lemma33.47.3 and extending it from a line-bundle hyperplane family to the explicit rank-three determinant condition. It neither attributes this proof to unread KM82 nor assumes the characteristic-zero conventions of another Swan formulation. There is no claim about the second, rank-two irreducible-curve Bertini application later in the article's paragraph; that is outside this assigned proposition.


## Rank-three alternating exterior class

[Open item](item-def-rank-three-euler-k-class) · level 12


### Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the suitable universes used in the vector-bundle classes definition. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme and let $E$ be a rank-three vector bundle on $X$: that is, a locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^3$. Write $K_0(X)=\pi_0\mathbb K(\operatorname{Perf}(X))$ for the supplied degree-zero perfect K-theory group, and write $[V]$ for the class in it of a vector bundle $V$ viewed as a complex in degree zero.

The **rank-three alternating exterior class** of $E$ is
$$\beta(E)=[\mathcal O_X]-[E]+[\Lambda^2E]-[\det E]\in K_0(X).$$
Here $\Lambda^iE$ is the $i$th exterior power and $\det E=\Lambda^3E$. Equivalently, in the functional convention, define $\lambda_{-1}(E):=\sum_{i=0}^{3}(-1)^i[\Lambda^iE]$; then $\beta(E)=\lambda_{-1}(E)$. This notation applies the alternating exterior-power expression to the bundle $E$; no extension to arbitrary virtual classes is asserted.

### Definition references

[def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme $X$, a rank-three vector bundle $E$, the Axiom of Choice and suitable universes as above.

**Goal:** Justify that the displayed expression defines an isomorphism-invariant element of $K_0(X)$ and equals the stated alternating sum.

[F1] For such $X$, the supplied $K_0(X)$ is an abelian group, and a vector bundle $V$ has an isomorphism-invariant class $[V]$ in it; its unit is $[\mathcal O_X]$. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

[F2] Exterior powers of a rank-three bundle are vector bundles, functorial in the bundle; $\Lambda^0E$ is canonically $\mathcal O_X$, $\det E=\Lambda^3E$, and $\Lambda^iE=0$ for $i>3$. [def-exterior-determinant-bundles](item-def-exterior-determinant-bundles)

[F3] The Axiom of Choice is assumed for the supplied perfect K-theory construction underlying the classes in [F1], with the same universe conventions as that supplier. This is the inherited use in step 1.1; the finite alternating-sum calculation requires no additional choice. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

### Justification

1.1 By [F2], $\mathcal O_X$, $E$, $\Lambda^2E$ and $\det E$ are vector bundles. Their classes exist in the abelian group $K_0(X)$ by [F1], so their indicated sum and differences define an element of that group. An isomorphism $E\cong E'$ induces isomorphisms of the corresponding exterior powers by functoriality; consequently [F1] gives $\beta(E)=\beta(E')$. [given, F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Expanding the four terms in the defining sum for $\lambda_{-1}(E)$ and using $\Lambda^0E\cong\mathcal O_X$ and $\Lambda^3E=\det E$ gives precisely the displayed formula for $\beta(E)$. The higher exterior powers vanish, so the same expression is the full finite alternating exterior-power sum. [F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Spectral K-zero equality gives an actual projective stabilization

[Open item](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-spectral-kzero-stability) · level 12


### Statement
Assume AC and the suitable universes used for the article's perfect K-theory construction. Let $A$ be a commutative unital noetherian ring, put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $E,F$ be vector bundles on $X$. Equality $[E]=[F]$ in the article's spectral $K_0(X)$ is equivalent to an isomorphism of $A$-modules $\Gamma(X,E)\oplus A^N\cong\Gamma(X,F)\oplus A^N$ for some integer $N\geq0$. This is the bundle/perfect K-zero interface, without a passage through coherent-sheaf G-theory.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the suitable universes of the supplied perfect K-theory construction, a commutative unital noetherian ring $A$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and vector bundles $E,F$ on $X$.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[A1] AC is used through the supplied affine spectral comparison, stable-equivalence result and bundle–module equivalence. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] In the stated universes, for an affine scheme the spectral group identifies with vector-bundle $K^0$ and preserves the classes of bundles concentrated in degree zero. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

[F2] Equality in $K^0$ is equivalent to stabilization by the same finite free bundle. [lem-k-zero-stable-equivalence](item-lem-k-zero-stable-equivalence)

[F3] Stabilization is carried to and from modules. [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-module-stabilization](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-module-stabilization)

### Proof

1.1 Suppose $[E]=[F]$ in spectral $K_0(X)$. The ring hypotheses make $X$ noetherian affine, and $E,F$ are vector bundles, so all three supplied interfaces apply under AC and the stated universes. By [F1] their classes agree in $K^0(X)$. By [F2] there is an integer $N\geq0$ with $E\oplus\mathcal O_X^N\cong F\oplus\mathcal O_X^N$. Applying [F3] gives $\Gamma(X,E)\oplus A^N\cong\Gamma(X,F)\oplus A^N$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Conversely, suppose the displayed module isomorphism holds for an integer $N\geq0$. By [F3] it gives $E\oplus\mathcal O_X^N\cong F\oplus\mathcal O_X^N$. By [F2] the bundle classes agree in $K^0(X)$, and [F1] identifies them with the given spectral classes. Thus $[E]=[F]$ in spectral $K_0(X)$, proving the equivalence together with step 1.1. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## The ordinary Chow Chern map on isomorphism classes

[Open item](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-chern-interface) · level 12

### Statement
Assume AC. For a smooth equidimensional finite-type scheme $X$ over a field and $r\geq1$, write $\mathrm{CH}^i(X)=A^i(X)$ for the group of codimension-$i$ cycles modulo rational equivalence. The tuple map $C_r:\mathrm{Vect}_r(X)\to\prod_{i=1}^r\mathrm{CH}^i(X)$ sends $[E]_{\mathrm{iso}}$ to $(c_i(E))_i$. It is well-defined and uses the quotient-projective-bundle convention: if $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$, its coefficients satisfy $\xi^r+\sum_{i=1}^r(-1)^i\pi^*c_i(E)\xi^{r-i}=0$. Equality of total Chern polynomials $1+\sum c_i(E)t^i$ is exactly equality of these tuples.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] Bundle isomorphism classes are a set. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

[F2] The Chow Chern classes are the unique coefficients of the quotient-projective-bundle relation and lie in $A^i(X)$. [math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle)

### Proof

1.1 An isomorphism $E\cong F$ identifies their quotient projective bundles, projections and tautological quotient lines. The projective relations therefore identify, and coefficient uniqueness gives $c_i(E)=c_i(F)$. The tuple consequently descends to the set in [F1]. [F1, F2]

2.1 For a formal variable $t$, a polynomial is its finite list of coefficients. Thus equality of the total polynomials is equivalent to equality in each degree $1,\ldots,r$, precisely equality of $C_r$. This fixes the actual operation and its sign normalization. [F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Rank-two Chern map and its fixed-invariant fibers

[Open item](item-def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers) · level 12

### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the supplied universe conventions. Let $X$ be a smooth affine scheme of finite type and pure dimension three over a field. Write $V=\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)$ for the set of isomorphism classes of rank-two finite locally free sheaves. The determinant of $E$ is the invertible sheaf $\det E=\bigwedge^2E$. The group $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible sheaves, under tensor product, with identity $[\mathcal O_X]$. The group $\mathrm{CH}^i(X)$ is the free abelian group on integral codimension-$i$ closed subschemes modulo rational equivalence: the subgroup generated by divisors of rational functions on integral codimension-$(i-1)$ closed subschemes. Use the supplied Chow-theoretic Chern classes, and use the determinant convention for the first invariant in $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$. Define
$$C_X:V\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(X)\times\mathrm{CH}^2(X),\qquad [E]\longmapsto([\det E],c_2(E)).$$
For a line-bundle class $L$ put $V_L=\{e\in V:[\det e]=L\}$. For $a\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)$ put $V_{L,a}=\{e\in V_L:c_2(e)=a\}$. These are sets of bundle isomorphism classes, without choices of a determinant trivialization. The target basepoint is $([\mathcal O_X],0)$ and the source basepoint is $[\mathcal O_X^{\oplus2}]$.

### Definition references
[def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

[math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle)

[math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** $X$ and the conventions in the Definition.

**Goal:** Justify the map and its fiber notation.

[F1] Bundle isomorphism classes form a set under the supplied conventions. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

[F2] On a smooth equidimensional scheme the supplied projective-bundle relation defines isomorphism-invariant Chern classes in the Chow ring; for a sum of trivial line bundles its positive Chern classes vanish. [math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle)

### Justification
1.1 Applying the second exterior-power functor to the local rank-two trivializations of $E$ gives rank-one trivializations with transition functions the determinants of the original matrices. The determinant identity for products verifies the cocycle condition. An isomorphism of bundles induces an isomorphism of their second exterior powers. Thus $[\det E]$ depends only on $[E]$. Tensor products and duals of invertible sheaves respectively give the stated group law and inverses on their isomorphism classes. [F1, construct]

2.1 The supplied Chern construction gives $c_2(E)\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)$ invariant under bundle isomorphism. Combining this with step 1.1 defines $C_X$ on the set $V$; separation defines the subsets $V_L$ and $V_{L,a}$. The determinant of the trivial rank-two bundle is trivial and its second Chern class is zero, so the chosen basepoints are respected. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎

### Source notes
The notation makes explicit the first coordinate of Asok–Fasel Theorem 1. No assertion that arbitrary pairs are realized, or uniquely realized, is part of this definition. The identification of the determinant coordinate with the usual $c_1$ coordinate in $\mathrm{CH}^1$ is included in the external comparison input below, rather than derived from a statement about abstractly isomorphic groups.

## Elmanto–Morrow smooth comparison input

### Statement
Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme, and $j\geq0$. The Elmanto–Morrow complex $\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)$ is equivalent in the derived category of abelian groups to Bloch's cycle complex, regarded cohomologically and shifted by $-2j$. It consequently represents the classical Voevodsky weight-$j$ motivic cohomology of $X$.

For the filtration comparison in the selected local perfect-$K$-theory realization, assume the Axiom of Choice and its fixed suitable universes. Under these assumptions the Elmanto–Morrow filtration of $K(X)$ is naturally equivalent as a multiplicative filtered spectrum to the filtration arising from Voevodsky's slice filtration.

The classical motivic complex and the slice filtration are the constructions recalled in the cited source §3.1. A multiplicative filtered equivalence is an equivalence of towers compatible with their transition maps and multiplication.

### External input
This is the cited theorem's smooth comparison, together with the identification recalled in §3.1. It is imported from the literature; its geometric proof and motivic-homotopy constructions are not locally reconstructed. The restriction to finite type matches the locally defined cycle complex.

**Goal:** Supply the complex and filtered-spectrum comparisons under those hypotheses.

This records the local supplier contract, without asserting foundational necessity for the published theorem.

### Proof
1.1 $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because it is finite type over a field, and it is smooth by hypothesis. Apply the complex comparison of [F1] in nonnegative weight. With the specified cycle and motivic-complex conventions this gives the derived equivalence and its classical interpretation. These are imported assertions, with no local reconstruction of their geometric proof. [given, F1]

2.1 For the filtration assertion, invoke the selected local tower under [A1]. ## Projective bundle closure and naturality of the actual decomposition

[Open item](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-base-change) · level 12


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. The category of qcqs $k$-schemes is closed under the positive-constant-rank projective bundles and their base changes required by the bigraded projective bundle contract. For every finite locally free $E$ of constant rank $r>0$, the decomposition isomorphisms in every integer bidegree $(a,b)$, given by $(x_m)_m\mapsto\sum_{m=0}^{r-1}\pi^*(x_m)c_1(\mathcal O(1))^m$, are natural under base change $f:Y\to X$, using $f^*E$ and the induced map $\bar f:Q_Y(f^*E)\to Q_X(E)$.

### Statement references
[def-bigraded-oriented-theory](item-def-bigraded-oriented-theory)

[lem-author-79117e1d72ed-all-bidegrees](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-all-bidegrees)

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice, as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). It discharges the projective-bundle construction and dual-convention hypotheses in step 1.1, and the all-bidegrees decomposition hypothesis in step 2.1.

[F1] [math:def-projective-bundle-scheme](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-projective-bundle-scheme) gives local projective-space charts and arbitrary base change. [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-dual-conventions](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-dual-conventions) identifies their tautological quotient with the source convention.

[F2] [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-bigraded-ring](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-bigraded-ring) gives natural ring pullbacks; [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-additive-c1](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-additive-c1) gives naturality of $c_1$; [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-all-bidegrees](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-all-bidegrees) gives the decomposition.

### Proof
**Given:** $X,Y,f,E$ as stated, and AC.

**Goal:** Check the scheme-category hypotheses and map-level naturality.

1.1 Choose a finite affine cover of $X$ trivializing $E$, possible by quasi-compactness, refining finite affine trivializations. Above each member the projective bundle has finitely many standard affine charts. Hence its total space is quasi-compact. For intersections of two such charts, cover the quasi-compact intersection of their base affines by finitely many affine opens. On each, the intersection is a homogeneous principal chart $D_+(l_1l_2)$ in a relative projective space, hence affine: $l_1,l_2$ are the linear coordinates for the two trivializations. Thus chart intersections are quasi-compact, proving quasi-separatedness. The same argument applies to $Y$ and $f^*E$. [A1, F1, given]

2.1 Under [A1], the decomposition of [F2] applies to both $X$ and $Y$. By base change, $\bar f^*\mathcal O_Q(1)=\mathcal O_{Q_Y(f^*E)}(1)$ and the projection square commutes. Therefore $\bar f^*\xi_X=\xi_Y$ by [F2]. For each summand, $\bar f^*(\pi_X^*x\,\xi_X^m)=\pi_Y^*(f^*x)\,\xi_Y^m$ by functoriality and multiplicativity. Summing proves the decomposition square commutes; it also holds on the zero negative-weight pieces. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every nonempty finite-dimensional Noetherian equicharacteristic scheme in EM’s sense lies in the source filtration’s finite-valuative-dimension domain: its structure map factors through a prime field $F=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$, it is qcqs, and its source valuative dimension equals its finite Krull dimension. Define its motivic filtration by the same source prime-field filtered algebra. On schemes over the standing field this is exactly the completed local filtration, including the actual stage maps to $K$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and a finite-dimensional Noetherian scheme $X$ with the stated global prime-field factorization, or its standing-field specialization.

**Goal:** Preserve the full equicharacteristic domain instead of silently restricting the theorem to one fixed base field.

No additional Choice step is needed for the geometric domain check.

### Proof
1.1 For nonempty $X$, a Noetherian scheme has a finite affine cover. Every intersection of two affine opens is a Noetherian open and therefore quasi-compact; hence $X$ is qcqs. Its chosen prime-field factorization places it in the domain of [F1]. Since it is locally Noetherian, [F2] gives $\dim_vX=\dim X<\infty$. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Under the assumed Choice premise in [F3], evaluate the actual prime-field filtered algebra of [F1] on $X$, with its source augmentation to stagezero $K(X)$. If $X$ carries a structure over the standing field, [F1] says its locally defined filtration is precisely this source functor precomposed with forgetting to the prime field. Thus stages, transitions, multiplication and augmentation are the same restricted diagram. There is no independently selected filtration to compare, and no finite-type or fixed-field condition was inserted into step 1.1. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎

## Spectral K-zero equality gives an actual projective stabilization

[Open item](item-lem-author-7dc5154c7a6f-spectral-kzero-stability) · level 12


### Statement
Assume AC and the suitable universes of the article's perfect K-theory construction. Let $A$ be a commutative unital noetherian ring, put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $E,F$ be vector bundles on $X$, meaning finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Equality $[E]=[F]$ in the article's perfect spectral $K_0(X)$ is equivalent to an isomorphism of finite projective $A$-modules $\Gamma(X,E)\oplus A^N\cong\Gamma(X,F)\oplus A^N$ for some integer $N\geq0$. This is the bundle/perfect K-zero interface, without a passage through coherent-sheaf G-theory.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the stated universes, a commutative unital noetherian ring $A$, the affine scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and vector bundles $E,F$ on $X$.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[A1] AC is assumed through the supplied affine perfect-K-zero comparison and affine bundle/module interfaces; their universe bounds are also assumed. No choice principle stronger than those supplier hypotheses is introduced. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] The spectral group identifies with vector-bundle $K^0$ and preserves bundle classes. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

[F2] Equality in $K^0$ is equivalent to stabilization by the same finite free bundle. [lem-k-zero-stable-equivalence](item-lem-k-zero-stable-equivalence)

[F3] Stabilization is carried to and from modules. [lem-author-7dc5154c7a6f-module-stabilization](item-lem-author-7dc5154c7a6f-module-stabilization)

### Proof

1.1 Suppose $[E]=[F]$ in spectral $K_0(X)$. The affine comparison identifies these classes with the classes of the bundles $E,F$ in $K^0(X)$. Since $X$ is noetherian affine and $E,F$ are vector bundles, [F2] gives $E\oplus\mathcal O_X^N\cong F\oplus\mathcal O_X^N$ for an integer $N\geq0$. By [F3], global sections give the asserted isomorphism of finite projective modules. The choice and size hypotheses required by these suppliers are included in the given assumptions. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Conversely, suppose the displayed module isomorphism holds for some integer $N\geq0$. By [F3] it gives a bundle isomorphism $E\oplus\mathcal O_X^N\cong F\oplus\mathcal O_X^N$. By [F2], $E$ and $F$ have equal classes in $K^0(X)$, and [F1] identifies these with their spectral classes. Together with step 1.1 this proves the equivalence. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## The zero-dimensional critical-rank boundary

[Open item](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-zero-boundary) · level 12


### Statement
Assume AC. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X$ be a nonempty smooth affine finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension zero, and let $E$ be a vector bundle of constant rank zero on $X$. Then $E=0$ and $c_0(E)=1\ne0$ in $\mathrm{CH}^0(X)$. There is no vector bundle $E\prime$ with $E\cong E\prime\oplus\mathcal O_X$. Thus the two conditions in the critical-rank splitting equivalence are both false in dimension zero.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The hypotheses and data in the statement, with AC and the article's fixed universes wherever perfect K-theory is used.

**Goal:** Establish the asserted conclusion.

[F1] The smooth affine scheme is a finite disjoint union of integral components. [lem-author-394a5b71198d-components](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-components)

[F2] By convention the zeroth Chern class is 1 for every bundle, including the zero bundle. [math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle)

[F3] The codimension-zero cycle group is freely generated by the irreducible components, and there are no rational-equivalence relations coming from larger-dimensional integral subschemes in dimension zero. [math:def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence)

[F4] A rank-zero locally free module is locally zero, hence zero. Local bundle ranks are nonnegative integers and add under direct sums. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

### Proof

1.1 By [F4], $E$ is the zero bundle. By [F1] and [F3], $\mathrm{CH}^0(X)$ is the free abelian group on its finitely many nonempty components. The unit class 1 has coefficient 1 on each component; since $X$ is nonempty, it is not zero. By [F2] this unit is exactly $c_0(E)$. [F1, F2, F3, F4]

2.1 If $E\cong E\prime\oplus\mathcal O_X$, taking a fiber at any point would give $0=\operatorname{rank}(E\prime)+1$, impossible for a bundle rank. Thus splitting and top-Chern vanishing both fail, as stated. [F4, step 1.1] ∎

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and compatible fixed universe size bounds for the small sites and derived categories used below. Let $k$ have prime subfield $F$, let $X/k$ be qcqs, $j\geq0$, and let $n\geq1$ be invertible in $k$. Then $X$ is a qcqs $F$-scheme, $n$ is invertible in $F$, and the completed motivic complex at $X$ is the actual source value $M_j(X)=\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot},F}(X)$. Put $B_j(X)=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_n^{\otimes j})$, using the intrinsic small étale site of $X$ and the specified tensor powers over $\mathbb Z/n$. Forgetting the k-structure changes neither this site nor its coefficient sheaf or derived evaluation. Thus the source complex $B_j(X)$ is exactly the completed local étale target, with its pullbacks.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the displayed construction or conclusion with its actual maps.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice and the fixed size bounds are retained for the K-injective derived-evaluation interface invoked in step 2.1. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

1.1 Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness belong to the underlying scheme, so forgetting to $F$ gives a source object. If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, invertibility of $n$ means $p\nmid n$, hence invertibility in $F=\mathbb F_p$; if the characteristic is zero, every positive integer is invertible in $F=\mathbb Q$. The motivic identification is the defining precomposition of [F1]. [F1]

2.1 An object of the small étale site is an étale morphism $U\to X$, and its covers and morphisms are defined over $X$. This category, its topology and the equation $u^n=1$ on its objects do not mention the presentation of $X$ over $k$ or $F$. The tensor powers, including the zeroth power $\mathbb Z/n$, are therefore the same sheaves. Retain the same size-bounded small site in both presentations. Under [A1], apply the K-injective derived-evaluation interface of [F2] to this same site and sheaf; the resulting derived-category value is independent of the resolution. Pullback along a $k$-morphism uses the same underlying morphism and coefficient maps after forgetting. This proves the claim about actual functors, not only abstract group isomorphisms. ## The root map through derived sections, truncation and localization

[Open item](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-truncated-root-map) · level 12


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and compatible universe bounds for the small étale sites, big sites, slices and products used below. Fix a prime $p$, a field $k$ in which $p$ is invertible, and an element $\zeta\in k$ of multiplicative order $p$. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[1/p]$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\mathcal C$ be the size-bounded category of qcqs $S$-schemes with BEM's big cdh topology, generated by finite Nisnevich covers and finitely presented abstract blowup covers. Equip $\mathcal C/U$, the category of qcqs $k$-schemes, with the induced topology. Let $j:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal C$ forget the structure map to $U$, and let $j^*$ be restriction of presheaves. Write $L_{\mathcal C}$ and $L_{\mathcal C/U}$ for the respective ordinary reflective sheafifications of $D(\mathbb Z)$-valued presheaves, using derived Čech descent for covering families on both sites.

For $V\in\mathcal C$, compute $R\Gamma_{\rm et}$ on the size-bounded small étale site of $V$, with constant sheaf $\mathbb Z/p$ and Tate coefficient $\mu_p^{\otimes3}$, where the tensor product is over $\mathbb Z/p$. Write $T(V)=\tau^{\leq3}R\Gamma_{\rm et}(V,\mu_p^{\otimes3})$ and $A(V)=\tau^{\leq3}R\Gamma_{\rm et}(V,\mathbb Z/p)$. Their actual coefficient map on the slice is an equivalence $j^*A\xrightarrow{t^{(3)}_\zeta}j^*T$. It induces a specified equivalence $j^*L_{\mathcal C}T\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathcal C/U}j^*A$, namely the slice/ambient comparison followed by the localized inverse of $t^{(3)}_\zeta$. Here $\tau^{\leq3}$ is objectwise cohomological truncation before sheafification.
