### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The Axiom of Choice is assumed through the supplied K-injective construction of derived sections; the compatible universes contain the sites, slices and products. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites) specify this assumption and its use. [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site) supplies the stated big site, slice and ordinary descent conventions.

[F1] [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-chosen-root](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-chosen-root) supplies the pullback-compatible coefficient isomorphism, and [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites) supplies derived sections as a functor.

[F2] [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-localization](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-localization) gives the actual unit-compatible slice comparison. Truncation $\tau^{\leq3}$ is the standard derived functor retaining cohomology through degree three and killing higher degrees.

### Proof
**Given:** The stated $p,k,\zeta,S,U,\mathcal C,j$, ordinary localizations, Choice and compatible universe bounds.

**Goal:** Construct the displayed map without assuming a root on the ambient site.

1.1 Apply derived étale global sections to the coefficient isomorphism on each $V/k$. Its inverse gives an inverse in $D(\mathbb Z)$, and pullback compatibility gives a natural transformation on the slice. Apply objectwise $\tau^{\leq3}$; as a functor it preserves equivalences and the inverse. This is the specified map $j^*A\to j^*T$, induced by the coefficient map $1\mapsto\zeta^{\otimes3}$. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Use [F2] to identify $j^*L_{\mathcal C}T$ with $L_{\mathcal C/U}j^*T$. Apply slice localization to the inverse map from step 1.1. Their composite is exactly the asserted equivalence, natural for $k$-scheme pullbacks and compatible with the appropriate localization units. This applies the root map only after restriction and uses a proved interchange; it does not apply an ambient functor to a nonexistent ambient root transformation. [F2, step 1.1] ∎


## The hypercomplete derived-localization model on the actual general site

[Open item](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-general-localization) · level 12


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the derived-sections suppliers. Fix the completed qcqs prime-field cdh site $\mathcal C_F$. Let $a$ be its abelian sheafification and $i$ its inclusion of abelian sheaves into presheaves. For a presheaf complex $C$ define $L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}C=Ri\,aC$: choose a K-injective sheaf complex $aC\to I$ and evaluate $I$ as a presheaf. This is localization at maps inducing isomorphisms on all associated cohomology sheaves; a complex is local precisely when its unit to this localization is an equivalence. By the exact linear input, hypercover-descent complexes are local in this same model. This defines the general-site version without modifying the completed narrower finite-type definition.

### Localization convention
In comparisons using both reflectors, write $L^{h,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}=L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}=Ri\,a$ for the hypercomplete reflector constructed in this item. Write $L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}$ for ordinary covering-family/Čech sheafification of $D(\mathbb Z)$-valued presheaves, as in the source comparisons. These notations do not identify the two reflectors on arbitrary unbounded inputs. The hypercover criterion used here concerns $L^{h,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}$; the particular ordinary-locality consequences used by consumers are separate arguments.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Choice and the stated bounds are used for the K-injective sheaf resolution and the derived inclusion/evaluation model. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the stated exact map or descent conclusion.

[F1] [lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site), [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites), [lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input](item-lem-author-a44f2061570d-site-derived-input).

[F2] [thm-author-7113c087ecba-linear-input](item-thm-author-7113c087ecba-linear-input).

### Proof
1.1 The site in [F1] is explicitly small after the fixed universe choice, so the completed arbitrary-site supplier gives K-injective resolutions. Abelian sheafification is exact: matching families preserve kernels, filtered refinements commute with finite limits of groups, and sheaf epimorphisms are locally surjective. Hence degreewise sheafification preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Its adjunction with inclusion yields $a\dashv Ri$ on derived categories, and $aRi\simeq\mathrm{id}$ by the sheaf resolution. Thus $Ri$ is fully faithful and $Ri\,a$ is the stated localization. [F1, construct, A1]

2.1 Its local equivalences are exactly the sheafified-cohomology equivalences, since $a$ is exact; the unit becomes a quasi-isomorphism under $a$. The linear source criterion [F2] identifies objects satisfying every hypercover descent with the local objects of this localization. These constructions apply to this actual site, independently of the narrower completed finite-type site. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Actual Chow localization gives surjectivity of the motivic arrow

[Open item](item-lem-author-8a080e7d9445-chow-restriction) · level 12


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the supplied comparisons. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X$ be an affine finite-type threefold over $k$, put $U=X_{\mathrm{smooth}/k}$, let $T\subset X$ be a closed subset contained in $U$, and put $V=U\setminus T$. Use the reduced structure on $T$ when a scheme structure is needed. For the actual open restriction $V\hookrightarrow U$, the map $\mathrm{CH}^3(U)\to\mathrm{CH}^3(V)$ is surjective. Under the preceding natural arrow comparison this is exactly the map $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(U,\mathbb Z)\to H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(V,\mathbb Z)$, which is therefore surjective.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** $k,X,U,T,V$ and the choice and size assumptions of the statement.

**Goal:** Prove surjectivity of Chow restriction and transfer it to this particular motivic restriction arrow.

[F1] The supported-cycle fiber sequence and the identity-on-cycles identification of degree-zero homology with ordinary Chow groups, compatible with open restriction. [def-supported-higher-cycle-complex](item-def-supported-higher-cycle-complex), [lem-bloch-chow-and-negative-range](item-lem-bloch-chow-and-negative-range)

[F2] The natural comparison for the actual restriction arrow under the intended geometry. [lem-author-8a080e7d9445-restriction-diagram](item-lem-author-8a080e7d9445-restriction-diagram)

[F3] For the stated $k,X,U,T,V$, the schemes $U,V$ are smooth separated finite type over the perfect field $k$. [lem-author-8a080e7d9445-geometry](item-lem-author-8a080e7d9445-geometry)

[F4] The Axiom of Choice is retained as an assumption of the supplied comparison framework; the following homology and square arguments make no additional choice. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof
1.1 By [F3], $U,V$ satisfy the smooth finite-type hypotheses of [F1]. Since $T$ is closed in $X$ and contained in $U$, it is closed in $U$ and has open complement $V$. The fixed-support cycle supplier gives the homological fiber sequence $z_T^3(U,\bullet)\to z^3(U,\bullet)\to z^3(V,\bullet)$. Its long exact homology sequence ends in $H_0z^3(U)\to H_0z^3(V)\to H_{-1}z_T^3(U)$. The last group is zero because the supported complex is concentrated in nonnegative homological degrees. Thus the first arrow is surjective. The identity-on-cycles identification of $H_0$ with ordinary Chow groups gives exactly the stated Chow restriction. [given, F1, F3]

2.1 Apply [F2] to this pair, retaining the choice and size assumptions recorded in [F4]. The comparison was constructed as an equivalence of actual restriction diagrams before taking $H^6$. The square of its degree-six maps commutes and its vertical maps are isomorphisms. Surjectivity therefore transfers across that square to the actual motivic arrow, not an arbitrarily identified homomorphism. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1] ∎


## Stable triviality fixes the K-zero class and determinant

[Open item](item-lem-author-b02e51f9da03-stable-invariants) · level 12

### Statement
Assume AC. If a rank-$r$ bundle $E$ on a noetherian affine scheme $X$ has a stable trivialization $E\oplus\mathcal O_X^N\cong\mathcal O_X^{r+N}$, then $[E]=r[\mathcal O_X]$ in the article\'s perfect spectral $K_0(X)$, and $\det E\cong\mathcal O_X$. Here $\det E=\Lambda^rE$ is the determinant line. These conclusions use the actual stable isomorphism; they do not assert that the bundle itself is trivial.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement, AC and the article's fixed universe bounds where its K-theory is used.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] The affine comparison takes vector-bundle exact-sequence classes to the article perfect spectral object classes. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

[F2] Determinants are the top exterior powers with their local wedge bases. [def-exterior-determinant-bundles](item-def-exterior-determinant-bundles)

[F3] The stable trivialization is the actual isomorphism in [def-stably-free-bundles](item-def-stably-free-bundles).

### Proof

1.1 The split exact-sequence relation gives $[E]+N[\mathcal O_X]=(r+N)[\mathcal O_X]$. Subtract the common class in the abelian group to obtain $[E]=r[\mathcal O_X]$, and use [F1] to read it in the spectral group. [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 Take top exterior powers of the stable isomorphism. Wedge the local basis of $E$ before the standard basis of the trivial summand; this gives $\det(E\oplus\mathcal O_X^N)\cong\det E$. The construction glues because changes of frame act by their determinant. The determinant of $\mathcal O_X^{r+N}$ is canonically trivial, so $\det E$ is trivial. [F2, F3, step 1.1, construct] ∎


## Every actual motivic stage on the empty scheme is zero

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-5eb16844831b-empty-motivic-stages) · level 12


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universes of the selected perfect-complex realization. For the empty scheme over any field, every integer stage of the actual motivic filtration is a zero spectrum:
$$F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(\varnothing)\simeq0\qquad(r\in\mathbb Z).$$
This includes the source filtration over either prime field and its restriction to any standing field, and is independent of any empty-dimension convention.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The empty scheme, the actual unital multiplicative filtration, Choice, and fixed universes.

**Goal:** Prove zero stage spectra before invoking any nonempty-scheme dimension result.

[F1] [def-scheme-perfect-complexes](item-def-scheme-perfect-complexes) and [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) identify the enhanced perfect category and its nonconnective K-theory. The selected realization is used under [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). [thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input](item-thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input) identifies its degree-zero homotopy with the cofiber Grothendieck group for an essentially small idempotent-complete stable category, computed using an equivalent small presentation.

[F2] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) identifies stage zero with $K$ and supplies the integer-indexed actual tower. [def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum](item-def-multiplicative-filtered-spectrum) supplies the unit $\eta:\mathbb S\to F^0$ and the unital action $F^0\wedge F^r\to F^r$. [def-stable-spectra-interface](item-def-stable-spectra-interface) identifies $\pi_0E$ with homotopy classes of maps $\mathbb S\to E$ and supplies smash, its zero object and unit constraints.

### Proof
1.1 A sheaf of modules on the empty scheme has only its forced zero value on the empty open set. Thus all complexes and their derived images are equivalent to zero, and the full perfect category is equivalent to the zero stable category. It is idempotent complete. Its cofiber Grothendieck group has only the generator $[0]$, and the cofiber sequence $0\to0\to0$ imposes $[0]=[0]+[0]$, so this group is zero. Applying [F1] under Choice gives $\pi_0K(\varnothing)=0$. [F1, given]

2.1 By [F2], $\pi_0F^0=0$, so the unit $\eta:\mathbb S\to F^0$ is nullhomotopic. For any integer $r$, the unit law identifies the composite $F^r\simeq\mathbb S\wedge F^r\xrightarrow{\eta\wedge1}F^0\wedge F^r\to F^r$ with $1_{F^r}$. The composite is nullhomotopic because smash preserves zero maps. Hence $1_{F^r}=0$ in the homotopy category, so the zero maps between $F^r$ and the zero spectrum are inverse there, and $F^r\simeq0$. This holds for all integers $r$. [F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Units and Picard groups in Nisnevich degree zero and one

[Open item](item-lem-nisnevich-line-bundle-torsors) · level 13


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe bounds in [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites). For a scheme $X$, use its small Nisnevich site, taken as a sufficiently small full subcategory of étale $X$-schemes containing $X$ and closed under the fibre products and Zariski refinements used below. Let $\mathbb G_m$ be the sheaf assigning $U$ the group $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$. Then

$$H^0_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,\mathbb G_m)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times,\qquad H^1_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,\mathbb G_m)\cong\operatorname{Pic}(X).$$

The second identification sends a line bundle to its frame torsor, with inverse obtained by descent from local frames. A line bundle is a Zariski locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of rank one; $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of its isomorphism classes under tensor product.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] The stated Choice assumption supplies the set-indexed choice of torsor sections in step 3.1 and is inherited by the selected derived-sections model. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

**Given:** $X$, its specified small Nisnevich site, the Axiom of Choice, and the stated size bounds.

**Goal:** Identify degrees zero and one, including the frame-torsor inverse.

[F1] Nisnevich covering families are jointly surjective étale families, and Zariski open covers are Nisnevich covers ([def-nisnevich-covering-interface](item-def-nisnevich-covering-interface)).

[F2] The structure presheaf is a sheaf on a site satisfying the listed full-subcategory, Zariski-refinement, terminal-object and fpqc-cover hypotheses. Jointly surjective étale families are fpqc; quasi-coherent modules have effective and fully faithful fpqc descent, and finite local freeness descends ([lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-fpqc-descent-input](item-lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-fpqc-descent-input)).

[F3] Units of a ring sheaf form a sheaf ([lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-units-sheaf](item-lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-units-sheaf)). Degree-zero derived sections of an abelian sheaf are its sections, under the derived conventions of [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites).

[F4] First cohomology classifies torsors as in [lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-h1-torsor-input](item-lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-h1-torsor-input). Frames and transition units have the properties in [lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-frame-transitions](item-lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-frame-transitions), [lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-torsor-cocycle](item-lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-torsor-cocycle), [lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-cocycle-morphism](item-lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-cocycle-morphism), and [lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-tensor-transitions](item-lem-author-8e1c0251ef0d-tensor-transitions).

[F5] The Picard group is the tensor-product group of line-bundle isomorphism classes ([math:def-picard-group-scheme](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-picard-group-scheme)).

### Proof

1.1 The site has the full-subcategory, Zariski-refinement and terminal-object properties required by [F2]. A covering sieve contains a Nisnevich family, and that family is jointly surjective étale by [F1], hence fpqc by [F2]. The sheaf condition can therefore be checked on those generating families. The structure presheaf is a sheaf, and its units form the abelian sheaf $\mathbb G_m$ by [F3]. Evaluation at the terminal object $X$ and [F3] give the stated degree-zero equality. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Let $L$ be a line bundle. On each étale $U\to X$, take frames of its pullback $L|_U$. The structure presheaf on the slice site over $U$ is a sheaf by the same argument as in step 1.1. Frames form a $\mathbb G_m$-torsor by [F4]: Zariski trivializations of $L|_U$ are Nisnevich covers by [F1]. Thus every line bundle determines a torsor. [F1, F4, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Conversely, let $P$ be a $\mathbb G_m$-torsor. Choose a Nisnevich covering family $U_i\to X$ with sections $s_i$. Its transition units $g_{ij}$ satisfy the cocycle equation by [F4]. On each $U_i$ take the free rank-one module with basis $e_i$; use the isomorphisms determined by $e_j=g_{ij}e_i$ on double fibre products. The cocycle equation is exactly the descent compatibility on triple fibre products. [F4, choose, construct, step 2.1, A1]

4.1 The family is fpqc by [F1] and [F2]. Effective descent gives a quasi-coherent module $L$ with these pullbacks and transition maps; finite local freeness descends by [F2]. At every point of $X$, choose a point of some $U_i$ over it. The fibre of $L$ becomes one-dimensional after extension to that point's residue field, so the rank of $L$ there is one. Hence $L$ is a line bundle. [F1, F2, step 3.1]

5.1 The descended frames have the same transitions as the $s_i$, so [F4] gives an equivariant isomorphism from the frame torsor of $L$ to $P$. Conversely, starting with a line bundle and using its local frames, full faithfulness of descent in [F2] identifies the descended module with the original bundle. These constructions are independent of choices: pass to a common refinement, use the change-of-section formula in [F4], and apply full faithfulness of descent. Thus line bundles up to isomorphism and torsors up to equivariant isomorphism are in bijection. [F2, F4, step 2.1, step 4.1]

6.1 By [F4], the torsor bijection gives a canonical bijection with $H^1$. It is compatible with the group laws: using an injective embedding $\mathbb G_m\hookrightarrow I$, the construction described in the cited torsor-classification input represents a class by a global section of $I/\mathbb G_m$, with its torsor the sheaf of local lifts. Adding two representatives adds their local lifts; their transition units multiply. By [F4], tensoring line bundles also multiplies their frame transitions. Therefore the bijection sends tensor products to sums in $H^1$. [F4, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 The unit line bundle has the trivial frame torsor by [F4]. Together with [F5] and steps 1.1 and 6.1, this proves both identifications and the stated inverse. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 6.1] ∎


## Open excision for a descent theory

[Open item](item-lem-open-excision-for-support-fibers) · level 13

### Statement
Let $X$ be a scheme, $T\subseteq X$ a closed subset, $W\subseteq X$ an open subset containing $T$, $U=X\setminus T$, and $V=W\cap U=W\setminus T$. Suppose a contravariant spectrum-valued theory $E$ is defined on these four opens, with coherent restriction maps, and that its restriction square
$$\begin{matrix} E(X)&\longrightarrow&E(W)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ E(U)&\longrightarrow&E(V) \end{matrix}$$
is homotopy cartesian: the induced map $E(X)\to E(W)\times_{E(V)}E(U)$ is an equivalence, where the product is a homotopy pullback. Define $E_T(X)=\operatorname{fib}(E(X)\to E(U))$ and $E_T(W)=\operatorname{fib}(E(W)\to E(V))$. Restriction induces an equivalence $E_T(X)\simeq E_T(W)$. It is natural for compatible maps of such coherent squares, and the square formed by the support-to-global maps and restriction to $W$ commutes coherently.

The same conclusion holds for cochain complexes of abelian groups, with equivalence replaced by quasi-isomorphism, under the following explicit form of two-open descent. Write $A=C(X)$, $B=C(W)$, $C=C(U)$, and $D=C(V)$, and suppose the restriction square is strictly commutative. If $u:B\to D$ and $v:C\to D$ are its lower restriction maps, require the canonical map
$$A\longrightarrow P:=\operatorname{fib}\bigl(B\oplus C\xrightarrow{u-v}D\bigr),\qquad a\longmapsto (a|_W,a|_U,0),$$
to be a quasi-isomorphism, using the explicit fiber complex of [def-supported-complex-indexing](item-def-supported-complex-indexing). Then restriction induces a quasi-isomorphism $C_T(X)\to C_T(W)$, compatible with the support-to-global maps and natural for maps of such squares. In particular it induces isomorphisms on supported cohomology in every degree. A quasi-isomorphism is a cochain map inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups.

These are conditional excision statements: a particular theory must supply the indicated restriction data and descent hypothesis, as well as any quasi-compactness, size, or other conditions required for that hypothesis. No descent property is asserted merely from the existence of a support fiber.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The opens and either a coherent spectrum square or a strictly commutative cochain-complex square as in the statement, satisfying the corresponding displayed descent hypothesis.

**Goal:** Prove the restriction equivalence or quasi-isomorphism of support fibers and its stated compatibility and naturality.

[F1] In the stable spectra interface, fibers and products over a common object are coherent homotopy pullbacks, characterized by their universal properties. [def-stable-spectra-interface](item-def-stable-spectra-interface)

[F2] For a cochain map $f:M\to N$, the support-fiber model has degree-$n$ group $M^n\oplus N^{n-1}$ and differential $(m,n)\mapsto(d_Mm,f(m)-d_Nn)$. A commutative square of cochain maps induces a map of these fibers, and if its two vertical maps are quasi-isomorphisms then so is the induced map on fibers. The support-to-global map is projection to the first factor. [def-supported-complex-indexing](item-def-supported-complex-indexing)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Paste homotopy pullbacks for spectra; for complexes, compare the explicit descent model with the fiber over the target complex.

1.1 In the spectrum case, the descent hypothesis identifies $E(X)$ with $E(W)\times_{E(V)}E(U)$, compatibly with its two projections. Taking the homotopy pullback of the projection to $E(U)$ along $0\to E(U)$ gives $E_T(X)\simeq (E(W)\times_{E(V)}E(U))\times_{E(U)}0 \simeq E(W)\times_{E(V)}0=E_T(W).$ The middle equivalence follows by the universal property of the homotopy pullback: a map into either side is a map into $E(W)$ together with a coherent nullhomotopy of its composite to $E(V)$. The displayed equivalence is the one induced by restriction. [F1, given]

2.1 The same universal property makes this construction natural for compatible maps of the coherent squares. Its projection to $E(W)$ is the composite of the projection $E_T(X)\to E(X)$ with restriction $E(X)\to E(W)$, with the coherence inherited from the pullback diagram. This proves the support-to-global compatibility. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 In the complex case, let $q:A\to P$ be the descent quasi-isomorphism and let $p:P\to C$ be projection. The equality $pq=A\to C$ gives a commutative square with vertical maps $q$ and $\operatorname{id}_C$. By [F2], it induces a quasi-isomorphism $\operatorname{fib}(A\to C)\to\operatorname{fib}(P\to C)$. [F2, given, step 2.1]

4.1 Write an element of $\operatorname{fib}(P\to C)^n$ as $(b,c,d,t)$, with $b\in B^n$, $c\in C^n$, $d\in D^{n-1}$ and $t\in C^{n-1}$. Its differential is $(db,dc,ub-vc-dd,c-dt),$ where each $d$ on the right denotes the differential of the appropriate complex. The map $(b,c,d,t)\longmapsto(b,d+vt)$ to $\operatorname{fib}(B\to D)$ is a cochain map: the second component of the differential becomes $ub-d_D(d+vt)$. It is split surjective as a cochain map, with section $(b,z)\mapsto(b,0,z,0)$. [F2, given, construct, step 3.1]

5.1 Its kernel consists of $(0,c,-vt,t)$ and is isomorphic to $\operatorname{fib}(\operatorname{id}_C)$, with differential $(c,t)\mapsto(dc,c-dt)$. This kernel is contractible: the degree-minus-one map $(c,t)\mapsto(t,0)$ satisfies $dh+hd=\operatorname{id}$. Hence the split surjective map in step 4.1 is a quasi-isomorphism. [step 4.1, construct]

6.1 The composite of the maps in steps 3.1 and 4.1 sends $(a,t)$ to $(a|_W,t|_V)$, exactly the restriction map between the two support-fiber models. It is therefore a quasi-isomorphism. The formula also shows that it commutes strictly with projection to $A$ and $B$ and is natural for maps of the given commutative squares. Taking cohomology gives the stated supported-cohomology isomorphisms. [F2, step 3.1, step 5.1]

7.1 Steps 1.1–2.1 and 3.1–6.1 establish both forms of open excision under their respective descent hypotheses. [step 2.1, step 6.1] ∎



## Motivic dimension vanishing

[Open item](item-thm-motivic-dimension-vanishing) · level 13

### Statement
Let $X$ be a Noetherian equicharacteristic scheme of finite dimension $d$, and let $j\geq0$. Then
$$H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)=0\qquad\text{for every }i>j+d.$$
Here equicharacteristic has the precise EM meaning: the structure map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}F$ for a prime field $F=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$. For such $X$ the groups mean $H^i(M_{j,F}(X))$ in the general prime-field interface. If $X$ is over the standing field $k$, this interface is exactly the theory already defined on $\mathrm{Sch}_k$, by restriction along its prime subfield. The theorem does not require that every $X$ be over that one standing field.

### Statement references
[def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology)

[lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-general-interface](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-general-interface)

[lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-prime-field-vanishing](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-prime-field-vanishing)

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The stated Noetherian finite-dimensional globally equicharacteristic scheme, nonnegative weight and the compatible actual EM interface.

**Goal:** Prove the unrestricted prime-field statement and identify its standing fixed-field specialization.

[F1] [lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-general-interface](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-general-interface) defines the actual general EM groups and proves compatibility with the completed fixed-field definition.

[F2] [lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-shifted-hypotheses](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-shifted-hypotheses) and [lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-fiber-bound](item-lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-fiber-bound) check and apply the imported geometric dimension criterion to the actual shifted comparison fiber.

For the empty scheme the complexes vanish by empty-cover descent, so the assertion is immediate. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 When $X$ additionally carries the standing $k$-structure, [F1] identifies this very complex and its pullbacks with those of the standing definition by actual restriction, so step 1.1 gives its stated specialization. No finite-type, smoothness, regularity or fixed-$k$ restriction has replaced the original Noetherian equicharacteristic hypotheses. This proves the theorem for exactly the defined range $j\geq0$. ## Smooth motivic comparison

[Open item](item-prop-smooth-motivic-comparison) · level 13


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a field, X a smooth finite-type k-scheme, j ≥ 0 and i an integer. The Elmanto–Morrow complex Z(j)_mot(X) is equivalent to $z^j(X,\bullet)[-2j]$, where the homological cycle complex is placed in cochain degree −n in homological degree n. Hence $H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong CH^j(X,2j-i)$, and these groups agree with classical Voevodsky motivic cohomology. The motivic filtration of K(X) agrees, by a natural multiplicative filtered equivalence, with the filtration arising from Voevodsky's slice filtration. In particular $H^{2r,r}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong CH^r(X)$ for r ≥ 0, and $H^{7,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)=0$; the latter includes the case of a smooth threefold.

Here $CH^j(X,n)$ is degree-n homology of Bloch's cycle complex, with negative degrees zero, and $CH^r(X)$ is codimension-r cycles modulo principal-divisor rational equivalence. The filtration is the decreasing Elmanto–Morrow tower on nonconnective K-theory of perfect complexes; its image filtration consists of the images of stage-to-zero maps on homotopy groups. The classical comparison and slice filtration are the constructions recalled in the imported smooth-comparison input.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a field k, a smooth finite-type k-scheme X, j ≥ 0 and i in Z.

**Goal:** Establish the smooth complex and filtration comparisons and the stated cohomological consequences.

[F1] The imported Elmanto–Morrow comparison supplies the derived equivalence, classical identification, and natural multiplicative filtered equivalence under these hypotheses. [thm-author-91088613574d-smooth-comparison-input](item-thm-author-91088613574d-smooth-comparison-input)

[F2] Motivic cohomology is cohomology of the Elmanto–Morrow complex. [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology)

[F3] Equivalent derived complexes have isomorphic cohomology; the cohomology of the shifted cycle complex is higher Chow homology in degree 2j−i. [lem-author-91088613574d-quasi-isomorphism](item-lem-author-91088613574d-quasi-isomorphism), [lem-author-91088613574d-cycle-reindex](item-lem-author-91088613574d-cycle-reindex), [def-bloch-higher-cycle-complex](item-def-bloch-higher-cycle-complex)

[F4] Degree-zero cycle homology is the ordinary Chow group, and negative cycle homology vanishes. [lem-bloch-chow-and-negative-range](item-lem-bloch-chow-and-negative-range)

[F5] The assumed Choice premise, [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), discharges the AC hypothesis of the selected perfect-complex realization when [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) is invoked. For nonnegative stages, the image filtration uses transitions to stage zero, and a filtered equivalence identifying stage zero with $K(X)$ identifies these images by [lem-author-91088613574d-filtered-images](item-lem-author-91088613574d-filtered-images). The integer-indexed convention of [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) extends the nonnegative tower constantly below zero, with stage $K(X)$ and identity augmentation. Apply the same constant extension to the classical tower when comparing integer indices. At every negative stage, both augmentation images are therefore the whole group $K_i(X)$. No transition from a negative stage to zero is used, and the image comparison makes no further choice.

### Proof
1.1 Apply the imported smooth comparison [F1] to X and j. This gives the displayed derived equivalence and the identification with the classical motivic complex; it also gives the multiplicative filtered equivalence. [given, F1]

2.1 Apply cohomology to the derived equivalence and use the explicit chain-to-cochain and shift translation in [F3]. Together with the definition in [F2], this gives $H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong CH^j(X,2j-i)$. The classical identification in step 1.1 identifies the same groups with classical Voevodsky motivic cohomology. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Put i = 2r and $j = r$ in step 2.1. The higher Chow index is zero, so [F4] identifies the result with $CH^r(X)$. Put $i = 7$ and $j = 3$: the index is −1, so the group is zero by [F4], independently of dimension. [F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Invoke the local motivic-filtration interface under the assumed Choice premise as specified in [F5]. The filtered equivalence of step 1.1 gives the asserted comparison of nonnegative towers. For each nonnegative stage, its compatibility with the transition to zero gives the commuting square of [F5], so the images in $K_i(X)$ agree. Under the common constant extension to negative indices, extend the equivalence there by its stage-zero identification; both negative-stage augmentations are identities on $K(X)$ and thus have image $K_i(X)$. This also compares the integer-indexed image filtrations without a negative-stage transition to zero. Steps 1.1 through 3.1 prove the cohomological assertions. [F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎


## Finite constant cdh sections

[Open item](item-lem-finite-constant-cdh-sections) · level 13

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $X$ a separated seminormal scheme of finite type over $k$, and $A$ a finite set. Put $Y_A=\coprod_{a\in A}\operatorname{Spec}k$. On the big cdh site of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, the constant cdh sheaf associated to $A$ is canonically isomorphic to $h_{Y_A}^{\mathrm{cdh}}$, the cdh sheafification of $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_k(T,Y_A)$. Consequently there are natural bijections
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{cdh}}(X,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(X,Y_A)\cong\operatorname{Map}(\pi_0(X),A).$$
These assertions include the empty set and empty scheme cases.

Here the constant cdh sheaf associated to $A$ is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value $A$ and identity restriction maps. Sections $\Gamma_{\mathrm{cdh}}(X,A)$ mean its value at $X$. The set $\pi_0(X)$ consists of the connected components of the underlying topological space; a connected component is a maximal subset that cannot be partitioned into two nonempty relatively open subsets. A finite-type $k$-scheme has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Seminormal means that every point has an affine neighbourhood with coordinate ring $R$ such that each pair $x,y\in R$ satisfying $x^3=y^2$ has a unique $a\in R$ with $a^2=x$ and $a^3=y$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, an algebraically closed field $k$, a separated seminormal finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, and a finite set $A$.

**Goal:** Identify the constant cdh sheaf with $h_{Y_A}^{\mathrm{cdh}}$ and obtain the displayed natural bijections.

[F1] The big cdh site has separated finite-type $k$-schemes as objects, and its coverings include Nisnevich coverings. In particular, an open cover is a cdh covering family: open immersions are étale and each point has a lift with unchanged residue field. [def-cdh-topology-interface](item-def-cdh-topology-interface)

[F2] Sheafification is left adjoint to the inclusion of sheaves into presheaves. A sheaf assigns a unique amalgamation to every compatible family on a covering sieve. [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification)

[F3] For a perfect field $k$ and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $T,Y$, the cdh sheafification of $h_Y$ evaluated at a seminormal $T$ is naturally $\operatorname{Hom}_k(T,Y)$. A field is perfect when every algebraic extension is separable. [prop-cdh-representable-seminormalization](item-prop-cdh-representable-seminormalization) [def-seminormal-scheme-interface](item-def-seminormal-scheme-interface)

[F4] Under the Axiom of Choice, if $T$ is a Noetherian $k$-scheme, morphisms $T\to Y_A$ correspond naturally to functions $\pi_0(T)\to A$. A Noetherian scheme has a Noetherian underlying space, meaning that descending chains of closed subsets stabilize. [lem-clopen-finite-constant-maps](item-lem-clopen-finite-constant-maps) [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Use the universal property of sheafification and the open decomposition induced by a map to the finite disjoint union, then apply the two stated suppliers.

1.1 Let $C_A$ be the constant presheaf. There is a natural map $C_A\to h_{Y_A}$ sending $a\in A$ to the composite $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y_A$ through the summand labelled $a$. The same definition covers $A=\varnothing$, when the map has empty domain at each object. [given, construct]

2.1 For any cdh sheaf $F$, restriction along this map gives a function $\operatorname{Hom}(h_{Y_A},F)\to\operatorname{Hom}(C_A,F)$. It is bijective. Indeed, given a presheaf map $u:C_A\to F$ and a morphism $f:T\to Y_A$, write $T_a$ for the inverse image of the $a$-summand. The $T_a$ are pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subschemes covering $T$; because $A$ is finite, they are objects of the site. On $T_a$ take $u_{T_a}(a)$. These sections agree on all overlaps: the overlaps are empty, and the sheaf axiom for the empty open cover gives $F(\varnothing)$ exactly one element. By the sheaf axiom they glue uniquely to an element of $F(T)$. Pullback of this decomposition and uniqueness of gluing show that the construction is natural in $T$, hence defines a presheaf map $h_{Y_A}\to F$. If $A$ is empty, a map $T\to Y_A=\varnothing$ exists only for $T=\varnothing$, and the same empty-cover argument applies. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 The construction in step 2.1 restricts to $u$: the constant morphism labelled $a$ has $T_a=T$ and all other inverse images empty. Conversely, any presheaf map $h_{Y_A}\to F$ must take $f$ to the glued section in step 2.1, since its restriction to each $T_a$ is determined by naturality and the constant map labelled $a$. Thus the two operations are inverse. By [F2], the induced map $a_{\mathrm{cdh}}C_A\to a_{\mathrm{cdh}}h_{Y_A}$ is an isomorphism: both sheaves represent the same natural functor of cdh sheaves. This proves the asserted canonical identification of sheaves. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 The finite disjoint union $Y_A$ is separated and of finite type over $k$, including when it is empty. An algebraically closed field is perfect, since every algebraic extension is the field itself. Thus [F3] applies to the given $X$ and $Y_A$, and the seminormality hypothesis gives $h_{Y_A}^{\mathrm{cdh}}(X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(X,Y_A)$. Together with step 3.1 this yields the first displayed bijection. [F3, given, step 3.1]

5.1 A finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian: its finite affine cover has finitely generated coordinate algebras, which are Noetherian by the Hilbert basis theorem, and a finite union of Noetherian open subspaces is Noetherian. Applying [F4] to $X$ gives the second displayed bijection. The two bijections are natural in $X$ and $A$: the first is induced by natural sheaf maps and the natural comparison in [F3], and the second is natural by [F4]. [F4, given, step 4.1]

6.1 Steps 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1 prove the sheaf identification and both claimed bijections, including the empty cases covered by the constructions and [F4]. [F4, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Singular Beilinson–Lichtenbaum input

[Open item](item-prop-singular-beilinson-lichtenbaum) · level 13


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and compatible universe bounds for the small étale sites, big cdh sites, slices and products in the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, let $p$ be a prime, and choose a primitive $p$th root $\zeta\in k$ (in particular this can be done for the article’s algebraically closed $k$). On all qcqs $k$-schemes there is the specified natural equivalence
$$\mathbb Z(3)_{\rm cdh}/p\simeq L_{\rm cdh,k}\tau^{\leq3}R\Gamma_{\rm et}(-,\mathbb Z/p).$$
Here the left side is the restriction of the actual EM cdh-local weight-three complex on qcqs $\mathbb Q$-schemes, with its objectwise derived quotient; $L_{\rm cdh,k}$ is BEM big-site complex-valued cdh localization on qcqs $k$-schemes, with the induced topology and ordinary reflective sheafification specified by the slice-site construction. Equivalently the right side is the restriction of the ambient localized Tate-twisted complex followed by the specified root trivialization. No comparison with a separately fixed separated finite-type or hypercomplete site is asserted.

### Statement references
[lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-site)

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Choice and the compatible site and universe bounds are used when invoking the derived-sections construction in [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-truncated-root-map](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-truncated-root-map). [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [thm-author-2ac325480ae8-bem-finite-comparison](item-thm-author-2ac325480ae8-bem-finite-comparison) supplies the actual ambient twisted comparison in weight3 mod-$p$.

[F2] [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-motivic-restriction-coefficients](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-motivic-restriction-coefficients) identifies its restricted left side with the specified EM finite quotient.

[F3] [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-localization](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-slice-localization) and [lem-author-2ac325480ae8-truncated-root-map](item-lem-author-2ac325480ae8-truncated-root-map) supply the actual slice-localization equivalence and the localized inverse of the root coefficient map.

### Proof
**Given:** $k,p,\zeta$ as stated, with fixed compatible universes and AC.

**Goal:** Prove the formula with the actual coefficient/truncation/localization maps.

1.1 Restrict the actual comparison of [F1] to the slice $\mathcal C/\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its source identifies with the left side of the statement by [F2]. Restriction is a functor, so this remains a natural equivalence, including after evaluation at any qcqs $X/k$. [F1, F2]

2.1 Since $k$ has characteristic zero, $p$ is invertible in $k$; the chosen primitive root, qcqs slice and ordinary localizations satisfy the hypotheses of the truncated-root-map supplier under [A1]. Apply [F3] to the target from step 1.1. The unit-compatible interchange identifies it with $L_{\rm cdh,k}\tau^{\leq3}R\Gamma_{\rm et}(-,\mu_p^{\otimes3})$ on the slice. Compose with localization of the inverse coefficient map induced by $1\mapsto\zeta^{\otimes3}$, after the stated objectwise truncation. The result is exactly the displayed right side. Every arrow is now a specified natural map of the stated complexes. [A1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The composite is an equivalence and is contravariantly natural on qcqs $k$-schemes. This proves the characteristic-zero application without a site substitution or any use of a degree-three truncated comparison in an unsupported degree. [step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Motivic and filtered K theory with support

[Open item](item-def-cohomology-with-support) · level 13


### Definition
Fix a field $k$ and the category $\mathrm{Sch}_k$ of quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-schemes from [def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions), together with the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the cited interfaces. Let $X$ be an object of this category, let $Y$ be a closed subset of $X$ equipped with its reduced induced closed-subscheme structure, and put $U=X\setminus Y$. The reduced structure has the same underlying closed subset and has no nonzero nilpotent local sections.

For the quotient notation, let $h_X(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(T,X)$ and let $h_U(T)$ be the subset of maps whose image lies in $U$, for $T\in\mathrm{Sch}_k$. On a size-bounded big Nisnevich site with these objects, let $\mathbb Z[h_X]$ and $\mathbb Z[h_U]$ denote the sheafifications of the presheaves of free abelian groups on these sets. Define the **quotient sheaf** $\mathbb Z[X/U]$ as the cokernel of $\mathbb Z[h_U]\to\mathbb Z[h_X]$, regarded when needed as a complex concentrated in degree zero. Here a cokernel is the quotient of the target sheaf by the image sheaf. This notation records the pair $(X,U)$; the support objects below are defined directly as fibers.

The supplied functors are defined on qcqs schemes. To cover an arbitrary open $U$, use the following explicit extension convention. For any such open $W\subseteq X$, let $\mathcal Q(W)$ be the poset of quasi-compact open subsets of $W$. For $j\geq0$, put
$$F^jK(W):=\operatorname*{holim}_{V\in\mathcal Q(W)^{\mathrm{op}}}F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(V),\qquad K(W):=\operatorname*{holim}_{V\in\mathcal Q(W)^{\mathrm{op}}}K(V),$$
and, writing $C_j(V)=\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}(V)$ and $HC_j(V)$ for its Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectrum,
$$M_j(W):=\operatorname*{holim}_{V\in\mathcal Q(W)^{\mathrm{op}}}HC_j(V).$$
The arrows in each inverse diagram are restrictions. Homotopy limits are limits in the stable category of spectra. When $W$ is qcqs, its identity open is terminal in $\mathcal Q(W)$, and these expressions recover the supplied values. For arbitrary $W$, these formulas specify an extension; they do not assert its comparison with any independently constructed theory on non-qcqs schemes.

Define the **filtered support spectrum**, the **K-theory support fiber**, and the **motivic support spectrum** by
$$F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X/U):=\operatorname{fib}(F^jK(X)\to F^jK(U)),\quad K(X/U):=\operatorname{fib}(K(X)\to K(U)),$$
$$M_j(X/U):=\operatorname{fib}(M_j(X)\to M_j(U)).$$
A fiber is the homotopy pullback of the displayed map along the map from the zero spectrum. The compatible stage-to-zero maps give a map $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X/U)\to K(X/U)$. For every integer $i$ define
$$F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_{i,Y}(X):=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_iF^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X/U)\to\pi_iK(X/U)\bigr).$$
The image is the subgroup consisting of values of this homomorphism. Define supported motivic cohomology for every integer $a$ by
$$H^{a,j}_{\mathrm{mot},Y}(X,\mathbb Z):=\pi_{-a}M_j(X/U).$$
Equivalently, define the shifted support spectrum $\mathbb Z(j)^{\mathrm{shift}}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X/U):=M_j(X/U)[2j]$. With this explicitly shifted meaning,
$$H^{2j-i,j}_{\mathrm{mot},Y}(X,\mathbb Z)=\pi_i\bigl(\mathbb Z(j)^{\mathrm{shift}}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X/U)\bigr).$$
The support-to-global maps are the first arrows of the defining fiber sequences. The image groups obtained after applying those maps are separate from the supported groups defined here.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** $k$, $X$, $Y$, $U$, $j\geq0$, and integers $i,a$ as above, with the stated choice and size conventions.

**Goal:** Justify the quotient notation, the support fibers and their maps, the image group, and the displayed indexing without assuming injectivity or a comparison with an independently constructed quotient evaluation.

[F1] [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification) supplies the site and sheafification conventions; [def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions) specifies qcqs schemes and their category.

[F2] The already assumed Axiom of Choice, [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), discharges the explicit Choice hypothesis when invoking the perfect-complex $K$-theory and filtration interface in [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration). That interface supplies the coherent restriction maps and stage-to-$K$ maps on qcqs schemes. [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) supplies the complex-valued restriction functor and identifies global $H^{a,j}$ with $H^a(C_j)$.

[F3] [def-stable-spectra-interface](item-def-stable-spectra-interface) supplies homotopy limits, fibers, suspension and the abelian groups $\pi_i$. [lem-filtered-support-exactness](item-lem-filtered-support-exactness) gives the stagewise support construction for a coherent filtered restriction diagram.

[F4] [lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index](item-lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index) gives $\pi_iHC\cong H^{-i}(C)$ and $\pi_i(E[2j])\cong\pi_{i-2j}E$ in the stated convention. [def-supported-complex-indexing](item-def-supported-complex-indexing) distinguishes unshifted support from its $2j$-shift.

### Justification
1.1 The subfunctor $h_U\subseteq h_X$ is stable under precomposition, so the induced map of free abelian presheaves and its sheafification are defined; the cokernel defines the stated quotient sheaf. Every open subset of a scheme is the union of its affine open subsets, and each affine open is quasi-compact. Since $X$ is quasi-separated, a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq X$ is quasi-separated as well; hence each $V\in\mathcal Q(W)$ belongs to $\mathrm{Sch}_k$. The restriction maps in [F2] therefore form the indicated coherent inverse diagrams, whose homotopy limits exist by [F3]. If $W$ itself is quasi-compact, its membership in $\mathcal Q(W)$ makes it initial in the opposite indexing category, so the limit is its supplied value. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Inclusions of open subsets induce restriction maps between these limits, and the coherent maps from filtration stages to $K$ induce a map of the two restriction arrows. Taking fibers produces the displayed support spectra and the map between them; the two sequences are fiber sequences by definition. The induced homomorphism on $\pi_i$ has a well-defined image subgroup. This is the stagewise construction of [F3], applied to the restriction diagram with the stated extension convention. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F4], the shifted support spectrum has $\pi_i(M_j(X/U)[2j])\cong\pi_{i-2j}M_j(X/U)$, which is the definition of $H^{2j-i,j}_{\mathrm{mot},Y}(X,\mathbb Z)$. For a qcqs global scheme, the same indexing lemma identifies $\pi_{-a}M_j(X)$ with $H^a(C_j(X))$; hence the first fiber arrow induces the degree-preserving support-to-global map. The construction does not require that the supported image map be injective. This justifies the definitions and their stated maps. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1] ∎

### Source notation and scope
The article prints $H^{2j-i,j}_{\mathrm{mot},Y}(X,\mathbb Z):=\pi_i(\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X/U))$ at Definition 2.7. The formula above specifies a $2j$-shift on the spectrum occurring on the right so that it is compatible with the cohomological convention of [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology). The unshifted realization instead has $\pi_i=H^{-i}$; the printed notation alone does not specify the comparison between these two conventions. The quotient sheaf and fiber definitions retain the article's pair and fiber sequences, but no identification of the displayed fibers with an independently defined evaluation on that sheaf is asserted here. In particular, $K(X/U)$ is not identified here with the K-theory of the category of perfect complexes supported on $Y$; such an identification needs a localization input with its own hypotheses.


## Motivic projective bundle formula

[Open item](item-prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula) · level 13


### Statement
Assume AC. On the article category of qcqs $k$-schemes, the supplied motivic cohomology, with $H^{a,b}(X)=0$ explicitly for $b<0$, is an additively oriented bigraded theory satisfying the projective bundle contract. This holds over any field $k$ (hence in particular the article’s algebraically closed base), without smoothness, reducedness, Noetherianity or dimension hypotheses. Its ring is the actual EM graded cup-product ring and its orientation is EM Definition5.2. For a bundle $E$ of constant rank $r>0$, the quotient convention $\mathbb P_X(E)=\operatorname{Proj}_X\operatorname{Sym}(E)$ with $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ gives, for every $(a,b)\in\mathbb Z^2$,
$$\bigoplus_{m=0}^{r-1}H^{a-2m,b-m}(X)\xrightarrow{\ \sum_m\pi^*(-)\xi^m\ } H^{a,b}(\mathbb P_X(E)),$$
a natural isomorphism. No rank-zero projective-bundle assertion is required.

### Statement references
[def-bigraded-oriented-theory](item-def-bigraded-oriented-theory)

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice, as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). It discharges the choice hypotheses of the projective-bundle contract in steps 1.1–1.2 and of all three projective-bundle suppliers in [F3] in step 2.1.

[F1] [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) fixes the groups in nonnegative weight. [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-bigraded-ring](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-bigraded-ring) supplies the extension, natural ring and first-degree sign.

[F2] [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-additive-c1](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-additive-c1) supplies the actual additive natural first Chern class.

[F3] [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-dual-conventions](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-dual-conventions), [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-all-bidegrees](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-all-bidegrees) and [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-base-change](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-base-change) supply the quotient convention, exact formula in all degrees, and category/base-change requirements. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes) specifies the finite locally free bundles.

[F4] [def-bigraded-oriented-theory](item-def-bigraded-oriented-theory) lists the four clauses of the contract.

### Proof
**Given:** The stated scheme category, AC and motivic suppliers.

**Goal:** Exhibit all four clauses with the actual source maps.

1.1 Use [F1] to define all integer bidegrees by zero extension and the direct-sum ring. Its unit, product bidegrees, associativity, graded commutativity and functorial unital pullbacks are precisely clauses1–2 of [F4]. [A1, F1, F4]

1.2 Use the map in [F2] for the orientation. Its additivity, zero value on the trivial line and naturality give clause3; no orientation is selected from an arbitrary Picard-group isomorphism. [A1, F2, F4]

2.1 Under [A1], by [F3] all projective bundles/base-change maps stay in the scheme category, and the displayed formula is the actual quotient-tautological-class map. It is an isomorphism for every integer bidegree, including zero source/target for negative target weights. This gives clause4, completing the contract and the proposition. [A1, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎


## Local application interface for a critical-rank cancellation theorem

[Open item](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-cancellation-interface) · level 13


### Statement
Assume AC and the suitable universes used for the article's perfect K-theory construction. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be noetherian affine and $r\geq0$. Suppose every constant-rank-$r$ finite projective $A$-module is cancellative in the free-stabilization sense. Then two rank-$r$ bundles $E,F$ on $X$ are isomorphic exactly when $[E]=[F]$ in the article\'s spectral $K_0(X)$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] Rank and isomorphism classes pass through the affine equivalence. [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-module-classes](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-module-classes)

[F2] Under AC and the stated universes, spectral K-zero equality for vector bundles on a noetherian affine scheme is equivalent to a common finite free module stabilization. [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-spectral-kzero-stability](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-spectral-kzero-stability)

[F3] The meaning of cancellative is fixed by [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-cancellative-free-summands](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-cancel-cancellative-free-summands).

### Proof

1.1 If the K-zero classes agree, let $P,Q$ be the modules of sections. They have constant rank $r$, and [F2] gives $P\oplus A^N\cong Q\oplus A^N$. By the assumed cancellativity, $P\cong Q$. By [F1], $E\cong F$. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 If $E\cong F$, the spectral object-class map assigns the same element to both; equivalently [F2] applies with $N=0$. Hence the converse holds too. [F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Chern data survive addition of trivial bundles

[Open item](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-stabilized-chern) · level 13


### Statement
Assume AC. Fix a field $k$ and a smooth equidimensional finite-type $k$-scheme $X$. Let $E,F$ be vector bundles on $X$, allowing locally constant finite ranks. Their ordinary Chow Chern polynomials are taken componentwise on the finite open-and-closed common rank partition. They satisfy $c_t(E\oplus\mathcal O_X^m)=c_t(E)$ for every integer $m\geq0$, and likewise for $F$. Consequently equal Chern tuples of rank-two bundles give equal first three Chern classes of $E\oplus\mathcal O_X$ and $F\oplus\mathcal O_X$: the common third class is zero. For every $k$-morphism $f:X'\to X$ from another smooth equidimensional finite-type $k$-scheme, these equalities remain true after pullback.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] The Chern class convention and tuple map on the stated smooth equidimensional finite-type schemes over $k$ are fixed in [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-chern-interface](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-chern-interface). Choice is used in invoking that qualified Chow interface. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F2] The operational Whitney identity gives $c_t(E\oplus G)=c_t(E)c_t(G)$, and $c_t(\mathcal O)=1$; the published Chow Chern definition gives naturality and rank vanishing. [math:lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula), [math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle)

[F3] The finite locally free sheaves $E,F$ on the qcqs scheme $X$ have a finite common open-and-closed rank partition, including rank-zero strata. [lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-finite-common-rank-strata](item-lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-finite-common-rank-strata)

### Proof

1.1 The finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ is noetherian and qcqs, so apply [F3] to $E,F$. Every integral cycle and every generating principal-divisor relation is supported in one of the open-and-closed strata, so the cycle groups and their rational-equivalence quotients split as finite direct sums over those strata. Thus Chow classes and polynomials are determined by their restrictions there, justifying the componentwise convention in the statement. The nonempty strata remain smooth equidimensional finite-type $k$-schemes, so [F1] and [F2] apply on each; for rank zero use the zero-bundle convention $c_t(0)=1$ in [F2]. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 On each stratum the $m=0$ equality is an identity. For $m>0$, Whitney applied $m$ times gives $c_t(E\oplus\mathcal O_X^m)=c_t(E)$, since each trivial line contributes the unit polynomial; the same holds for $F$. Step 1.1 assembles these equalities on $X$. If $E,F$ have rank two and equal Chern tuples, their first two coefficients agree by [F1] and both third coefficients vanish by [F2]. Stabilization therefore gives identical first three coefficients, with third coefficient zero. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Both schemes and $f$ have the specified base-field and finiteness scope. Pullback preserves direct sums and trivial bundles and pulls the rank partition back to an open-and-closed partition of $X'$. On each nonempty inverse-image stratum naturality in [F2] gives $c_i(f^*E)=f^*c_i(E)$ and the analogous identities for $F$ and their stabilizations. Apply this coefficientwise to step 2.1 and assemble over the strata as in step 1.1. All asserted equalities persist on $X'$, including the zero third coefficient. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Mohan Kumar–Murthy rank-three Chow classification

[Open item](item-thm-author-f08c343a07fc-local-kumar-murthy-chow-input) · level 13

### Statement
Assume AC. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic and $Y$ a smooth affine threefold over $k$. Then $C_3:\mathrm{Vect}_3(Y)\to\mathrm{CH}^1(Y)\times\mathrm{CH}^2(Y)\times\mathrm{CH}^3(Y)$, $[G]_{\mathrm{iso}}\mapsto(c_1(G),c_2(G),c_3(G))$, is bijective. The classes are the ordinary integral Chow Chern classes with the quotient-projective-bundle normalization. Thus every triple occurs, and two such bundles are isomorphic exactly when their triples agree.

### External input
Only the established classification statement is imported, via the exact authoritative subsequent statement. Standard ordinary Chern classes, rather than abstract unnamed isomorphic invariants, are specified there. The local projective-bundle coefficient interface fixes the same sign convention. This is not a comparison with a singular motivic Chern operation. The surface branch below uses a cylinder reduction; it does not claim to reproduce either the original Murthy–Swan argument or the original Mohan Kumar–Murthy proof.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] The exact classical rank-three Chern bijection is the external input stated by Asok–Fasel p. 2 and attributed to Mohan Kumar–Murthy.

[F2] The ordinary Chow Chern map and its coefficient convention are fixed in [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-chern-interface](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-chern-interface).

### Proof

1.1 Apply the external rank-three classification with the given algebraically closed field and smooth affine threefold. The recalled classical theorem imposes no characteristic restriction; the separate nearby rank-two theorem is not being applied. Its map is the ordinary Chern tuple map fixed by [F2]. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Surjectivity supplies a rank-three bundle for each triple, and injectivity says that equal triples have the same bundle isomorphism class. Conversely an isomorphism gives equal Chern classes by [F2]. These are the asserted existence and uniqueness conclusions. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Fixed determinant isolates the actual Chern fiber

[Open item](item-lem-author-9b282fc59773-fixed-determinant-fibers) · level 13

### Statement
For the map $C_X$ and subsets just defined, the fiber $C_X^{-1}(L,a)$ is exactly $V_{L,a}$. The map $C_X$ is bijective if and only if for every line-bundle class $L$ and every class $a\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)$ the set $V_{L,a}$ has exactly one element. This classification forgets every choice of an isomorphism $\det E\cong L$.

### Statement references
[def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers](item-def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers)

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** $X$, $C_X$ and $V_{L,a}$ from [F1].

**Goal:** Identify the fibers and the exact existence-and-uniqueness criterion.

[F1] $C_X([E])=([\det E],c_2(E))$, and $V_{L,a}$ imposes these two equalities on bundle isomorphism classes. [def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers](item-def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers)

### Proof
1.1 An element $e$ belongs to $C_X^{-1}(L,a)$ precisely when both coordinates of $C_X(e)$ equal the displayed coordinates. The first equality says $e\in V_L$, and the second says $e\in V_{L,a}$. This proves equality of the two subsets, without adding a determinant isomorphism to their elements. [F1, given]

2.1 If all these fibers have one element, every target pair has a preimage and any two elements with equal images lie in the same singleton fiber; hence $C_X$ is surjective and injective. Conversely, a bijection has exactly one preimage for each target element. Step 1.1 translates that fact to the asserted sets. [step 1.1, given] ∎


## Asok–Fasel Chern-compatible comparison and lifting input

[Open item](item-thm-author-9b282fc59773-asok-fasel-comparison-input) · level 13

### Statement
Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic different from two, and $X$ a smooth affine $k$-scheme of finite type of pure dimension three. For the defined $V=\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)$ and $T=\operatorname{Pic}(X)\times\mathrm{CH}^2(X)$, there exist sets $M,N$, bijections $v:V\to M$, $b:N\to T$, and a surjection $t:M\to N$ with $b t v=C_X$. For every $n\in N$, there are abelian groups $A_n,H_n,D_n$ and homomorphisms exact at the middle group in $A_n\to H_n\to D_n$, with $A_n=D_n=0$, such that the nonempty fiber $t^{-1}(n)$ is a surjective image of the underlying set of $H_n$. Under the ordinary divisor-class identification $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\cong\mathrm{CH}^1(X)$, the first coordinate $[\det E]$ is the usual first Chern class $c_1(E)$; the second coordinate is the usual Chow-theoretic $c_2(E)$, with its standard projective-bundle sign convention.

### Statement references
[def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers](item-def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers)

### External input
This is an explicitly imported established theorem interface, extracted from Asok–Fasel, arXiv:1204.0770v5, Theorem 1 (p. 2), Proposition 6.2 (p. 24), Proposition 6.3 and Proposition 6.5 (p. 25), and the complete proof of Theorem 6.6 (p. 26). It is not a locally reconstructed obstruction-theory theorem. The sets-and-maps formulation records exactly what is needed for the local application; none of the extra symbols is defined by circular appeal to the desired classification.

In the source, $M=[X,B\mathrm{GL}_2]_{\mathbb A^1}$ is the set of morphisms in the unstable $\mathbb A^1$-homotopy category, that is, the category of simplicial Nisnevich sheaves localized at Nisnevich local weak equivalences and at the projections $U\times\mathbb A^1\to U$. Here $B\mathrm{GL}_2$ is the simplicial classifying space of the sheaf of invertible two-by-two matrices, and brackets denote unpointed homotopy classes. The map $v$ is affine vector-bundle representability. The set $N$ is the set of maps to its second Postnikov stage: the truncation preserving homotopy sheaves through degree two and killing the higher ones. The map $t$ is induced by that truncation. These constructions and representability are imported, not proved here.

Proposition 6.3 describes the second stage by a line bundle $L$ and a degree-two class with coefficients in the $L$-twisted Milnor–Witt K-theory sheaf. Corollary 5.3 identifies that degree-two cohomology with ordinary Milnor K-theory cohomology, hence with $\mathrm{CH}^2(X)$ by the source's Chow identification. The first two paragraphs of the proof of Theorem 6.6 identify the resulting maps, not merely the groups: the first stage is determinant, and the second coordinate is the composite with the universal second Chern class (using Morel, Remark 7.22). This is the map-level content of $b t v=C_X$.

For precision about the imported uniqueness mechanism, the groups in the statement are the source's Nisnevich cohomology groups
$$A_n=H^3_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,T'_4),\qquad H_n=H^3_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,\pi^{\mathbb A^1}_3(B\mathrm{GL}_2)(\xi)),\qquad D_n=H^3_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,\mathrm{GW}^2_3(L)).$$
Here $L$ is the line-bundle coordinate of $b(n)$ and $\xi$ its associated multiplicative-group torsor (the complement of its zero section); twisting uses that torsor. Nisnevich cohomology means the derived cohomology of sections on the site of étale maps with covers admitting a residue-field-preserving lift of each point. The symbols $\pi^{\mathbb A^1}_3$, $T'_4$ and $\mathrm{GW}^2_3$ denote respectively the homotopy sheaf, the kernel sheaf of Theorem 3.3 for $n=1$, and the Grothendieck–Witt sheaf in the source; their constructions are part of this external input, not additional locally defined suppliers. The exact sequence is displayed in the proof of Theorem 6.6. Proposition 6.2 supplies surjectivity of $t$ in dimension three; the preceding lifting discussion, pp. 23–24, supplies the quotient description of a nonempty lift fiber used in the statement. In that description one may choose a representative and a lift; only existence of the resulting surjection of sets is asserted here.

The last paragraph of the proof of Theorem 6.6 establishes $A_n=D_n=0$. It uses Theorem 3.3, Proposition 6.5, Proposition 5.1 to kill the relevant fundamental-ideal sheaf, Proposition 5.4 with modulus twelve to kill the top Milnor-K quotient cohomology, and Proposition 4.16 to make the twisted Grothendieck–Witt group a quotient of $\mathrm{CH}^3(X)/2$. Divisibility of zero-cycles on this smooth affine threefold makes this last quotient zero. Thus the imported input includes all hypotheses needed for both existence and uniqueness, for every determinant class, not merely the trivial determinant.

### Source notes
Read Theorem 1 and introductory outline, pp. 2–3; §6, pp. 22–26, including Theorem 6.1, Proposition 6.2 and its proof, Proposition 6.3 and its proof, Proposition 6.5 and the complete proof of Theorem 6.6. Also read Theorem 3.3 statement (p. 10), Proposition 4.16 statement (p. 17), and Proposition 5.1, Corollary 5.3 and Proposition 5.4 with the adjacent displayed arguments (pp. 20–21). Visually inspected PDF p. 26. Did not reconstruct §§2–5, Morel Remark 7.22, the cited representability theorem, Bloch identification, or the zero-cycle divisibility theorem; these remain part of the explicit published external input, not locally proved results.

## The actual exterior-dual class in affine perfect K zero

[Open item](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-exterior-dual-interface) · level 13

### Statement
Assume AC. On a noetherian affine scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and for a rank-$r$ bundle $E$, define $\varepsilon(E)=\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i[\Lambda^iE^\vee]\in K_0(X)$, where $K_0(X)$ is the article\'s perfect spectral K-zero group and brackets are degree-zero bundle object classes. For $P=\Gamma(X,E)$ the ordinary projective-module expression $C^K_r(P)=\sum_i(-1)^i[\Lambda^iP^*]$, $P^*=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)$, maps to exactly $\varepsilon(E)$ under the affine comparison. Moreover $\lambda_{-1}(E)=(-1)^r[\det E]\varepsilon(E)$, so these two exterior conventions vanish simultaneously. For a regular section of $E$, its Koszul complex uses $E^\vee$ and has ambient class $\varepsilon(E)$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The hypotheses and data in the statement, with AC and the article's fixed universes wherever perfect K-theory is used.

**Goal:** Establish the asserted conclusion.

[F1] The affine comparison identifies the module/bundle Grothendieck classes with perfect spectral object classes, and the affine equivalence preserves duals and tensor products. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes), [lem-affine-bundle-module-interface](item-lem-affine-bundle-module-interface)

[F2] Exterior powers and determinants are functorial, finite locally free and have the increasing-wedge bases. [def-exterior-determinant-bundles](item-def-exterior-determinant-bundles)

[F3] The exterior-duality identity is $\lambda_{-1}(E)=(-1)^r[\det E]\lambda_{-1}(E^\vee)$ with the determinant factor a unit. [lem-exterior-euler-duality](item-lem-exterior-euler-duality)

[F4] A regular section of $E$ is a functional on $E^\vee$; its Koszul class has the dual exterior sum. [lem-regular-zero-koszul-euler-class](item-lem-regular-zero-koszul-euler-class)

### Proof

1.1 The finite sum defining $\varepsilon(E)$ exists and is invariant under bundle isomorphisms by [F1] and [F2]. Sheafification identifies $P^*$ with $E^\vee$ by [F1]. The natural map from the sheaf associated to $\Lambda^iP^*$ to $\Lambda^iE^\vee$ is an isomorphism: on a principal cover trivializing $P^*$ both sides have the same increasing-wedge bases and the map carries each basis to itself. The affine comparison thus carries every summand of $C^K_r(P)$ to the displayed summand of $\varepsilon(E)$. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 Tensor compatibility makes the affine comparison respect multiplication on these bundle classes; the product is tensor product on both presentations. Therefore [F3] carries its determinant-unit identity into spectral $K_0(X)$ and proves simultaneous vanishing. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply the regular-section clause of [F4] to $E$ itself. Its complex has terms $\Lambda^iE^\vee$, so its alternating ambient class is precisely $\varepsilon(E)$. This calculation fixes the source convention but supplies no converse splitting theorem. [F4, step 1.1] ∎
