### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and compatible fixed universe size bounds for the small sites and derived categories used below. For every qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, $j\geq0$ and $n\geq1$ invertible in $k$, the actual comparison map gives a natural equivalence
$$\tau^{\leq j}(\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)/n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\leq j}R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_n^{\otimes j})$$
and natural isomorphisms $H^{a,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z/n)\to H^a_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_n^{\otimes j})$ for all $a\leq j$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the displayed construction or conclusion with its actual maps.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice and fixed size bounds are inherited when applying the prime-field helper in steps 1.1 and 2.1, specifically its K-injective derived-evaluation identification. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [lem-author-e71ff76fe904-comparison-composite](item-lem-author-e71ff76fe904-comparison-composite) supplies the actual source comparison and its objectwise cofiber bound.

[F2] [lem-author-e71ff76fe904-prime-field-coefficients](item-lem-author-e71ff76fe904-prime-field-coefficients) identifies the underlying prime-field object and the intrinsic étale target under [A1]; [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) fixes its motivic source and finite coefficients.

### Proof
1.1 Apply the source comparison of [F1] at the underlying prime-field object given by [F2]. Precomposition evaluates the same actual map and its same cofiber. Its triangle $A\xrightarrow{f}B\to C$ has $H^a(C)=0$ for $a\leq j$. For $a\leq j$, both $H^{a-1}(C)$ and $H^a(C)$ are zero, so the long exact sequence shows $H^a(f)$ is an isomorphism. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Standard cohomological truncation preserves these cohomology groups in degrees at most $j$ and makes all larger ones zero. Hence $\tau^{\leq j}f$ is a quasi-isomorphism and therefore an equivalence in $D(\mathbb Z)$. The coefficient and derived-evaluation identifications of [F2] identify its terms with the displayed ones. Applying cohomology gives the asserted degree-$a$ isomorphisms by the completed motivic definition. All steps use functors or the natural source triangle, so commute with pullback in $X$. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Coherent dual extension supplies global Swan controlling sections

[Open item](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-dual-global-controls) · level 13

### Statement
Assume AC. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an integral normal affine threefold over an algebraically closed field, let $S$ be the finite smooth zero set of the preceding point functional, let $U=X\setminus S$, and let $Q$ be its coherent kernel on $X$. Put $E=(Q|_U)^\vee$. For any nonempty open $W\subset U$ there is a finite indexed family of global sections of $E$ which generates $E$ on $U$, spans first jets at every smooth closed point of $U$, and contains Swan's controlling family on each member of a finite smooth principal cover of $W$ when $W$ is smooth. The parameters are an affine space $T=\mathbb A^N_k$; repetitions or linear relations in the indexed family are allowed.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The stated $X,S,U,Q,W$. A controlling family in a free rank-two chart consists of a frame and all its products by affine embedding coordinates, as used in Swan Theorem1.4's proof.

**Goal:** Supply global functionals on the actual quasi-affine $U$, including sufficient local families without extending a vector bundle across $S$.

[F1] [prop-swan-bertini-point-section](item-prop-swan-bertini-point-section) gives coherent $Q$ on $X$ and rank-two $Q|_U$. [lem-affine-coherent-global-generation](item-lem-affine-coherent-global-generation) gives finite generators of every coherent sheaf on $X$ and their restrictions. [lem-surjection-kernel-bundle](item-lem-surjection-kernel-bundle) gives local splitting where needed.

[F2] Noetherianity, finite principal covers and rational closed points are used with [thm-author-fc2380accb47-finite-type-geometric-input](item-thm-author-fc2380accb47-finite-type-geometric-input), [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice).

### Proof
1.1 The sheaf $F=\mathcal Hom_X(Q,\mathcal O_X)$ is coherent: on an affine chart it is a submodule of a finite free module over the Noetherian ring, from a finite presentation of $Q$. Localization of that presentation identifies $F|_U$ with $E$. By [F1] choose finite sections $\psi_j$ of $F$ generating it; they generate $E$ on $U$. No local freeness of $F$ at $S$ is asserted. Choose algebra generators $f_l$ of $A$. Include all $\psi_j$ and $f_l\psi_j$ in the indexed family. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 At a smooth closed point $x$, the $f_l-f_l(x)$ span $\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$, and the $\psi_j(x)$ span $E(x)$. Values can first be prescribed with linear combinations of $\psi_j$; the combinations $(f_l-f_l(x))\psi_j$ then change arbitrary derivatives without changing the value. Thus the family spans the eight-dimensional first-jet space $E_x/\mathfrak m_x^2E_x$. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 If $W$ is smooth, choose finitely many principal opens $D(g_i)\subset W$ on each of which two of the $\psi_j$ form a frame. Such opens cover because these values generate, and $W$ is quasi-compact. On $D(g_i)$ use the frame $g_i\psi_a,g_i\psi_b$ and the algebra generators $f_l,1/g_i$ of $A_{g_i}$. Its controlling family consists of $g_i\psi_a,g_i\psi_b$, their $f_l$-multiples, and $\psi_a,\psi_b$. All are restrictions of global sections on $U$. Add these finitely many sections for every chart to the family in step 1.1. This proves all assertions, including that the controlling sections genuinely come from global functionals on $Q|_U$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct] ∎


## The actual cdh-localization unit is an equivalence

[Open item](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-locality-unit) · level 13


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the derived-sections and general-localization suppliers. Write $L^{h,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}=Ri\,a$ for the hypercomplete reflector denoted $L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}$ by the general-localization supplier, and $L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}$ for ordinary source sheafification. For a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$, the canonical unit $E_\Lambda\to L^{h,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}E_\Lambda$ is an equivalence on the exact qcqs prime-field cdh site. Its evaluation gives natural equivalences
$$R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\Lambda)\simeq(L^{h,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}E_\Lambda)(X).$$
This is derived locality with respect to all sheafified-cohomology equivalences, and in particular implies ordinary locality. Thus the ordinary source unit $E_\Lambda\to L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}E_\Lambda$ is also an equivalence.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Choice and the stated bounds are inherited from the K-injective localization and derived-evaluation constructions. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)
**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the stated exact map or descent conclusion.

[F1] [lem-author-7113c087ecba-general-localization](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-general-localization) and [lem-author-7113c087ecba-cdh-hyperdescent](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-cdh-hyperdescent).

### Proof
1.1 The preceding hyperdescent lemma verifies every hypercover required by the linear criterion in the general-localization lemma. That criterion identifies $E_\Lambda$ as a local object of $Ri\,a$. An object in the essential image of a reflective localization has invertible unit, by full faithfulness of its right adjoint. Therefore the hypercomplete unit is an equivalence. Hypercover descent includes covering-family/Čech descent, so $E_\Lambda$ is also an ordinary sheaf and its ordinary localization unit is an equivalence by the same reflective universal property. [F1, A1]

2.1 Evaluate this actual natural unit at $X$ and use the chosen derived-evaluation model. Evaluation preserves equivalences, so the displayed equivalence follows and is compatible with every pullback. In particular it is valid at the article’s affine threefold, without any change to the chosen big site. [F1, step 1.1] ∎


## Perfect-field cancellation removes exactly d coefficient twists

[Open item](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-cancel-twists) · level 13


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the supplied classical derived-category model. Let $k$ be perfect, let $A$ be an object of $DM^{\mathrm{eff},-}_{\mathrm{Nis}}(k,\mathbb Z)$, and let $d\geq0$, $j\geq d$ and $i\in\mathbb Z$. The canonical Tate coefficient convention and repeated cancellation give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A(d)[2d],\mathbb Z(j)[i])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathbb Z(j-d)[i-2d]).$$
For $A=M(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ with $L/k$ finite separable, the right side is $H^{i-2d,j-d}_{\mathrm{mot}}(L,\mathbb Z)$ under the actual smooth/classical comparison. This argument supplies no effective negative-weight coefficient when $j<d$; that range is computed by the preceding cycle lemma.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The effective category, perfect field and exact integer range just stated, together with the ambient Choice and site/universe assumptions.

**Goal:** Prove the previously missing coefficient-twist comparison with its correct bounds.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice and the fixed small-site/universe bounds are inherited from the source contract of the classical derived-category input in [F2]. They are used for its coefficient models and representability, including the field-group identification in step 2.1. The smooth-comparison use in [F3] is only its complex comparison, not its Choice-qualified filtered-spectrum assertion. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [thm-author-59b1a831fe59-perfect-cancellation](item-thm-author-59b1a831fe59-perfect-cancellation) imports Voevodsky's perfect-field full faithfulness of tensoring by the Tate motive.

[F2] [thm-author-59b1a831fe59-classical-derived-input](item-thm-author-59b1a831fe59-classical-derived-input) fixes the actual Tate convention $\mathbb Z(r)(d)\cong\mathbb Z(r+d)$ for $r,d\geq0$, and classical representability on smooth schemes. [lem-author-9415fc97ee80-purity-shift-index](item-lem-author-9415fc97ee80-purity-shift-index) supplies the source-shift sign.

[F3] The smooth comparison identifies the classical motivic complex with the EM complex on a smooth finite-type scheme over a field in nonnegative weight. [thm-author-91088613574d-smooth-comparison-input](item-thm-author-91088613574d-smooth-comparison-input)

### Proof
1.1 Put $r=j-d\geq0$. Apply [F1] repeatedly $d$ times to $A$ and $\mathbb Z(r)[i-2d]$. At each step both objects remain effective and the coefficient twist remains nonnegative, so every application has its stated hypotheses. This gives the inverse of the canonical bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathbb Z(r)[i-2d])\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(A(d),\mathbb Z(r)(d)[i-2d]).$ Use [F2] to identify the last coefficient with $\mathbb Z(j)$. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 Shifting the source by $[2d]$ subtracts $2d$ from the target cohomological shift, by [F2]. This gives exactly the displayed formula. For $A=M(\operatorname{Spec}L)$, representability identifies its right side with the classical weight-$r$ field group; $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is smooth separated finite type over the perfect field $k$ because $L/k$ is finite separable, and $r=j-d\geq0$. Thus [F3] identifies that classical group with the specified EM field group under its exact hypotheses. If $j<d$, step 1.1 would require $r<0$ and is not invoked. Thus there is no concealed cancellation into a negative effective coefficient. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## Weight zero is the locally constant rank function

[Open item](item-lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-zero-projection-rank) · level 13


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be any field, and $X$ a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme. Under the canonical weight-zero comparison, the actual EM map $\pi_0q_0:K_0(X)\to H^0(X,\mathbb Z(0)_{\mathrm{mot}})$ is the locally constant rank function, component by component. Consequently $\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^1K(X)=\ker(\operatorname{rank}:K_0(X)\to H^0(X,\mathbb Z))$, and $\pi_1\operatorname{Fil}^1K(X)\to K_1(X)$ is an isomorphism. These are statements about stage groups, not an assumed equality of a stage with its image.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and fixed bounds discharge the selected low-weight tower in [F1] and the affine perfect-$K$ comparison and filtration in [F2], used in steps 1.1–2.1. The pointwise unital rank test and the long exact sequence introduce no further choice.

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, the fixed compatible bounds, smooth finite-type $X/k$, all fields in their prime-field category, and the actual unital multiplicative EM tower.

**Goal:** Normalize $q_0$ and identify its first-stage homotopy groups.

[F1] [thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-em-map-normalizations](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-em-map-normalizations) supplies the canonical $\operatorname{gr}^0$ comparison and the unital $q_0$; its target on a smooth scheme is the ordinary locally constant integer sheaf in degree zero. Negative cohomology of this sheaf vanishes.

[F2] [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge) identifies degree-zero perfect K-theory with finite-projective classes on affines, so $K_0$ of a field is $\mathbb Z$ with generator its unit line. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) supplies the actual exact fiber sequence $\operatorname{Fil}^1K\to K\to\operatorname{gr}^0K$.

### Proof
1.1 On a field extension $L$ of the prime field, $K_0(L)=\mathbb Z$ generated by $[L]$. The graded-zero comparison is unital, so the unital homomorphism $\pi_0q_0:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ is identity. For $x\in X$, naturality of $q_0$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ therefore evaluates $q_0(\alpha)$ as the rank of $\alpha$ at $x$. On a smooth $X$, the weight-zero target is the locally constant integer function sheaf, so its sections are determined by these values at points. Thus $q_0$ equals the full rank function, including on disconnected $X$. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 In the fiber sequence of [F2], $\pi_i\operatorname{gr}^0K=H^{-i}(X,\mathbb Z)=0$ for $i>0$ by [F1]. Its long exact sequence therefore identifies $\pi_1\operatorname{Fil}^1K$ with $K_1$, and identifies $\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^1K$ injectively with the kernel of $\pi_0q_0$. Apply step 1.1 to obtain precisely the two asserted identifications. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Perfect K theory localization and open excision

[Open item](item-prop-perfect-k-localization-input) · level 14

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix the suitable universes of the supplied derived and K-theory constructions. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and $U\subseteq X$ a quasi-compact open with closed complement $T$. For the specified nonconnective perfect-complex K-theory there is a natural fiber sequence
$$K_T(X)\longrightarrow K(X)\longrightarrow K(U).$$
For every cover $X=U\cup V$ by quasi-compact opens, the restriction square is homotopy cartesian, equivalently
$$K(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}K(U)\times_{K(U\cap V)}K(V).$$
Thus K-theory has open-cover Mayer–Vietoris (and the corresponding finite quasi-compact-open covering form by iteration). If $T$ is closed with quasi-compact complement and $T\subseteq W\subseteq X$ with $W$ quasi-compact open, restriction gives the natural support excision equivalence $K_T(X)\simeq K_T(W)$, compatible with the support-to-global and restriction maps. All these assertions use the nonconnective spectra and their groups in every integer degree, without a regularity, field or resolution-property assumption.

### Statement references
[def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface)

[lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-enhanced-localization](item-lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-enhanced-localization)

[lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-supported-open-equivalence](item-lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-supported-open-equivalence)

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Choice and the universe bounds are used to invoke the enhanced perfect-category and K-theory suppliers. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

**Given:** The schemes, opens and closed supports in the Statement, with the supplied essentially small sheaf-derived perfect categories and nonconnective functor.

**Goal:** Deduce localization, Mayer–Vietoris and open excision in exactly that model.

[F1] [lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-enhanced-localization](item-lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-enhanced-localization) proves the actual enhanced quotient exactness and resulting K fiber sequence, using [lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-kernel](item-lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-kernel), [lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-quotient-full-faithfulness](item-lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-quotient-full-faithfulness) and [lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-retract-density](item-lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-retract-density).

[F2] [lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-supported-open-equivalence](item-lem-author-50b5133c29cc-klocal-supported-open-equivalence) gives the actual support restriction equivalence and compatibility with global restriction.

[F3] [def-stable-spectra-interface](item-def-stable-spectra-interface) supplies coherent pullbacks and stable fiber/cofiber sequences. [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) identifies the K functor and all integer groups.

### Proof
1.1 The localization sequence is [F1] applied to $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and its full kernel $\mathrm{Perf}_T(X)$. This identifies the category-defined $K_T(X)$ with the actual fiber, without assuming that identification in its definition or comparing with a different K-theory model. [F1, F3]

2.1 For a two-open cover $X=U\cup V$, quasi-separatedness makes $U\cap V$ quasi-compact, so [F1] applies both to $U\subseteq X$ and $U\cap V\subseteq V$. Put $T=X\setminus U$, a closed subset of $X$ contained in $V$. Their fiber terms are $K_T(X)$ and $K_T(V)$, and [F2] identifies the induced map between these fibers with an equivalence. The coherent restriction square therefore has equivalent horizontal fibers. To check it is cartesian, put $P=K(U)\times_{K(U\cap V)}K(V)$. The induced map $K(X)\to P$ lies over $K(U)$; its fiber map over that base is exactly $K_T(X)\to K_T(V)$ because pullbacks commute. Thus its map on fibers is an equivalence and its map on bases is the identity. The long exact sequences of spectrum homotopy groups give isomorphisms $\pi_iK(X)\to\pi_iP$ for all integers $i$, hence an equivalence of spectra. This proves Mayer–Vietoris. Repeated binary covering decompositions give the finite covering form. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 For the stated support excision take $W$ in [F2]. Its support equivalence is induced by actual restriction and is compatible with inclusions. Because $X\setminus T$ is quasi-compact, so is $W\setminus T=W\cap(X\setminus T)$ by quasi-separatedness; hence both support terms are also the fibers in step 1.1 with their natural maps. This proves the entire interface, with every original qcqs, closed-support and quasi-compact-open condition retained. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Gysin purity for a smooth closed pair

[Open item](item-prop-smooth-pair-gysin-input) · level 14


### Statement
Let $k$ be a perfect field and let $X$ be in $\mathrm{Sm}/k$, meaning a smooth separated scheme of finite type over $k$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth closed subscheme of pure codimension $c\geq0$, and put $U=X\setminus Z$. In the classical category $DM^{\mathrm{eff},-}_{\mathrm{Nis}}(k,\mathbb Z)$ there is the distinguished Gysin triangle
$$M(U)\longrightarrow M(X)\xrightarrow{\gamma}M(Z)(c)[2c]\longrightarrow M(U)[1].$$
Here $M(W)$ is the source motive of $W$, represented by $\mathbb Z_{\mathrm{tr}}(W)$ and isomorphic in this category to $C_*\mathbb Z_{\mathrm{tr}}(W)$; $(c)$ is the Tate twist by tensoring with $\mathbb Z(c)$, and $[2c]$ is cohomological translation. The first arrow is induced by the open immersion, and $\gamma$ is the source's Gysin map.

Equivalently one may take the relative motive of the pair, a cofiber of $M(U)\to M(X)$, to be $M(Z)(c)[2c]$. Any separately chosen cone triangle for that first arrow admits a compatible isomorphism of its third object with this one; a unique or functorial choice of that cone is not asserted from triangulated axioms alone.

This is a classical smooth-pair input, not a purity statement for a singular curve. A separately supplied compatible comparison of theories on both $X$ and $U$ suffices, by the transport construction, to identify the article's support complex; a direct compatible comparison of support objects is another possible input. Computing its cohomological twist shift further requires the relevant coefficient representability and twist comparison in the weights used. Under precisely those premises the formal shift is $(a,j)\mapsto(a-2c,j-c)$, not $(a+2c,j-c)$. No negative-weight convention or comparison outside its given scope is silently introduced.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The perfect field, the two smooth schemes, closed immersion and pure codimension in the Statement; the ambient workflow permits AC. Additional application premises are as explicitly stated.

**Goal:** Record the exact imported triangle and give its rigorous formal interpretation without claiming a local proof of Gysin purity.

[F1] MVW Theorem 15.15 supplies the displayed triangle for precisely this smooth pair. The source's category and $M(W)\cong C_*\mathbb Z_{\mathrm{tr}}(W)$ notation are fixed in Definition 14.1 and Lemma 14.4. These are explicit external inputs in the source records.

[F2] A relative cone has the quotient model only when the chosen complex map is termwise monomorphic; it is a cofiber construction, without that extra condition in general. [lem-author-9415fc97ee80-relative-cone-quotient-model](item-lem-author-9415fc97ee80-relative-cone-quotient-model)

[F3] Contravariant Hom reverses this triangle to the cohomological restriction long exact sequence; an enhanced derived Hom identifies the relative object with the fiber of restriction only when that enhancement is supplied. [lem-author-9415fc97ee80-contravariant-relative-hom](item-lem-author-9415fc97ee80-contravariant-relative-hom)

[F4] A supplied twist comparison gives the cohomological shift $a-2c$ and weight $j-c$ with its exact weight bounds. [lem-author-9415fc97ee80-purity-shift-index](item-lem-author-9415fc97ee80-purity-shift-index)

[F5] Compatible isomorphisms on the two initial objects transport cone triangles, and compatible derived comparisons on $X,U$ transport the support fiber. [lem-author-9415fc97ee80-compatible-relative-transport](item-lem-author-9415fc97ee80-compatible-relative-transport), [def-supported-complex-indexing](item-def-supported-complex-indexing)

[F6] Identity, zero and split-pair maps have the formal relative/support special cases already computed, independently of Gysin purity. [lem-author-9415fc97ee80-relative-empty-split-cases](item-lem-author-9415fc97ee80-relative-empty-split-cases)

### External input
Import the whole smooth-pair Gysin theorem in [F1]. The five local prerequisites establish setup, covariance, indexing, transport and boundary cases. They do not reconstruct the normal-bundle proof, the affine-space Gysin normalization, or Exercise 15.14. The source's displayed proof invokes those established ingredients; this authoring assistance does not claim to have filled their foundational proofs.

### Justification of the formal reformulation

1.1 Apply the imported [F1] to the stated perfect-field smooth pair. Its third term, with its map from $M(X)$ and connecting map, is a specified cofiber in the triangulated sense. If another relative cone was chosen for the same first arrow, [F5] applied with identities on $M(U)$ and $M(X)$ gives a compatible isomorphism to this third term. This establishes the relative-motive reformulation without asserting uniqueness of that isomorphism. [F1, F5, given]

2.1 In a complex model, [F2] explains when the source's quotient notation for relative motives is valid. Apply [F3] to the distinguished triangle of step 1.1 to obtain its contravariant Hom long exact sequence. If the application additionally supplies the enhanced mapping-object premise, its support complex is the homotopy fiber of restriction. If a second theory has a compatible derived comparison on both $X$ and $U$, [F5] transports that fiber to the second theory's support fiber. These are applications of explicit premises, not automatic identifications with the article's motivic complex. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 If coefficient representability and the twist identification of [F4] are also supplied, apply it with $A=M(Z)$. The relative Hom group in degree $a$ becomes the coefficient group on $Z$ in degree $a-2c$ and weight $j-c$. Only the supplied weight range is used. For empty or split support cases satisfying the independent functor premises of [F6], its direct calculations give the indicated formal boundary cases without invoking an extension of purity. [F4, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

### Scope and application limit
Both smoothness hypotheses matter. In particular a possibly singular integral curve inside a smooth threefold is not covered by this input merely because its embedding has pure codimension. Nor does the source's Sm/k statement automatically extend to every qcqs scheme, a nonseparated smooth scheme, or an arbitrary smooth locus without checking the actual finite-type pair to which it is applied. The article's smooth motivic comparison and any twist/cancellation comparison retain their own authoring and scope obligations; this target supplies neither by renaming the classical cohomology theory.


## Dévissage of K zero with regular ambient support

[Open item](item-prop-supported-k-zero-devissage) · level 14


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. Let $U$ be a regular Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme and $i:T\hookrightarrow U$ any closed subscheme with defining ideal $\mathcal I$. Let $K_0^{|T|}(U)=\pi_0K_{|T|}(U)$ for the specified nonconnective K-theory of the current supported perfect category. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$K_0^{|T|}(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_0(T),$$
where $G_0(T)$ is the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves on $T$ with short exact relations. For a supported perfect object $E$ it is the coherent-cohomology Euler class followed by ideal-power dévissage, explicitly
$$[E]\longmapsto\sum_n(-1)^n\sum_{r\geq0}[\mathcal I^rH^n(E)/\mathcal I^{r+1}H^n(E)].$$
Each quotient is regarded as a coherent $\mathcal O_T$-module; both sums are finite after deleting zero terms, and the resulting class is independent of the chosen annihilating powers. The inverse sends $[F]$ to the class of the perfect $U$-object $i_*F[0]$.

Under this isomorphism the support-to-global map $K_0^{|T|}(U)\to K_0(U)$ is coherent pushforward $G_0(T)\xrightarrow{i_*}G_0(U)$ followed by the regular ambient perfect comparison $G_0(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_0(U)$, sending $[M]$ to $[M[0]]$. No regularity of $T$, global vector-bundle resolution or resolution-property assumption is imposed. No analogous identification for singular ambient $U$ is asserted.

### Statement references
[def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface)

[lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-postnikov](item-lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-postnikov)

[lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-devissage-naturality](item-lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-devissage-naturality)

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] The Choice assumption in Given and the stated universes are used through the essentially small perfect-category presentations and the specified nonconnective K-theory model. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)
**Given:** $U,T,i,\mathcal I$ as in the Statement, AC and fixed suitable universes. The supported category is the supplied full sheaf-derived $\mathrm{Perf}_{|T|}(U)$, not complexes internally constructed in a coherent abelian category.

**Goal:** Prove the stated comparison and support-to-global compatibility in the current nonconnective model.

[F1] [lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-heart](item-lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-heart), [lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-euler](item-lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-euler) and [lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-postnikov](item-lem-author-7ef3227685d9-supported-k0-postnikov) give the actual bounded supported t-structure, additive coherent Euler map and Postnikov inverse, together with the general spectral $\pi_0$ premise [thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input](item-thm-author-3a003d7b5208-nonconnective-k-zero-input).

### Proof
1.1 By [F1], the degree-zero group of the current nonconnective functor identifies with $G_0(\mathcal A_T)$ by the coherent-cohomology Euler map. By [F2], closed coherent pushforward gives $G_0(T)\simeq G_0(\mathcal A_T)$. Compose the former map with the inverse of the latter. This is an isomorphism, and its displayed formula is exactly the Euler sum followed by the ideal-power quotient sum. Finiteness and independence follow from [F1]–[F2]. [F1, F2, F3, A1]

2.1 The two inverse constructions take $[F]$ first to $[i_*F]$ and then to the class of $i_*F[0]$ by [F1]–[F2]. This object is perfect by the imported local regular-perfect theorem applied to its coherent degree-zero cohomology. Thus the inverse has the asserted actual-object interpretation without any global locally free resolution. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The Euler/Postnikov comparisons commute with supported-to-global inclusion by [F1]. Under abelian dévissage the corresponding map is precisely coherent pushforward by [F2]. Their commutative squares compose to the stated support-to-global formula, using the same ambient comparison with $T=U$. This establishes the full proposition in the specified nonconnective model. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

## Prime-to-characteristic étale comparison

$$\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)/n\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_n^{\otimes j}),$$
whose cofiber has cohomology only in degrees $>j$. In particular it induces a natural equivalence
$$\tau^{\leq j}(\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)/n)\simeq\tau^{\leq j}R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_n^{\otimes j})$$
and isomorphisms $H^{a,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z/n)\cong H^a_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_n^{\otimes j})$ for $a\leq j$. The quotient is derived, the tensor power uses the specified small étale coefficient sheaf, and the natural map is the composite through source cdh-local motivic cohomology fixed in the prerequisites.

## Integer cdh sections on seminormal schemes

[Open item](item-lem-cdh-integer-sections) · level 14


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $X$ a separated seminormal scheme of finite type over $k$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of abelian groups $H^0_{\mathrm{cdh}}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{\pi_0(X)}$. In particular, if $X$ is nonempty and connected, this group is canonically $\mathbb Z$.

Here $\pi_0(X)$ is the set of connected components of the underlying topological space: a connected component is a maximal nonempty connected subset, and connected means that the subset has no partition into two nonempty relatively open subsets. In particular, $\pi_0(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. The group $\mathbb Z^{\pi_0(X)}$ consists of all functions from that set to $\mathbb Z$, with pointwise addition; for the empty set it is the zero group. The cdh site used here is the big site of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with the cdh topology. The constant integer cdh sheaf is the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value $\mathbb Z$, and $H^0_{\mathrm{cdh}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is its group of sections over $X$. Seminormality means that each point has an affine neighbourhood whose coordinate ring $R$ has the property that each pair $x,y\in R$ satisfying $x^3=y^2$ has a unique $a\in R$ with $a^2=x$ and $a^3=y$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, an algebraically closed field $k$, and a separated seminormal finite-type $k$-scheme $X$.

**Goal:** Construct the stated canonical group isomorphism, including the empty-scheme case.

[F1] For every finite set $A$, the constant cdh sheaf $\underline A$ has a natural bijection $\underline A(X)\cong\operatorname{Map}(\pi_0(X),A)$ under these hypotheses and the Axiom of Choice. This bijection is natural in maps of finite sets. [lem-finite-constant-cdh-sections](item-lem-finite-constant-cdh-sections)

[F2] Every section of the constant integer cdh sheaf over $X$ factors through $\underline A(X)$ for some finite subset $A\subseteq\mathbb Z$. [prop-cdh-cover-refinement](item-prop-cdh-cover-refinement)

[F3] Sheafification of a set-valued presheaf is the twofold plus construction: a plus section is represented by a matching family on a covering sieve, and two families represent the same section when they agree on a common covering subsieve. Restriction uses pullback of sieves. The sheafification is functorial and left adjoint to inclusion of sheaves. [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification)

[F4] A finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian, and under the Axiom of Choice its connected components are finite in number and clopen. In particular every integer-valued function on $\pi_0(X)$ has finite image. [lem-clopen-finite-constant-maps](item-lem-clopen-finite-constant-maps) [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Pass from finite constant sets to integers, using finite local values and the natural finite-set identifications.

1.1 A pointwise injective map of presheaves $F\to G$ induces a pointwise injective map $F^+\to G^+$. Indeed, if two matching families from $F$ have equal images in $G^+(T)$, their images agree on some common covering subsieve by [F3]. Pointwise injectivity makes the original families agree there, so they represent the same element of $F^+(T)$. Applying the same argument again shows that sheafification preserves such injections. In particular, for every inclusion of sets $A\subseteq B$, the induced map $\underline A\to\underline B$ is pointwise injective. [F3, construct]

2.1 For finite $A\subseteq\mathbb Z$, [F1] identifies $\underline A(X)$ with functions $\pi_0(X)\to A$. By naturality, whenever $A\subseteq B$ are finite subsets of $\mathbb Z$, the map between these section sets corresponds to inclusion of the corresponding function sets. By step 1.1, the map from each $\underline A(X)$ into $\underline{\mathbb Z}(X)$ is injective. Moreover, the images for two finite subsets $A,B$ are both contained in the image for the finite union $A\cup B$. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F2], the images in step 2.1 cover $\underline{\mathbb Z}(X)$. They therefore give a well-defined bijection from $\underline{\mathbb Z}(X)$ to the set of finite-image functions $\pi_0(X)\to\mathbb Z$: if a section is represented using two finite subsets, injectivity into the integer sheaf and passage to their union show that the two representations coincide there, and [F1] then gives the same function. Conversely every finite-image function is obtained from [F1] using its finite image as $A$. This also handles an empty image and an empty scheme. [F1, F2, step 2.1]

4.1 The bijection respects addition. If sections are represented by finite-value functions with values in $A$ and $B$, their sum is represented by the induced map of sheaves $\underline A\times\underline B\to\underline C$, where $C=\{a+b:a\in A,b\in B\}$, followed by $\underline C\to\underline{\mathbb Z}$. This follows locally from the addition map of constant presheaves and the sheaf axiom; its value on each component is the sum of the two values. Thus the bijection is a group isomorphism onto the finite-image functions. [F1, F3, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 By [F4], $\pi_0(X)$ is finite, so every function on it has finite image. Step 4.1 is consequently the claimed isomorphism to $\mathbb Z^{\pi_0(X)}$. The construction uses natural sheaf maps and the natural bijections in [F1], so it is canonical. If $X$ is nonempty and connected, it has exactly one connected component and the target is $\mathbb Z$; if $X$ is empty, the target is the zero group. [F4, step 4.1] ∎


## Étale derived cdh locality on the actual qcqs site

[Open item](item-prop-etale-cdh-descent) · level 14


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the supplied derived-localization constructions. On the entire qcqs prime-field cdh site specified in the qcqs-site supplier, the functor $E(X)=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)$, for any prime $p$, is cdh-local in the hypercomplete derived-sheaf sense. Write $L^{h,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}=Ri\,a$ for the general-localization supplier’s reflector, and $L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}$ for ordinary source sheafification. Thus $E\xrightarrow{\sim}L^{h,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}E$ is its hypercomplete unit equivalence. It is also an ordinary cdh sheaf, so its ordinary source unit $E\to L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}E$ is an equivalence. It satisfies Nisnevich descent and sends every source abstract blowup square to a cartesian square. More generally these statements hold for constant coefficients in any finite commutative ring. In particular they apply to the article’s characteristic-zero argument. The claim does not depend on replacing the qcqs site by its separated finite-type subcategory.

### Statement references

[lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site)

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** Choice, the fixed universe and site-size bounds, the qcqs prime-field site, and a finite commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ as in the statement.

**Goal:** Prove hypercomplete and ordinary cdh locality, Nisnevich descent, and descent for every specified abstract blowup square of the actual complex $E_\Lambda(X)=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\underline\Lambda_X)$.

[A1] Choice and the fixed bounds are inherited from the selected K-injective resolution and derived inclusion/evaluation model used in steps 1.1 and 4.1. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] The entire qcqs prime-field site, including its finitely presented closed centers and finitely presented proper maps, is fixed by [lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site).

[F2] The hypercomplete reflector on this site is $Ri\,a$, and hypercover-descent complexes are its local objects. This is the arbitrary-small-site linear criterion, with cochain reindexing and product totalization, used by [lem-author-7113c087ecba-general-localization](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-general-localization).

[F3] Every specified cdh generator is an arc cover, including on nonnoetherian qcqs schemes. [lem-author-7113c087ecba-generators-arc](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-generators-arc)

[F4] Derived endomorphisms of the constant unit in the finite-coefficient constructible category give the actual complex $E_\Lambda$, with its pullbacks, and satisfy arc hyperdescent. The imported theorem is explicitly hypercomplete and requires only a finite coefficient ring. [lem-author-7113c087ecba-endomorphism-hyperdescent](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-endomorphism-hyperdescent)

[F5] The actual complex satisfies cdh hyperdescent and Nisnevich descent on this site, sends each specified abstract blowup square to a cartesian square, and has $E_\Lambda(\varnothing)=0$. The empty value is included when applying the source square criterion. [lem-author-7113c087ecba-cdh-hyperdescent](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-cdh-hyperdescent)

[F6] For this same reflector and actual complex, the hypercomplete unit is an equivalence; hyperdescent also gives ordinary locality and the ordinary unit equivalence. [lem-author-7113c087ecba-locality-unit](item-lem-author-7113c087ecba-locality-unit)

### Proof
1.1 Fix $\Lambda$ and the site of [F1]. Apply [F2] under [A1] to use the specified hypercomplete derived-localization model on that entire site. Its local objects are characterized by descent for all hypercovers, rather than merely for ordinary ideal blowup squares. Evaluation on formal coproducts of representables is interpreted by products in this criterion. [given, F1, F2, A1]

2.1 By [F3], every matching map of a cdh hypercover is also locally surjective for the finer arc topology. Apply [F4]: the constant coefficient unit is bounded constructible, its derived pullback is the constant unit, and mapping objects between that unit and all its shifts preserve the descent limit. Thus the comparison concerns the entire derived complex with its actual pullbacks. No invertibility hypothesis on the order of $\Lambda$ is required. [F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply [F5] on this exact site to obtain cdh hyperdescent, Nisnevich descent and cartesian values on every specified abstract blowup square. Its zero value on the empty scheme supplies the empty-cover condition in the source square criterion. Both finite-presentation conventions are retained. [F1, F5, step 2.1]

4.1 The hyperdescent just established meets [F2], so [F6] gives the equivalence of the actual unit $E_\Lambda\to L^{h,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}E_\Lambda$. Hyperdescent includes ordinary covering-family descent; [F6] therefore also gives $E_\Lambda\to L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}E_\Lambda$ as an equivalence. Set $\Lambda=\mathbb Z/p$ for any prime $p$ to recover the article input, including characteristic zero. All arguments took place on the full qcqs site, so the other finite rings and every original scope assertion follow as well. [F2, F6, A1, step 3.1] ∎

## Images of support groups in global groups

[Open item](item-def-support-image-groups) · level 14


### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the support construction. Fix a field $k$, a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme $X$, and a closed subset $Y\subseteq X$ with its reduced induced closed-subscheme structure. Put $U=X\setminus Y$. Let $j\geq0$ and $i\in\mathbb Z$.

Use the support spectra and their support-to-global maps from the preceding support definition. In particular, $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_{i,Y}(X)$ is the image of $\pi_iF^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X/U)$ in $\pi_iK(X/U)$, and $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_i(X)$ is the image of $\pi_iF^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ in $K_i(X)=\pi_iK(X)$. An image is the subgroup consisting of the values of the indicated homomorphism. Define

$$F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_i(Y;X):=\operatorname{im}\bigl(F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_{i,Y}(X)\longrightarrow F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_i(X)\bigr),$$

where the arrow is induced by the support-to-global map on $K$-theory. For supported motivic cohomology $H^{a,j}_{\mathrm{mot},Y}(X,\mathbb Z)$ and global motivic cohomology $H^{a,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$, define

$$H^{a,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(Y;X):=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^{a,j}_{\mathrm{mot},Y}(X,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^{a,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\bigr)$$

for every integer $a$; in particular this includes the article's degree $a=2j-i$. The arrow is the support-to-global map. Finally, put

$$K_0(Y;X):=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_0K(X/U)\longrightarrow K_0(X)\bigr).$$

These are image subgroups of the respective global groups; the supported groups are their domains before the final image is taken. No injectivity of a support-to-global map is part of the definition.

### Definition references
[def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support)

[def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration)

[def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology)

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The field, scheme, closed subset, complement, choice and size conventions, and indices in the definition.

**Goal:** Show that each displayed map has the stated target and that each image is a well-defined subgroup.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice, [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), discharges the inherited Choice hypotheses of the support and global filtration constructions invoked in [F1] and [F2]. The subgroup-image argument below requires no additional choice principle.

[F1] [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support) supplies the filtered and unfiltered support spectra as fibers, their compatible maps to the corresponding global spectra, and the supported motivic cohomology groups and support-to-global homomorphisms. Its construction also specifies the extension used when $U$ is not quasi-compact.

[F2] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) defines $K_i(X)=\pi_iK(X)$ and $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_i(X)$ as the image of the global stage-to-$K$ homomorphism. The stage-to-$K$ maps are compatible with restriction.

[F3] [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) defines the global group $H^{a,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. The support definition in [F1] identifies its support-to-global target with this group, using the stated cohomological indexing convention.

### Justification
1.1 The compatible support and global stage-to-$K$ maps form a commutative square after applying $\pi_i$. If an element of $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_{i,Y}(X)$ is represented by an element of $\pi_iF^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X/U)$, its image in $K_i(X)$ is represented by the image of that element in $\pi_iF^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$. It therefore belongs to $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_i(X)$. The map is the restriction of the homomorphism on unfiltered $K$-theory, so it is independent of the chosen representative. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 The image of a group homomorphism is a subgroup: zero is the image of zero, and the difference of two image elements is the image of the difference of their preimages. Apply this to the homomorphism in step 1.1 and to the support-to-global homomorphisms for motivic cohomology and unfiltered $K$-theory. The resulting subgroups are exactly the three displayed definitions. The construction uses no injectivity; it justifies the definitions and their stated targets. [F1, F3, step 1.1] ∎

### Indexing and scope
The supported cohomology supplier uses an explicit $2j$ shift to reconcile the article's displayed $\pi_i$ notation with the global cohomological convention. The image in degree $2j-i$ is taken using that supplier's support-to-global map. The construction does not identify $K(X/U)$ with the $K$-theory of a category of supported perfect complexes.


## Motivic Chern classes

[Open item](item-def-motivic-chern-classes) · level 14


### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the suitable universes used by the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme, and $E$ a vector bundle of constant rank $n\geq 0$ on $X$. A vector bundle means a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module. Write $H^{a,b}(X)$ for the supplied integral motivic cohomology $H^{a,b}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$, with its natural bigraded ring structure.

If $n>0$, let $\pi:\mathbb P_X(E)\to X$ be the projective bundle of rank-one quotients of $E$, let $\mathcal O(1)$ be its tautological quotient line bundle, and put $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))\in H^{2,1}(\mathbb P_X(E))$, using the supplied orientation on line bundles. Define the **motivic Chern classes** $c_i(E)\in H^{2i,i}(X)$ for $1\leq i\leq n$ as the unique coefficients satisfying
$$\xi^n+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(-1)^i\pi^*c_i(E)\,\xi^{n-i}=0.$$
Set $c_0(E)=1\in H^{0,0}(X)$ and $c_i(E)=0$ for $i>n$. For the rank-zero bundle use the same conventions $c_0(E)=1$ and $c_i(E)=0$ for $i>0$, without using a projective bundle. The **total Chern series** of an actual bundle is $c_t(E)=\sum_{i\geq0}c_i(E)t^i$, a polynomial with constant term one.

For every $i\geq0$ this construction defines a map $c_i:\mathrm{Vect}_n(X)\to H^{2i,i}(X)$, where $\mathrm{Vect}_n(X)$ is the set of isomorphism classes of rank-$n$ bundles. It is natural under pullback of $k$-schemes. These definitions apply to singular as well as smooth schemes. The article also uses total Chern classes of virtual bundle classes; their extension and its Whitney identity are supplied separately and are not part of this definition.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $k$, a qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, a constant-rank bundle $E$, the Axiom of Choice and the suitable universes of the supplied constructions.

**Goal:** Define the stated coefficients and justify their existence, uniqueness, invariance under bundle isomorphism and pullback naturality.

[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice, as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). This discharges the Choice hypotheses of the projective-bundle and coefficient-uniqueness suppliers [F1] and [F2] in steps 1.1–3.1, and of the bundle-class supplier [F3] in step 2.1.

[F1] The supplied motivic cohomology, extended by zero in negative weights, is an additively oriented bigraded theory on qcqs $k$-schemes. For a positive-rank bundle its quotient projective bundle has the projective-bundle isomorphism in every bidegree, with powers of the first Chern class of the tautological quotient line. Pullbacks preserve the unit and ring operations. [prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula](item-prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula)

[F2] In such a theory, for a rank-$n>0$ bundle the displayed monic relation has unique coefficients in the stated bidegrees, and those coefficients commute with pullback. The rank-zero convention is preserved by pullback. [lem-chern-relation-uniqueness](item-lem-chern-relation-uniqueness)

[F3] A vector bundle is finite locally free; $\mathrm{Vect}_n(X)$ is the set of isomorphism classes of rank-$n$ bundles. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

### Justification

1.1 The hypotheses of [F1] and [F2] hold for $X$ and $E$. When $n>0$, [F2] therefore supplies exactly one coefficient $c_i(E)$ in each indicated bidegree satisfying the displayed relation. The unit and zero classes used for $c_0$ and for indices above the rank exist in the bigraded ring; the separate rank-zero prescription is consequently defined without a projective-bundle assertion. These choices give a polynomial $c_t(E)$ with constant coefficient one. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 An isomorphism $E\cong E'$ induces an isomorphism of quotient projective bundles over $X$ carrying the tautological quotient line to the corresponding quotient line. By naturality of its first Chern class, the two defining relations correspond. Their coefficients agree by uniqueness in [F2]. The prescribed zero and unit coefficients also agree, so each $c_i$ is well-defined on the set of isomorphism classes in [F3]. The same conclusion holds in rank zero by its explicit convention. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 For a morphism $f:Y\to X$ of qcqs $k$-schemes, the pullback bundle has rank $n$. For $1\leq i\leq n$, [F2] gives $f^*c_i(E)=c_i(f^*E)$; for $i=0$ or $i>n$ this follows from preservation of the unit and zero. The rank-zero case follows from the same conventions. Thus the maps are natural, and no smoothness hypothesis has been used. This completes the justification. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Motivic splitting principle

[Open item](item-thm-motivic-splitting-principle) · level 14

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be the article's algebraically closed field, let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme, and let $V$ be a vector bundle on $X$. There is a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme $Y$ and a morphism $q:Y\to X$ with the following properties.

The finitely many nonempty rank strata $X_\alpha$ of $V$ are open and closed. The scheme $Y$ is the finite disjoint union of schemes $Y_\alpha$ over $X_\alpha$, and on each $Y_\alpha$ the bundle $q^*V$ has a finite filtration by locally direct-summand subbundles whose successive quotients are line bundles. The filtration has length equal to the rank on $X_\alpha$; at rank zero it is the zero filtration and $Y_\alpha=X_\alpha$ with the identity map.

For every $i\in\mathbb Z$ and $j\geq0$, pullback
$$q^*:H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,R)\longrightarrow H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(Y,R)$$
is injective for $R=\mathbb Z$ and for $R=\mathbb Z/n$, $n>0$. With the explicit convention $H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(-,R)=0$ for $j<0$, this also holds for all integer weights.

Write $L_{\alpha,s}$ for the line-quotient bundles on $Y_\alpha$ and $j_\alpha:Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y$ for the clopen inclusions. In the vector-bundle Grothendieck group,
$$[q^*V]=\sum_{\alpha,s}[j_{\alpha,*}L_{\alpha,s}],$$
where $j_{\alpha,*}L_{\alpha,s}$ is extension by zero: it is $L_{\alpha,s}$ on $Y_\alpha$ and zero on the other components. If $V$ has constant rank, $[q^*V]$ is a sum of global line-bundle classes on $Y$, with the empty sum in rank zero. In particular, equality of natural motivic Chern-class expressions of the same bidegree can be checked after pullback to this tower and hence on its rank components.

A vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module, and a line bundle is one of rank one. A rank stratum is the locus where the locally constant rank has a specified value. Quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means intersections of quasi-compact open subsets are quasi-compact. The vector-bundle Grothendieck group is generated by isomorphism classes of vector bundles subject to $[E]=[E']+[E'']$ for short exact sequences $0\to E'\to E\to E''\to0$. The motivic groups and functorial pullbacks in nonnegative weights are those of [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology).

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the field $k$, the qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, and the vector bundle $V$ as in the statement.

**Goal:** Construct the componentwise line-quotient tower and establish motivic detection and the stated class formulas.

[F1] For a finite family of finite locally free bundles on a qcqs scheme, [lem-flag-tower-line-quotients](item-lem-flag-tower-line-quotients) constructs a finite clopen rank partition and a qcqs componentwise flag tower with locally split line-quotient filtrations. Rank-zero towers are identities. Its construction assumes AC.

[F2] [lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection](item-lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection) proves that this componentwise tower detects the actual motivic cohomology of qcqs schemes over the stated field for every cohomological degree and nonnegative weight, integrally and with finite coefficients. It also proves the componentwise class formulas and their global clopen extensions by zero. It does not assert injectivity on the vector-bundle Grothendieck group.

[F3] [prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula](item-prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula) supplies the explicit zero extension in negative weights and the functorial motivic theory in all integer bidegrees. [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) supplies the nonnegative-weight groups and their functorial pullbacks.

[F4] AC is the choice assumption used by the flag construction. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Construct the flag tower separately on the finite clopen rank strata and apply motivic detection componentwise.

1.1 The rank of $V$ is locally constant because $V$ is locally free of finite rank. Its rank fibers are open, and each complement is the union of the other fibers, so each is also closed. They cover $X$; quasi-compactness gives only finitely many nonempty fibers. Apply [F1] to $V$ on each fiber and take the finite disjoint union of the resulting towers. This gives $q:Y\to X$ with $Y$ qcqs, the asserted locally split filtrations, and the identity tower and zero filtration on every rank-zero stratum. [given, F1, F4, construct]

2.1 By [F2], pullback along the tower of step 1.1 is injective on $H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(-,R)$ for every integer $i$, every $j\geq0$, and both specified kinds of coefficients. If $j<0$, the source and target are zero under the explicit convention in [F3], so pullback is injective there as well. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

2.2 On each component the short exact sequences associated with the filtration give the sum of the classes of its line quotients. By [F2], extension by zero along the clopen component inclusions yields the displayed equality in the global vector-bundle Grothendieck group. When the rank is constant, the tower and its filtration are global, so the summands are global line bundles; when the rank is zero the sum is empty. The supported extensions in the varying-rank formula need not themselves be global line bundles. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Let $u$ and $v$ be natural motivic Chern-class expressions of the same bidegree on $X$. Naturality identifies their pullbacks with the corresponding expressions formed from the pulled-back data. If those expressions agree on every $Y_\alpha$, they agree on the finite disjoint union $Y$ by the finite-clopen motivic restriction isomorphism included in [F2]. Thus $q^*(u-v)=0$, and injectivity from step 2.1 gives $u=v$. No injectivity assertion for the Grothendieck group is used. [F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 Steps 1.1 through 3.1 prove the stated construction, detection, class formulas and identity-checking consequence. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎

## Critical-rank cancellation used in the article

[Open item](item-thm-critical-rank-cancellation) · level 14

### Statement
Assume AC and the universes of the article\'s K-theory construction. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ a nonempty affine finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension $d$. For any two vector bundles $E,F$ of the same constant rank $r\geq d$, $E\cong F$ if and only if $[E]=[F]$ in the article\'s perfect spectral $K_0(X)$. In particular this applies to rank $d$ on every normal affine surface or threefold in the article. Here $[E]$ is the perfect-K-theory object class, and the affine comparison identifies it with the vector-bundle Grothendieck class; no coherent-sheaf G-zero identification is used.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] The precise module cancellation input applies in every characteristic to this affine algebra and ranks at least d. [thm-author-7dc5154c7a6f-suslin-module-input](item-thm-author-7dc5154c7a6f-suslin-module-input)

[F2] The local application lemma proves the K-zero/isomorphism equivalence whenever the corresponding constant-rank projective modules are cancellative. [lem-author-7dc5154c7a6f-cancellation-interface](item-lem-author-7dc5154c7a6f-cancellation-interface)

[F3] The affine perfect/bundle comparison and stable-equivalence supplier fix the actual class map. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes), [lem-k-zero-stable-equivalence](item-lem-k-zero-stable-equivalence)

### Proof

1.1 A finite-type algebra over a field is noetherian, so the local affine K-zero application applies to $X$. The imported cancellation theorem makes every constant-rank-$r$ projective module cancellative since $r\geq d$. Thus [F2] gives the desired equivalence for $E,F$, using the class convention in [F3]. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 A normal affine surface or threefold in the article is an affine finite-type scheme over the same algebraically closed field, and its critical rank is respectively $d=2$ or $d=3$. Substitution $r=d$ yields exactly the original assertion. Isomorphic bundles always have equal object classes, so both directions have been retained. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎

### Source notes
The original article invokes Sus77 on pp. 2, 12 and 17 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22679v1). Its rank-d normal settings are preserved as special cases of the broader precise sourced theorem. The proof is a local application of an imported theorem; no proof acceptance is asserted.


## Surface uniqueness from the cylinder and cancellation

[Open item](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-surface-uniqueness-reduction) · level 14


### Statement
Assume AC. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension two, and put $Y=X\times_k\mathbb A^1_k$. Suppose rank-three bundles on $Y$ with equal ordinary Chow Chern triples are isomorphic. If rank-two bundles on $X$ cancel a common trivial line, then rank-two bundles on $X$ with the same first two Chern classes are isomorphic.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] The cylinder is a smooth affine threefold and its zero section retracts projection. [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-cylinder-geometry](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-cylinder-geometry)

[F2] Stabilization and pullback preserve the relevant Chern data, with third class zero. Both schemes are smooth equidimensional and finite type over $k$, and projection and the zero section are $k$-morphisms, as required by this supplier. [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-stabilized-chern](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-stabilized-chern)

[F3] The maps use the ordinary Chow classes, with equality interpreted coefficientwise. [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-chern-interface](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-chern-interface)

### Proof

1.1 Let $E,F$ have equal first two classes. By [F2], $p^*(E\oplus\mathcal O_X)$ and $p^*(F\oplus\mathcal O_X)$ have identical Chern triples. The assumed rank-three uniqueness on $Y$ gives an isomorphism between them. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Pull back along $s$ and use $s^*p^*=\operatorname{id}$ to obtain $E\oplus\mathcal O_X\cong F\oplus\mathcal O_X$. The assumed cancellation of a common trivial line yields $E\cong F$. [F1, given, step 1.1] ∎


## Surface existence from rank-three existence on the cylinder

[Open item](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-surface-existence-reduction) · level 14


### Statement
Assume AC. Fix a field $k$, let $X$ be a smooth affine finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension two, and put $Y=X\times_k\mathbb A^1_k$. Suppose every triple in $\prod_{i=1}^3\mathrm{CH}^i(Y)$ is realized by a rank-three bundle. Then every $(a_1,a_2)\in\mathrm{CH}^1(X)\times\mathrm{CH}^2(X)$ is realized by a rank-two bundle on $X$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] The projection and zero section have $ps=\operatorname{id}$ and the cylinder is a smooth affine threefold. [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-cylinder-geometry](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-cylinder-geometry)

[F2] Chern classes are natural between smooth schemes. [math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle)

[F3] A rank-three bundle on a noetherian affine surface splits as a trivial line plus a rank-two bundle. [thm-serre-affine-splitting](item-thm-serre-affine-splitting)

[F4] Both $X$ and $Y$ are smooth equidimensional finite-type schemes over $k$, and projection and the zero section are $k$-morphisms. In this scope splitting off a trivial line does not change Chern coefficients. [lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-stabilized-chern](item-lem-author-f08c343a07fc-local-stabilized-chern)

### Proof

1.1 Realize the triple $(p^*a_1,p^*a_2,0)$ by a rank-three bundle $G$ on $Y$, using the assumed existence. Naturality gives $c_i(s^*G)=s^*p^*a_i=a_i$ for $i=1,2$, since pullback is functorial and $ps=\operatorname{id}$. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 By [F3] write $s^*G\cong\mathcal O_X\oplus E$ with $E$ of rank two. By [F4], $c_i(E)=c_i(s^*G)=a_i$ for $i=1,2$. Thus $E$ realizes the prescribed pair. [F3, F4, step 1.1] ∎


## Chern-compatible presentation transports the exact fibers

[Open item](item-lem-author-9b282fc59773-compatible-presentation-fibers) · level 14

### Statement
Let $C_X:V\to T=\operatorname{Pic}(X)\times\mathrm{CH}^2(X)$ be the defined map. Suppose $M,N$ are sets, $v:V\to M$ and $b:N\to T$ are bijections, and $t:M\to N$ is a map satisfying $b\circ t\circ v=C_X$. For $y=(L,a)\in T$, let $n$ be its unique preimage under $b$. The restriction of $v$ is a bijection from $V_{L,a}$ onto $t^{-1}(n)$.

### Statement references
[def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers](item-def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers)

[lem-author-9b282fc59773-fixed-determinant-fibers](item-lem-author-9b282fc59773-fixed-determinant-fibers)

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The sets and maps in the Statement, including the actual equality $b t v=C_X$.

**Goal:** Produce the asserted fiber bijection.

[F1] The fiber of $C_X$ over $(L,a)$ is $V_{L,a}$. [lem-author-9b282fc59773-fixed-determinant-fibers](item-lem-author-9b282fc59773-fixed-determinant-fibers)

### Proof
1.1 If $e\in V_{L,a}$, then $b(t(v(e)))=C_X(e)=y=b(n)$. Injectivity of $b$ yields $t(v(e))=n$. Conversely, if $m\in t^{-1}(n)$, its unique preimage $e$ under $v$ satisfies $C_X(e)=b(t(m))=y$, so $e\in V_{L,a}$. [F1, given]

2.1 The restrictions of $v$ and its inverse therefore map the two specified subsets into each other. Their composites remain the respective identity maps because they were inverse on the ambient sets. This proves the bijection of fibers. Mere abstract bijections of the ambient sets without the compatibility equality would not imply this conclusion. [step 1.1, given] ∎

## Explicit eventual-stage thresholds in every fixed homotopy degree

[Open item](item-lem-author-0cc80c1b5792-threshold) · level 14


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be as above with bound $B=B(X)$. For every fixed $q\in\mathbb Z$ and every integer anchor $t$, put
$$\ell_0(q,t)=\max(0,B+q+1-t).$$
Then $\pi_qF^{t+\ell}_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0$ for all integers $\ell\geq\ell_0(q,t)$. In particular the claim holds with $t=\dim X$ and every fixed $q\leq0$ needed in the article.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and fixed $q,t$, the actual stage bound and $\ell\geq\ell_0(q,t)$.

**Goal:** Exhibit a threshold for the actual stage group rather than assume that high-stage images detect it.

[F1] [lem-author-0cc80c1b5792-actual-bound](item-lem-author-0cc80c1b5792-actual-bound) gives vanishing if $q<r-B$.

[F2] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) discharges the inherited Choice premise of [F1] when its bound for the selected actual filtration is invoked. Taking a maximum of two integers adds no choice requirement.

### Proof
1.1 By the definition of the maximum, $t+\ell\geq B+q+1$. Set $r=t+\ell$. Then $r-B\geq q+1>q$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Under the inherited Choice premise in [F2], apply [F1] to this strict inequality. It gives the asserted zero stage group for every such $\ell$. The choice of $q$ was arbitrary, so the same argument covers in particular the required fixed nonpositive degrees; the threshold is allowed to depend on $q$. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## A split trivial line annihilates the exterior and top Chow classes

[Open item](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-split-vanishing) · level 14

### Statement
Assume AC. Let $r\geq1$ and let $E\cong\mathcal O_X\oplus F$ be a rank-$r$ bundle on a noetherian affine scheme, with $F$ of rank $r-1$. Then $\varepsilon(E)=0$. If $X$ is smooth and equidimensional over a field, then also $c_r(E)=0$ in the ordinary integral Chow group $\mathrm{CH}^r(X)$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The hypotheses and data in the statement, with AC and the article's fixed universes wherever perfect K-theory is used.

**Goal:** Establish the asserted conclusion.

[F1] The actual exterior-dual class is defined in [lem-author-394a5b71198d-exterior-dual-interface](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-exterior-dual-interface).

[F2] Exterior powers have their increasing-wedge bases. [def-exterior-determinant-bundles](item-def-exterior-determinant-bundles)

[F3] Whitney gives $c_t(E)=c_t(\mathcal O_X)c_t(F)=c_t(F)$, and Chern classes vanish above the rank. [math:lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula), [math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle)

### Proof

1.1 Dualize the splitting. For each $i$, exterior multiplication identifies $\Lambda^i(\mathcal O_X\oplus F^\vee)$ with $\Lambda^iF^\vee\oplus\Lambda^{i-1}F^\vee$, where nonexistent exterior degrees are zero: wedges either contain the chosen generator 1 of the trivial line or do not. The basis formula proves the identification locally and its naturality in $F$ glues it. In the finite alternating sum, each $[\Lambda^iF^\vee]$ occurs once with each opposite sign, so the total is zero. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 By [F3], $c_t(E)=c_t(F)$ and the rank-$(r-1)$ bundle $F$ has zero coefficient in degree $r$. Hence $c_r(E)=0$. This is the necessary direction for an actual splitting. [F3, step 1.1] ∎


## Determinants detect vanishing of the rank-one exterior-dual class

[Open item](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-line-determinant) · level 14

### Statement
Assume AC. For a line bundle $L$ on a noetherian affine scheme, $\varepsilon(L)=1-[L^\vee]$ in the article\'s perfect $K_0$, and $\varepsilon(L)=0$ if and only if $L\cong\mathcal O_X$. Thus the rank-one vanishing criterion uses the actual line bundle, not an abstract identification of its target groups.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The hypotheses and data in the statement, with AC and the article's fixed universes wherever perfect K-theory is used.

**Goal:** Establish the asserted conclusion.

[F1] For rank one the exterior-dual sum has only its degree-zero and degree-one terms. [lem-author-394a5b71198d-exterior-dual-interface](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-exterior-dual-interface)

[F2] The affine perfect/bundle comparison identifies object classes, and equality in the latter group is equivalent to a common finite free stabilization. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes), [lem-k-zero-stable-equivalence](item-lem-k-zero-stable-equivalence)

[F3] Determinant is the top exterior power, with the increasing-wedge local bases. [def-exterior-determinant-bundles](item-def-exterior-determinant-bundles)

### Proof

1.1 By [F1], vanishing is exactly $[L^\vee]=[\mathcal O_X]$. By [F2] this yields $L^\vee\oplus\mathcal O_X^N\cong\mathcal O_X^{N+1}$ for some $N\geq0$.
