## Swan chartwise integrality glues on the actual quasi-affine open

[Open item](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-chartwise-integrality) · level 15


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the integral case let $W=U\setminus(Z\cup U_{\mathrm{sing}})$, and use the finite principal charts $W_i=D(g_i)$ and global controlling family above. There is a nonempty parameter open on which the entire zero scheme in $U$ is a nonempty smooth geometrically integral curve of pure codimension two, avoiding $Z$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, the actual global sections, fixed $Z$, and the finite cover of the nonempty smooth integral threefold $W$.

**Goal:** Obtain global irreducibility, not merely smoothness or an expected dimension.

[F1] [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-dual-global-controls](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-dual-global-controls) supplies the controlling family on each smooth affine chart.

[F2] [thm-author-27d786ff4d27-swan-controlled-bertini](item-thm-author-27d786ff4d27-swan-controlled-bertini) gives a nonempty parameter open $G_i$ where that chart's zero scheme is empty or a smooth geometrically integral curve, of dimension $3-2=1$.

[F3] [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-common-core-nonempty](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-common-core-nonempty) and [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-fixed-locus-avoidance](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-fixed-locus-avoidance) provide nonempty-core and avoidance opens. Rational points of finite-type parameter opens use [thm-author-fc2380accb47-finite-type-geometric-input](item-thm-author-fc2380accb47-finite-type-geometric-input).

[A1] [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) is assumed when invoking the controlling-family supplier in [F1] and its applications in [F3]. The finite intersections of parameter opens and the common-core gluing introduce no further arbitrary choice.

### Proof
1.1 Every $W_i$ is a nonempty open of the integral $X$, so their finite intersection contains a nonempty principal open $O$ of $X$. Apply the common-core lemma to this $O$. Intersect its nonempty open $T_O$, the avoidance open, and all finitely many $G_i$. This is a nonempty open $G\subset\mathbb A^N$, and has a $k$-point. The local Swan conditions apply to the restrictions of the very same global parameter family, since its indexed list contains the controlling sections of each chart. [F1, F2, F3, A1]

2.1 Choose that parameter and let $Y$ be its scheme-theoretic zero locus in $U$. Avoidance places $Y$ in $W$. Each $Y_i=Y\cap W_i$ is smooth geometrically integral of dimension one by [F2], and is nonempty because it contains the nonempty open subset $Y\cap O$. The latter is an open subset of $Y_1$, hence irreducible, and is a nonempty open, therefore dense, in every $Y_i$. Its closure in $Y$ contains every $Y_i$, and these cover $Y$. Thus $Y$ is irreducible; it is smooth and reduced because these are local and hold on this cover. The dimension and codimension assertions follow from those on every chart. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The same common-core and open-cover argument survives every extension of $k$: each chart curve is geometrically integral, and the common core remains a nonempty open in it. The extended cover is therefore still irreducible and reduced. Consequently $Y$ is geometrically integral. This proves the assertion for the actual quasi-affine $U$ without claiming that global generation alone implies irreducibility. [F2, step 2.1] ∎


## Slice localization and the actual root-of-unity coefficient map

[Open item](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-coefficient-trivialization) · level 15


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the supplied derived-localization constructions. Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $p$ invertible in $k$, and $X/k$ qcqs, with the fixed choice and universe conventions. On $\mathcal C_F$ use the qcqs prime-field cdh site, and on $\mathcal C_F/X$ its induced slice topology. In this item $L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}=L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}$ and $L_{\mathrm{cdh},X}=L^o_{\mathrm{cdh},X}$ mean ordinary covering-family/Čech sheafification of $D(\mathbb Z)$-valued presheaves. With $r_XP(U\to X)=P(U)$, restriction commutes with this localization, including its units:
$$r_XL^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}P\simeq L^o_{\mathrm{cdh},X}r_XP.$$
Choose a primitive $p$th root $\zeta\in k$. Its pullbacks give a natural coefficient equivalence $r_XB\simeq r_XB_3$, where $B=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(-,\mathbb Z/p)$ and $B_3=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(-,\mu_p^{\otimes3})$. Both restricted targets are ordinary local. Consequently, at the terminal slice object $X\to X$, the actual maps $L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}\tau^{\leq3}B\to B$ and $L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}\tau^{\leq3}B_3\to B_3$ correspond under these equivalences. No root over $F$ or equality of ordinary and hypercomplete reflectors on arbitrary inputs is assumed.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Choice and the stated bounds are inherited through the finite-coefficient locality, ordinary slice localization and derived-evaluation suppliers used below. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)
**Given:** The stated field, prime, scheme and fixed choice/universe conventions.

**Goal:** Compare ordinary localization units and the actual coefficient maps on the slice.

[F1] [lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site) fixes the actual site. Its generating Nisnevich and finitely presented abstract blowup covers are stable under base change. Ordinary sheafification is the reflective localization into covering-family/Čech descent objects.

[F2] [def-etale-tate-coefficients](item-def-etale-tate-coefficients) gives the primitive-root coefficient isomorphism on every small étale site over $k$. [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites) fixes its derived evaluation.

[F3] [prop-etale-cdh-descent](item-prop-etale-cdh-descent) proves hypercomplete and hence ordinary locality of $B$ on the whole prime-field site. Only its ordinary consequence is needed here.

### Proof
1.1 Define $R_XQ(V)=Q(V\times_FX\to X)$. These products remain qcqs. There is an adjunction $r_X\dashv R_X$: a map $r_XP\to Q$ gives $P(V)\to P(V\times_FX)\to Q(V\times_FX\to X)$; conversely a map $P\to R_XQ$ restricts along the graph $U\to U\times_FX$ for every $U\to X$. The projection–graph identities make the constructions inverse, naturally on mapping spaces. [F1, construct, A1]

2.1 Restriction preserves ordinary sheaves because covers and their Čech diagrams over $(U\to X)$ are exactly those over $U$. The functor $R_X$ also preserves them: base change by $X$ carries the generators in [F1], their iterated pullbacks and their Čech diagrams to the same kind of covering diagrams on the slice. For an ordinary local equivalence $v$ and any slice sheaf $Q$, adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Map}(r_Xv,Q)$ with $\operatorname{Map}(v,R_XQ)$, an equivalence. Thus $r_X$ preserves ordinary local equivalences as well as local objects. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 Restrict $P\to L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}P$. By step 2.1 this is a local equivalence into a slice sheaf, so the reflective universal property identifies it with the slice localization unit. The resulting equivalence is natural and respects all maps induced by that unit. Evaluation at $X\to X$ is evaluation of the ambient presheaf at $X$. [F1, step 2.1]

4.1 Pull back $\zeta$ to every scheme over $X$. By [F2] these maps give the actual natural equivalence $r_XB\simeq r_XB_3$. By [F3] and step 2.1, $r_XB$ is ordinary local; its equivalent target $r_XB_3$ is therefore ordinary local too. Truncation, localization and the naturality of the units in step 3.1 now conjugate the two induced maps from localized truncations into those local targets. Evaluate at the terminal object to obtain the claimed actual comparison. [F2, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎


## Low-degree consequences of a weight-one comparison

[Open item](item-lem-author-13e6fe931c45-weight-one-identifications) · level 15

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site-size bounds of [lem-author-13e6fe931c45-shifted-units](item-lem-author-13e6fe931c45-shifted-units). Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme over a field, and suppose a morphism $f:R\Gamma_{\rm Nis}(X,\mathbb G_m)[-1]\to\mathbb Z(1)_{\rm mot}(X)$ has cofiber supported in degrees $>3$. Then it induces $H^{i-1}_{\rm Nis}(X,\mathbb G_m)\cong H^{i,1}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)$ for $i\leq3$. In particular the motivic groups are zero for $i\leq0$, global units for $i=1$, and the Picard group for $i=2$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $X$, $f$, the cofiber bound, Choice, and the site-size bounds.

**Goal:** Derive the displayed cohomology identifications.

[F1] The cofiber bound gives an isomorphism on cohomology through degree three ([lem-author-13e6fe931c45-cone-exact-range](item-lem-author-13e6fe931c45-cone-exact-range)).

[F2] The source groups and their low degrees are identified in [lem-author-13e6fe931c45-shifted-units](item-lem-author-13e6fe931c45-shifted-units). Motivic cohomology is cohomology of the target complex ([def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology)).

### Proof

1.1 Apply [F1] to $f$. By [F2], the source of the resulting degree-$i$ isomorphism is $H^{i-1}_{\rm Nis}(X,\mathbb G_m)$ and the target is $H^{i,1}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)$. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Substitute the computations of [F2] for $i\leq2$. This gives zero, units and the Picard group in the stated ranges, retaining the assumptions required by the supplier. [F2, step 1.1] ∎

## An actual non-A¹ P¹-spectrum for the supplied EM complexes

[Open item](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-p1-model) · level 15


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. For every qcqs scheme $S$ over a field $k$, restriction of the supplied EM complexes to smooth qcqs $S$-schemes admits a canonical homotopy-commutative motivic ring spectrum model $\mathcal E_S$ in the non-$\mathbb A^1$ category of Annala–Iwasa. Its nonnegative levels are $\Omega^\infty A_n$ where $A_n(Y)=\mathbb Z(n)_{\rm mot}(Y)[2n]$. For every $i\geq0$ its diagonal group $\mathcal E_S^{2i,i}(Y)$ is naturally $H^{2i,i}_{\rm mot}(Y,\mathbb Z)$, with the actual product. No $\mathbb A^1$ localization is taken.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and fixed size bounds discharge the selected graded/PBF input [thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-graded-input](item-thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-graded-input) when constructing the graded algebra and using its actual projective-line equivalence in steps 1.1–2.1. The model and coefficient-stabilization constructions retain those same bounds.

[F1] [thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-graded-input](item-thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-graded-input) supplies the natural commutative graded spectra $A_n$, the actual pointed class $b=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ on $(\mathbb P^1,\infty)$, and the complex-level P¹ formula.

[F2] [thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-p1-spectrum-input](item-thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-p1-spectrum-input) supplies the symmetric P¹-spectrum model: a commutative symmetric sequence with a map from the free graded sphere algebra on P¹ in degree1 is a commutative lax P¹-spectrum; it is a P¹-spectrum when the adjoint bonding maps are equivalences. It also supplies coefficient stabilization and the evaluation/shift rule.

### Proof
**Given:** $S$ qcqs over a field, the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Construct the actual model and diagonal identification.

1.1 Use the graded algebra $A_n$ from [F1], with trivial symmetric-group actions on each level and the induced coherent symmetric products. Equivalently restrict its grading along the symmetric monoid $B\Sigma\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. The class $b:\Sigma^\infty(\mathbb P^1,\infty)\to A_1$ defines an algebra map from the free graded sphere algebra of [F2]. Thus $A$ is a commutative lax P¹-spectrum in Zariski sheaves of ordinary spectra; its bonding maps are multiplication by this very class. [A1, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 The adjoint map $A_n(Y)\to\operatorname{fib}(A_{n+1}(\mathbb P^1_Y)\to A_{n+1}(Y))$ is the second summand of the actual P¹ formula in [F1], hence an equivalence. The fiber uses the infinity section, on which $b$ is zero with the trivial-line nullhomotopy supplied by its pointed Picard map. Consequently $A$ is already an Ω-P¹-spectrum, so its levels need no replacement by unrelated objects. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply the lax monoidal right adjoint Ω∞ of coefficient stabilization in [F2]. It preserves the adjoint bonding equivalences and gives the stated ring spectrum $\mathcal E_S$ with levels $\Omega^\infty A_n$. By the shift/evaluation rule, $\mathcal E_S^{2i,i}(Y)=\pi_0 A_i(Y)=H^{2i}(\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}(Y))$. The maps arise from the actual graded products, so this identification preserves their multiplication and naturality. All constructions restrict from all qcqs schemes over the prime field, so they apply when $S$ is singular. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## An actual non-A¹ P¹-spectrum for the supplied EM complexes

[Open item](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-em-p1-model) · level 15


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. For every qcqs scheme $S$ over a field $k$, restriction of the supplied EM complexes to smooth qcqs $S$-schemes admits a canonical homotopy-commutative motivic ring spectrum model $\mathcal E_S$ in the non-$\mathbb A^1$ category of Annala–Iwasa. Its nonnegative levels are $\Omega^\infty A_n$ where $A_n(Y)=\mathbb Z(n)_{\rm mot}(Y)[2n]$. For every $i\geq0$ its diagonal group $\mathcal E_S^{2i,i}(Y)$ is naturally $H^{2i,i}_{\rm mot}(Y,\mathbb Z)$, with the actual product. No $\mathbb A^1$ localization is taken.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and fixed size bounds discharge the selected graded/PBF input [thm-author-32887006bdff-em-graded-input](item-thm-author-32887006bdff-em-graded-input) when constructing the graded algebra and using its actual projective-line equivalence in steps 1.1–2.1. The model and coefficient-stabilization constructions retain those same bounds.

[F1] [thm-author-32887006bdff-em-graded-input](item-thm-author-32887006bdff-em-graded-input) supplies the natural commutative graded spectra $A_n$, the actual pointed class $b=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ on $(\mathbb P^1,\infty)$, and the complex-level P¹ formula.

It also supplies coefficient stabilization and the evaluation/shift rule.

### Proof
**Given:** $S$ qcqs over a field, the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Construct the actual model and diagonal identification.

1.1 Use the graded algebra $A_n$ from [F1], with trivial symmetric-group actions on each level and the induced coherent symmetric products. Equivalently restrict its grading along the symmetric monoid $B\Sigma\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. The class $b:\Sigma^\infty(\mathbb P^1,\infty)\to A_1$ defines an algebra map from the free graded sphere algebra of [F2]. Thus $A$ is a commutative lax P¹-spectrum in Zariski sheaves of ordinary spectra; its bonding maps are multiplication by this very class. [A1, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 The adjoint map $A_n(Y)\to\operatorname{fib}(A_{n+1}(\mathbb P^1_Y)\to A_{n+1}(Y))$ is the second summand of the actual P¹ formula in [F1], hence an equivalence. The fiber uses the infinity section, on which $b$ is zero with the trivial-line nullhomotopy supplied by its pointed Picard map. Consequently $A$ is already an Ω-P¹-spectrum, so its levels need no replacement by unrelated objects. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply the lax monoidal right adjoint Ω∞ of coefficient stabilization in [F2]. It preserves the adjoint bonding equivalences and gives the stated ring spectrum $\mathcal E_S$ with levels $\Omega^\infty A_n$. By the shift/evaluation rule, $\mathcal E_S^{2i,i}(Y)=\pi_0 A_i(Y)=H^{2i}(\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}(Y))$. The maps arise from the actual graded products, so this identification preserves their multiplication and naturality. All constructions restrict from all qcqs schemes over the prime field, so they apply when $S$ is singular. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## The support long exact sequence kills degree seven

[Open item](item-lem-author-8a080e7d9445-degree-seven-les) · level 15


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the supplied comparisons. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension three, put $U=X_{\mathrm{smooth}/k}$, and let $T\subset X$ be a closed subset contained in $U$. Use the reduced structure on $T$ when a scheme structure is needed. Put $V=U\setminus T$ and $W=X\setminus T$. For the actual motivic support fiber on $U$ in weight three, its degree-seven group is zero. Via excision the same holds for support $T$ on $X$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** $k,X,U,T,V,W$ and the choice and size assumptions of the statement.

**Goal:** Construct the stated actual maps and prove their consequence.

[F1] [lem-author-8a080e7d9445-support-fiber](item-lem-author-8a080e7d9445-support-fiber), [lem-author-8a080e7d9445-chow-restriction](item-lem-author-8a080e7d9445-chow-restriction) and [lem-fiber-sequence-homotopy-exactness](item-lem-fiber-sequence-homotopy-exactness).

[F2] [prop-smooth-motivic-comparison](item-prop-smooth-motivic-comparison), applied to the actual smooth $U$.

[F3] The assumed Axiom of Choice, [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), discharges the foundational hypotheses of the support and Chow suppliers in [F1] and the smooth comparison in [F2], invoked in step 1.1. The following exact-sequence deduction makes no additional choice.

### Proof
1.1 Apply the long exact cohomology sequence of the actual support fiber to obtain $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(U)\to H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(V)\to H^{7,3}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(U)\to H^{7,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(U)$. The first arrow is surjective by the preceding local Chow-restriction lemma. The last group is zero by the completed smooth comparison: $2\cdot3-7=-1$ and the cycle complex has no negative homology. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Exactness gives zero for the middle supported group: its map to the zero last group has kernel equal to the image of the preceding zero connecting map. The support-fiber lemma gives the actual excision equivalence to support on $X$, proving the claim there as well. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## A coherent comparison of the particular open restriction

[Open item](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-restriction-diagram) · level 15


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the support and comparison constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, let $X$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension three, and let $T\subset X$ be a closed subset contained in the smooth locus $U=X_{\mathrm{smooth}}$ of $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Equip $T$ with its reduced induced structure, and put $V=U\setminus T$ and $W=X\setminus T$. For the actual arrow $V\hookrightarrow U$, the weight-three motivic restriction diagram is equivalent to the actual cycle restriction diagram
$$[\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(U)\to\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(V)]\simeq[z^3(U,\bullet)[-6]\to z^3(V,\bullet)[-6]].$$
It follows in particular that its $H^6$ arrow is ordinary Chow restriction. The square is supplied before applying cohomology. In the cycle complexes, homological degree $n$ is reindexed as cochain degree $-n$ before the shift by $-6$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement, with the Axiom of Choice and fixed universe bounds.

**Goal:** Construct the stated actual maps and prove their consequence.

[F1] [thm-author-149a02132c3b-em-regular-input](item-thm-author-149a02132c3b-em-regular-input) and [lem-author-149a02132c3b-geometry](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-geometry).

[F2] [thm-author-149a02132c3b-open-natural-classical-input](item-thm-author-149a02132c3b-open-natural-classical-input) with [lem-bloch-chow-and-negative-range](item-lem-bloch-chow-and-negative-range).

[F3] The assumed Axiom of Choice, [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), and the fixed size bounds discharge the inherited hypotheses of the geometry and comparison constructions. Their comparison maps are natural transformations on the stated diagrams.

### Proof
1.1 Under the stated Choice and size assumptions, the geometry lemma makes the specified $U$ and $V$ regular Noetherian schemes. Apply the natural regular comparison of [F1] to these two objects and their open arrow. This gives an equivalence of arrow diagrams from the motivic arrow to the cdh arrow. It applies although k need not be finitely generated over its prime field. [F1, F3, given]

2.1 Apply the open-natural classical interface of [F2] over the fixed perfect k. Compose the equivalences of diagrams, inverting only natural equivalences. Its bottom arrow is the actual open restriction on cycles. Taking $H^6$ gives its degree-zero cycle homology arrow, which is ordinary Chow restriction by the completed degree-zero cycle supplier. This establishes the arrow identification before inferring any surjectivity. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## The actual smooth restriction arrow gives the point-supported cycle fiber

[Open item](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-actual-support) · level 15


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. For $V,L,x$ above and every $j\geq0$, the actual restriction arrow of the specified EM complexes is equivalent, as an arrow diagram, to
$$[z^j(V,\bullet)[-2j]\longrightarrow z^j(V\setminus\{x\},\bullet)[-2j]].$$
Its fiber is therefore $z_x^j(V,\bullet)[-2j]$. These equivalences compare actual restriction maps and the fiber projections before taking cohomology. The same diagram identifies the arrow with the classical coefficient-complex restriction used below. No hypothesis that $k$ be finitely generated over its prime field is required.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and fixed compatible site and universe bounds discharge the inherited premises of the neighbourhood and support constructions and the open-natural classical comparison in [F1]–[F3] at the annotated applications below. The chain, dimension and formal fiber computations introduce no additional choice principle.

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, the fixed compatible site and universe bounds, and the exact smooth finite-type pair $x\in V$, its residue field $L$ from the neighbourhood supplier, and $j\geq0$.

**Goal:** Transfer the actual support fiber, not choose isomorphisms of its groups after the fact.

[F1] [thm-author-8a080e7d9445-em-regular-input](item-thm-author-8a080e7d9445-em-regular-input) gives the natural EM-to-cdh transformation on qcqs prime-field schemes and its equivalence on regular Noetherian schemes, for every nonnegative weight.

[F2] [thm-author-8a080e7d9445-open-natural-classical-input](item-thm-author-8a080e7d9445-open-natural-classical-input) gives, for each nonnegative weight, the BEM fixed-site comparison to cycles and the MVW classical coefficient zigzag on all opens of the single smooth ambient $S=V$ over perfect $k$. [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-neighborhood](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-neighborhood) verifies its hypotheses on $V$ and its complement.

[F3] [def-supported-higher-cycle-complex](item-def-supported-higher-cycle-complex) gives the supported cycle complex as the actual restriction fiber by its imported Bloch localization theorem; [def-supported-complex-indexing](item-def-supported-complex-indexing) fixes fiber and cohomological shifts.

### Proof
1.1 Both smooth objects are regular Noetherian after forgetting to the prime field. Apply [F1] to their actual open arrow. Apply [F2] on the single fixed ambient $S=V$, restricting its equivalence to the opens $V$ and $V\setminus\{x\}$. The MVW coefficient functor on this same open diagram is equivalent to the cycle functor, whose arrow is actual open restriction. Compose in the functor category of arrows, inverting only its natural equivalences. This proves the displayed arrow equivalence in arbitrary nonnegative weight. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 Fibers are functorial finite limits of coherent arrows. Taking them in step 1.1 preserves equivalences and their projections. Apply [F3] to replace the derived cycle fiber by its fixed-support subcomplex; cochain reindexing and shift $[-2j]$ commute with fibers. This gives the asserted fiber equivalence. The same construction through the classical intermediate identifies the actual classical restriction fiber, and not an unrelated relative-motive group. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## The actual first EM stage is the rank-zero K space on all qcqs schemes

[Open item](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage) · level 15


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fixed compatible site and universe size bounds for the constructions below. Let $k$ be any field. On its qcqs schemes, the actual EM weight-zero map $q_0:K\to\operatorname{gr}^0K$ induces the locally constant Euler rank on $K_0$. Moreover $\Omega^\infty\operatorname{gr}^0K$ is the discrete Nisnevich sheaf $\underline{\mathbb Z}$ of locally constant integer functions. Thus $S=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^1K$ is the actual rank-zero fiber of $\Omega^\infty K\to\underline{\mathbb Z}$, and $\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^1K(X)$ identifies injectively with $\ker(\operatorname{rank}:K_0(X)\to\underline{\mathbb Z}(X))$ for every qcqs $X$.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds are retained when applying [prop-motivic-weight-zero](item-prop-motivic-weight-zero) in [F1], specifically its derived constant-sheaf interpretation and negative-degree vanishing in step 2.1 and the resulting rank-fiber computation in step 3.1. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-em-map-normalizations](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-em-map-normalizations) and [prop-motivic-weight-zero](item-prop-motivic-weight-zero) identify the actual unital gr⁰ map with $R\Gamma_{\rm cdh}(\mathbb Z)$ on the precise prime-field qcqs site of [lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site).

[F2] [math:thm-etale-morphisms-open-and-quasi-finite](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-etale-morphisms-open-and-quasi-finite) makes surjective étale covers open quotient maps; [math:thm-proper-morphism-closed-image](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-proper-morphism-closed-image) makes proper surjections closed quotient maps. [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge) gives $K_0$ of a field as $\mathbb Z$ with unit generator. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) supplies the actual fiber sequence Fil¹K→K→gr⁰K.

### Proof
**Given:** Any field $k$ and qcqs $X/k$, with the supplied actual tower.

**Goal:** Identify weight-zero sections, its map and the whole first-stage fiber.

1.1 The presheaf $L(V)$ of locally constant integer functions on $|V|$ is a cdh sheaf on the site in [F1]. Indeed, for a finite Nisnevich cover its disjoint-union map is a surjective open quotient map by [F2]; for an abstract blowup covering its disjoint-union map is proper surjective and hence closed quotient. Matching functions are constant on each set-theoretic fiber: two points over the same base point have a common point in their scheme fiber product since the tensor product of their residue fields over that base field is nonzero. A matching function therefore descends uniquely, and the quotient topology makes the descended function continuous to the discrete set $\mathbb Z$. This proves descent for the generators and hence the generated topology. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 The map from the constant presheaf to $L$ is locally an isomorphism: locally constant functions are constant on an open cover (finite after quasi-compactness), and equality of constant values is detected there. The empty object uses its empty cover and the zero group. Thus $L$ is the ordinary cdh constant sheaf. Consequently $H^0_{\rm cdh}(X,\mathbb Z)=L(X)$ and negative cohomology is zero, as for the derived sections of any ordinary sheaf. Applying Ω∞ to gr⁰ therefore gives precisely the discrete sheaf $L$. This is computation on the actual big site, not a small-site substitution. [A1, F1, step 1.1]

3.1 For every point $x$ of $X$, pull back $q_0$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. Its $K_0$ and weight-zero target are $\mathbb Z$, and the map is unital by [F1], hence identity. Its value at $x$ on any perfect class is therefore its Euler rank. Values at all points determine the function in $L(X)$, so $q_0$ is the full rank function. Finally Ω∞ preserves fibers, and the discrete target has no positive homotopy groups; the fiber sequence in [F2] gives the asserted rank-zero space and the injective identification on $\pi_0$. [A1, F1, F2, step 2.1] ∎


## The actual EM comparison commutes with the Picard first-Chern map

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-em-picard-square) · level 15

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the existing universe bounds. Let $F$ be the prime subfield of a perfect field $k$. Denote by $\eta:\mathbb Z(\star)_{\rm mot}\to\mathbb Z(\star)_{\rm cdh}$ the actual EM graded comparison, and by $\gamma:\mathbb Z(\star)_{\rm cdh}\to\mathbb Z(\star)_{\mathbb A}$ the canonical structured comparison to the represented slice theory. The canonical base-independent cdh identification is understood in this notation. On smooth finite-type $k$-schemes, the natural graded map $\theta=\gamma\eta$ is an equivalence and satisfies the actual Picard-space square
$$\theta_1[2]\,c_1^{\rm EM}\simeq c_1^{\mathbb A}:\mathrm{Pic}\longrightarrow\Omega^\infty\mathbb Z(1)_{\mathbb A}[2].$$
Together with the unit-induced field zigzag, this supplies an actual orientation-preserving comparison between Spitzweck/classical and EM coefficients. The assertion is integral, also in characteristic $p$.

### Statement references

[lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag)

[lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-picard-map-detection](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-picard-map-detection)

[thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-field-map-input](item-thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-field-map-input)

[thm-author-32887006bdff-em-graded-input](item-thm-author-32887006bdff-em-graded-input)

[prop-smooth-motivic-comparison](item-prop-smooth-motivic-comparison)

[thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison)

### Facts & Assumptions
[A8] The current smooth comparison fixes the ordinary Voevodsky/Bloch model and the actual augmented EM comparison, with its AC premise. [prop-smooth-motivic-comparison](item-prop-smooth-motivic-comparison), [thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison)

[A9] Choice is inherited through the current smooth motivic comparison and its classical/cycle model. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-field-map-input](item-thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-field-map-input) specifies the actual multiplicative maps, their naturality and regular-Noetherian equivalence hypotheses. EM Lemma 5.1/Definition 5.2 fixes its Picard map by (4.9), and the proof describes its Nisnevich-local left-Kan construction. Lemma 5.12, with Construction 5.11, identifies its normalized reduced line class as the actual edge image of $1-[\mathcal O(-1)]$. BEM's Picard map is the actual determinant/edge square (4.36), extended by (4.42).

[F2] [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag) and [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-picard-map-detection](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-picard-map-detection) supply the unit-induced ring zigzag and actual Picard-map detection; the completed EM Picard supplier identifies the actual normalized first class, not an independently chosen Picard-group isomorphism.

### Proof
**Given:** $F\subseteq k$, smooth schemes, the specified coefficient maps, AC and the stated universe bounds.

**Goal:** Prove compatibility of the actual first-Chern maps before using it to identify higher operations.

1.1 On smooth $F$-schemes, EM defines its spectral first class using the actual graded map (4.9). Remark 4.37 identifies its composite with $\eta$ as the canonical classical-to-cdh counit. The classical filtration here is the KGL slice filtration. BEM Theorem 7.5 and Remark 7.6 identify its prime-field cdh-local Kan extension with the restriction of BEM's cdh construction, including the filtered augmentation, not just its graded groups. The map (7.14) is induced from the inverse of (4.19) on smooth $\mathbb Z$-schemes; after the canonical base-identification counit, its composite back to the represented filtration is the classical slice comparison. EM Lemma 5.12 identifies its reduced line class with the graded image of $1-[\mathcal O(-1)]$. Since these are maps of augmented filtered objects, the structured comparison takes this to the edge image of the same virtual line class in the represented slice tower. By BEM Construction 4.35 and its determinant square (4.36), this is exactly the unit-normalized class $c_1^{\mathbb A}(\mathcal O(1))$: $\det(1-[L^\vee])=L$. Apply Picard-map detection in [F2] to $\mathbb Z(\star)_{\mathbb A}[2\star]$, whose negative weights vanish and whose normalized class gives PBF. The resulting homotopy identifies the full Picard-space maps. After Nisnevich sheafification on the smooth prime-field site, the source and target weight-one sheaves are both equivalent to $\mathbb G_m[-1]$ (classically and by BEM Corollary 6.26). A degree-zero map between two objects of the same shifted heart is determined by its homomorphism of abelian sheaves. That homomorphism is detected by $\pi_1$ after shifting by two and passing to the associated Picard-space map. The preceding homotopy in the functor category therefore identifies the spectral first-class maps on this site. This uses the single-sheaf calculation; it does not infer equality of arbitrary spectral maps from their underlying spaces. [F1, F2, A8, A9]

2.1 This square extends as a square of presheaf maps on all qcqs $F$-schemes. Explicitly, the proof of EM Lemma5.1 identifies the source Picard coefficient presheaf as the Nisnevich sheafification of the left Kan extension of its restriction to smooth $F$-algebras (before sheafification the source is $(\tau^{\leq1}R\Gamma_{\rm Zar}(-,\mathbb G_m))[-1]$). Both targets are Nisnevich local. By the left-Kan/sheafification adjunction, maps out of that source are determined by the actual smooth-affine maps. Step 1.1 therefore identifies the composites as maps after this construction. BEM constructs its natural first-class map on all qcqs schemes by cdh-local left Kan extension over $\mathbb Z$, followed by the Nisnevich-to-cdh source map (Theorem 4.39(4) and Remark 4.45). Restrict this natural transformation to $F$-schemes. Since its target is Nisnevich local, the same source adjunction determines it from its restriction to smooth $F$-algebras. Thus the equality in step 1.1 extends to this particular BEM map, without assuming that extension over $\mathbb Z$ and extension over $F$ are literally the same construction. No comparison of affine Picard groups is being used. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 Restrict step 2.1 along $\mathrm{Sch}_k\to\mathrm{Sch}_F$. Smooth finite-type $k$-schemes are regular Noetherian as absolute $F$-schemes, irrespective of finite generation of $k/F$. EM Theorem6.1(2) makes $\eta$ an equivalence on them, and BEM Corollary1.11 makes $\gamma$ an equivalence in equal characteristic, with the canonical field identification of Theorem7.5/Remark7.9. Thus the claimed square and equivalence hold for every fixed perfect $k$. Multiplication and units are those of the structured graded maps in [F1]. Inverting these equivalences in the functor category retains the square and all restriction coherences. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Transport the actual Spitzweck Picard-space map along the unital field zigzag of [F2]. By [F1], its reduced projective-line class is the unit-adjoint class in the matched Tate-coordinate convention; these unital maps preserve it. The represented theory has zero negative weights and PBF with its actual first class, so the Picard-map detector of [F2] identifies this transported full Picard-space map with $c_1^{\mathbb A}$. Combine this homotopy with the EM square from step 3.1 and invert the equivalences as natural transformations. This gives the claimed orientation-preserving Spitzweck/classical-to-EM comparison. [F1, F2, A9, step 3.1] ∎


## Smooth threefold rank-two classification

[Open item](item-thm-smooth-threefold-rank-two-classification) · level 16

### Statement
Use the Axiom of Choice and the supplied universe conventions. Let $X$ be a smooth affine threefold over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic different from two. The first two Chern classes give a pointed bijection
$$\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Pic}(X)\times\mathrm{CH}^2(X),\qquad [E]\longmapsto(c_1(E),c_2(E)).$$
Here the first coordinate is $[\det E]$ in $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$, equivalently its usual first Chern class under $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\cong\mathrm{CH}^1(X)$. Thus every pair of classes is attained by exactly one bundle isomorphism class. No determinant trivialization is included in the classification data.

### Statement references
[def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers](item-def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers)

[thm-author-9b282fc59773-asok-fasel-comparison-input](item-thm-author-9b282fc59773-asok-fasel-comparison-input)

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A smooth affine $k$-scheme of finite type of pure dimension three, with $k$ algebraically closed and $\operatorname{char}(k)\ne2$, and the stated set-theoretic conventions.

**Goal:** Prove bijectivity for the actual pair of Chern classes and identify the basepoints.

[F1] The map $C_X([E])=([\det E],c_2(E))$ is well-defined and takes the trivial rank-two bundle to $([\mathcal O_X],0)$. [def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers](item-def-author-9b282fc59773-chern-map-and-fibers)

[F2] Under exactly these hypotheses, the external Asok–Fasel comparison gives compatible maps $v,t,b$ and exact obstruction-group sequences with zero end groups, together with the nonempty lift-fiber quotient descriptions. It also identifies the determinant coordinate with $c_1$ and the second coordinate with the ordinary $c_2$. [thm-author-9b282fc59773-asok-fasel-comparison-input](item-thm-author-9b282fc59773-asok-fasel-comparison-input)

[F3] Compatible presentation maps with this lifting and vanishing interface imply singleton Chern fibers and bijectivity. [lem-author-9b282fc59773-unique-lifting-criterion](item-lem-author-9b282fc59773-unique-lifting-criterion)

### Proof
1.1 The field and scheme satisfy all hypotheses of [F2]: algebraic closure, characteristic different from two, smoothness, affineness, and dimension three. Apply that input to $X$. It gives bijections $v$ and $b$, a surjective $t$, the equality $b t v=C_X$, and, over every second-stage class, the exact sequence and zero end groups required by [F3]. No assertion about arbitrary singular threefolds or characteristic two is used. [given, F1, F2]

2.1 Applying [F3] to these actual maps makes $C_X$ a bijection, with one bundle isomorphism class for every pair. By [F2] this is precisely the displayed pair of Chern classes, and by [F1] it preserves the specified basepoints. This proves the full stated classification. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎

## Smooth critical-rank splitting criterion

[Open item](item-thm-smooth-top-chern-splitting) · level 16


### Statement
Assume AC and the article\'s universe bounds. Let $X$ be a nonempty smooth affine variety of dimension $d\geq0$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, and let $E$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d$. Then there exists a vector bundle $E\prime$ with $E\cong E\prime\oplus\mathcal O_X$ if and only if $c_d(E)=0$ in the ordinary integral Chow group $\mathrm{CH}^d(X)$. For $d\geq1$ the complement necessarily has rank $d-1$. For $d=0$, the convention is $c_0(E)=1$, and both splitting and vanishing are false. Chern classes are the usual quotient-projective-bundle classes; on a possibly disconnected smooth variety the codimension Chow grading and classes are understood componentwise. Splitting off a trivial line is equivalently the existence of a unimodular global section on this affine scheme.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The hypotheses and data in the statement, with AC and the article's fixed universes wherever perfect K-theory is used.

**Goal:** Establish the asserted conclusion.

[F1] Smooth affine schemes have the finite integral clopen decomposition, lower-dimensional components split by Serre, and componentwise splittings glue. [lem-author-394a5b71198d-components](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-components)

[F2] The actual module exterior-dual class maps to the spectral bundle class epsilon. [lem-author-394a5b71198d-exterior-dual-interface](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-exterior-dual-interface)

[F3] An actual split trivial line gives zero top Chow class in positive rank. [lem-author-394a5b71198d-split-vanishing](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-split-vanishing)

[F4] The dimension-one actual first Chern map is Picard/divisor class and detects trivial line bundles; its exterior-dual K-class is detected by determinants. [lem-author-394a5b71198d-curve-picard](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-curve-picard), [lem-author-394a5b71198d-line-determinant](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-line-determinant)

[F5] The dimension-zero boundary is explicit. [lem-author-394a5b71198d-zero-boundary](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-zero-boundary)

[F6] In dimension at least two, the closed-point cycle map sends the ordinary top Chow Chern class to the projective-module exterior-dual class, is an isomorphism, and supplies absence of factorial torsion. The supplier proves the canonical comparison $j:K_0^{\mathrm{proj}}(A)\to K_0(\mathcal H(A))$ with inverse $\chi((M))=\sum_i(-1)^i[P_i]$ for a finite projective resolution of $M$. Here $\mathcal H(A)$ consists only of modules admitting such resolutions. Its proof checks resolution independence, exact additivity and both inverse identities, and identifies the point subgroups, the actual cycle map and each projective exterior term. [thm-author-394a5b71198d-murthy-chow-to-k-input](item-thm-author-394a5b71198d-murthy-chow-to-k-input)

[F7] The module converse splitting theorem applies to reduced affine algebras over an algebraically closed field, in dimension at least two, with the stated factorial-torsion hypothesis. Its supplier uses the same canonical resolution comparison on the point subgroup and on the exterior-dual class; it requires no identification with all coherent-module classes on a singular ring. [thm-author-394a5b71198d-murthy-module-splitting-input](item-thm-author-394a5b71198d-murthy-module-splitting-input)

[F8] The affine module/bundle equivalence preserves rank and direct sums, and a free line summand corresponds to a unimodular section. [lem-affine-bundle-module-interface](item-lem-affine-bundle-module-interface), [def-unimodular-sections](item-def-unimodular-sections)

### Proof
1.1 If $d=0$, [F5] proves that both conditions are false, so their equivalence holds with the stated convention. Assume $d\geq1$ henceforth. If $E$ splits off a trivial line, its restriction to each component has rank-$d-1$ complement. By [F3] its degree-$d$ Chern class vanishes on every component, so it vanishes globally under [F1]. [F1, F3, F5, given]

1.2 For the converse suppose $c_d(E)=0$. Use the finite integral clopen decomposition $X=\coprod_jX_j$ from [F1] and set $d_j=\dim X_j$. If $d_j<d$, Serre splitting in [F1] gives a trivial line summand of $E|_{X_j}$. It remains to treat the components of dimension exactly $d$. [F1, given]

2.1 If $d=1$, the restriction to each dimension-one component is a line bundle. Its actual first Chern class is zero, so [F4] makes it trivial. This is $E|_{X_j}\cong\mathcal O_{X_j}\oplus0$. The same local result also identifies vanishing of the actual exterior-dual K-class via the determinant, without invoking the dimension-at-least-two comparison. [F4, step 1.2]

2.2 If $d\geq2$, write a dimension-$d$ component as $X_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$. Smoothness over the algebraically closed perfect field makes $A_j$ regular, hence reduced, and [F1] makes it integral. It is an affine algebra of dimension $d$. Let $P_j=\Gamma(X_j,E|_{X_j})$, a finite projective module of constant rank $d$ by [F8]. These are exactly the ring and rank hypotheses of [F6], and the reduced affine hypotheses of [F7]. [F1, F6, F7, F8, step 1.2]

3.1 Apply the canonical comparison in [F6] to $A_j$. For each selected smooth height-$d$ point $x$, $\chi((k(x)))$ is its finite-resolution Euler class, so $j$ and $\chi$ restrict to inverse maps on the subgroups generated by these points. If $\phi_{\mathcal H}$ is the source cycle map, $\chi\phi_{\mathcal H}$ is therefore the stated projective-module cycle map $\phi$. For every $i$, the module $\Lambda^iP_j^*$ is finite projective and its length-zero resolution gives $\chi((\Lambda^iP_j^*))=[\Lambda^iP_j^*]$. Thus this is the same comparison of actual classes used by [F7], including the factorial-torsion condition. [F6, F7, step 2.2]

4.1 The component restriction of $c_d(E)$ vanishes by [F1]. Apply [F6] through the comparison of step 3.1: $\phi(c_d(E|_{X_j}))=C^K_d(P_j)=0$, and $F^dK_0^{\mathrm{proj}}(A_j)$ has no $(d-1)!$ torsion. For the source torsion theorem, regularity supplies its regular-in-codimension-one alternative when $d\geq3$, and $d=2$ is its separate alternative. The module-to-spectral expression is exactly that in [F2]. This uses the specified point-cycle map and its compatibility with the exterior-dual expression. [F1, F2, F6, step 1.2, step 2.2, step 3.1]

5.1 By steps 2.2, 3.1 and 4.1, all the hypotheses of [F7] hold for $A_j,P_j$ with the identical exterior-dual obstruction and point subgroup, so $P_j\cong A_j\oplus Q_j$ with $Q_j$ finite projective of rank $d-1$. By [F8] this sheafifies to a trivial line summand of $E|_{X_j}$. Together with steps 1.2 and 2.1 every component has such a splitting. By [F1] they glue to $E\cong\mathcal O_X\oplus E\prime$. [F1, F7, F8, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.1]

6.1 The necessary direction in step 1.1 and sufficient direction in step 5.1 establish the equivalence for all $d\geq1$, while step 1.1 covers $d=0$. Local ranks add, so the positive-dimensional complement has rank $d-1$. Finally [F8] gives exactly the unimodular-section formulation. [F8, step 1.1, step 5.1] ∎

### Source notes
The article p. 1 attributes the criterion to Mur94 Remark 3.6 and Theorem 3.7. ## Motivic weight one

[Open item](item-prop-motivic-weight-one) · level 16


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site-size bounds of [lem-author-13e6fe931c45-weight-one-identifications](item-lem-author-13e6fe931c45-weight-one-identifications). Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme. There is a natural map
$$R\Gamma_{\rm Nis}(X,\mathbb G_m)[-1]\longrightarrow\mathbb Z(1)_{\rm mot}(X)$$
that is an equivalence in degrees at most three: it induces an isomorphism on cohomology in every degree $i\leq3$. Here $\mathbb G_m$ is the sheaf of invertible regular functions on the small Nisnevich site, and $\mathbb Z(1)_{\rm mot}(X)$ is the complex of [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology). Consequently, for $i\leq2$,
$$H^{i,1}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong H^{i-1}_{\rm Nis}(X,\mathbb G_m)\cong\begin{cases}0&i\leq0,\\\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times&i=1,\\\operatorname{Pic}(X)&i=2.\end{cases}$$
The Picard group is the group of isomorphism classes of line bundles, meaning locally free rank-one $\mathcal O_X$-modules, under tensor product.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $k$, $X$, Choice, and the stated site-size bounds.

**Goal:** Construct the comparison and establish its degree range and the displayed groups.

[F1] Passing to the prime subfield preserves the underlying scheme, the small Nisnevich units, and the value of the restricted motivic functor ([lem-author-13e6fe931c45-prime-field-restriction](item-lem-author-13e6fe931c45-prime-field-restriction)).

[F2] The Elmanto–Morrow external input supplies the natural comparison with cofiber supported in degrees $>3$ for qcqs schemes over a prime field ([lem-author-13e6fe931c45-weight-one-external](item-lem-author-13e6fe931c45-weight-one-external)).

[F3] Under Choice and the specified size bounds, such a comparison yields the stated low-degree identifications ([lem-author-13e6fe931c45-weight-one-identifications](item-lem-author-13e6fe931c45-weight-one-identifications)).

### Proof

1.1 Let $F$ be the prime subfield of $k$. By [F1], $X$ is a qcqs $F$-scheme, and the source and target of the comparison over $F$ are the displayed objects for $X$ over $k$. Apply [F2] to obtain the natural map with cofiber supported in degrees greater than three. Naturality on $k$-schemes follows by restricting naturality on $F$-schemes. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Apply [F3] to this map. It gives an isomorphism in every degree at most three and the zero, units and Picard identifications through degree two. These are the claimed equivalence range and formula. [F3, step 1.1] ∎

### Reading limits
The article's property (2) and equation (2.3) were read. The comparison is used through the explicitly identified external input; its underlying proof is not reconstructed here.


## Smooth-point K theory class map

[Open item](item-def-smooth-point-cycle-map) · level 16

### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the support construction. Let $k$ be a perfect field, $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme, and $x$ a closed point at which $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. A perfect field is a field all of whose algebraic extensions are separable; smooth at $x$ means that $x$ has an open neighbourhood on which the structure morphism is smooth. Put $U=X\setminus\{x\}$.

Write $K(X/U)$ for the fiber of the restriction map $K(X)\to K(U)$, and $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$. The support-image group $K_0(\{x\};X)$ is the image of $\pi_0K(X/U)\to K_0(X)$. Let $p_x:\pi_0K(X/U)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Z$ be the canonical isomorphism of [prop-smooth-point-excision-purity](item-prop-smooth-point-excision-purity), normalized so that the supported class of the residue sheaf $i_*\kappa(x)$ maps to $1$, where $i:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow X$ is the closed immersion. Define

$$\varphi_x:\mathbb Z\longrightarrow K_0(\{x\};X)\subseteq K_0(X)$$

as $p_x^{-1}$ followed by the support-to-global homomorphism, with its codomain restricted to its image. In particular, $\varphi_x(n)=n[i_*\kappa(x)]$ in $K_0(X)$, where the bracket is the class of the perfect residue sheaf. The map need not be injective.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and size conventions discharge the inherited premises of the supported purity isomorphism [F1] and the support-image definition [F2] in steps 1.1–3.1. Taking an inverse isomorphism and composing the given homomorphisms adds no choice requirement.

**Given:** The field, scheme, point, choice and size conventions in the definition.

**Goal:** Establish that $\varphi_x$ is a well-defined homomorphism with the stated target and normalization.

[F1] [prop-smooth-point-excision-purity](item-prop-smooth-point-excision-purity) gives the canonical isomorphism $p_x$ under these hypotheses and identifies the inverse image of $1$ with the supported residue-sheaf class; its support-to-global image is the class of the perfect sheaf $i_*\kappa(x)$ in $K_0(X)$.

[F2] [def-support-image-groups](item-def-support-image-groups) defines $K_0(\{x\};X)$ as the image of the support-to-global homomorphism and hence as a subgroup of $K_0(X)$, without asserting injectivity.

### Justification
1.1 By [F1], $p_x$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups, so its inverse is a well-defined homomorphism from $\mathbb Z$ to $\pi_0K(X/U)$. Composing it with support-to-global gives a homomorphism to $K_0(X)$. [A1, F1, given]

2.1 By [F2], every value of this composite lies in $K_0(\{x\};X)$, so restricting its codomain defines the displayed homomorphism. Since $p_x^{-1}$ is surjective, its composite has image exactly $K_0(\{x\};X)$. [A1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F1], the value at $1$ is $[i_*\kappa(x)]$. Additivity gives the formula for every integer $n$. The construction makes no injectivity assertion about support-to-global; thus it does not assert that $\varphi_x$ is injective. This establishes the definition and its stated properties. [A1, F1, F2, step 2.1] ∎

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Then for each fixed integer $q\leq0$ used in the article there is $\ell_0(q)$ such that
$$\pi_qF^{d+\ell}_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0\qquad(\ell\geq\ell_0(q)).$$

## Componentwise curve construction and the scope of global irreducibility

[Open item](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-clopen-scope) · level 16


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension three, and let $P$ be a rank-three vector bundle on $X$. Fix a functional $s:P\to\mathcal O_X$ whose scheme-theoretic zero locus $S=V(\operatorname{im}s)$ is finite and smooth over $k$ and lies in $X_{\mathrm{sm}/k}$; $S$ may be empty. Put $Q=\ker s$ and $U=X\setminus S$. Then $Q$ is coherent on $X$, and $Q|_U$ is a rank-two vector bundle in the exact sequence $0\to Q|_U\to P|_U\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal O_U\to0$. Fix a closed subset $Z\subset U$ of codimension at least two before choosing the next functional.

Write $X=\coprod_a X_a$ for its finite clopen integral-component decomposition, and put $U_a=U\cap X_a$, $Z_a=Z\cap U_a$, $E_a=(Q|_{U_a})^\vee$ and $W_a=U_a\setminus(Z_a\cup(U_a)_{\mathrm{sing}})$. The integral construction uses on each component a finite indexed family of actual global sections of $E_a$ which generates $E_a$, spans $E_{a,x}/\mathfrak m_x^2E_{a,x}$ at every smooth closed point $x\in U_a$, and contains a controlling family on every member of a finite principal cover $W_a=\bigcup_i D(g_{a,i})$. Here each chart is a smooth affine open of $X_a$ on which $E_a$ has a frame $e_1,e_2$; its controlling family consists of that frame and all products $f_\ell e_r$, where the $f_\ell$ generate the chart's coordinate algebra over $k$. These families can be chosen for every fixed setup above by taking global generators of the coherent dual of $Q$ on each affine component and adjoining the required coordinate multiples; the chart families are restrictions of the same global indexed family on $U_a$.

There is a functional $t:Q|_U\to\mathcal O_U$ whose scheme-theoretic zero locus is a finite disjoint union of nonempty smooth geometrically integral curves of pure codimension two in $U$, one on each $X_a$, disjoint from $Z$ and contained in $U_{\mathrm{sm}/k}$. In particular it is a single such curve when $X$ is integral. The functional may depend on the fixed $Z$. A globally irreducible zero scheme cannot in general be demanded for an arbitrary fixed preceding pair $(U,Q)$ on a disconnected normal threefold, even when $P$ is trivial and its first two Chern classes vanish. This obstruction concerns that fixed pair, rather than the global theorem or every possible preceding point functional.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** AC and the field, affine finite-type pure threefold, bundle, fixed point functional, kernel, open set and prescribed avoidance locus specified in the Statement. A functional on $Q|_U$ is a section of its dual, and its zero scheme is defined locally by its coefficients. The finite point scheme is reduced with $k$-rational points because it is smooth over the algebraically closed field.

**Goal:** Establish the componentwise curve construction with all its actual hypotheses, and retain the precise disconnected fixed-pair obstruction.

[F1] [thm-author-fc2380accb47-normal-geometric-input](item-thm-author-fc2380accb47-normal-geometric-input) gives the finite clopen integral decomposition and normality's codimension-two bound for the singular locus, with regular and smooth loci equal over the perfect field $k$. [prop-swan-bertini-point-section](item-prop-swan-bertini-point-section) supplies a possible $s$ with the specified zero scheme under AC; its coherent-kernel and off-zero exactness argument applies to the fixed $s$ above.

[F2] [thm-author-27d786ff4d27-determinantal-height](item-thm-author-27d786ff4d27-determinantal-height) bounds the height of the proper ideal of maximal minors of a $2\times3$ matrix by two.

[F3] [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-dual-global-controls](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-dual-global-controls) supplies the actual finite global dual-section families, their first jets and their controlling chart restrictions. [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-chartwise-integrality](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-chartwise-integrality) applies to those families on $W_a$, using its common-core nonemptiness and fixed-locus avoidance opens, to produce a nonempty smooth geometrically integral zero curve. The AC assumption of these suppliers and the point-section supplier is carried here through [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). It is inherited at these invocations; the subsequent finite clopen assembly introduces no arbitrary-index choice requirement.

### Proof
1.1 By [F1], the components $X_a$ are finitely many clopen normal integral affine finite-type threefolds. Restriction of $s$ has zero scheme $S\cap X_a$, still finite and smooth in the smooth locus; its coherent kernel restricts to $Q|_{X_a}$ and has rank two on $U_a$. The closed $Z_a$ has codimension at least two there, and normality over the perfect field makes $W_a$ a nonempty smooth integral threefold. Apply the global dual construction of [F3] on each component with this particular $W_a$, obtaining the indexed family described in the Statement. In particular, in its construction a frame $g_{a,i}\psi_1,g_{a,i}\psi_2$ on $D(g_{a,i})$ has globally extendable controlling products even for the coordinate $1/g_{a,i}$, whose products with the frame are $\psi_1,\psi_2$. Thus the chartwise lemma in [F3] applies to the actual global family, including its common-core and avoidance conditions, and gives a functional on each $Q|_{U_a}$ with the stated zero curve. Sections on a finite disjoint union are tuples of sections, so these functionals assemble into $t$. Its zero scheme is precisely the disjoint union of the component zero schemes; smoothness, geometric integrality of each curve, pure codimension two and avoidance hold componentwise. When $X$ is integral this is a single curve. The fixed $Z$ was chosen before these parameters. [F1, F3, given]

1.2 For the obstruction take two copies of $X_0=\mathbb A_k^3$, with $P=\mathcal O^3$ and point functional $(x,y,z)$ on each. Its zero set is the reduced origin, an allowed smooth point section. On $U_0=X_0\setminus\{0\}$ let $Q_0$ be its rank-two kernel. Dualizing the locally split sequence gives $0\to\mathcal O_{U_0}\xrightarrow{(x,y,z)^t}\mathcal O_{U_0}^3\to Q_0^\vee\to0$. Every section of $Q_0^\vee$ is represented by a polynomial vector $b\in k[x,y,z]^3$: indeed $\Gamma(U_0,\mathcal O)=A$ since $A_x\cap A_y\cap A_z=A$ in the fraction field, and $H^1(U_0,\mathcal O)=0$. For the latter, use the affine cover $D(x),D(y),D(z)$: its augmented localization complex is the filtered colimit of cochain Koszul complexes on $x^n,y^n,z^n$. These are regular sequences, so the Koszul cohomology below degree three is zero (by induction, tensoring the one-element complexes and using that each next element is a nonzerodivisor on the previous quotient). Filtered colimits of modules are exact. The resulting vanishing in augmented degree two is precisely $H^1(U_0,\mathcal O)=0$. The long exact section sequence gives the claimed polynomial representative. [given, algebra]

2.1 The zero scheme of this section on $U_0$ is defined by the $2\times2$ minors of the matrix with rows $(x,y,z)$ and $b$: locally one of $x,y,z$ is invertible, and elementary row/column elimination identifies the two residual coordinates with those minors up to that unit. Its minor ideal $J\subset A$ is proper because every minor vanishes at the origin. By [F2] $J$ has a prime over it of height at most two. Such a prime is not the origin's maximal ideal of height three, so $V(J)\cap U_0$ is nonempty. Thus no functional $Q_0\to\mathcal O_{U_0}$ is nowhere zero. On two copies every global functional has zeros in both clopen components, and its zero locus is disconnected and cannot be irreducible. Trivial $P$ has $c_1=c_2=0$, so that additional article hypothesis does not remove this fixed-pair counterexample. This does not obstruct first reducing the global theorem to components, or assert that every possible preceding point section gives the same pair. [F2, step 1.2, algebra] ∎


## Cancellation at the required dimension-bounded evaluation objects

[Open item](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-evaluation-equivalence) · level 16


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the supplied derived-localization constructions. At every finite-type $X/k$ over algebraically closed $k$ with $\dim X\leq3$ and $p$ invertible, the actual map
$$\epsilon_X:(L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}\tau^{\leq3}R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(-,\mathbb Z/p))(X)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)$$
is an equivalence. Consequently $L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}(\tau^{>3}R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(-,\mathbb Z/p))(X)=0$. Here $L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}=L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}$ is ordinary source sheafification. Localization remains on the entire qcqs prime-field site, which has objects of unbounded dimension; no global vanishing or global equivalence of the unlocalized truncation map is asserted.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Choice and the stated bounds are inherited through the finite-coefficient locality, ordinary slice localization and derived-evaluation suppliers used below. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)
**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement, using the ordinary source reflector $L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}=L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}$.

**Goal:** Establish the stated exact map or descent conclusion.

[F1] The preceding three local lemmas, with the actual source locality and localization from their completed factorization supplier.

### Proof
1.1 For twisted coefficients the preceding lemmas give $\beta_X=\epsilon_X\gamma_X$, with both $\beta_X$ and $\gamma_X$ independently equivalences. Thus $\epsilon_X=\beta_X\gamma_X^{-1}$ is an equivalence. The coefficient-trivialization lemma conjugates this map to the displayed constant-coefficient map. This is cancellation of two actual equivalences, not cancellation from $\beta$ alone. [F1, A1]

2.1 The finite-coefficient descent theorem [prop-etale-cdh-descent](item-prop-etale-cdh-descent) makes $B$ ordinary cdh-local on the entire prime-field site. The primitive root is needed only on the slice in step 1.1; it does not conjugate $B_3$ to $B$ globally on that site. The source localization is an exact functor on the stable derived categories. Apply it to $\tau^{\leq3}B\to B\to\tau^{>3}B$ and evaluate at $X$; the first arrow is the displayed equivalence. Its cofiber is therefore zero. This reasoning proves the claim at the listed evaluation objects without a dimension-bounded site/cofinality assertion. [F1, step 1.1] ∎


## Actual EM orientation and projective bundle maps on that model

[Open item](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-orientation) · level 16


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. The model $\mathcal E_S$ carries a linear orientation whose first Chern class on every $Y\in\mathrm{Sm}_S$ is exactly the supplied EM class. It satisfies Annala–Iwasa’s projective bundle formula with that orientation, for all finite projective spaces and bundles. The diagonal identifications in the preceding lemma preserve these actual maps.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and fixed bounds discharge the inherited premises of the actual graded/PBF input [thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-graded-input](item-thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-graded-input) and model [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-p1-model](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-p1-model) in steps 1.1–3.1. All orientation and projective-bundle maps are those of these supplied constructions.

[F1] [thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-graded-input](item-thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-graded-input) supplies the pointed Picard map $R\Gamma_{\rm Nis}(\mathbb G_m)[-1]\to\mathbb Z(1)_{\rm mot}$ and its actual products/PBF.

[F2] [thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-p1-spectrum-input](item-thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-p1-spectrum-input) identifies a linear orientation with a Picard class lifting the unit along $[\mathcal O(1)]:\mathbb P^1\to\mathrm{Pic}$; orientable spectra are fundamental and their stable coefficient model has the same module/cohomology operations. [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-p1-model](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-p1-model) supplies that model.

### Proof
**Given:** The model $\mathcal E_S$, the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Verify orientation and the full source PBF hypotheses.

1.1 Shift the Picard map in [F1] by2. Since $\mathrm{Pic}(Y)\simeq\Omega^\infty R\Gamma_{\rm Nis}(Y,\mathbb G_m)[1]$, this gives a pointed map $\mathrm{Pic}\to\Omega^\infty A_1$. Multiplication gives the associated module map $\mathrm{Pic}\otimes\mathcal E_S\to\mathbb P^1\otimes\mathcal E_S$. On the universal $\mathcal O(1)$ this is exactly the bonding class used in the model; by its Ω-condition it restricts to the identity under P¹ suspension. Thus it is the linear orientation of [F2], with the original EM first Chern class, not an arbitrarily chosen group isomorphism. [A1, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 The actual complex PBF in [F1] is compatible with multiplication and the bonding class. Levelwise its reduced P-space formula is the source PBF for the stable coefficient model. Negative level indices that occur are zero: reduced weight-zero P¹ cohomology is zero by [F1], so looping $A_0$ by P¹ is zero, and further negative shifts remain zero. Thus the levelwise formulas also cover the low-level boundary, not only sufficiently large levels. [A1, F1, step 1.1]

3.1 Orientability and [F2] identify the space and stable coefficient models on fundamental spectra, so the formula of step 2.1 is the required equivalence of oriented motivic modules. Its products and tautological class are those in step 1.1. The general bundle version follows from the source PBF or its local descent statement, preserving the same class. No affine-torsor detection or homotopy invariance has been assumed. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎
