## Excision and the exact fixed-support cycle fiber

[Open item](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-support-fiber) · level 16


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the support and comparison constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, let $X$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension three, and let $T\subset X$ be a closed subset contained in the smooth locus $U=X_{\mathrm{smooth}}$ of $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Equip $T$ with its reduced induced structure, and put $V=U\setminus T$ and $W=X\setminus T$. Write $\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X):=\operatorname{fib}(\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)\to\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(W))$ for the unshifted cohomological support fiber. There is an actual equivalence of support fibers
$$\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X)\simeq\operatorname{fib}(\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(U)\to\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(V))\simeq z_T^3(U,\bullet)[-6].$$
Here $z_T^3(U,\bullet)$ is reindexed from homological degree $n$ to cochain degree $-n$ before shifting. Support complexes are unshifted cohomological fibers, so, for every integer $a$, $H^{a,3}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong H_{6-a}z_T^3(U,\bullet)$. These maps respect the support-to-global maps, followed by restriction to $U$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement, with the Axiom of Choice and fixed universe bounds.

**Goal:** Construct the stated actual maps and prove their consequence.

[F1] [lem-author-149a02132c3b-geometry](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-geometry), [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support), [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) and [lem-open-excision-for-support-fibers](item-lem-open-excision-for-support-fibers).

[F2] [lem-author-149a02132c3b-restriction-diagram](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-restriction-diagram) and [def-supported-higher-cycle-complex](item-def-supported-higher-cycle-complex).

[F3] The assumed Axiom of Choice, [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), discharges the inherited Choice hypotheses of the geometry, support and comparison suppliers; their constructions use the fixed size bounds.

### Proof
1.1 Under the Choice and size assumptions in [F3], the EM complex supplier gives derived Nisnevich descent. The geometry lemma supplies the actual two-open cover $X=U\cup W$ with $U\cap W=V$ and its restriction square, so that square is homotopy cartesian. Apply the completed open-excision supplier to obtain the first support equivalence, with its support-to-global compatibility. All these objects are qcqs, so the arbitrary-open extension convention is unnecessary here. [F1, F3, given]

2.1 Taking homotopy fibers is a functor on coherent arrow diagrams. Apply it to the restriction-diagram equivalence of [F2] for this $V\hookrightarrow U$. The completed fixed-support cycle definition gives the quasi-isomorphism from $z_T^3(U,\bullet)$ to the homotopy fiber of the actual unshifted homological cycle restriction. Reindex to cochains and shift by $-6$, which commutes with fibers. This gives the second equivalence and $H^a=H_{6-a}$, with the indicated projection maps. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Point-supported cycles give all-weight chain purity and low-weight zero

[Open item](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-cycle-complex) · level 16


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be a perfect field, let $V$ be a smooth affine $k$-scheme of finite type and pure dimension $d$, and let $x\in V$ be a closed point of codimension $d$. Set $L=\kappa(x)$; this is a finite separable extension of $k$, so $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is smooth of finite type over $k$. For $r\geq0$, write $C_r(T)$ for the specified unshifted EM motivic coefficient complex on $T$, put $C_r(L)=C_r(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ and $C_{r,x}(V)=\operatorname{fib}(C_r(V)\to C_r(V\setminus\{x\}))$, and let $z_x^r(V,\bullet)$ be the subcomplex of Bloch's unnormalized cycle complex generated by admissible integral cycles supported on $\{x\}\times_k\Delta_k^\bullet$.

For every $n\geq0$ one has $z_x^j(V,n)=0$ if $0\leq j<d$. If $j\geq d$, the closed immersion $x\times\Delta^n=\Delta_L^n\hookrightarrow V\times\Delta_k^n$ identifies integral generators and gives an isomorphism of chain complexes
$$z^{j-d}(\operatorname{Spec}L,\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}z_x^j(V,\bullet).$$
It preserves the actual face-intersection multiplicities and the alternating boundary signs. Consequently
$$C_{j,x}(V)\simeq C_{j-d}(L)[-2d]\quad(j\geq d),\qquad C_{j,x}(V)\simeq0\quad(0\leq j<d),$$
using the preceding actual smooth comparisons on both sides. At $j=d$, the positive cycle $[x]$ corresponds to $1\in z^0(L,0)$, with no residue-field degree factor.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and fixed compatible site and universe bounds discharge the inherited premises of the neighbourhood and actual-support comparison in [F2] at the annotated applications below. The chain, dimension and formal fiber computations introduce no additional choice principle.

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, the fixed compatible site and universe bounds, a perfect field $k$, a smooth affine finite-type $k$-scheme $V$ of pure dimension $d$, a closed point $x\in V$ of codimension $d$, its residue field $L=\kappa(x)$ finite separable over $k$, the supported-cycle and unshifted coefficient conventions in the Statement, and $j\geq0$.

**Goal:** Prove the point-cycle calculation, including the complete low-weight range and coefficients of the boundary.

[F1] [def-supported-higher-cycle-complex](item-def-supported-higher-cycle-complex) defines admissible integral supported cycles and their actual alternating face boundary. [def-bloch-higher-cycle-complex](item-def-bloch-higher-cycle-complex) supplies the same convention over $L$.

[F2] [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-neighborhood](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-neighborhood) and [thm-author-fc2380accb47-finite-type-geometric-input](item-thm-author-fc2380accb47-finite-type-geometric-input) give dimension $d+n$ of the ambient product and dimension $n$ of $\Delta_L^n$. [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-actual-support](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-actual-support) gives its actual motivic fiber comparison. The same supplier applies to the smooth zero-dimensional neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}L$ with its unique closed point and empty open complement; the source component of its arrow equivalence gives $C_q(L)\simeq z^q(\operatorname{Spec}L,\bullet)[-2q]$ for every $q\geq0$. Finite separability verifies smoothness over the same perfect base $k$.

### Proof
1.1 Every integral cycle supported in $x\times\Delta^n$ has dimension at most $n$, so its codimension in $V\times\Delta^n$ is at least $d$. Thus there are no generators in weights $j<d$, in any degree. For $j\geq d$, an integral closed subscheme of this support has ambient codimension $j$ precisely when it has codimension $j-d$ in $\Delta_L^n$. These are literally the same integral subschemes with reduced structure. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 For a face of simplex dimension $m$, the ambient admissibility bound is $\dim(Z\cap(V\times\Delta^m))\leq d+m-j$. On the support this is exactly $\dim(Z\cap\Delta_L^m)\leq m-(j-d)$. Thus admissible generators correspond in every degree. For a codimension-one face the quotient by its coordinate equation is formed on the same integral cycle on both sides. Its generic quotient-local lengths, and hence all coefficients of the face cycle, are identical. The simplex face order and signs are unchanged. The generator bijections therefore commute with the full chain differential, giving the stated chain isomorphism, rather than equality only modulo rational equivalence. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 In cochains the support complex is $z_x^j[-2j]$. Apply step 2.1 and write $[-2j]=[-2(j-d)][-2d]$. The finite residue extension $L/k$ is separable because $k$ is perfect. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a smooth affine finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension zero, and [F2]'s source comparison applies to its unique closed point and empty open complement with $q=j-d\geq0$. It identifies $z^{j-d}(\operatorname{Spec}L,\bullet)[-2(j-d)]$ with $C_{j-d}(L)$. This proves both derived statements using step 1.1 for the zero case. In degree zero and $j=d$, the same generator is $\operatorname{Spec}L$ itself, so its coefficient is $+1$, not $[L:k]$; no pushforward to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has occurred. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## The identified support fiber is the classical relative Hom before Gysin

[Open item](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-relative-gysin) · level 16


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the completed site and universe bounds of the supplied point-support and classical derived-category constructions. For $j\geq0$, the actual point-supported cohomology on $V$ is
$$H^i(C_{j,x}(V))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{DM^{\mathrm{eff},-}_{\mathrm{Nis}}}\bigl(\operatorname{cofib}(M(V\setminus x)\to M(V)),\mathbb Z(j)[i]\bigr).$$
Here the relative motive is the image of the cone of the actual open-immersion map of transfer-representable complexes. The smooth-pair Gysin input applies to this exact first arrow and identifies its cofiber with $M(\operatorname{Spec}L)(d)[2d]$. For $j\geq d$, the preceding coefficient cancellation therefore computes the group as $H^{i-2d,j-d}_{\mathrm{mot}}(L,\mathbb Z)$. No Gysin statement for singular closed subschemes or an independently chosen quotient evaluation is used.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The actual smooth finite-type pair, its identified restriction arrow, $j\geq0$, the Axiom of Choice, and the completed site and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Supply the exact classical relative-object interpretation before applying the imported Gysin triangle.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the neighbourhood and actual-support constructions in [F1]–[F2], the source contract of the classical derived-category input in [F1], and the coefficient comparison in [F3]. It is used when those supplied constructions are invoked; the Hom/fiber and shift calculations add no further choice. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-actual-support](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-actual-support) supplies an equivalence of actual EM and classical restriction diagrams. [thm-author-59b1a831fe59-classical-derived-input](item-thm-author-59b1a831fe59-classical-derived-input) supplies the natural derived Yoneda model and the A¹-local target interpretation.

[F2] [prop-smooth-pair-gysin-input](item-prop-smooth-pair-gysin-input) supplies the Gysin cofiber for this perfect-field smooth separated finite-type pair. [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-neighborhood](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-neighborhood) verifies both smoothness conditions and pure codimension.

[F3] [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-cancel-twists](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-cancel-twists) supplies the precise coefficient comparison for $j\geq d$. [def-supported-complex-indexing](item-def-supported-complex-indexing) fixes the actual fiber convention.

### Proof
1.1 In the derived category of Nisnevich sheaves with transfers, let $f:\mathbb Z_{\mathrm{tr}}(V\setminus x)\to\mathbb Z_{\mathrm{tr}}(V)$ be the actual map and let $D=\operatorname{cone}(f)$. Resolve the A¹-local coefficient by the derived-Hom model in [F1]. Yoneda evaluation on that resolution makes the two Hom complexes exactly the classical values on $V$ and $V\setminus x$, with the actual restriction between them. Applying Hom to the ordinary cone identifies $R\operatorname{Hom}(D,\mathbb Z(j))$ with the fiber of that arrow. By [F1], this is the already identified EM support fiber. Taking cohomology, A¹-locality of the target identifies these derived Hom groups with the displayed groups in $DM$, by the localization property in [F1]. No unrelated objectwise equivalences have entered this construction. [A1, F1]

2.1 In $DM$, the image of $D$ is a cofiber of $M(V\setminus x)\to M(V)$, the same first arrow as in [F2]. Its Gysin cofiber is therefore compatibly isomorphic to $M(\operatorname{Spec}L)(d)[2d]$; no uniqueness of cone is asserted from the triangulated axioms alone. Substitute this isomorphism in step 1.1. For $j\geq d$, apply [F3] to obtain exactly the stated residue-field group. This proves the Gysin/coefficient route for the actual support fiber, with its full scope checked before use. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## Negative coefficients of the actual EM projective-line model

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-a8be8a17c858-negative-model-coefficients) · level 16


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds. Let $S$ be a qcqs scheme over a field, and let $\mathcal E_S$ be the actual non-$\mathbb A^1$ EM projective-line spectrum in the supplied model. For every smooth qcqs $S$-scheme $Y$, every integer $a$ and every integer $b<0$, its actual coefficient group is zero:
$$\mathcal E_S^{a,b}(Y)=0.$$
Here the bidegree convention is $\mathcal E_S^{a,b}(Y)=\pi_{2b-a}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Sp}_{\mathbb P^1}(\mathrm{Sp})}(\Sigma^\infty_{\mathbb P^1}Y_+,\Sigma_{\mathbb P^1}^{b}\mathcal E_S)$, using the spectrum-valued coefficient stabilization. The pointed projective line uses its infinity section. This asserts vanishing for the represented model itself, rather than merely assigning the symbol for a negative motivic complex the value zero.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $S,Y,a,b$, Choice and size bounds as stated.

**Goal:** Compute the negative twists of the actual coefficient model at level zero.

[F1] [lem-author-32887006bdff-em-p1-model](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-em-p1-model) constructs an actual coefficient-valued $\Omega$-$\mathbb P^1$ spectrum whose nonnegative levels are $A_n=\mathbb Z(n)_{\mathrm{mot}}[2n]$. Its multiplication and restrictions are those of the actual EM complexes.

[F2] The actual projective-line formula of [thm-author-32887006bdff-em-graded-input](item-thm-author-32887006bdff-em-graded-input) at weight zero says that pullback $A_0(Y)\to A_0(\mathbb P^1_Y)$ is an equivalence. Its composite with restriction to infinity is identity. This is an assertion about the actual nonnegative level $A_0$, not about an unspecified negative level.

[F3] [thm-author-32887006bdff-p1-spectrum-input](item-thm-author-32887006bdff-p1-spectrum-input) gives the shift/evaluation rule for $\Omega$-$\mathbb P^1$ spectra and their spectrum-valued coefficient stabilization. Evaluation of $\Sigma_{\mathbb P^1}^{-m}\mathcal E_S$ at level zero is $\Omega_{\mathbb P^1}^{m}A_0$ for $m\geq1$. On coefficient sheaves, $(\Omega_{\mathbb P^1}A)(Y)=\operatorname{fib}(A(\mathbb P^1_Y)\to A(Y))$, with the arrow induced by infinity. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) states the inherited Choice assumption.

### Proof

1.1 By [F2], restriction $A_0(\mathbb P^1_Y)\to A_0(Y)$ is inverse to the displayed pullback equivalence. Its fiber is therefore contractible. This is natural for every $Y$ in the smooth qcqs site, so $\Omega_{\mathbb P^1}A_0=0$ as an actual sheaf of spectra. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Write $b=-m$ with $m\geq1$. By the shift/evaluation rule in [F3], the zeroth coefficient sheaf of $\Sigma_{\mathbb P^1}^{b}\mathcal E_S$ is $\Omega_{\mathbb P^1}^{m}A_0$. Iterating the reduced-loop functor on the zero sheaf in step 1.1 gives zero for this sheaf. This uses the actual negative twists of the constructed spectrum. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The suspension/evaluation adjunction identifies the mapping spectrum from $\Sigma^\infty_{\mathbb P^1}Y_+$ to that twist with the evaluation of its zeroth coefficient sheaf on $Y$, which is zero by step 2.1. All of its homotopy groups vanish, in particular degree $2b-a$ for every $a$. This proves the assertion without any dimension or Noetherian hypothesis on $S$. [F3, step 2.1] ∎


## Motivic purity and lower-weight vanishing at a smooth closed point

[Open item](item-lem-smooth-point-motivic-purity) · level 17

### Statement
Assume AC and the completed size conventions. Let $k$ be a perfect field, let $X$ be a qcqs $k$-scheme of pure finite dimension $d$, and let $x\in X$ be a closed point in its smooth locus. Write $L=\kappa(x)$, a finite separable extension of $k$. For every $i\in\mathbb Z$ and $j\geq d$ there is the purity isomorphism
$$H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X/(X\setminus\{x\}),\mathbb Z)\cong H^{i-2d,j-d}_{\mathrm{mot}}(L,\mathbb Z).$$
For every $i$ and $0\leq j<d$, the supported group on the left is zero. If the notation $C_j=0$ and $H^{i,j}=0$ is explicitly adopted for $j<0$, the displayed formula holds for every integer $j$, and the left groups vanish for all $j<d$. This extends the nonnegative EM weight system by zero; it does not assert an unstated negative-weight EM construction.

The quotient notation denotes the actual coherent restriction fiber of the completed support definition. The statement neither requires $x$ to be $k$-rational nor $X$ to be smooth away from an affine neighbourhood of $x$. No separability, perfectness, finite-type-neighbourhood or excision premise is suppressed. For $d=0$ the shift is zero and the argument includes the identity neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}L$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The stated field, scheme, point, indices and choice/size conventions. $H^{i,j}$ is cohomology in degree $i$ of the unshifted coefficient/support complex.

**Goal:** Establish the actual support purity isomorphism and the full lower-weight vanishing range with the correct $(2d,d)$ shift.

[F1] [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-neighborhood](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-neighborhood) gives the exact smooth finite-type pair and the actual EM excision equivalence.

[F2] [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-actual-support](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-actual-support) compares the actual smooth open restriction with the classical and cycle arrows for every nonnegative weight. [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-cycle-complex](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-cycle-complex) computes its fixed-point-supported chain complex, including multiplicities and low-weight zero.

[F3] [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-cancel-twists](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-cancel-twists) supplies coefficient cancellation over the perfect field for $j\geq d$. [lem-author-59b1a831fe59-relative-gysin](item-lem-author-59b1a831fe59-relative-gysin) identifies the already compared fiber with relative classical Hom and applies the completed Gysin input under its exact hypotheses.

[F4] [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support) fixes the current supported object and cohomological indexing. The negative-weight extension is the explicit zero convention in the Statement, agreeing with classical MVW Definition3.1 as recorded by [thm-author-59b1a831fe59-classical-derived-input](item-thm-author-59b1a831fe59-classical-derived-input).

### Proof
1.1 Apply [F1]. It supplies a smooth affine separated finite-type pure-$d$ neighbourhood $V$ and smooth closed point $\operatorname{Spec}L\hookrightarrow V$ of codimension $d$, and identifies the actual point-support complex on $X$ with that on $V$. Thus all subsequent operations apply to the actual restriction arrow and preserve supported cohomology. [F1, F4, given]

2.1 For $j\geq d$, [F2] identifies that arrow with its classical counterpart before taking fibers. Apply [F3] to obtain relative Hom out of the cofiber of $M(V\setminus x)\to M(V)$. The smooth-pair Gysin theorem identifies this cofiber with $M(\operatorname{Spec}L)(d)[2d]$; perfect-field cancellation then identifies its coefficient Hom group with weight $j-d$ and degree $i-2d$ on $L$. This proves the displayed formula. Independently, [F2]'s chain calculation identifies the support complex with $C_{j-d}(L)[-2d]$, confirming the same shift directly in the actual support model; no comparison is inferred just from equality of groups. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 For $0\leq j<d$, [F2] proves that the fixed-support cycle complex has no generators in any degree. Its actual support fiber is therefore zero, so every degree-$i$ group vanishes. This argument does not cancel a positive Tate twist into an undefined negative effective coefficient. If $j<0$, [F4]'s explicit zero extension makes both sides zero; if $0\leq j<d$, it also gives zero to the negative-weight residue-field side. This proves the all-integer notation version exactly under that convention, and completes the original lower-weight assertion. [F2, F4, step 1.1] ∎


## Bertini curve functional with a prescribed avoidance locus

[Open item](item-prop-bertini-curve-section) · level 17

### Statement
Assume AC and the preceding point-section construction over an algebraically closed field $k$ of any characteristic. First suppose the normal affine threefold $X$ is integral. Let $U=X\setminus S$ and $Q|_U$ be its rank-two kernel bundle. For every fixed closed subset $Z\subset U$ of codimension at least two, there exists a functional $t:Q|_U\to\mathcal O_U$ whose scheme-theoretic zero locus $Y$ is nonempty, geometrically integral, smooth over $k$, and of pure codimension two in $U$, and satisfies $Y\cap Z=\varnothing$. In particular it is smooth outside $U_{\mathrm{sing}}$, and can be chosen entirely inside $U_{\mathrm{sm}/k}$ by adjoining $U_{\mathrm{sing}}$ to the fixed avoidance set. The parameter may depend on $Z$.

For a normal affine threefold understood as a finite disjoint union of integral threefolds, apply this assertion on each clopen component: there is a single functional with zero scheme a finite disjoint union of nonempty smooth geometrically integral codimension-two curves, one per component, avoiding the prescribed $Z$. Global irreducibility is asserted in the integral case, not for every arbitrary fixed pair $(U,Q)$ on a disconnected scheme; the counterexample and exact scope correction are proved in the component lemma. The global theorem6.7 can be reduced to these components and does not require a new connectedness hypothesis. If “threefold” is interpreted as allowing additional lower-dimensional components, the curve assertion concerns its three-dimensional clopen components; the theorem's lower-dimensional cases must be handled in their own dimension, rather than falsely called curves here.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The exact preceding coherent kernel $Q$ and open $U$, the fixed $Z$, AC, and the stated component convention. A functional is a section of $(Q|_U)^\vee$ and its zero locus is defined by its coefficient ideal.

**Goal:** Supply actual nonempty irreducible Bertini curves in all characteristics with the correct avoidance quantifier and component scope.

[F1] [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-dual-global-controls](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-dual-global-controls) builds the global dual-section family and controlling charts of $W=U\setminus(Z\cup U_{\mathrm{sing}})$.

[F2] [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-common-core-nonempty](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-common-core-nonempty), [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-fixed-locus-avoidance](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-fixed-locus-avoidance) and [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-chartwise-integrality](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-chartwise-integrality) prove the simultaneous nonempty smooth geometrically integral curve using the exact Swan input.

[F3] [lem-author-27d786ff4d27-clopen-scope](item-lem-author-27d786ff4d27-clopen-scope) proves the componentwise assertion and its fixed-pair limitation. [prop-swan-bertini-point-section](item-prop-swan-bertini-point-section) supplies coherence and the preceding pair; [lem-regular-section-parameter-family](item-lem-regular-section-parameter-family) fixes the actual incidence/zero-ideal convention.

### Proof
1.1 In the integral case normality and dimension theory make $Z\cup U_{\mathrm{sing}}$ closed of dimension at most one, so its complement $W$ is a nonempty smooth integral threefold. Apply [F1] to the coherent dual extension on $X$ and this $W$. This supplies global functionals on $Q|_U$, not merely unrelated functions on its affine charts. [F1, F3, given]

2.1 Apply [F2]. The finite intersection of coefficient opens supplies a $k$-parameter avoiding the fixed bad locus, having a nonempty zero on the common core, and giving smooth geometrically integral one-dimensional zero schemes on all charts. Their common open core is dense in every chart zero, proving global irreducibility. This proves every claimed property of the scheme-theoretic zero locus $Y$. The chosen coefficient open depends on $Z$, exactly expressing $\forall Z\,\exists t$. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 In the finite clopen threefold-component case apply step 2.1 separately to each component and assemble the sections, as proved in [F3]. This gives the asserted finite union and retains codimension, smoothness and avoidance. [F3] proves why one globally irreducible zero curve cannot generally be promised for an arbitrary fixed pair under the broader disconnected convention. Thus the integral theorem and strongest componentwise construction are both retained, without turning conventional prescribed-avoidance wording into an article defect. This completes the stated scope. [F3, step 2.1] ∎

### Source/application note
The article's existence sentence and condition(4) are read in their ordinary prescribed-locus sense. Taking $Z=Y$ after choosing $t$ reverses the intended quantifiers and is not an original-paper counterexample. KM82 section3 full text was not read; the substantial external theorem actually used is Swan1974 Theorem1.4 and its explicit controlling-family proof, read in the original scans. The support consumer may use the integral case on each clopen component, or carry the finite union; it must not silently assume a globally irreducible curve on every disconnected fixed pair.


## Stage bounds imply completeness and finite multiplicative convergence

[Open item](item-lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-bounded-convergence) · level 17


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. If $X$ has finite valuative dimension, the actual motivic filtration is complete and the preceding multiplicative spectral sequence converges with
$$E_\infty^{a,b}\simeq F^{-b}_{\mathrm{mot}}K_{-a-b}(X)/F^{-b+1}_{\mathrm{mot}}K_{-a-b}(X).$$
Each $K_n(X)$ has its finite image filtration in this assertion; no splitting of that filtration is claimed.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The Axiom of Choice and the fixed size conventions of the cited constructions are inherited through [lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-page-product-transport](item-lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-page-product-transport). They discharge that supplier’s local-realization premise at its first application below. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the fixed size conventions of the cited constructions, together with a qcqs scheme $X$ over the standing field with finite valuative dimension, and the actual tower.

**Goal:** Check the stagewise hypotheses for convergence and the zero-limit assertion.

[F1] [thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-stage-bound-input](item-thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-stage-bound-input) supplies $B\geq0$ with $F^rK(X)\in\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq r-B}$. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) identifies every stage $r\leq0$ and its augmentation with $K$.

[F2] [prop-tower-exact-couple-interface](item-prop-tower-exact-couple-interface) gives finite convergence from actual high-stage vanishing and low-stage isomorphisms. [def-stable-spectra-interface](item-def-stable-spectra-interface) supplies stable limits; [lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-page-product-transport](item-lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-page-product-transport) identifies the source products and their abutment maps.

### Proof
1.1 Use the supplied realization under [A1]. Regard $X$ as a scheme over the prime field of its standing field, so the stage-bound supplier in [F1] applies to this actual restricted tower. Choose its integer $B=B(X)\geq0$. Its contract covers every qcqs scheme of finite valuative dimension, including the empty scheme. Use that bound uniformly: for any fixed integer $n$, set $U_n=\max(1,B+n+1)$ and $L_n=0$. If $r\geq U_n$ then $n<r-B$, so $\pi_nF^r=0$. If $r\leq L_n$, the map to $K$ is an equivalence by [F1]. These are precisely the high/low hypotheses of [F2], including actual vanishing of stage groups rather than only their images. The resulting additive convergence and displayed associated-graded identification are therefore those of [F2]. [A1, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 Completeness also follows from the stage bound. The sequential limit of spectra is the fiber of $1-\mathrm{shift}:\prod_{r\geq0}F^r\to\prod_{r\geq0}F^r$. For any fixed degree $n$, the groups $\pi_nF^r$ and $\pi_{n+1}F^r$ are zero for sufficiently large $r$ by step 1.1. On their finite-support products $1-\mathrm{shift}$ is an isomorphism, with inverse the finite geometric sum of the nilpotent shift. The fiber long exact sequence thus gives $\pi_n\lim_rF^r=0$ for every $n$, hence the limit spectrum is zero. Restricting to stages $r\geq0$ is cofinal for this tower limit. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 The image filtration on each $K_n$ is full for $r\leq0$ and zero for $r\geq U_n$, so it is finite. The product identification in [F2] makes the convergence in step 1.1 multiplicative with exactly this finite filtered abutment. This proves all claims. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

[Open item](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-affine-vanishing) · level 17



### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the supplied derived-localization constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $p$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $X$ an affine finite-type $k$-scheme. Then $H^a_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)=0$ for $a>\dim X$, hence for $a\geq4$ when $\dim X\leq3$. If in addition $\dim X\leq3$, let $F$ be the prime field of $k$, put $B=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(-,\mathbb Z/p)$ on the supplied qcqs prime-field cdh site, and let $L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}$ denote ordinary source sheafification. Then $(L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}\tau^{\leq3}B)(X)$ has $H^5=0$. Both assertions include singular and nonreduced schemes.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Choice and the stated bounds are inherited through the finite-coefficient locality, ordinary slice localization and derived-evaluation suppliers used below. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

**Given:** The algebraically closed field $k$, the invertible prime $p$, the affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, and the Choice, universe and site-size conventions in the statement. For the localized-complex conclusion also assume $\dim X\leq3$.

**Goal:** Prove the affine cohomological bound and the dimension-bounded localized $H^5$ vanishing.

[F1] [thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-artin-affine](item-thm-author-c5b0693f4fc3-top-torsion-artin-affine) gives the affine Artin bound for $\mu_p^{\otimes3}$ under exactly the stated field, prime and finite-type hypotheses, without smoothness or reducedness.

[F2] [lem-author-58e57d689702-coefficient-trivialization](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-coefficient-trivialization) gives the primitive-root coefficient equivalence on the slice over $X$ and its compatibility with ordinary localization units.

[F3] [lem-author-58e57d689702-evaluation-equivalence](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-evaluation-equivalence) identifies $(L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}\tau^{\leq3}B)(X)$ with $B(X)$ when $X$ is finite type over $k$ and $\dim X\leq3$.

### Proof

1.1 Choose a primitive $p$th root in $k$. The coefficient equivalence of [F2], evaluated at $X$, identifies $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)$ with $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mu_p^{\otimes3})$. Apply [F1] with twist $3$: its hypotheses hold for the stated affine finite-type $X/k$ and invertible $p$. Taking cohomology yields $H^a_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)=0$ for $a>\dim X$, in particular for $a\geq4$ if $\dim X\leq3$. [given, F1, F2, A1, choose]

2.1 Under the additional hypothesis $\dim X\leq3$, apply the actual evaluation equivalence [F3] for the ordinary source reflector. It gives $H^5((L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}\tau^{\leq3}B)(X))\cong H^5_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)=0$ by step 1.1, since $5>\dim X$. This proves the localized consequence at $X$; it does not assert a global equivalence between $B$ and its unlocalized truncation on the unbounded qcqs site. [given, F3, A1, step 1.1] ∎

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site-size and universe bounds of the supplied motivic constructions. For a line the first coefficient is the original additive EM orientation and all higher coefficients are zero.

[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated site-size and universe bounds. This supplies the foundational hypotheses of the model and Chern-coefficient constructions invoked in steps 1.1 and 2.1; no additional bundle or affine-torsor choices are made here.

**Goal:** Identify the actual coefficients and signs.

1.1 For $r>0$ the source relation is $\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^j\xi^j\pi^*\widetilde c_{r-j}(V)=0$, with $\widetilde c_0=1$. Multiply by $(-1)^r$ and set $i=r-j$. It becomes $\xi^r+\sum_{i=1}^r(-1)^i\pi^*\widetilde c_i(V)\xi^{r-i}=0$. The orientation and quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ are the same by [F1]. Hence coefficient uniqueness in [F2] gives $\widetilde c_i(V)=c_i(V)$ for $1\leq i\leq r$; both zeroth coefficients are the unit. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 For rank1, the quotient projective bundle is $Y$, its tautological quotient is $V$, and the relation is $\xi-c_1(V)=0$. It therefore identifies the first coefficient with the original orientation, which is additive under tensor product. Above positive rank the declared zero-coefficient extension agrees with the supplied convention. In rank zero the source-side series is $1$ by our explicit local extension of Definition 4.4.1, and the supplied series is $1$ by [F2]; no relation on the empty projective bundle is used. These statements identify the whole actual series, with no virtual extension used. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## The source Chern classes are the supplied projective-relation classes

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible universe and site-size bounds of the supplied motivic constructions. **Given:** $k,S,Y,V$ as stated, with constant rank $r$, the assumptions [A1], and the explicitly extended source-side coefficients.

1.1 The smooth qcqs $S$-scheme $Y$ is a qcqs $k$-scheme, so both supplied constructions apply. For $r>0$ the source relation is $\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^j\xi^j\pi^*\widetilde c_{r-j}(V)=0$, where $\pi:\mathbb P_Y(V)\to Y$ classifies rank-one quotients and $\xi$ is the first class of its tautological quotient line. Multiplying by $(-1)^r$ and setting $i=r-j$ gives $\xi^r+\sum_{i=1}^r(-1)^i\pi^*\widetilde c_i(V)\xi^{r-i}=0$. The actual orientation and quotient line agree by [F1], including after evaluation on this projective bundle, which is again smooth qcqs over $S$. Coefficient uniqueness in [F2] gives $\widetilde c_i(V)=c_i(V)$ for $1\leq i\leq r$, and the zeroth coefficients are both the unit. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 For $r=1$, the quotient projective bundle is $Y$ and its tautological quotient is $V$; the relation is $\xi-c_1(V)=0$. Thus the first coefficient is the original EM line class, additive under tensor product by [F1]. For every positive rank, the explicitly extended source polynomial and the supplied convention both have zero coefficients above rank. For rank zero, both series are $1$ by the declared local extension and [F2], without applying a relation on an empty projective bundle. This proves agreement in every nonnegative degree and rank, together with the line normalization. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## The divisor presentation and actual Picard surjection

[Open item](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-normalization-surjection) · level 17


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the motivic and support constructions. Let $k$ be an arbitrary algebraically closed field, let $X$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension three, and put $U=X_{\mathrm{smooth}}$. Let $T\subset X$ be a closed integral curve contained in $U$, with normalization $\nu:\widetilde T\to T$. Let $U_d\subset U$ be the open-and-closed relative-dimension stratum containing $T$. If $d=3$, the fixed-support group is the actual divisor quotient
$$\mathrm{CH}^3_T(U)=\operatorname{coker}(k(T)^\times\xrightarrow{\operatorname{div}_T}\bigoplus_{x\in T\ \mathrm{closed}}\mathbb Z[x]),$$
and normalization gives the surjection $q:\operatorname{Pic}(\widetilde T)\twoheadrightarrow\mathrm{CH}^3_T(U)$ induced by $[y]\mapsto[\nu(y)]$. If $d<3$, this supported group is zero. Thus the support-fiber identification gives an actual surjection from a divisible group onto $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X,\mathbb Z)$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The algebraically closed field $k$, affine finite-type threefold $X$, smooth locus $U$, closed integral curve $T\subset U$, normalization and stratum specified in the statement, the Axiom of Choice, and the fixed site and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Construct the stated actual maps and prove their consequence.

[F1] [lem-author-149a02132c3b-geometry](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-geometry) and [lem-author-149a02132c3b-support-fiber](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-support-fiber).

[F2] [lem-affine-curve-normalization-interface](item-lem-affine-curve-normalization-interface), [lem-curve-support-divisor-complex](item-lem-curve-support-divisor-complex) and [prop-affine-curve-picard-divisible](item-prop-affine-curve-picard-divisible) apply with the stated Choice and size assumptions. Their normalization, divisor and Picard constructions use the Axiom of Choice, recorded by [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). The Picard divisibility includes all nonzero integers, with no characteristic restriction.

### Proof
1.1 The curve is affine by the geometry lemma. The completed normalization supplier therefore gives finite smooth affine $\widetilde T$ over the perfect field, with every closed residue field equal to k. On the smooth pure-three-dimensional stratum containing T, the completed divisor supplier gives its displayed quotient and the actual pushforward $q$. It proves that pushforward sends principal divisors to the length-order divisor downstairs, with residue degrees one; hence the map descends and is surjective, even if T is singular. The other open-and-closed strata do not meet T and contribute zero support. [F1, F2]

2.1 If T instead lies on a smooth stratum of dimension $d<3$, there are no codimension-three cycles in degree zero on that stratum; hence $z_T^3(U,0)=0$ and $H_0z_T^3(U)=0$. This branch is zero and already divisible. In the dimension-three case the completed affine Picard supplier makes $\operatorname{Pic}(\widetilde T)$ divisible by every nonzero integer, including the characteristic when the characteristic is positive. Compose $q$ with the actual supported-comparison isomorphism of the support-fiber lemma, obtaining the claimed surjection to supported motivic cohomology. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Normal dimension strata and the actual residue class model

[Open item](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata) · level 17

### Statement
Assume AC and the completed size conventions. Let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type scheme over a perfect field $k$, of dimension $d$. Its finitely many integral components are clopen. For $0\leq e\leq d$, let $X_e$ be the union of its dimension-$e$ components. These form a finite clopen partition, each nonempty $X_e$ is pure-dimensional, and
$$K(X)\simeq\prod_eK(X_e),\qquad K_0(X)\cong\bigoplus_eK_0(X_e).$$
Restriction is the displayed equivalence. Extension by zero along $i_e:X_e\hookrightarrow X$ is exact on perfect complexes and induces the corresponding zero-in-other-factors inclusion. For a smooth closed point $x\in X_e$, the current point class $\varphi_x(1)$ is this zero extension of the perfect residue-sheaf class. Under the completed affine $K_0$ comparison, it is the classical Euler class $[\kappa(x)]$ used for the source cycle map; no opposite sign or degree factor is inserted.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The stated normal affine scheme, field, AC and current nonconnective perfect-complex model.

**Goal:** Supply finite dimension bookkeeping and actual point-class/model compatibility.

[F1] [thm-author-fc2380accb47-normal-geometric-input](item-thm-author-fc2380accb47-normal-geometric-input) gives finite clopen integral components in the Noetherian case.

[F2] [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) gives exact-category functoriality; [prop-perfect-k-localization-input](item-prop-perfect-k-localization-input) gives the support-category fiber sequence for a qcqs scheme with quasi-compact open complement.

[F3] [lem-koszul-point-support-class](item-lem-koszul-point-support-class), [def-smooth-point-cycle-map](item-def-smooth-point-cycle-map) and [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge) identify the point with the positive residue-sheaf class and identify its affine perfect-complex class with the alternating finite-projective Euler class. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) supplies inherited Choice.

### Proof
1.1 Finite type over a field makes $X$ Noetherian and gives finitely many irreducible components. Normality and [F1] make them disjoint and open as well as closed. Group them by dimension to obtain the finite clopen $X_e$; each is affine and all its components have dimension $e$. [F1, given]

2.1 A sheaf complex on a finite clopen union is exactly a tuple of complexes on its pieces. Perfection is local, so zero extension is exact, preserves perfect objects, restricts to identity on its own piece and to zero on the others. The supported category for a clopen piece is its perfect category. Apply [F2] to that piece and its clopen complement. The resulting fiber sequence is split by zero extension of the complement, and restrictions identify it with the split product sequence. Iteration gives the displayed equivalence of actual K-spectra and hence the direct-sum formula on $\pi_0$. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F3], the current point map sends $1$ to the globally defined perfect sheaf $i_*\kappa(x)$, and every local Koszul representative resolves that same object. On an affine scheme its bounded finite-projective representative maps, under the actual affine bridge, to its alternating Euler class. This is the classical $[\kappa(x)]$ convention in $K_0$ of projective modules. Zero extension of that sheaf agrees literally with the same residue sheaf on $X$ and has zero restriction to every other clopen piece, by step 2.1. These facts establish model and sign compatibility, without identifying coherent G-theory with perfect K-theory in a singular ambient scheme. [F3, step 2.1] ∎


## The globally normalized first-layer Picard map is determinant

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fixed compatible site and universe size bounds for the constructions below. On the big Nisnevich site of qcqs $k$-schemes for any field $k$, identify $\Omega^\infty\operatorname{gr}^1K$ with the line-bundle stack $B\mathbb G_m$ by the actual EM weight-one comparison. Then the actual map $q_1:S=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^1K\to B\mathbb G_m$ is the perfect-complex determinant/Picard map on the rank-zero fiber. In particular it determines global determinant line classes, including on singular nonaffine schemes.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds are retained when applying [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage) in [F3] to the actual rank fiber and its homotopy groups in steps 1.1 and 2.1. [F2] [thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-determinant-one-type-input](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-determinant-one-type-input) supplies the extended determinant/Picard construction, local $K_0=\mathbb Z$, local $K_1=\mathbb G_m$ by the actual determinant, and fully faithful classification of pointed connected1-types in any infinity-topos. [lem-unit-section-of-k-one-determinant](item-lem-unit-section-of-k-one-determinant) identifies the loop of the line-class construction with its unit section.

[F3] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage) identifies $S$ as the actual rank-zero space. [lem-nisnevich-line-bundle-torsors](item-lem-nisnevich-line-bundle-torsors) gives the line-frame-torsor convention for $B\mathbb G_m$.

### Proof
**Given:** The actual maps on the stated big Nisnevich site, AC and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Extend the completed smooth-site Postnikov argument using its exact premises, not local Picard-group agreement.

1.1 The sheaf $S$ is connected: every rank-zero perfect class is locally zero on affine free-complex charts, where its object class is its alternating free rank. Its fundamental-group sheaf is $\mathbb G_m$ through determinant by the local-ring calculation in [F2]; positive homotopy groups of the rank fiber agree with those of K by [F3]. Thus its pointed first Postnikov truncation is $B\mathbb G_m$, with its identification fixed by the actual determinant construction. These are local statements about sheaves of K-spaces and their isomorphisms, not statements that the global Picard group vanishes. [A1, F2, F3]

1.2 The composite $q_1\kappa:B\mathbb G_m\to B\mathbb G_m$ is a pointed stack map. By [F2] it is classified by a sheaf-group endomorphism of $\mathbb G_m$. This group is represented on the qcqs $k$-site by $\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$; Yoneda and the Laurent-unit calculation over a field make the endomorphism $t\mapsto t^n$. The normalization of [F1] on $\mathcal O(-1)$ over $\mathbb P^1_k$ gives $\mathcal O(-n)=\mathcal O(-1)$ in $\operatorname{Pic}(\mathbb P^1_k)=\mathbb Z$, hence $n=1$. The same universal test applies on this larger site, so $q_1\kappa$ is identity as an actual pointed stack map. [F1, F2]

2.1 On fundamental-group sheaves, $\kappa$ is the unit section, and the determinant of that section is identity by [F2]. Hence $\kappa_*$ is the inverse of the determinant isomorphism on local K₁. Step1.2 forces $(q_1)_*$ to be determinant. Maps from the connected sheaf $S$ into the1-type $B\mathbb G_m$ factor through $\tau_{\leq1}S$; the full faithfulness in [F2] now identifies $q_1$ with the actual determinant/Picard map. Evaluate this equality of stack maps at any $X/k$ to retain its full line-bundle descent data. No inference from agreement of Picard groups on affine opens occurs. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds. For every qcqs scheme $X$ over a field and every integer $i\geq1$, the specified natural stable pointed universal bundle maps $c_{i,n}:BGL_n\to K(D_i,2i)$ extend by the formal Gillet completion construction to pointed operations on the local perfect K-space model. Here $D_i$ denotes the weight-$i$ coefficient complex, and $K(D_i,2i)=\Omega^\infty(D_i[2i])$ is its derived Eilenberg target. The construction uses the local equivalence $\Omega BQ\mathcal P\simeq\underline{\mathbb Z}\times\mathbb Z_\infty BGL$, projection away from trivial rank, completion of the specified stable class, and $\mathbb Z_\infty K(D_i,2i)\simeq K(D_i,2i)$. It is natural in the coefficient maps and restrictions and retains the original universal bundle classes.

For the actual EM complexes, the supplied non-$\mathbb A^1$ $\mathbb P^1$-model and its actual orientation provide these projective-relation classes on $\mathrm{Vect}_{n,X}$, with their stability. The natural full affine comparison, including degree zero, identifies the sheaf Q-space model with the local sheaf model of the specified perfect K-space. Compose with the canonical perfect K-space local-replacement unit to obtain the actual operations on global perfect K-spaces and their restriction arrows. This applies on the small site of opens of $X$ and on its smooth big site, with Zariski or Nisnevich topology and the same stalkwise local homotopy convention for the source and derived Eilenberg targets. The affine-basis comparison is valid before and after this local replacement; no identification of ordinary and hypercomplete localizations is required. It requires neither global bundle-difference representatives for perfect $K_0$ nor $\mathbb A^1$-invariance of EM.

For every closed support $Z\subseteq X$, taking the homotopy fibers of these pointed restriction arrows gives the supported operations and their forget-support squares. For a non-quasi-compact open complement, extend the actual K-spaces and coefficient targets by the inverse limits over its quasi-compact open subsets, using the declared support convention; the compatible operations extend by the same limits. When the complement is quasi-compact, identification with category-defined supported perfect K-theory uses the separate localization input when that interpretation is needed. No such category comparison is inferred for an arbitrary open complement. The index-zero convention is separately $C_0=1$ as an unpointed constant. It is the constant term of the total Chern series, not a pointed map to the additive coefficient target; no index-zero support-fiber operation is supplied by this pointed construction.

Index zero is treated separately in the source as unpointed constant one and cannot be substituted into this additive pointed-fiber argument. The formal-series constant remains one. ### Statement
For the source’s linearly oriented homotopy-commutative non-A¹ motivic ring spectrum with PBF, the actual map $\mathrm{Gr}_n\to\mathrm{Vect}_n$ induces the universal Chern-coordinate isomorphism
$$E^{*,*}(\mathrm{Vect}_{n,+}\otimes R)\cong E^{*,*}(R)\lbrack\!\lbrack c_1,\ldots,c_n\rbrack\!\rbrack$$
for every homotopy-cocommutative motivic coring $R$. This is the map-induced identification of Theorem4.4.6/Corollary4.4.7, with finite Grassmannian formula Lemma4.4.4 and Corollary4.4.5. Taking products of two classifying stacks is allowed by applying the coring version successively; restriction to their finite Grassmannian approximations jointly detects the universal coefficients.
The variables have bidegrees $(2j,j)$ and stabilize under adding a trivial line. For the completed EM model, assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied model and negative-coefficient constructions. Under these premises negative coefficient weights are zero in every cohomological degree. Hence for any fixed target Chern weight $i$, only monomials of total weight at most $i$ can occur; the relevant mapping-space $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ systems stabilize as both ranks exceed $i$. This last finiteness consequence is used explicitly in the local Cartan proof to rule out a phantom term.

Import the actual Vect/Grass cohomology comparison and finite Grassmannian formula from the precisely cited source. Theorem 4.4.6 is formulated after the source's elementary-excision localization; Corollary 4.4.7 is the stated cohomological consequence under PBF. No bundle-group presentation or affine Picard-group detection substitutes for the map-induced comparison.

[A1] The assumed [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and fixed size bounds discharge the actual model and negative-coefficient premises in [F2]–[F3], first used in step 1.1. [F1] The external Annala–Iwasa input above gives the actual universal-coordinate comparison, including the coring version. Its Choice and universe assumptions are inherited here. It computes the reduced projective-line loop of $A_0$, rather than identifying formal zero complexes with negative twists without an argument.


**Given:** The external input and its hypotheses; for the local consequence, a qcqs field-scheme $S$, its actual EM model, inherited Choice and universe bounds, and an integer $i\geq0$.

**Goal:** Verify the bounded-weight consequence and finite transition ranges for the universal one-factor and two-factor mapping spaces used by the consumers.

### Proof
1.1 In the coefficient convention of [F3], mapping homotopy degree $u$ into the weight-$i$ target is cohomological bidegree $(2i-u,i)$. The vanishing is about the actual represented model by [F3]. The general coring formula in [F1] remains valid, but negative-weight vanishing for an arbitrary coring is not being inferred from vanishing over $S$. [A1, F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Apply the finite basis formula in [F1] to $G(n,N)$, and successively to $G(n,N)\times_S G(m,M)$ using the same actual class maps. The latter mapping groups in homotopy degree $u$ have a finite additive basis $c^\alpha d^\beta$ with $|\alpha|\leq N-n$ and $|\beta|\leq M-m$; their coefficients are $\mathcal E_S^{2(i-w)-u,i-w}(S)$ for $w=w(\alpha)+w(\beta)$. For any surviving monomial, step 1.1 gives $w\leq i$, hence $|\alpha|\leq i$, $|\beta|\leq i$, and every variable index occurring is at most $i$. Consequently $N-n\geq i$ and $M-m\geq i$ include every potentially nonzero monomial. The one-factor assertion follows by omitting $\beta$. [Open item](item-lem-smooth-leading-cycle-normalization) · level 18


### Statement
Assume AC and the compatible universe and Nisnevich-site size bounds of the supplied constructions, and use the specified perfect-complex nonconnective K-spectrum and its actual EM motivic filtration. For a smooth finite-type scheme $X$ over a field $k$, the weight-zero projection is the locally constant rank function. The first-stage projection gives
$$\widetilde K_0(X)=\pi_0F^1K(X)\longrightarrow H^{2,1}(X)=\operatorname{Pic}(X),\quad x\longmapsto c_1(x)=\det(x),$$
and
$$K_1(X)=\pi_1F^1K(X)\longrightarrow H^{1,1}(X)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times,\quad z\longmapsto\det(z).$$
Here reduced $K_0$ means the kernel of the locally constant rank map, component by component; determinant on perfect complexes uses its alternating graded-line convention.

For the supported assertion let $k$ be perfect (in particular the article's algebraically closed field qualifies), let $U$ be smooth of finite type and pure dimension three over $k$, and let $i:C\hookrightarrow U$ be an integral codimension-two closed curve. Neither smoothness nor normality of $C$, nor global quasi-projectivity of $U$, is required. Write
$$K_C(U)=\operatorname{fib}(K(U)\to K(U\setminus C)),\quad F^j_CK(U)=\operatorname{fib}(F^jK(U)\to F^jK(U\setminus C)).$$
The actual augmentation $\epsilon_2:F^2_CK(U)\to K_C(U)$ is an equivalence, and the supported layer is canonically
$$\pi_0\operatorname{gr}^2_CK(U)=H_C^{4,2}(U)=H_0z_C^2(U,\bullet)=\mathbb Z[C].$$
This is the supported cycle group, not the image of $[C]$ in ambient Chow cohomology. For $\xi\in\pi_0F^2_CK(U)$ let $E$ denote its augmented class in the actual supported $K_0$, using support-category localization. Then its specified stage-to-layer projection is
$$p_2(\xi)=\left(\sum_n(-1)^n\ell_{\mathcal O_{U,\eta}} H^n(E)_\eta\right)[C],\qquad \eta=\operatorname{generic}(C).$$
The notation for a virtual class $E$ means the additive extension of this formula from supported perfect complexes. Equivalently $p_2\circ(\pi_0\epsilon_2)^{-1}$ on supported $K_0$ is alternating generic length times the positive cycle. In particular $i_*\mathcal O_C[0]$ maps to $+[C]$, and every closed-point-supported class maps to zero.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the stated universe and site-size bounds, the smooth scheme/field hypotheses in each part, and the current augmented tower, support and K-model contracts. The supported part uses a perfect field only; it does not extend the imported classical supported comparison to an imperfect field.

**Goal:** Normalize the actual maps, including the domain and positive generator of the supported weight-two projection.

[A1] The stated Choice and size assumptions are inherited from the determinant and weight-one suppliers in [F1] at step 1.1. They cover the enhanced K-model, the compatible big Nisnevich stack comparison, and the specified small-site frame-torsor and derived-sections constructions. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-zero-projection-rank](item-lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-zero-projection-rank) and [lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-first-chern-and-k-one-determinant](item-lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-first-chern-and-k-one-determinant) identify the actual weight-zero and weight-one maps, using the canonical EM comparisons and the actual determinant map supplied before the Postnikov identification. The determinant input now specifies true/enhanced cofiber coherence and its Waldhausen-to-current-model bridge; arbitrary ordinary-triangle-diagram functoriality is not used.

[F2] [thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison) supplies the actual natural augmented filtered bridge to classical slice K-theory, with its exact arbitrary-field source-coverage qualification. [lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-augmented-filtered-support-transport](item-lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-augmented-filtered-support-transport) transports its support fibers, projections and augmentations. Its coefficient is restriction to $G_0(k(\eta))=\mathbb Z$ by dimension, with positive residue-field generator.

[F6] [lem-adjudicate-f6007757a8ac-raw-simplicial-descent](item-lem-adjudicate-f6007757a8ac-raw-simplicial-descent) proves the canonical raw-to-Zariski-derived-sections unit on possibly nonseparated smooth finite-type schemes. Apply the natural graded comparison of [F2] on the affine Zariski basis and pass to derived sheaf sections; the actual unit identifies those sections with the original raw Bloch complexes. This gives the same open-restriction-compatible graded comparison globally. The exact source-version qualification of [F2], including EM v1 Remark3.6’s then-in-preparation input, remains binding.

### Proof

1.1 Apply [F1] to $X$. It proves the rank formula and the identifications of the first-stage degree-zero and degree-one groups, then identifies their actual projection with the determinant/Picard map and its unit map. The Chern sign is fixed there by $1-[\mathcal O(-1)]\mapsto+c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; it is not chosen from an abstract isomorphism with Picard groups. This proves the first three assertions, with all their field hypotheses. [F1, given, A1]

1.2 For $U,C$, apply the natural graded comparison in [F2], with the raw global interpretation justified in [F6], to $U$ and its open complement and take their restriction fiber. [F3] makes the supported weights zero and one zero. The cofiber sequences for the two successive supported transitions therefore identify $F^2_CK$ with $F^0_CK=K_C$ by the actual augmentation. The same comparison gives the target $\mathbb Z[C]$ with the shift stated in [F5]. This proves the precise domain and target of $p_2$, independently of its as yet uncomputed coefficient. [F2, F3, F5, F6, given]

2.1 Choose an affine open neighbourhood $V\subset U$ of $\eta$. It is smooth quasi-projective over the perfect field; $C\cap V$ is integral of codimension two, although it may be singular. Apply [F4] on this pair. By [F2] its actual inverse-augmentation slice map is the transport of the current map of step 1.2 restricted to $V$: the transition, augmentation and layer-projection squares commute. Thus its positive generic coefficient on the augmented class is the actual K-to-G generic restriction followed by dimension. [F2, F4, step 1.2]

3.1 By [F5] that generic coordinate equals the finite alternating length sum in the Statement, in the current K-model. Neither this coordinate nor its sign changes on restricting from $U$ to $V$. By [F3] restriction on the bottom supported cycle target sends $[C]$ to $[C\cap V]$ and is an isomorphism. Equality of the coefficient after this restriction therefore proves the displayed formula on $U$, by [F5]'s detection lemma. The length of the residue-field stalk of $i_*\mathcal O_C[0]$ is one and its cohomological degree is zero; closed-point-supported stalks vanish at $\eta$. This proves the positive and zero tests. All asserted formulas are now proved for the actual projection and its inverse-augmentation version. [F3, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Motivic graded pieces and spectral sequence

[Open item](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) · level 18


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible size conventions of the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be any field. For a qcqs $k$-scheme $X$ and every $r\geq0$, the actual source graded comparison gives a natural exact triangle
$$F^{r+1}_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z(r)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)[2r].$$
The associated multiplicative spectral sequence has
$$E_2^{a,b}=H^{a-b,-b}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\Longrightarrow K_{-a-b}(X),\qquad d_s:E_s^{a,b}\to E_s^{a+s,b-s+1}.$$
The right-hand symbol denotes the filtered abutment when convergence holds. In the full-plane E2 formula the complex of a negative weight is explicitly extended by zero, agreeing with the source’s vanishing negative graded terms. Products add bidegrees and agree with the source motivic cup products; the differential satisfies the Leibniz rule with sign $(-1)^{a+b}$ for a class in bidegree $(a,b)$. If $X$ has finite valuative dimension, the filtration is complete and the spectral sequence converges multiplicatively to $K_*(X)$ with its finite image filtration and associated graded groups as stated by the tower interface.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The Axiom of Choice and fixed compatible size conventions discharge the selected local perfect-$K$-theory realization premise when invoking the actual tower and its source inputs. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration)

**Given:** Choice, these size conventions, an arbitrary specified field $k$, and the actual motivic tower and complex functors restricted from its prime field, with their specified products. The specified $k$ overrides the default algebraic-closedness convention.

**Goal:** Establish the natural triangles, products, page indices and finite-valuative-dimension convergence for this field.

[F1] [prop-tower-exact-couple-interface](item-prop-tower-exact-couple-interface) applies to any decreasing tower with the stated graded equivalences. [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) supplies the cohomology notation. The quotient-map and index calculations in [lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-graded-comparison](item-lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-graded-comparison) and [lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-index-calculation](item-lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-index-calculation) record the corresponding formal calculations for the standing-field restriction; below they are repeated on the specified restriction.

[F2] [lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-graded-products](item-lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-graded-products) and [lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-page-product-transport](item-lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-page-product-transport) record how the actual graded multiplication and the exact-couple comparison identify products, signs and filtered abutment maps. The source data on the larger category used below are supplied directly by [F4].

[F3] [lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-bounded-convergence](item-lem-author-74a9c17e63f1-bounded-convergence) gives the formal high/low-stage and zero-limit argument from a stagewise bound and constant nonpositive stages. [def-valuative-dimension-and-boundedness](item-def-valuative-dimension-and-boundedness) defines valuative dimension using the affine rings of the underlying scheme.

[F4] [thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input](item-thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input) supplies the actual natural graded algebra comparison and source tower pairings on all qcqs schemes over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$. [thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-stage-bound-input](item-thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-stage-bound-input) supplies the qualitative bound for those schemes of finite valuative dimension. Their Choice-qualified realization is the one in [A1]; neither input assumes algebraic closedness.

### Proof
1.1 Under [A1], let $F$ be the prime field of $k$. Composing structure morphisms gives a functor from qcqs $k$-schemes to qcqs $F$-schemes: underlying schemes are unchanged, and every $k$-morphism is an $F$-morphism. By the local definitions, both the tower and motivic complexes are restrictions along this functor. Restrict the actual natural equivalence $\gamma_r$ and the stage and quotient maps of [F4]. Cofibers of functor diagrams are evaluated objectwise, so the canonical quotient followed by $\gamma_r$ gives the asserted triangle. For $r<0$, the constant nonpositive stages make the transition an equivalence, including at $r=-1$, hence its cofiber is zero. This proves the negative-weight zero convention without a new geometric hypothesis. [A1, F1, F4]

2.1 Apply the generic tower construction in [F1] to these actual diagrams. Its initial page is $\pi_{-a-b}\operatorname{gr}^{-b}$, and its cochain shift calculation is $\pi_n(C[2r])=H^{2r-n}(C)$. Substitution of $r=-b$ and $n=-a-b$ gives $2r-n=a-b$. Thus the page is the stated motivic group, with zero terms for negative weights. The tower reindexing gives the displayed differential; its target has total homotopy degree $-(a+s)-(b-s+1)=-a-b-1$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Suppose $X$ has finite valuative dimension. Forgetting its $k$-structure changes neither its affine opens nor their rings, so the dimension condition in [F3] holds for its prime-field scheme. Apply the stage bound in [F4] to this very tower and choose its integer $B=B(X)\geq0$. For any integer $n$, put $U_n=\max(1,B+n+1)$ and $L_n=0$. If $r\geq U_n$, then $n<r-B$, so $\pi_nF^r=0$; if $r\leq L_n$, the map to $K(X)$ is an equivalence. The generic tower interface in [F1] therefore gives finite convergence and its associated-graded identification, with the actual image filtration. This argument also applies to the empty scheme under the same source contract. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Restrict the coherent filtered products of [F4] along the same functor. On the associated graded, their transport along the restricted $\gamma_r$ is precisely the source motivic product. The source and local exact couples use the same restricted stage/cofiber maps and connecting homomorphisms. The identity on stages and the actual graded comparisons therefore commute with all exact-couple arrows. Deriving couples takes images and kernel quotients functorially, so induction identifies all pages and differentials, as in the construction recorded in [F2]. Transport the source pairings through these page identifications. Products add bidegrees by step 2.1. The derivation sign is the parity of homotopy degree $-a-b$, hence $(-1)^{a+b}$; the shifts by $2r$ are even. This establishes the claimed products and Leibniz rule using actual source pairings. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Repeat the zero-limit calculation of [F3] on these restricted diagrams. The sequential limit is the fiber of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on $\prod_{r\geq0}F^r$. In each degree $n$, both $\pi_nF^r$ and $\pi_{n+1}F^r$ are eventually zero by step 2.2. Each of the resulting products of groups has only finitely many possibly nonzero factors; the transition shift is nilpotent, so $1-\mathrm{shift}$ is invertible by a finite geometric sum. The fiber exact sequence makes every homotopy group of the limit zero, hence the limit spectrum is zero. The image filtration is full for $r\leq0$ and zero for $r\geq U_n$. The transported source abutment pairings in step 3.1 identify its products with those in $K_*(X)$. This proves completeness and multiplicative convergence with the full stated scope. [F2, F3, step 3.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Affine étale vanishing and the actual localized evaluation

[Open item](item-prop-affine-artin-vanishing) · level 18


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds of the supplied derived-localization constructions. Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $X/k$ affine of finite type with $\dim X\leq3$, and $p$ an invertible prime. Then $H^a_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)=0$ for $a\geq4$. Let $F$ be the prime subfield of $k$. Use the site of all qcqs $F$-schemes in the fixed universe, with topology generated by Nisnevich covers and abstract blowup families whose closed immersion and proper morphism are finitely presented. Write $L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}=L^{o,F}_{\mathrm{cdh}}$ for ordinary $D(\mathbb Z)$-valued cdh sheafification. The natural map induced by truncation is an equivalence:
$$(L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}\tau^{\leq3}R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(-,\mathbb Z/p))(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p).$$
For this affine $X$, its left side has $H^5=0$. The evaluation equivalence itself holds for every finite-type $X/k$ of dimension at most three, including nonaffine $X$. Thus the full characteristic-zero affine-threefold application in Proposition 2.6 is retained. Localization is on the entire qcqs prime-field site; the equivalence is asserted at these evaluation objects, without asserting a global equivalence on that site.

### Statement references
[lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site)

[lem-author-58e57d689702-evaluation-equivalence](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-evaluation-equivalence)

[lem-author-58e57d689702-affine-vanishing](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-affine-vanishing)

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe and site-size bounds are inherited by the finite-coefficient locality, slice localization and derived-evaluation constructions. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

**Given:** The field, prime, scheme and size conventions of the statement; affineness is needed for the cohomological vanishing, while the evaluation comparison only needs finite type and dimension at most three.

**Goal:** Establish the actual evaluation equivalence and the affine $H^a$ and localized $H^5$ vanishings.

[F1] [lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site) fixes the entire qcqs prime-field cdh site and its finitely presented abstract blowup generators.

[F2] [lem-author-58e57d689702-coefficient-trivialization](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-coefficient-trivialization) compares constant and weight-three Tate coefficients on the slice over $X$, commutes restriction with ordinary localization including its units, and identifies the actual induced maps at $X$.

[F3] [lem-author-58e57d689702-independent-gamma](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-independent-gamma) supplies the full canonical equivalence $\gamma_X:\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)/p\simeq(L^F_{\mathrm{cdh}}\tau^{\leq3}B_3)(X)$, where $B_3=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}(-,\mu_p^{\otimes3})$. Independently, [lem-author-58e57d689702-topweight-map](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-topweight-map) supplies the full canonical equivalence $\beta_X:\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)/p\simeq B_3(X)$ and the identity $\beta_X=\epsilon_X^{(3)}\gamma_X$ for the actual map $\epsilon_X^{(3)}$ induced by truncation. Both equivalences apply to finite-type $X/k$ with $\dim X\leq3$ without affineness, smoothness or reducedness.

[F4] [lem-author-58e57d689702-evaluation-equivalence](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-evaluation-equivalence) packages cancellation and the coefficient change as the exact constant-coefficient evaluation equivalence for ordinary source sheafification, with the same Choice and size hypotheses.

[F5] [lem-author-58e57d689702-affine-vanishing](item-lem-author-58e57d689702-affine-vanishing) supplies the affine Artin bound $H^a_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)=0$ for $a>\dim X$, including singular and nonreduced affine finite-type schemes.

### Proof
1.1 Work first with any finite-type $X/k$ of dimension at most three, viewed as a qcqs $F$-scheme on the site in [F1]. By [F3], $\beta_X=\epsilon_X^{(3)}\gamma_X$, and both $\beta_X$ and $\gamma_X$ are full equivalences. Cancellation gives $\epsilon_X^{(3)}=\beta_X\gamma_X^{-1}$ as an equivalence. The argument uses the actual source maps and their factorization. [given, A1, F1, F3]

2.1 Choose a primitive $p$th root in the algebraically closed field $k$. By [F2], the slice coefficient equivalence conjugates the twisted evaluation map in step 1.1 to the constant-coefficient map displayed in the statement, compatibly with ordinary localization units. Equivalently this is the precise cancellation result [F4]. It holds for nonaffine as well as affine $X$ in this dimension range. The root is used only over $X$; no root in $F$ or change to a dimension-bounded localization site is required. [A1, F2, F4, step 1.1, choose]

3.1 If $X$ is affine, [F5] gives $H^a_{\mathrm{et}}(X,\mathbb Z/p)=0$ for $a>\dim X$, hence for every $a\geq4$. Taking $H^5$ in the equivalence of step 2.1 gives zero on its left side since $5>\dim X$. This includes the characteristic-zero affine threefold used in the original Proposition 2.6. [given, A1, F5, step 2.1] ∎

The evaluation argument uses the separate canonical comparison in Theorem 4 of the [published Oberwolfach report](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/52244), at an invertible prime, through the existing top-weight supplier. The report's characteristic-prime square and its Remark 5 duality display are not premises here. The exact factorization is checked against [Elmanto-Morrow v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.08463v1), especially the proof of Theorem 4.33(1).

The original article's passage from affine Artin vanishing to a global truncation equivalence on the entire qcqs site remains a recorded proof-step gap. The present proof instead establishes the needed evaluation comparison before using the affine vanishing bound. The substantial published comparisons and Artin theorem remain external inputs with the reading limits recorded above; this draft supplies no new proof or acceptance of those theorems.

## Actual exact-sequence Whitney and filtered-root formula on singular qcqs schemes

[Open item](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-whitney) · level 18


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site-size and universe bounds of the supplied motivic constructions. Let $X$ be any qcqs $k$-scheme over a field, and let $0\to V^{\prime}\to V\to V^{\prime\prime}\to0$ be an exact sequence of constant-rank finite locally free sheaves. Then $c_t(V)=c_t(V^{\prime})c_t(V^{\prime\prime})$. If $V$ has a filtration by subbundles with line quotients $L_s$, then $c_t(V)=\prod_s(1+c_1(L_s)t)$. These refer to the supplied projective-relation classes, not to an assumed Chern polynomial of a K-zero equality.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. These discharge the foundational hypotheses of the EM comparison and Chern constructions used in steps 1.1–3.1.

[F1] [thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-non-a1-whitney-input](item-thm-author-4f94f7982b0d-non-a1-whitney-input) supplies Lemma4.4.3(ii)–(iii) for a homotopy-commutative linearly oriented non-A¹ motivic ring spectrum with PBF over any qcqs derived base $S$, evaluated on $Y\in\mathrm{Sm}_S$.

[F2] [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-relation-comparison](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-relation-comparison) supplies the actual EM class comparison for a field $k$, qcqs $k$-base $S$ and smooth qcqs $S$-scheme $Y$, under [A1]. Its source-side conventions are zero coefficients above rank and $\widetilde c_t(0)=1$. [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes) gives the corresponding supplied zero-bundle convention and invariance under bundle isomorphism.

### Proof

**Goal:** Apply the full source theorem within its real hypotheses.

## Divisibility survives the quotient and the support image
