### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the motivic and support constructions. Let $k$ be an arbitrary algebraically closed field, let $X$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension three, put $U=X_{\mathrm{smooth}}$, and let $T\subset X$ be a closed integral curve contained in $U$. The group $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is divisible, and its image under the actual support-to-global map into $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is divisible. No injectivity of that map is required.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The algebraically closed field $k$, affine finite-type threefold $X$, smooth locus $U$, closed integral curve $T\subset U$, Axiom of Choice, and fixed site and universe bounds in the statement.

**Goal:** Construct the stated actual maps and prove their consequence.

[F1] [lem-author-149a02132c3b-normalization-surjection](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-normalization-surjection) supplies an actual surjection from a divisible group onto the supported group under exactly the stated geometry, field, Choice and size hypotheses. This includes the zero case on a lower-dimensional smooth stratum. Choice is inherited from its normalization and Picard constructions; [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) records that premise.

[F2] [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support) gives the actual support-to-global homomorphism under the stated Choice and size conventions.

### Proof
1.1 For any surjection $q:D\to A$ with D divisible, fix $a\in A$ and positive n. Choose $d\in D$ with $q(d)=a$, then $e\in D$ with $ne=d$. Thus $nq(e)=a$. Negative integers are handled by negation. Apply this to the actual surjection in the preceding lemma (or to its zero case). This proves divisibility of the supported group. [F1, construct]

2.1 Let $s:A\to G$ be the support-to-global homomorphism fixed by the completed support definition. For $s(a)$ and positive n, choose b in A with $nb=a$ from step 1.1. Then $ns(b)=s(a)$, so every element of the image has an n-th root in that same image. Again handle negative n by negation. This proves the asserted image divisibility without identifying the support group with its image. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Levine–Weibel relations split on clopen pure-dimensional components

[Open item](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-quotients) · level 18


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed size conventions of the supplied constructions. Fix a perfect field $k$. For a finite clopen union $T=\coprod_\alpha T_\alpha$ of normal affine finite-type $k$-schemes, each of pure dimension $e\geq1$, the completed pure-dimensional Levine–Weibel definition gives
$$\operatorname{CH}^{LW}_0(T)\cong\bigoplus_\alpha\operatorname{CH}^{LW}_0(T_\alpha),$$
with the component inclusions induced by zero extension of point cycles. For a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $d\geq1$ which need not be pure, Krishna's exact dimension-$d$ convention has generators only on the regular parts of its $d$-dimensional components. In this convention
$$\operatorname{CH}^{d}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(X)\cong\operatorname{CH}^{LW}_0(X_d).$$
The left notation denotes precisely Krishna's Section2.1 group, not a redefinition of the completed pure-dimensional local item. Its source “singular locus” in this nonpure convention includes all lower-dimensional clopen components, even if they are geometrically smooth.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The stated perfect field, finite-type schemes, Choice and size bounds, the clopen decomposition and the exact Cartier-curve/semilocal-unit/principal-divisor relations of [def-levine-weibel-zero-cycles](item-def-levine-weibel-zero-cycles).

**Goal:** Match the actual source quotient, including which smooth points are permitted.

[F1] [lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata) gives the finite clopen pieces and equality of their intrinsic smooth/regular loci over the perfect field.

[F2] [thm-author-80f982ded420-quotient-cycle-map-input](item-thm-author-80f982ded420-quotient-cycle-map-input) records Krishna's actual Section2.1 top-dimensional generator convention.

[F3] [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) supplies the Choice assumption inherited by the completed cycle definition and normal-component supplier. Affine finite type over $k$ gives quasi-projectivity, and normality gives reducedness. The equal pure dimensions in the first assertion make the completed cycle definition applicable to every piece and to their finite union.

### Proof
1.1 The free point-cycle group is the direct sum of those on the clopen pieces. A Cartier curve $C\subset T$ splits as $C\cap T_\alpha$, a finite clopen decomposition; each nonempty piece is reduced purely one-dimensional. No-component-in-the-forbidden-set and the regular-sequence condition at forbidden points are checked in the same local rings, so each is a relative Cartier curve on its piece. The semilocal unit data splits as a product of the corresponding unit data, and its componentwise divisor is the sum of the same divisors supported on the pieces. Conversely a Cartier curve and a unit on one clopen piece define the identical allowed curve and relation on $T$. Thus the relation subgroup is exactly the direct sum of the component relation subgroups. Quotienting proves the first isomorphism. [F1, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 In the nonpure normal case [F2] excludes all lower-dimensional components from its permitted generator locus and includes them in the forbidden set. Since these components are clopen, a Cartier curve with a component on one of them would have that entire curve component contained in the forbidden set, which is not allowed. Every allowed curve is therefore contained in $X_d$. Its remaining local regular-sequence conditions and divisors are exactly those in the completed definition on $X_d$. Both the free generators and the relation subgroup coincide, proving the second isomorphism. This identifies the source convention without altering the completed pure-dimensional definition. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎

## The actual determinant fiber is a natural retract of the rank-zero K-space

[Open item](item-lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber) · level 18


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fixed compatible site and universe size bounds for the constructions below. On the Nisnevich site of qcqs schemes over a field, put $S=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^1K$, $B=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{gr}^1K\simeq B\mathbb G_m$ and $T=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^2K$. The actual first projection $d:S\to B$ is determinant. Its actual pointed section $\kappa:B\to S$ sends a line to $[L]-1$. There is a natural equivalence of spaces over $B$, $T\times B\simeq S$, with map $(t,b)\mapsto i(t)+\kappa(b)$, and consequently a pointed retraction $r:S\to T$ of $i:T\to S$. On underlying K-classes, $r(s)=s-\kappa(d(s))$. For every qcqs $Y$, both $\pi_0T(Y)\to\pi_0S(Y)$ and $\pi_0S(Y)\to K_0(Y)$ are injective. The space $T$ is the actual homotopy fiber, retaining determinant-trivialization data.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds are retained for [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection) in [F1] and [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage) in [F2]. Step 1.1 uses their actual rank and determinant maps and homotopies; step 3.1 uses their evaluated fiber identifications. The translation and retraction arguments then use these supplied maps. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection) supplies the actual pointed maps $d,\kappa$ and the pointed homotopy $d\kappa\simeq\mathrm{id}_B$, not merely equality on Picard groups. [prop-motivic-weight-one](item-prop-motivic-weight-one) identifies $B$ as the actual Picard 1-type with its additive structure.

[F2] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) makes $d$ a map of grouplike infinite-loop spaces and $T$ its homotopy fiber. [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage) identifies $S$ with the rank fiber over the discrete locally constant rank sheaf.

### Proof
**Given:** These actual sheaf maps, their homotopies, AC and the existing universe bounds.

**Goal:** Construct the fiber retraction and prove injectivity without a fiber-preservation assertion for a plus map.

1.1 Define $\Phi:T\times B\to S$ by addition of $i(t)$ and $\kappa(b)$. Additivity of $d$ and the chosen homotopy in [F1] make this a map over $B$. On the fiber over any generalized point $b$, translation by $\kappa(b)$ is an equivalence from the fiber over zero to the fiber over $b$; its inverse is translation by $-\kappa(b)$, using that same homotopy. Therefore $\Phi$ is an equivalence over $B$. This argument is internal to the sheaf infinity-topos and hence is natural on restriction. It does not require $\kappa$ to be additive. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Take $r$ to be the first component of $\Phi^{-1}$. Its underlying expression is $s-\kappa(d(s))$ with the nullhomotopy furnished by $d\kappa\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Because $\kappa$ is pointed, the restriction over zero identifies $ri$ with identity, including the fiber path. This constructs an actual homotopy-fiber map rather than choosing a lift of an object class. [step 1.1]

3.1 Evaluation of the section makes $\pi_1S(Y)\to\pi_1B(Y)$ surjective. The fiber exact sequence thus makes $\pi_0T(Y)\to\pi_0S(Y)$ injective; equivalently use the product equivalence. The rank target in [F2] is discrete on derived sections, so its $\pi_1$ vanishes and the rank-fiber sequence makes $\pi_0S(Y)\to K_0(Y)$ injective. No assertion about generation by global bundles is involved. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

Removing that split constant summand shows that restriction on the reduced groups $\widetilde H^{2i-1,i}(B_{n+1})\to\widetilde H^{2i-1,i}(B_n)$ is also surjective. The classical coefficient target is Nisnevich local, so adjunction for sheafification computes the same mapping groups on the Nisnevich site. [F1, F2]

2.1 Let $T_n$ be the derived spectrum of pointed maps from $B_n$ to the coefficient spectrum $H(\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm cl}[2i])$; equivalently use reduced free abelian chains of $B_n$ and their derived Hom complex into $\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm cl}[2i]$. Then $\Omega^\infty T_n=\operatorname{Map}_*(B_n,Y_i)$ and $\pi_1T_n=\widetilde H^{2i-1,i}(B_n)$. The stabilized general-linear source of [F1] is this colimit: each simplex is a finite tuple of matrices and lies in some $GL_n$, so filtered colimits commute with the finite products in the nerve, and local sheafification preserves this colimit. The actual coherent colimit defining $B_\infty$ then gives $\operatorname{Map}_*(B_\infty,Y_i)\simeq\Omega^\infty\varprojlim_n T_n$. In this enhanced setting the product-difference triangle of [F3], or its derived-complex version, therefore gives the exact sequence $\prod_n\pi_1T_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n\pi_1T_n\to\pi_0\varprojlim_nT_n\to\prod_n\pi_0T_n$, where $s((a_n))_n=f_n(a_{n+1})$ for the restriction maps $f_n$. This uses genuine coherent mapping objects before taking homotopy classes. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The first arrow in step 2.1 is surjective. Given $(b_n)$, set $a_1=0$ and recursively choose $a_{n+1}$ with $f_n(a_{n+1})=a_n-b_n$, using the surjectivity in step 1.1 and [A1]. Then $(1-s)(a_n)=(b_n)$. Exactness now makes $\pi_0\varprojlim_nT_n\to\prod_n\pi_0T_n$ injective; its image lies in the compatible inverse limit. This proves the claimed injectivity and kills precisely the potential $R^1\varprojlim$ ambiguity, rather than assuming compatible finite-rank homotopies. [A1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Two existing stable maps with equal finite-rank restrictions consequently belong to the same component of $\operatorname{Map}_*(B_\infty,Y_i)$, so there is a pointed homotopy in the sheaf category itself. The splitting into the basepoint value and the reduced mapping object also shows that finite-rank equality of their unpointed coefficient classes suffices when both maps are pointed. Transport by the equivalence in [F1] proves the assertion for the EM target. A homotopy of sheaf maps restricts as a single natural transformation to the site over any smooth base, hence gives a homotopy of its entire restriction diagram after derived sections. This claims existence, not a contractible space of choices, and uses no affine-$K_0$ detection. [F1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎


## Smooth point classes lie in the top filtration piece

[Open item](item-lem-smooth-point-filtration) · level 19

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the support construction. Let $k$ be a perfect field, let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme of pure finite dimension $d$, and let $x$ be a closed point in the smooth locus of $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Put $U=X\setminus\{x\}$. A perfect field is one whose algebraic extensions are separable; smoothness at $x$ means that $x$ has a neighbourhood smooth over $k$.

Write $K(X/U)$ for the restriction fiber $\operatorname{fib}(K(X)\to K(U))$ and $F^jK(X/U)$ for the corresponding fiber at motivic filtration stage $j$, using the extension to arbitrary open subsets in [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support). Then the stage-to-$K$ map induces a surjection
$$\pi_0F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X/U)\longrightarrow\pi_0K(X/U).$$
Consequently, with $K_0(\{x\};X)$ the image of $\pi_0K(X/U)\to K_0(X)$ and $F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ the image of $\pi_0F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to K_0(X)$,
$$K_0(\{x\};X)\subseteq F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X).$$
In particular, the smooth-point class map of [def-smooth-point-cycle-map](item-def-smooth-point-cycle-map) has image in this filtration subgroup. No injectivity of either support-to-global map is asserted.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The field, scheme, point, choice and size hypotheses in the statement. Set $T=\{x\}$ and write $F^j_TK(X)=F^jK(X/U)$. A decreasing filtration is a sequence of spectra with compatible transition maps $F^{j+1}\to F^j$; its $j$th graded spectrum is their cofiber. A fiber is the homotopy pullback over the zero spectrum.

**Goal:** Prove surjectivity from supported stage $d$ to supported $K_0$, and then the global image containment.

[F1] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) gives a functorial tower with $F^0K\simeq K$. [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support) defines its supported stages as restriction fibers, including the homotopy-limit extension when $U$ is not quasi-compact, and identifies $\pi_0$ of the shifted supported weight-$j$ motivic spectrum with $H^{2j,j}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X,\mathbb Z)$.

[F2] [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) gives, naturally for every qcqs scheme and $j\geq0$, the graded triangle with third term $\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}[2j]$. [lem-filtered-support-exactness](item-lem-filtered-support-exactness) identifies the graded spectrum of a supported tower with the fiber of the corresponding graded restriction arrow. The stable spectra interface [def-stable-spectra-interface](item-def-stable-spectra-interface) supplies the finite limits and cofiber–fiber identification used for the open-set homotopy-limit extension.

[F3] [lem-smooth-point-motivic-purity](item-lem-smooth-point-motivic-purity) gives $H^{i,j}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X,\mathbb Z)=0$ for every integer $i$ and $0\leq j<d$ under the given perfect-field, smooth-point, choice and size hypotheses.

[F4] [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) gives exactness of $\pi_0F^{j+1}_T K(X)\to\pi_0F^j_T K(X)\to\pi_0\operatorname{gr}^j_TK(X)$. [def-support-image-groups](item-def-support-image-groups) and [def-smooth-point-cycle-map](item-def-smooth-point-cycle-map) specify the global image subgroup and the smooth-point map.

### Proof
**Proof technique:** Use lower-weight supported motivic vanishing to lift successively through the finite sequence of filtration stages, then apply the natural support-to-global square.

1.1 For each $j\geq0$, the natural graded triangle in [F2] applies on $X$ and on every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq U$. Taking the homotopy limit of the triangles over these $V$ preserves fiber sequences: limits commute with the finite limits defining fibers, and in spectra cofibers and fibers differ by suspension. Thus the graded triangle also holds for the explicitly extended values on $U$. Taking the fiber of the graded restriction arrow, [F2] identifies $\operatorname{gr}^j_TK(X)$ with the shifted supported weight-$j$ motivic spectrum. Hence
$$\pi_0\operatorname{gr}^j_TK(X)\cong H^{2j,j}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X,\mathbb Z).$$
The identification uses the actual coherent restriction maps, not merely separate isomorphisms of groups. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 For $0\leq j<d$, [F3] makes the right side in step 1.1 zero. Exactness in [F4] therefore makes each transition $\pi_0F^{j+1}_T K(X)\to\pi_0F^j_T K(X)$ surjective. [F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Composing these finitely many surjections gives a surjection $\pi_0F^d_TK(X)\to\pi_0F^0_TK(X)$. When $d=0$ this is the identity, the empty composite. The natural stage-zero equivalences on $X$ and on the opens used to define $U$ identify $F^0_TK(X)$ with $K(X/U)$; compatibility of transitions identifies the composite with the stated stage-to-$K$ map. This proves the supported surjectivity. [F1, step 2.1]

4.1 The support-to-global maps and stage-to-$K$ maps form a commutative square by the functorial fiber construction. Given an element of $K_0(T;X)$, choose a supported $K_0$ representative and lift it to supported stage $d$ by step 3.1. Its image in global stage $d$ maps to the original element of $K_0(X)$. The definition of the global image filtration therefore gives the containment. The image of the point class map is $K_0(T;X)$ by [F4], yielding the final assertion. This completes the proof. [F1, F4, step 3.1] ∎

## Weight-one K-one projection is determinant

[Open item](item-lem-k-one-projection-determinant) · level 19


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fixed compatible site and universe size bounds for the big Nisnevich comparison and its small-site derived sections. Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $X$ be a normal quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme. For the specified motivic filtration on the nonconnective $K$-theory of perfect complexes, the actual augmentation induces an isomorphism
$$\pi_1F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_1(X).$$
Under this isomorphism and the natural identification $H^{1,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times$, the actual first-stage projection
$$\pi_1F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow H^{1,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$$
is the determinant homomorphism $\det_X:K_1(X)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times$. It is surjective, with section taking a unit $u$ to the $K_1$-class of multiplication by $u$ on $\mathcal O_X$.

Here normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated means that intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact. A global unit is a global regular function with a multiplicative inverse. The spectrum $K(X)$ is the specified nonconnective $K$-theory of perfect complexes, $K_1(X)=\pi_1K(X)$, and the augmentation is the first transition $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^0_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=K(X)$. The first-stage projection is induced by the actual map from that stage to its weight-one graded piece, whose first homotopy group is $H^{1,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. This includes the article's normal finite-type schemes and its full normal qcqs scope; no finite-type, Noetherian or dimension hypothesis is used.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An algebraically closed field $k$, a normal qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, the Axiom of Choice, and the fixed site-size bounds in the Statement.

**Goal:** Prove the augmentation isomorphism, identify the actual first-stage projection with determinant, and exhibit its unit section.

[F1] The filtration has a natural identification $F^0_{\mathrm{mot}}K(Y)=K(Y)$ for each qcqs $k$-scheme $Y$, and its transitions are natural in $Y$ ([def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration)). The stated qcqs hypothesis puts $X$ in this category ([def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions)).

[F2] For every such $Y$ the natural graded triangle at weight zero is $F^1K(Y)\to K(Y)\to\mathbb Z(0)_{\mathrm{mot}}(Y)$. Its homotopy long exact sequence identifies $\pi_n\mathbb Z(0)_{\mathrm{mot}}(Y)$ with $H^{-n,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}(Y,\mathbb Z)$ ([prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence)). The latter group vanishes in negative cohomological degrees ([prop-motivic-weight-zero](item-prop-motivic-weight-zero)).

[F3] Under AC and the stated site-size bounds, the weight-one comparison naturally identifies $H^{1,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(Y,\mathbb Z)$ with $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)^\times$ for qcqs $Y$; the bounds fix small sites and universe sizes for derived sections ([prop-motivic-weight-one](item-prop-motivic-weight-one), [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites)). The graded triangle at weight one gives the actual projection, naturally in $Y$ ([prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence)).

[F4] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection) identifies the actual map $\Omega^\infty F^1K\to\Omega^\infty\operatorname{gr}^1K\simeq B\mathbb G_m$ with the perfect-complex determinant/Picard map on the big Nisnevich site of every qcqs field-scheme, including its actual loop map and descent data. Its Choice and compatible site/universe bounds are those assumed here. At $X$, loops at the trivial line in $B\mathbb G_m(X)$ are its global units. Thus taking $\pi_1$ uses the actual determinant rather than agreement of Picard groups on affine opens.

[F5] Under AC, for every qcqs scheme $Y$ there is a natural determinant homomorphism $\det_Y:K_1(Y)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)^\times$. The natural map $s_Y(u)=[\mathcal O_Y\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal O_Y]$ satisfies $\det_Y\circ s_Y=\operatorname{id}$ ([lem-unit-section-of-k-one-determinant](item-lem-unit-section-of-k-one-determinant)). AC is the assertion that every family of nonempty sets admits a choice function ([math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)).

### Proof

1.1 Apply the weight-zero long exact sequence in [F2] to $X$. The two groups surrounding $\pi_1F^1K(X)\to K_1(X)$ are $H^{-2,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ and $H^{-1,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$, both zero by [F2]. Hence the actual augmentation is an isomorphism, in the full stated qcqs scope. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 By [F4], the first-stage projection on spaces is the actual determinant/Picard map. Evaluate its pointed natural map at $X$ and take $\pi_1$. Its target identifies with the global units by [F3] and the trivial-line automorphism description in [F4]. Under the augmentation isomorphism in step 1.1 the resulting map is precisely $\det_X:K_1(X)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times$, with the actual automorphism normalization in [F5]. This identifies the specified projection, without choosing a smooth locus or a global bundle representative. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 For every global unit $u$, [F5] gives $\det_X([\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal O_X])=u$. Combining this identity with step 2.1 proves surjectivity and supplies exactly the asserted unit section, using step 1.1 for the domain identification. [F5, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

## High filtration vanishing

[Open item](item-lem-high-filtration-vanishing) · level 19

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension $d$ over a field $k$, and let $i$ and $j$ be integers. For the motivic filtration of [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration),
$$\pi_jF^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0\quad\text{if }i\geq d\text{ and }j<0,$$
and
$$\pi_0F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0\quad\text{if }i>d.$$
Here $F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ is the $i$th spectrum in the decreasing motivic tower of nonconnective $K$-theory, and $\pi_j$ is its $j$th stable homotopy group. These are assertions about the stage groups themselves, not merely their images in $K_j(X)$. The field is arbitrary; in applying the fixed-field definitions below, take the standing field to be $k$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a Noetherian finite-dimensional $k$-scheme $X$, and integers in either of the two stated ranges.

**Goal:** Prove the two stage-group vanishing assertions.

[F1] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) supplies the actual decreasing tower on qcqs schemes over an arbitrary specified field, with the stated choice assumption. A Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

[F2] For $r\geq0$, [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) identifies the actual cofiber of $F^{r+1}_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ with $\mathbb Z(r)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)[2r]$. By [lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index](item-lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index), its $j$th homotopy group is $H^{2r-j,r}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$.

[F3] [thm-motivic-dimension-vanishing](item-thm-motivic-dimension-vanishing) gives $H^{a,r}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)=0$ for $r\geq0$ and $a>r+d$. Its equicharacteristic hypothesis holds because $X$ is a scheme over a field, hence over that field's prime subfield.

[F4] [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) gives exactness of $\pi_jF^{r+1}\to\pi_jF^r\to\pi_j\operatorname{gr}^r$ for a decreasing filtered spectrum. [prop-filtration-eventual-vanishing](item-prop-filtration-eventual-vanishing) gives, for each fixed $j$, vanishing of $\pi_jF^N_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ at all sufficiently large $N$; it also records vanishing of the stages on the empty scheme.

### Proof
1.1 If $X$ is empty, the stage spectra vanish by [F4], and both assertions follow. Otherwise $d\geq0$. Since a Noetherian scheme is qcqs and its structure map factors through the prime field of $k$, all hypotheses of [F1]–[F4] apply. [F1, F3, F4, given]

2.1 Fix $j<0$ and $i\geq d$. For every integer $r\geq i$, we have $r\geq0$ and $2r-j>r+d$, because $r-d\geq0$ and $-j>0$. By [F2] and [F3], $\pi_j\operatorname{gr}^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0$. Exactness in [F4] therefore makes each transition $\pi_jF^{r+1}_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to\pi_jF^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ surjective. [F2, F3, F4, given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Choose $N\geq i$ large enough that $\pi_jF^N_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0$, using [F4]. The finite composite of the surjections from stage $N$ to stage $i$ is surjective, so its target is zero. This proves the negative-degree assertion. [F4, step 2.1]

4.1 Now let $j=0$ and $i>d$. For every $r\geq i$, we have $r\geq0$ and $2r>r+d$. The same application of [F2]–[F4] makes every transition $\pi_0F^{r+1}_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to\pi_0F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ surjective. Eventual vanishing in degree zero supplies an $N\geq i$ with zero source; composing down to stage $i$ proves $\pi_0F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0$. Thus both stated assertions hold. [F2, F3, F4, given, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Filtration projections and multiplication

[Open item](item-prop-filtration-product-projection) · level 19

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix the compatible universe and site-size bounds of the specified constructions. Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme, and $i,j\geq0$. Write $F^r=F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ for the $r$th stage of the specified multiplicative motivic filtration of the nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum of perfect complexes. Let $M_r=\mathbb Z(r)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)[2r]$, regarded as a spectrum via the Eilenberg–Mac Lane construction, and let $p_r:F^r\to M_r$ be the actual graded projection. Then the following square commutes up to the coherent homotopy supplied by the filtered multiplication:

$$\begin{array}{ccc} F^i\wedge F^j&\xrightarrow{p_i\wedge p_j}&M_i\wedge M_j\\ \downarrow\!\mu_{i,j}&&\downarrow\!\smile\\ F^{i+j}&\xrightarrow{p_{i+j}}&M_{i+j}. \end{array}$$

Here $\wedge$ is the smash product of spectra; the right vertical map is the product transported from the graded motivic algebra. The corresponding product on homotopy groups is the motivic cup product.

Suppose additionally that $k$ is algebraically closed, $X$ is normal, and the fixed universe size bounds for the small Nisnevich sites and derived sections in the low-stage comparison hold. For $0\leq i,j\leq2$, the canonical maps identify $\pi_0F^i$ and $\pi_0F^j$ with their images $F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ and $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ in $K_0(X)$. Under these identifications, taking degree-zero products gives the commutative square

$$\begin{array}{ccc} F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)&\xrightarrow{p_i\otimes p_j}&H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^{2j,j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\!\smile\\ \pi_0F^{i+j}&\xrightarrow{p_{i+j}}&H^{2i+2j,i+j}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z). \end{array}$$

The left vertical map multiplies the unique stage representatives. In particular, for $a\in F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ and $b\in F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$, their stage representatives multiply to a class $c\in\pi_0F^{i+j}$ mapping to $ab\in K_0(X)$, and $p_{i+j}(c)=p_i(a)\smile p_j(b)$. This assertion does not require $p_{i+j}$ to descend to the image group when $i+j>2$.

Normal means that every local ring of $X$ is an integrally closed domain. The image group $F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of $\pi_0F^r\to K_0(X)$; motivic cohomology is $H^{a,r}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)=H^a(\mathbb Z(r)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X))$. Choice means that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A field $k$, a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme $X$, nonnegative integers $i,j$, Choice, and the stated compatible size bounds. For the second square, also assume that $k$ is algebraically closed, $X$ is normal, and $i,j\leq2$.

**Goal:** Prove the actual graded multiplication square and its degree-zero form, preserving the stage target and the original normal qcqs scope.

[F1] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) defines the actual tower, augmentation and products by restriction from the prime subfield of $k$. [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) defines the motivic complexes by the same restriction and identifies $\pi_0M_r$ with $H^{2r,r}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$.

[F2] The graded-construction clause of [thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input](item-thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input) supplies, on every qcqs $\mathbb Q$-scheme or $\mathbb F_p$-scheme, the actual equivalences $\operatorname{gr}^rF\simeq\mathbb Z(r)_{\mathrm{mot}}[2r]$ and their graded algebra structure. Its induced product is the source motivic cup product. This clause uses Elmanto–Morrow v1, Section 2.2 and Definitions 4.9/4.23, without any finite-valuative-dimension hypothesis.

[F3] [lem-image-filtration-products](item-lem-image-filtration-products) supplies compatibility of stage products with both augmentation and graded projection. It requires no injectivity for the stage-level identity.

[F4] [lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber](item-lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber) supplies, on every qcqs field-scheme $X$, the actual spaces $S=\Omega^\infty F^1$, $T=\Omega^\infty F^2$, and injective maps $\pi_0T(X)\to\pi_0S(X)\to K_0(X)$. Its actual pointed determinant section makes $\pi_1S(X)\to\pi_1B(X)$ surjective for $B=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{gr}^1F$, which kills the boundary obstructing degree-zero injectivity of the fiber map. Only these degree-zero conclusions are needed here. Choice, as in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), and the compatible size bounds discharge the inherited local-realization assumptions of these suppliers.

### Proof
1.1 Let $P\subseteq k$ be the prime subfield, either $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$. Composing $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ leaves the underlying qcqs scheme unchanged, and every $k$-morphism is a $P$-morphism. Apply [F2] on this prime-field category under the assumed Choice and compatible size bounds. By [F1], restriction along this forgetful functor gives exactly the specified tower and motivic complexes on $k$-schemes. Restriction evaluates the same natural diagrams at the same objects and maps, preserving their cofiber projections, graded equivalences, multiplication and coherent homotopies. Thus this applies for arbitrary $k$. [F1, F2, given]

1.2 In stage zero the augmentation is identity by [F1]. In stages one and two, [F4] gives its injectivity on $\pi_0$, since $\pi_0\Omega^\infty F^r(X)=\pi_0F^r(X)$ and the composite of the two injections there is the stage-two augmentation. Each augmentation is surjective onto its image by definition, so its corestriction is an isomorphism for $0\leq r\leq2$. This applies in particular on every normal qcqs $X$ over the algebraically closed field in the second assertion, including its finite-type special case. [F1, F4, given]

2.1 The cofiber compatibility in [F3] gives the coherent multiplication square from $F^i\wedge F^j$ through the graded pieces to $\operatorname{gr}^{i+j}F$. Transport its graded terms along the actual equivalences restricted in step 1.1. Their graded algebra structure in [F2] identifies the transported product with the specified motivic cup product, proving the first square. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 For $x\in\pi_0F^i$ and $y\in\pi_0F^j$, their stage product lies in $\pi_0F^{i+j}$. Applying the first square to their representing sphere maps gives $p_{i+j}(xy)=p_i(x)\smile p_j(y)$. The augmentation sends $xy$ to the product of the augmented classes in $K_0(X)$. These pairings are bilinear, hence factor through tensor products of abelian groups. [F1, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 Under the second assertion's hypotheses, step 1.2 supplies unique representatives $x,y$ for any $a\in F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ and $b\in F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. Define the left vertical map on $a\otimes b$ by $xy$ and extend bilinearly, using the inverse source-group isomorphisms from step 1.2. Step 3.1 proves that $c=xy$ maps to $ab$ in $K_0(X)$ and satisfies $p_{i+j}(c)=p_i(a)\smile p_j(b)$, proving the second square. The target remains $\pi_0F^{i+j}$; no injectivity or descent for that output stage is required when $i+j>2$. [F3, step 3.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Graded filtration projections

[Open item](item-def-filtration-projections) · level 19


### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix compatible site and universe size bounds for the specified motivic and weight-one constructions. Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme, and $i\geq0$. Write $F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ for stage $i$ of the specified motivic filtration of the nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum of perfect complexes. The **stage projection**
$$p_i:\pi_0F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$$
is induced by the map from that stage to its graded cofiber $\mathbb Z(i)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)[2i]$. Here $H^{a,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is degree-$a$ cohomology of the specified weight-$i$ motivic complex. Both the filtration and the complex are restricted from the prime field of $k$.

The image filtration group $F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of the stage-to-$K(X)$ homomorphism on $\pi_0$; write $q_i:\pi_0F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ for its canonical corestriction. If $k$ is algebraically closed and $X$ is normal, then for $0\leq i\leq2$ the map $q_i$ is an isomorphism. For these indices the same symbol $p_i$ also denotes the transported homomorphism
$$F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\xrightarrow{\ q_i^{-1}\ }\pi_0F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\xrightarrow{\ p_i\ }H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z).$$
This convention covers every normal qcqs $k$-scheme, including the normal finite-type case. It requires no finite-type, Noetherian or dimension bound. At stage zero, the equivalence $F^0_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=K(X)$ already identifies the stage and image for every $X$ above. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Finite type means that $X$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. Choice means that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the small sites and ambient universes of the specified constructions.

For $i=3$ the stage projection has domain $\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$. The low-stage identification above does not itself identify this domain with $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$; image-domain notation at stage three requires a separate justification.

[def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration)

[def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology)

[thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input](item-thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input)

[lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber](item-lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber)

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A field $k$, a qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, Choice, compatible site and universe size bounds, and $i\geq0$. For the image-domain convention in stages one and two, also assume that $k$ is algebraically closed and $X$ is normal.

**Goal:** Define the actual stage projections and justify their low-stage image-domain convention throughout the original normal qcqs scope.

[F1] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) supplies the actual tower, compatible augmentations, the stage-zero equivalence with $K(X)$ and the image groups. It and [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) specify restriction from the prime field. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) supplies the assumed Choice premise for the perfect-complex realization and site constructions.

[F2] [thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input](item-thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input) supplies the natural equivalence $\operatorname{gr}^iF_{\mathrm{mot}}K\simeq\mathbb Z(i)_{\mathrm{mot}}[2i]$ on qcqs prime-field schemes under the given Choice and size assumptions. The complexes and graded cofibers are those of the same actual tower; no convergence hypothesis is needed. [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) specifies their cohomology notation.

[F3] [lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber](item-lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber) applies to all qcqs schemes over a field under Choice and the existing size bounds. For $S=\Omega^\infty F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K$, $B=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{gr}^1F_{\mathrm{mot}}K$ and $T=\Omega^\infty F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K$, it supplies the actual pointed section $\kappa:B\to S$ of $d:S\to B$ and injections $\pi_0T(X)\to\pi_0S(X)\to K_0(X)$. The section is a map of spaces and need not be additive. The second injection uses the actual rank fiber over a discrete target.

[F4] [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) gives homotopy exactness and the criterion for a stage projection to descend to its image: the kernel of the augmentation must lie in the kernel of the projection. In particular an injective augmentation suffices.

### Justification
1.1 Let $\mathbb F$ be the prime field of $k$. Forgetting to $\mathbb F$ preserves the underlying qcqs scheme and takes each $k$-morphism to an $\mathbb F$-morphism. Under the Choice and size assumptions in [F1], restrict the natural graded equivalence in [F2] along this forgetful functor. By the definitions in [F1], its source and target are exactly the specified tower's graded cofiber and the specified shifted motivic complex on $X$. This applies over every field $k$ without a finite-type or convergence hypothesis. [F1, F2, given]

1.2 Apply [F3] to the given qcqs $X$. Evaluating $d\kappa\simeq\mathrm{id}$ at $X$ makes $\pi_1S(X)\to\pi_1B(X)$ surjective. The actual fiber sequence therefore has zero boundary into $\pi_0T(X)$, and its transition $\pi_0F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to\pi_0F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ is injective. The first-stage augmentation is injective by the rank-fiber assertion in [F3]. Their composite is the second-stage augmentation by [F1], so it too is injective. Stage zero has its augmentation equivalence. Thus every $q_i$ for $0\leq i\leq2$ is injective and is surjective onto its image by definition; in particular this applies on the stated normal qcqs schemes. [F1, F3, F4, given]

2.1 The cofiber sequence $F^{i+1}_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to\operatorname{gr}^iF_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ and step 1.1 give the stage-to-complex map. Applying $\pi_0$ identifies its target with $H^0(\mathbb Z(i)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)[2i])=H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. This defines the displayed homomorphism for every $i\geq0$, naturally under pullback. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Each $q_i$ in step 1.2 is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Compose its inverse with the projection in step 2.1 to obtain the displayed image-domain homomorphism. It is the unique map whose composite with $q_i$ is the stage projection, since $q_i$ is surjective. Equivalently, [F4]'s kernel criterion holds because the augmentation is injective. The construction is natural and agrees with the same transport in the finite-type special case. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 1.2]

4.1 Step 1.2 identifies only the augmentations in stages zero, one and two. It gives no third-stage injectivity, so $p_3$ retains the stage domain of step 2.1 until a separate result supplies image-domain identification or descent. This establishes all stated conventions. [step 2.1, step 1.2, step 3.1] ∎

## Divisibility of curve-supported top cohomology

[Open item](item-lem-curve-supported-degree-six-divisible) · level 19


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the completed size conventions. Let $X$ be an affine finite-type threefold over an arbitrary algebraically closed field k, $U=X_{\mathrm{smooth}}$, and $T\subset X$ a closed integral curve contained in U. Then the actual support fiber has
$$H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X/(X\setminus T),\mathbb Z)\cong\mathrm{CH}^3_T(U),$$
and this group and its image in $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ are divisible. On the three-dimensional smooth stratum the right side is the length-order divisor quotient of k(T) on closed points of T and receives the actual surjection from $\operatorname{Pic}(\widetilde T)$, with residue degrees one. No smoothness or normality of T, characteristic restriction on divisibility, or injectivity of support-to-global is assumed.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement, with the Axiom of Choice and fixed universe bounds.

**Goal:** Construct the stated actual maps and prove their consequence.

[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. These are used when applying the actual geometry, comparison and support inputs in step 1.1 and the normalization and divisibility inputs in step 2.1.

[F1] [lem-author-149a02132c3b-geometry](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-geometry) supplies the qcqs two-open geometry and the smooth separated finite-type pairs. [lem-author-149a02132c3b-restriction-diagram](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-restriction-diagram) supplies the actual weight-three motivic-to-cycle restriction diagram over the stated arbitrary algebraically closed field.

[F2] [lem-author-149a02132c3b-support-fiber](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-support-fiber) identifies the unshifted cohomological support fiber with $z_T^3(U,\bullet)[-6]$, after reindexing homological degree $n$ as cochain degree $-n$. In particular its degree-six cohomology is $H_0z_T^3(U,\bullet)=\mathrm{CH}^3_T(U)$, with the actual support maps.

[F3] [lem-author-149a02132c3b-normalization-surjection](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-normalization-surjection) gives the surjection from the divisible Picard group of the normalization in the dimension-three stratum, and zero in a lower-dimensional smooth stratum. [lem-author-149a02132c3b-divisible-image](item-lem-author-149a02132c3b-divisible-image) proves divisibility of the support group and its actual support-to-global image.

### Proof

1.1 Under [A1], apply [F1] to the stated $X,U,T$. All schemes in its two-open diagram are qcqs and the smooth pair is separated finite type over the perfect field $k$. The compatible comparison and excision in [F2] identify the actual unshifted support fiber with $z_T^3(U,\bullet)[-6]$. Taking degree-six cohomology gives $H_0z_T^3(U,\bullet)$, proving the displayed supported Chow isomorphism with the declared cohomological indexing. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 Apply [F3] to this same curve and field. On the three-dimensional smooth stratum its actual normalization map sends each point to its image with residue degree one and surjects from a divisible Picard group to the divisor quotient. In a lower-dimensional stratum the support group is zero. In either case it is divisible; [F3] also gives divisibility of its image under the actual support-to-global homomorphism. This proves every stated assertion without assuming that homomorphism injective. [A1, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## Second stage with integral curve support

[Open item](item-lem-curve-supported-second-stage) · level 19

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe bounds of the completed comparison suppliers. Let $k$ be a perfect field, $U$ a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension three, and $C\subset U$ an integral closed curve of codimension two. In particular, this includes the curve in the smooth locus used in Theorem 6.7 over an algebraically closed field. Neither smoothness nor normality of $C$ is assumed.

Use the actual Elmanto–Morrow motivic filtration $F^\bullet K$ and write
$$K_C(U)=\operatorname{fib}(K(U)\to K(U\setminus C)),\qquad F_C^jK(U)=\operatorname{fib}(F^jK(U)\to F^jK(U\setminus C)).$$
Here $\operatorname{fib}$ is the homotopy fiber of the restriction map, and $K_0(U/(U\setminus C))$ means $\pi_0K_C(U)$. The actual augmentation $\epsilon_2:F_C^2K(U)\to K_C(U)$ is an equivalence. Thus its induced isomorphism identifies $\pi_0F_C^2K(U)$ with $K_0(U/(U\setminus C))$, as in the article. Under this identification there is an exact sequence
$$\pi_0F_C^3K(U)\longrightarrow K_0(U/(U\setminus C))\longrightarrow H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot},C}(U,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z[C]\cong\mathbb Z.$$
The second arrow is the actual stage-to-layer projection composed with $(\pi_0\epsilon_2)^{-1}$. The generator $[C]$ is the positive fundamental cycle in the supported cycle group. On a supported perfect complex $E$, the arrow sends its class to $\sum_n(-1)^n\ell_{\mathcal O_{U,\eta}}H^n(E)_\eta$ times $[C]$, where $\eta$ is the generic point of $C$ and $\ell$ denotes module length. It extends additively to virtual classes. This group is supported cohomology, not the image of $[C]$ in the Chow group of $U$.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The field, smooth threefold, integral closed curve, choice and universe hypotheses in the statement, and the actual augmented motivic tower and restriction maps.

**Goal:** Identify the second supported stage with supported $K$-theory and prove the displayed exact sequence, including the actual map and its positive generator.

[F1] [lem-smooth-leading-cycle-normalization](item-lem-smooth-leading-cycle-normalization) applies to this perfect-field smooth pair with AC. It supplies the actual equivalence $\epsilon_2$, identifies $\pi_0\operatorname{gr}_C^2K(U)$ with $H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot},C}(U,\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[C]$, and identifies the actual projection after inverse augmentation with the alternating generic-length map and positive generator. Its proof uses AC and the stated fixed universe bounds.

[F2] [lem-filtered-support-exactness](item-lem-filtered-support-exactness) constructs the supported filtered tower by restriction fibers and its graded cofiber sequence. [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) supplies the natural actual motivic graded triangle; [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support) fixes its supported cohomological indexing.

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Apply the homotopy exact sequence of the supported graded cofiber sequence and transport it along the actual augmentation.

1.1 The hypotheses of [F1] hold: $k$ is perfect, $U$ is smooth finite type and pure three-dimensional, and $C$ is integral, closed and codimension two. Therefore the actual augmentation $\epsilon_2$ is an equivalence and induces an isomorphism on $\pi_0$. This identifies the second supported stage with $K_0(U/(U\setminus C))$; the identification is the map induced by $\epsilon_2$, not an equality inferred from abstract group isomorphism. [F1, given]

2.1 By [F2], taking restriction fibers of the actual weight-two graded triangle gives the cofiber sequence $F_C^3K(U)\longrightarrow F_C^2K(U)\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_C^2K(U).$ Its long exact homotopy sequence is exact at $\pi_0F_C^2K(U)$. By [F1] and the indexing in [F2], the last term on $\pi_0$ is $H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot},C}(U,\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[C]$. Transporting the middle term along the isomorphism in step 1.1 gives the displayed exact sequence. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 The transported second arrow is precisely the actual projection after $(\pi_0\epsilon_2)^{-1}$. The normalization in [F1] computes it as alternating generic length times the positive supported cycle $[C]$; the isomorphism $\mathbb Z[C]\cong\mathbb Z$ sends $[C]$ to $1$. This identifies the arrow and sign, and completes the proof without requiring purity for the possibly singular curve. [F1, step 2.1] ∎

## Clopen rank extension and genuine representative independence

[Open item](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-virtual-independence) · level 19


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site-size and universe bounds of the supplied motivic constructions. Let $k$ be a field and $X$ any qcqs $k$-scheme. For arbitrary finite locally free bundles on $X$, extend the supplied classes from constant-rank clopen strata by their unique finite-clopen gluing. The actual series are natural and satisfy Whitney for every exact sequence. Consequently they define a unique natural homomorphism $c_t:K^0_{\rm vb}(X)\to 1+\prod_{i\geq1}H^{2i,i}(X)t^i$ with multiplicative-series target, and $c_t([V]-[W])=c_t(V)c_t(W)^{-1}$ independently of the representative. No identification of $K^0_{\rm vb}$ with perfect $K_0$ on general schemes is asserted.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. These discharge the foundational hypotheses of [F1]–[F3] in steps 1.1–4.1. The finite rank stratification introduces no new arbitrary choice.

[F1] [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-whitney](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-whitney) proves actual Whitney and root factorization at constant rank; [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes) gives naturality.

[F2] [lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection](item-lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection) includes finite common clopen rank partitions and the actual motivic restriction isomorphism to their finite products.

[F3] [lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface](item-lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface) gives the unique extension precisely when the actual exact-sequence identity holds; [lem-third-order-chern-inversion](item-lem-third-order-chern-inversion) gives formal coefficient arithmetic.

### Proof
**Given:** A field $k$, a qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, the Axiom of Choice and the stated site-size and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Close every hypothesis of virtual extension without circularity.

1.1 Each bundle has a locally constant rank function with finite image by quasi-compactness. On the finite common clopen rank partition for any finite bundle family, [F2] identifies cohomology with the product of component groups. Define each $c_i$ by the unique class restricting to the constant-rank values from [F1]; refinement does not change it by uniqueness. The rank has a finite maximum, so coefficients above that maximum vanish and the actual series is a polynomial. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct]

2.1 Pullback refines the rank partition and preserves the constant-rank classes, hence preserves the glued classes. For an exact sequence, use a common rank partition. On each component apply actual Whitney [F1]; joint injectivity in [F2] gives the global identity coefficient by coefficient. The same argument preserves isomorphism invariance. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 All hypotheses of [F3] now hold. Its construction kills every exact-sequence relation in the presentation of $K^0_{\rm vb}(X)$, so descends to a unique homomorphism. Its value on any difference is the stated quotient, with the inverse defined recursively in formal series, not by convergence. Two differences representing the same class have the same image because this is a map on the presented group. Its naturality also follows from [F3]. Thus this is genuine representative independence. [A1, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 The degree-zero series group is commutative because all coefficient first degrees are even. The product and inverse formulas through degree3 in [F3] therefore apply. In particular higher coefficients need not be additive, whereas $c_1$ is additive on virtual sums and $c_2(x+y)=c_2(x)+c_1(x)c_1(y)+c_2(y)$. [A1, F3, step 3.1] ∎


## Clopen rank extension and genuine representative independence

[Open item](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-virtual-independence) · level 19


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible universe and site-size bounds of the supplied motivic constructions. Let $k$ be a field and $X$ any qcqs $k$-scheme. For arbitrary finite locally free bundles on $X$, extend the supplied classes from constant-rank clopen strata by their unique finite-clopen gluing. The actual series are natural and satisfy Whitney for every exact sequence. Consequently they define a unique natural homomorphism $c_t:K^0_{\rm vb}(X)\to 1+\prod_{i\geq1}H^{2i,i}(X)t^i$ with multiplicative-series target, and $c_t([V]-[W])=c_t(V)c_t(W)^{-1}$ independently of the representative. No identification of $K^0_{\rm vb}$ with perfect $K_0$ on general schemes is asserted.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. These are inherited from the actual Whitney, motivic-class, derived-sheaf and virtual-extension constructions in [F1]–[F3] when invoked in steps 1.1–6.1. The finite common rank partition requires no additional arbitrary choice.

[F1] [lem-author-32887006bdff-actual-whitney](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-actual-whitney) proves actual Whitney and root factorization at constant rank; [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes) gives naturality.

[F2] For every field $k$, the actual weight-$j$ motivic complex, $j\geq0$, is the restriction of a homotopy-coherent derived Nisnevich sheaf on qcqs schemes over the prime subfield. [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) Finite clopen descent identifies such a sheaf with the product of its values on the pieces, including zero on the empty scheme. [lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-clopen-derived-descent](item-lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-clopen-derived-descent) Cohomology commutes with finite derived products, and motivic cohomology is cohomology of the actual complexes. [lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-finite-derived-products](item-lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-finite-derived-products), [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology)

[F3] [lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface](item-lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface) gives the unique extension precisely when the actual exact-sequence identity holds; [lem-third-order-chern-inversion](item-lem-third-order-chern-inversion) gives formal coefficient arithmetic.


**Given:** A field $k$, a qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, AC and the stated compatible universe and site-size bounds.

**Goal:** Close every hypothesis of virtual extension without circularity.

### Proof

1.1 Each bundle has a locally constant rank function, so the common rank loci for a finite bundle family are pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subschemes covering $X$. Quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover, which contains every nonempty locus by disjointness. Each locus is quasi-compact because it is closed in $X$, and quasi-separated because it is open in $X$. Thus this is a finite clopen partition by qcqs $k$-schemes. For empty $X$ use the empty partition. [given, construct]

2.1 Let $F$ be the prime subfield of $k$. Forgetting to $F$ changes neither the underlying qcqs schemes nor the clopen cover and its fiber products. For every $j\geq0$, [F2] therefore supplies the actual derived Nisnevich sheaf and applies finite-clopen descent to exactly this cover. It gives $\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)\simeq\prod_\alpha\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X_\alpha)$ by restriction. Taking cohomology and using finite-product compatibility in [F2] gives $H^{a,j}(X)\cong\prod_\alpha H^{a,j}(X_\alpha)$ for every integer $a$. The same holds for every finite clopen refinement. Empty covers give the zero complex and zero groups. This argument imposes no algebraic-closure assumption. [A1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 For each $i\geq1$, use the isomorphism of step 2.1 in bidegree $(2i,i)$ to define $c_i$ as the unique class restricting to the constant-rank values from [F1]. Refinement leaves this class unchanged by uniqueness and naturality of those values. Use the unit for $c_0$. For nonempty $X$ the rank has a finite maximum, so coefficients above that maximum vanish by injectivity of restriction; on empty $X$ all coefficient groups are zero and the series is the prescribed unit. Thus the actual series is a polynomial in every case. [A1, F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Pullback refines the rank partition and preserves the constant-rank classes, hence preserves the glued classes by step 2.1. For an exact sequence, use a common rank partition. On each component apply actual Whitney [F1]; joint injectivity from step 2.1 gives the global identity coefficient by coefficient. The same argument preserves isomorphism invariance. [A1, F1, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 All hypotheses of [F3] now hold. Its construction kills every exact-sequence relation in the presentation of $K^0_{\rm vb}(X)$, so descends to a unique homomorphism. Its value on any difference is the stated quotient, with the inverse defined recursively in formal series, not by convergence. Two differences representing the same class have the same image because this is a map on the presented group. Its naturality also follows from [F3]. Thus this is genuine representative independence. [A1, F3, step 4.1]

6.1 The degree-zero series group is commutative because all coefficient first degrees are even. The product and inverse formulas through degree3 in [F3] therefore apply. In particular higher coefficients need not be additive, whereas $c_1$ is additive on virtual sums and $c_2(x+y)=c_2(x)+c_1(x)c_1(y)+c_2(y)$. [A1, F3, step 5.1] ∎


## Finite clopen restrictions split the actual motivic image filtration

[Open item](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) · level 19


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe size bounds of the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a qcqs $k$-scheme, and $X=\coprod_eX_e$ any finite clopen partition. For this partition and every $j\geq0$, actual restrictions induce equivalences
$$F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\simeq\prod_eF^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X_e)$$
commuting with the stage-to-zero maps. Hence
$$F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\cong\bigoplus_eF^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X_e)$$
inside the actual $K_0$ product. In particular zero extension of a class in $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X_e)$ belongs to $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. This does not assume that motivic stages have arbitrary proper pushforward maps.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The Axiom of Choice and the fixed size conventions of the cited constructions are inherited through [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence). They discharge that supplier’s local-realization premise at its first application below. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and the fixed size conventions of the cited constructions, together with the exact finite clopen partition and current augmented tower.

**Goal:** Justify filtration membership after zero extension using actual restriction diagrams.

[F1] [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) defines the actual spectra from the enhanced perfect categories and their exact pullbacks. [prop-perfect-k-localization-input](item-prop-perfect-k-localization-input) supplies the support-category fiber sequence for every qcqs scheme with quasi-compact open complement. For a finite clopen partition all pieces and complements are qcqs. A perfect complex supported on a clopen piece is exactly its perfect complex extended by zero; this is an exact equivalence of categories. These inputs apply without normality, affineness, finite type or dimension bounds.

[F2] [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) gives derived Nisnevich sheaves at each weight; [lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-clopen-derived-descent](item-lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-clopen-derived-descent) gives their finite-clopen product equivalences and value zero at the empty scheme.

[F3] [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) supplies the natural triangle $F^{j+1}K\to F^jK\to\mathbb Z(j)_{\mathrm{mot}}[2j]$, and [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) fixes its actual augmentation/image group.

### Proof
1.1 First establish the stage-zero restriction equivalence in the full stated scope. For a binary clopen decomposition $X=A\amalg B$, extension by zero identifies $\operatorname{Perf}(A)$ with the perfect category supported on $A$. The localization sequence of [F1] is therefore $K(A)\to K(X)\to K(B)$; its last arrow has the exact zero-extension section from $B$. Restriction to $A$ is identity on the first factor and zero on that section. Thus the actual restriction map $K(X)\to K(A)\times K(B)$ is an equivalence of the split fiber sequences. Iterate for a finite nonempty partition. For the empty scheme, apply the same localization contract to its identity open: its fiber is zero, while its supported perfect category is the whole perfect category, giving $K(\varnothing)=0$. This also handles the empty partition. Extension by zero gives the coordinate inclusions in each case. [A1, F1, given]

2.1 Identify stage zero with K by [F3]. Suppose the actual stage restriction is an equivalence at $j$. Compare the natural triangle of [F3] on $X$ with the finite product of its triangles on the $X_e$. The middle vertical arrow is an equivalence by induction and the right arrow is one by [F2]. Finite products preserve fiber sequences, so taking fibers makes the left arrow an equivalence. Induction proves the assertion at every $j\geq0$, including the empty partition since [F2] gives zero graded terms there. These are the actual restrictions of a single tower; hence they commute with transitions and augmentations. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply $\pi_0$ to the commuting augmentation diagrams of step 2.1. The image of a finite product of homomorphisms is the product of its images: a tuple of image elements has a tuple of preimages. For finitely many abelian groups the product is also their direct sum. This proves the asserted image-filtration decomposition inside actual $K_0$. A stage preimage on one piece, together with zero preimages on the others, gives a stage class on $X$ by step 2.1. By step 1.1 its augmentation is exactly the K-class extended by zero, proving the final membership assertion without requiring filtered proper pushforwards. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

The stage-zero argument uses the current general perfect-K localization contract. The earlier normal affine finite-type stratum lemma remains valid but is not used to infer a qcqs or nonaffine product assertion. ## The stable free-class comparison is locally integrally acyclic

[Open item](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-local-free-test) · level 19


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible universe and site-size bounds of the supplied constructions.

Fix a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $X$ over a field and its small Nisnevich site, with the completed local K-space model. Write $\mathcal K=\Omega^\infty K_{\rm Perf}$ and $\mathcal B=BGL=\operatorname{colim}_nBGL_n$. The actual stable free-class construction gives a natural map $j:\underline{\mathbb Z}\times\mathcal B\to\mathcal K$, taking $(m,g)$ to the rank-$m$ translate of the reduced free-bundle class of $g$. It is an integral homology equivalence locally on this site. The product $j\times j$ has the same property. This is a sheaf-local assertion: it is not an assertion that this map is a homology equivalence on every affine ring with nonfree projective classes.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated universe and site-size bounds. They are inherited from the plus and actual sheaf K-space comparisons in [F1]–[F2] when constructing and identifying the local free-class map at step 1.1. The product chain calculation in step 2.1 adds no further choice principle.

[F1] [thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-plus-model-input](item-thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-plus-model-input) identifies the canonical free-class map at a Nisnevich local ring $R$ with $\mathbb Z\times BGL(R)\to\mathbb Z\times BGL(R)^+\simeq\Omega^\infty K(R)$. Projectives over $R$ are free and $K_0(R)=\mathbb Z$.

[F2] [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) fixes this actual sheaf K-space comparison, its completion construction, and the present perfect K-theory model. Direct sum induces the actual K-space addition; on stable free classes it is the block-sum operation, coherently.

### Proof
**Given:** The stated scheme/site/model, AC and the existing size bounds.

**Goal:** Identify the precise local acyclic comparison and its product.

1.1 Construct $j$ using the actual core/free-module map into K, stabilization by a trivial line, and rank translation. Its addition square is the block-sum/direct-sum square of [F2]. On the local stalks of the site it is exactly the canonical plus comparison in [F1], so the plus map gives an isomorphism on all integral homology groups there. The sheaf of ranks is the locally constant integer sheaf, not an arbitrary objectwise constant value on disconnected objects. [F1, F2, construct, A1]

2.1 On each local component pair the homotopy fiber of the product plus map is the product of the two acyclic fibers. The integral Eilenberg–Zilber/Künneth calculation makes that fiber acyclic: normalized integral chains of simplicial sets are nonnegative complexes of free groups, and tensoring their augmentation quasi-isomorphisms gives the augmentation quasi-isomorphism for the product. Equivalently the product induces the same integral homology isomorphism. Products commute with taking local stalks here, proving the assertion for $j\times j$. Nothing says the affine global projective classes are all free. [F1, step 1.1] ∎


## Local free chains detect natural perfect operations on every qcqs base

[Open item](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-local-chains) · level 19


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible universe and site-size bounds of the supplied perfect-K-space and derived-sheaf constructions. Let $X$ be any qcqs scheme over a field. On its small Zariski site let $\mathcal K=\Omega^\infty K_{\rm Perf}$ and $j:\underline{\mathbb Z}\times BGL\to\mathcal K$ be the actual stable free-class map, with locally constant ranks. The maps $j$, $j\times j$, and the component-zero map $j_0:BGL\to S$ into the actual rank-zero fiber induce local quasi-isomorphisms on normalized free integral chains. Therefore precomposition detects homotopy classes of derived sheaf maps into each actual abelian EM coefficient target $A_i=\Omega^\infty(\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}[2i])$. No noetherianness, dimension bound, or continuity of motivic complexes is assumed.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] AC and fixed universe bounds are assumed for the small presentations and enhanced realizations in the suppliers. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [thm-adjudicate-9ead0798f06a-projective-q-w-comparison](item-thm-adjudicate-9ead0798f06a-projective-q-w-comparison) supplies the full natural Quillen-to-bounded-projective Waldhausen K-space comparison, including its degree-zero object map, and the canonical acyclic plus map for every commutative local ring. The latter clause covers Zariski local rings. [thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-plus-model-input](item-thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-plus-model-input) fixes the actual free-object/addition comparison used by the completed sheaf model; its stated Nisnevich-local scope alone is not used to infer the all-local-ring clause.

[F2] [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) supplies the actual sheaf model, coefficient targets and completion construction. On the small site of open subschemes of $X$, write $D(\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\rm Zar},\mathbb Z))$ for the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves, localized at cohomology-sheaf isomorphisms, with its derived mapping spaces and cochain convention $H^a(C[s])=H^{a+s}(C)$. Define $R\Gamma_{\rm Zar}(U,C)=R\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z[U],C)$, where $\mathbb Z[U]$ is the free abelian sheaf on the represented open. For a space-valued sheaf $Y$, its derived free integral chains are sheafified normalized free chains of a simplicial resolution, placed in nonpositive cochain degrees. The right adjoint is the underlying derived abelian EM-space functor, using the nonpositive truncation for Dold–Kan. Thus the actual target associated to $C_i[2i]$, with $C_i=\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}$, is $A_i(U)=\Omega^\infty H(R\Gamma_{\rm Zar}(U,C_i[2i]))$. These are local Zariski conventions, not an enlargement of the separately scoped derived-sections definition. The actual complexes satisfy Zariski descent, so restriction is evaluated by these derived sections.

[F3] [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge) identifies the actual nonconnective perfect $K_0$ on every affine ring with its finite-projective Grothendieck group, by the object-class map; it uses the idempotent completeness of $\mathrm{Perf}$. The Quillen and bounded-projective degree-zero object maps in [F1] send each generator to that same class.

[F4] [lem-author-4f716d60801a-finite-projective-model](item-lem-author-4f716d60801a-finite-projective-model) supplies the actual bounded finite-projective enhanced model and K-projective mapping property. [lem-author-4f716d60801a-lifted-affine-equivalence](item-lem-author-4f716d60801a-lifted-affine-equivalence) supplies the actual associated-sheaf equivalence with the affine perfect category, including preservation of shifts and cones.

[F5] [thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-enhanced-comparisons](item-thm-author-da44cda020c0-units-k1-enhanced-comparisons) supplies the natural Waldhausen-to-connective equivalence under factorization and DHKS-saturation, its actual core/object maps, and the canonical connective-to-nonconnective comparison in positive degrees. Its statement does not by itself supply the missing degree-zero comparison; [F3] does.


**Given:** $X$ as stated, AC and the fixed universe bounds.

**Goal:** Supply the locality and derived-map argument beyond the earlier finite-dimensional scope.

### Proof
1.1 Finite projective modules over a filtered colimit of rings descend: represent one by an idempotent finite matrix, and descend its finitely many entries and idempotent equations. Morphisms, their equalities, inverses, and split exact sequences descend by the same finite-matrix argument. A Quillen Q morphism is a finite admissible diagram modulo an isomorphism of such diagrams; the diagram, its splitting data, and any witnessing isomorphism descend. Consequently every finite simplex of the Q nerve descends, with equality after a further index. Realization preserves filtered colimits, and finite homotopy data and the finite limits defining based loops commute with filtered colimits of spaces. Thus $K^Q(P(-))$ commutes with these ring colimits, including its components. [given, construct]

1.2 The full Q/Waldhausen comparison of [F1] applies because surjections of finite projectives split. Bounded projective complexes admit mapping-cylinder factorization within this category, and their acyclic cones are contractible by [F4]. A quasi-isomorphism is therefore a homotopy equivalence; conversely a map invertible in the localization induces an isomorphism on cohomology, so DHKS-saturation holds. Their actual localization is the affine enhanced perfect category by [F4], and extension of scalars preserves split cofibrations and contractible cones. Hence [F5] applies naturally. The resulting comparison to the actual nonconnective perfect K-space is an isomorphism in every positive degree. On degree zero, the Q and Waldhausen object classes generate their Grothendieck groups, and [F3] identifies their image with the same finite-projective class in actual perfect $K_0$. Thus this canonical comparison is also an isomorphism on components. Translation in these grouplike K-spaces identifies all components, so it is an equivalence of the full K-spaces. Choice is used in the supplied small presentations and enhanced realizations, not as a substitute for the component argument. [A1, F1, F3, F4, F5]

2.1 Combine the natural full-space comparison in step 1.2 with the Q continuity in step 1.1. This identifies the connective space of actual perfect K-theory of a filtered colimit ring with the filtered colimit of the corresponding spaces, compatibly with free-object maps. Only this K-theoretic continuity is used. No assertion about continuity of motivic complexes enters. [step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 At a Zariski point $x$, the affine-neighborhood rings have colimit $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Step 2.1 identifies the stalk of $\mathcal K$ with its actual K-space. Finite matrices and invertibility descend in the same way, so the source stalk is $\mathbb Z\times BGL(\mathcal O_{X,x})$. Finite projectives over this local ring are free, and the actual free-class map is componentwise the acyclic plus map of [F1]. The rank map on its $K_0$ is the isomorphism to $\mathbb Z$, so taking the fiber over zero selects precisely the zero component. This proves the integral chain quasi-isomorphism for $j$ and for $j_0$. [F1, F2, step 2.1]

4.1 Eilenberg–Zilber identifies normalized chains of a product with the tensor product of the two chain complexes. These complexes are degreewise free and bounded below in homological grading, hence K-flat; tensoring the chain quasi-isomorphisms for $j$ therefore preserves them. This proves the assertion for $j\times j$. Stalks commute with these finite products and chain constructions, and Zariski points detect isomorphisms of abelian sheaves on every scheme, without a dimension hypothesis. [step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Sheafify normalized free integral chains. Abelian sheafification is exact, so steps 3.1 and 4.1 give quasi-isomorphisms of complexes of sheaves for all three maps. The free-abelian and normalized-chain adjunctions, applied to simplicial resolutions and derived EM targets as in [F2], identify maps of space-valued sheaves into $A_i$ with derived maps from these chains into $C_i[2i]$. Precomposition by a chain quasi-isomorphism is an equivalence of these derived mapping spaces and hence detects their homotopy classes. This uses no stalk calculation or filtered-colimit assertion for the motivic coefficients. Applying derived sections on $X$ to an equality of derived sheaf-map classes retains its descent data. [F2, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎



## Projective relations transport the actual universal Chern operations

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-chern-operation-transport) · level 19


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the existing universe bounds. Under the specified integral smooth-field coefficient comparison, every actual universal projective-relation Chern map agrees in the two theories. For every $i\geq1$, the completed pointed perfect-$K$-space Chern maps agree after applying the coefficient comparison, and so do their maps on every closed-support fiber. The coefficient $c_0=1$ is preserved separately as the unpointed total-series constant; it supplies no additive-target support-fiber operation. These are natural map identities on the smooth site.

### Statement references

[lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag)

[lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-em-picard-square](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-em-picard-square)
