[thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space)

[def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes)

[lem-adjudicate-00232ac8c49e-stable-universal-class-detection](item-lem-adjudicate-00232ac8c49e-stable-universal-class-detection)

### Facts & Assumptions

[A9] Choice is inherited through the current smooth motivic comparison and its classical/cycle model. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag) and [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-em-picard-square](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-em-picard-square) provide actual product/unit/first-Picard-map compatibility. [lem-chern-relation-uniqueness](item-lem-chern-relation-uniqueness) gives the unique coefficients of the monic quotient-projective relation.

[F2] [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) supplies the specified formal completion of the actual universal bundle classes, functorially in coefficient maps; it does not identify the result by affine $K_0$ agreement. [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes) fixes the original quotient convention.

[F3] [lem-adjudicate-00232ac8c49e-stable-universal-class-detection](item-lem-adjudicate-00232ac8c49e-stable-universal-class-detection) proves that restrictions to finite $BGL_n$ jointly detect stable pointed classes for these smooth-field coefficient targets. Its surjectivity calculation in reduced $H^{2i-1,i}(BGL_n)$ removes the possible inverse-limit ambiguity. The resulting homotopy is a homotopy of sheaf maps, so its restrictions are coherent.


**Given:** A smooth $k$-scheme and a bundle on it, including universal bundles on classifying stacks, AC and the stated universe bounds.

**Goal:** Transport the actual higher operations, then their support maps.

### Proof

1.1 In the quotient-projective relation, the comparison takes $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ to the target $\xi$, by [F1], and preserves its products and pullbacks. It takes the relation to the same monic relation. Apply coefficient uniqueness, including its stack-level projective-bundle version supplied in [F2], to identify the actual coefficients on each $BGL_n$. These are equal classes of maps of the entire classifying stack, not merely equal values on isomorphism classes of bundles over affine schemes. For $i\geq1$ both universal maps are pointed, and the split basepoint evaluation into the abelian derived target makes forgetting pointing injective on these mapping classes, as in [F3]. Thus their finite-rank pointed mapping classes agree. Passing between line and quotient projectivizations uses the dual bundle, with the same Picard operation. [F1, F2, F3, A9]

2.1 Fix $i\geq1$ and take the two existing stable pointed universal maps on $BGL_\infty$ supplied by [F2], placing their targets in one coefficient theory using [F1]. Step 1.1 identifies every finite-rank restriction. Apply [F3]: the odd reduced cohomology restriction system is surjective, its $R^1\varprojlim$ obstruction vanishes, and the two stable maps therefore admit a homotopy in the pointed sheaf category. This supplies the missing stable homotopy, with all site-restriction coherences, before completion. No claim that arbitrarily chosen finite-rank homotopies assemble has been used. [F1, F2, F3, A9, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply the functorial completion construction of [F2] to the stable maps and the homotopy in step 2.1. Complete, project away from trivial rank, and use the abelian target's completion equivalence. Coefficient naturality identifies the resulting completed maps. Transport through the same natural local perfect-$K$-space comparison and its canonical local-replacement unit. This gives a homotopy of the pointed perfect-$K$-space operations as natural transformations on the smooth site. [F1, F2, step 2.1]

4.1 For a closed subset $Z\subseteq V$, evaluate the single natural homotopy of step 3.1 on the restriction arrow $V\to V\setminus Z$. It is a homotopy of diagram maps, not two independently selected homotopies at its ends. Applying the homotopy-fiber functor gives the comparison of the supported operations, and the fiber projections give its forget-support square. Retain [F2]'s inverse-limit extension if an open complement requires it; no extra category-localization identification is inferred. The separate index-zero identity follows from preservation of the unit: $c_0=1$ is the unpointed series constant and the positive pointed construction is not applied to it. This proves every asserted map comparison with its original smooth scope. [F1, F2, step 3.1] ∎


## Total Chern series for actual and virtual bundles

[Open item](item-def-total-chern-class) · level 20



### Definition
Assume AC and the supplied universe conventions. Let $k$ be a field and $X$ any qcqs $k$-scheme. For an actual finite locally free bundle $V$, put
$$c_t(V)=1+\sum_{i\geq1}c_i(V)t^i,$$
using the supplied projective-relation classes on constant-rank clopen components and their unique gluing for varying rank. This is a polynomial, with $c_i(V)\in H^{2i,i}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)$; it is $1$ in rank zero.
Let $K^0_{\rm vb}(X)$ be the group on finite locally free bundles modulo the exact-sequence relations. Define its **total virtual Chern series** to be the unique natural homomorphism to the multiplicative group of formal series with constant coefficient $1$ and coefficient of $t^i$ in $H^{2i,i}(X)$ extending the actual series. Equivalently,
$$c_t([V]-[W])=c_t(V)c_t(W)^{-1}.$$
Inverses are formal, computed recursively coefficient by coefficient; no convergence or dimension truncation is assumed. For this actual motivic theory, however, each positive Chern coefficient of a bundle is nilpotent. Consequently the formal inverse of any actual bundle polynomial, and hence the value on every virtual bundle class, is itself a polynomial. Its finite degree follows from nilpotence for the chosen bundles, without any finite-dimensionality assumption on $X$. The formal-series target and coefficient formulas remain valid. This uses only nonnegative weights (the theory’s explicit negative-zero extension is unchanged).
For locally Noetherian $X$, the group is the published vector-bundle $K^0(X)$. On affines it may also be identified with the supplied spectral $K_0$ through its completed affine comparison. No general equality with perfect $K_0$ or coherent G-theory is asserted.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated universe bounds. These are the foundational hypotheses of the model, comparison and virtual-extension suppliers used below; the finite nilpotent-ideal argument uses no additional arbitrary choice.

[F1] [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-virtual-independence](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-virtual-independence) supplies the actual Whitney identity, clopen extension and unique natural virtual extension, using [lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface](item-lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface) only after the actual identity. [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes) gives the constant-rank coefficients and their bidegrees.

[F2] [thm-adjudicate-9c15b20e1f5d-oriented-chern-nilpotence-input](item-thm-adjudicate-9c15b20e1f5d-oriented-chern-nilpotence-input) imports positive Chern-coefficient nilpotence for an oriented homotopy-commutative motivic ring spectrum with PBF over a qcqs derived base $S$, on smooth qcqs $S$-schemes.

[F3] [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-p1-model](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-em-p1-model) gives the actual non-$\mathbb A^1$ homotopy-commutative EM ring spectrum over every qcqs field-base $S$. [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-orientation](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-orientation) supplies its actual orientation and PBF. [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-relation-comparison](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-relation-comparison) identifies the source Chern coefficients with the supplied motivic classes. [lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection](item-lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection) supplies the finite-clopen motivic restriction isomorphism.

[F4] [lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface](item-lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface) identifies the locally Noetherian vector-bundle presentation; [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes) supplies the affine identification with the specified spectral perfect $K_0$.


**Given:** $k,X$, actual bundles or an element of $K^0_{\rm vb}(X)$, AC and the stated universe bounds.

**Goal:** Justify the representative-independent definition and polynomiality of its actual virtual values in the full qcqs scope.

### Justification
1.1 Apply [F1] to define the actual polynomial with its unit and zero conventions and natural coefficients. Its exact-sequence Whitney identity has been established for the actual projective-relation classes before virtual extension. [A1, F1, given]

2.1 The extension in [F1] is defined on the generator-and-relation group itself, kills all defining relations, and is unique on the bundle generators. Its difference formula therefore has the same value for every representative of a virtual class. Its formal inverse and coefficient bidegrees are those verified in the extension supplier. [A1, F1, step 1.1]

2.2 To apply [F2], first take a constant-rank bundle on a qcqs $k$-scheme and set $S=X$, regarded as a classical derived scheme, with $Y=X$ via the smooth identity. By [F3] the actual EM model is homotopy-commutative, oriented and satisfies the source PBF; its product-preserving coefficient identifications carry the source projective-relation coefficients to our $c_i$. Thus [F2] makes every positive $c_i$ nilpotent. For a varying-rank bundle, quasi-compactness gives finitely many clopen rank strata. On each nonempty stratum the same application with that stratum as base gives a nilpotence exponent. For each fixed $i$, take the maximum of these finitely many exponents; the corresponding power vanishes globally by the joint restriction isomorphism in [F3]. Rank zero and coefficients above rank are zero. On the empty scheme the same restriction isomorphism has empty product target, so all coefficient groups are zero and the conclusion holds as well. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 For a bundle $W$, write $c_t(W)=1+q(t)$ with $q(t)=\sum_{i=1}^m a_i t^i$, where $m$ bounds its rank and $a_i=c_i(W)$. If $q=0$, its inverse is $1$. Otherwise choose positive integers $n_i$ with $a_i^{n_i}=0$, using step 2.2. In the commutative diagonal ring $R_X=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}H^{2i,i}(X)$ put $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ and $N=1+\sum_{i=1}^m(n_i-1)$. Every monomial of degree $N$ in these generators contains some $a_i^{n_i}$, so $I^N=0$ and $q(t)^N=0$ in $R_X[t]$. Hence $(1+q(t))^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-q(t))^j$ is a polynomial. Multiplying by $c_t(V)$ proves polynomiality for every difference $[V]-[W]$, and every class has such a representative by [F1]. Each coefficient retains its required bidegree. This finite formula is the same as the unique formal inverse of step 2.1. [A1, F1, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 The locally Noetherian and affine interpretations are exactly [F4]. None of the preceding steps identifies the bundle presentation with perfect $K_0$ on general schemes or with coherent G-theory. All original coefficient formulas and naturality survive in the formal-series target, while step 3.1 gives the stronger polynomial-value assertion without a dimension restriction. [A1, F1, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎



## Whitney identities and virtual Chern arithmetic

[Open item](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) · level 20


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible universe and site-size bounds of the supplied motivic constructions. Let $k$ be any field. For every qcqs $X/k$ and exact sequence $0\to V^{\prime}\to V\to V^{\prime\prime}\to0$ of finite locally free sheaves, $c_t(V)=c_t(V^{\prime})c_t(V^{\prime\prime})$. In particular $c_t(V\oplus W)=c_t(V)c_t(W)$, $c_1(V\oplus W)=c_1(V)+c_1(W)$ and $c_2(V\oplus W)=c_2(V)+c_1(V)c_1(W)+c_2(W)$. A line has no higher classes, $c_1(L\otimes M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M)$, and on a flag filtration all coefficients are elementary symmetric polynomials in its line roots. The resulting representative-independent virtual series satisfy $c_t(-W)=1-c_1(W)t+(c_1(W)^2-c_2(W))t^2+(-c_1(W)^3+2c_1(W)c_2(W)-c_3(W))t^3+\cdots$. These statements concern $K^0_{\rm vb}$; only the completed affine comparison or locally Noetherian vector-bundle $K^0$ convention may be used for further group identifications.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. These discharge the foundational hypotheses of the supplied actual and virtual constructions [F1] and of the line comparison [F2] in steps 1.1–3.1.

[F1] [lem-author-32887006bdff-actual-whitney](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-actual-whitney) supplies actual Whitney/filtered roots; [lem-author-32887006bdff-virtual-independence](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-virtual-independence) extends to varying ranks and to the presented virtual group without using this proposition or the same-wave total-class definition.

[F2] [lem-author-32887006bdff-relation-comparison](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-relation-comparison), applied with $S=Y=X$ under [A1], supplies line normalization and the actual additive orientation on every qcqs $X/k$. [lem-third-order-chern-inversion](item-lem-third-order-chern-inversion) supplies the formal product/inverse arithmetic.

### Proof
**Given:** A field $k$, qcqs $X/k$, the stated bundles/filtrations/classes, and [A1].

**Goal:** Prove all actual and virtual formulas in their actual dependency order.

1.1 Apply [F1] first to actual bundles. The split sequence gives the direct-sum identity. The filtered formula identifies its coefficients with elementary symmetric polynomials in the actual line first classes. Varying ranks use the finite-clopen interpretation of [F1]. [A1, F1]

2.1 Compare coefficients of $t$ and $t^2$ in the direct-sum polynomial, using commutativity of the even-degree coefficient ring, to obtain the two displayed formulas. The line assertions follow from [F2]; they use the original EM Picard map. [A1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Only now use the virtual extension in [F1], which has already killed every exact-sequence relation. Its value at $-[W]$ is the inverse of its actual value at $W$. Apply the recursive inverse formula of [F2] to get the displayed expansion through degree3 and its continuation as a formal series. No coefficientwise additivity of higher classes is inferred. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Low-stage homotopy equals its image

[Open item](item-lem-low-filtration-homotopy) · level 20


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fixed compatible site and universe size bounds for the big Nisnevich comparison and its small-site derived sections. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $X$ a normal quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme. For every $0\leq i\leq2$ and $j\geq0$, the canonical homomorphism
$$\pi_jF^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K_j(X)$$
is an isomorphism.

Normal means that every local ring of $X$ is an integrally closed domain; quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated means that intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact. Here $K(X)$ is the specified nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum of perfect complexes, $K_j(X)=\pi_jK(X)$, and $F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ is the $i$th stage of its motivic filtration. The group on the right is the image of the stage-to-$K(X)$ map on $\pi_j$, and the displayed homomorphism is its corestriction to that image. The fixed size bounds specify the small sites and ambient universes for derived sections; Choice says that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An algebraically closed field $k$, a normal quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme $X$, Choice, the stated site-size bounds, and integers $0\leq i\leq2$ and $j\geq0$.

**Goal:** Prove that the canonical stage-to-image map is an isomorphism.

[F1] The specified filtration has $F^0_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=K(X)$, compatible transition maps, and image groups defined as in the statement. The given scheme is qcqs, so the stated suppliers apply ([def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions), [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration)).

[F2] For each $r\geq0$, the graded triangle is $F^{r+1}_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to\mathbb Z(r)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)[2r]$. Its graded homotopy group in degree $n$ is $H^{2r-n,r}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$, where motivic cohomology is the cohomology of the specified motivic complex. The triangle gives the corresponding long exact homotopy sequence ([prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence), [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology), [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence)).

[F3] Weight-zero motivic cohomology vanishes in negative cohomological degrees. Under Choice and the stated site-size bounds, weight-one motivic cohomology vanishes in degrees at most zero and $H^{1,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is naturally the group of global units ([prop-motivic-weight-zero](item-prop-motivic-weight-zero), [prop-motivic-weight-one](item-prop-motivic-weight-one), [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites)).

[F4] Under the given field, normality, qcqs, Choice and size hypotheses, the actual projection $\pi_1F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to H^{1,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is surjective: after the actual augmentation isomorphism and the global-units identification it is determinant, which has the unit section ([lem-k-one-projection-determinant](item-lem-k-one-projection-determinant)). Choice is as stated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice).

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Use the exact sequences of the weight-zero and weight-one graded triangles and the surjectivity of the actual determinant projection.

1.1 Write $F^r=F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ and $q_r:\pi_jF^r\to K_j(X)$ for the map induced by the transition to stage zero. For $r=0$, [F1] identifies $q_0$ with the identity, so its corestriction to its image is an isomorphism. By definition, every $q_r$ is surjective onto its image; it remains to prove injectivity for $r=1,2$. [F1, given]

2.1 The weight-zero part of [F2] gives the exact segment $H^{-j-1,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\to\pi_jF^1\xrightarrow{q_1}K_j(X)$. Since $j\geq0$, the first group is zero by [F3]. Thus $q_1$ is injective, and its corestriction to $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_j(X)$ is an isomorphism. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The weight-one part of [F2] gives the exact segment $H^{1-j,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\to\pi_jF^2\to\pi_jF^1$. If $j\geq1$, its first group vanishes by [F3], so the transition $\pi_jF^2\to\pi_jF^1$ is injective. Its composite with $q_1$ is $q_2$ by compatibility of transitions; therefore $q_2$ is injective by step 2.1. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1]

3.2 If $j=0$, the weight-one exact sequence contains $\pi_1F^1\to H^{1,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\to\pi_0F^2\to\pi_0F^1$. The first map is surjective by [F4], so exactness makes the connecting map zero and the following transition injective. Composing with the injective $q_1$ from step 2.1 shows that $q_2$ is injective also in degree zero. [F1, F2, F4, step 2.1]

4.1 Steps 1.1 through 3.2 establish injectivity of each relevant stage-to-$K$ map. Its corestriction is surjective onto the image by definition, hence is an isomorphism for all stated $i$ and $j$. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

No new external-source reading or independent acceptance is asserted.


## Zeroth projection is rank

[Open item](item-lem-zero-projection-rank) · level 20


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied weight-zero and perfect K-theory constructions. Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme. Under the canonical identifications
$$H^{0,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong H^0_{\mathrm{cdh},F}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{LC}(|X|,\mathbb Z),$$
the actual zeroth filtration projection $p_0:K_0(X)\to H^{0,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is the locally constant Euler rank. Here $F$ is the prime subfield of $k$, and the cdh group uses the supplied entire qcqs $F$-scheme site. The group $\operatorname{LC}(|X|,\mathbb Z)$ consists of functions on the underlying topological space that are constant on a neighbourhood of every point, with pointwise addition. No seminormality, normality, separatedness, finite-type or dimension hypothesis is needed for this rank identification.

In the original separated seminormal finite-type case over an algebraically closed field, the same identifications agree naturally with the constant-integer sections on the separated finite-type $k$-scheme cdh site and give
$$H^{0,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong H^0_{\mathrm{cdh}}(X,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{\pi_0(X)}.$$
Here $\pi_0(X)$ is the finite set of connected components, and its components are open and closed. Thus the original componentwise statement, including disconnected and empty schemes, is retained. On general qcqs schemes the locally constant-function description is used; arbitrary functions on connected components are not asserted to be locally constant.

The spectrum $K(X)$ is the specified nonconnective K-theory of perfect complexes and $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves. Its Euler rank at a point is the alternating dimension of its derived fiber over the residue field. The projection is the actual stage-zero-to-graded map, with $F^0_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=K(X)$. A qcqs scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Seminormality in the finite-type specialization has the supplied local square-and-cube-root convention.

### Statement references

[lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage)

[prop-motivic-weight-zero](item-prop-motivic-weight-zero)

[lem-author-a279c89ed6c8-cdh-zero-site-comparison](item-lem-author-a279c89ed6c8-cdh-zero-site-comparison)

[lem-cdh-integer-sections](item-lem-cdh-integer-sections)

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $k$, a qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, Choice and compatible site and universe bounds. For the final specialization also assume the separated seminormal finite-type and algebraically closed hypotheses.

**Goal:** Identify the actual projection in qcqs scope and recover the original finite-type component formula on its original site.

[A1] The stated Choice and size premises are inherited from the actual rank, perfect K-theory and weight-zero constructions in [F1]–[F3]. They are used when applying those suppliers at steps 1.1–2.1. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) identifies stage zero with K. [def-filtration-projections](item-def-filtration-projections) defines $p_0$ as the actual stage-to-graded map on every qcqs field-scheme. [prop-motivic-weight-zero](item-prop-motivic-weight-zero) identifies its target with the constant-integer derived sections on the general qcqs prime-field cdh site.

[F2] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage) computes that site's degree-zero constant sections as locally constant integers, identifies $\Omega^\infty\operatorname{gr}^0K$ as this discrete sheaf, and identifies the actual map on perfect $K_0$ as the locally constant Euler rank. This is an actual map identification over every field, without a smooth-locus premise.

[F3] [lem-author-a279c89ed6c8-cdh-zero-site-comparison](item-lem-author-a279c89ed6c8-cdh-zero-site-comparison) gives the natural comparison with separated finite-type $k$-site sections when $X$ is separated finite type. [lem-cdh-integer-sections](item-lem-cdh-integer-sections) identifies the latter with $\mathbb Z^{\pi_0(X)}$ under the additional seminormal and algebraically closed hypotheses.



### Proof

1.1 Apply [F1] and [F2] to the given qcqs field-scheme under [A1]. Their source is the same specified K-spectrum, and their map is the same stage-zero cofiber projection. The discrete zeroth-space identification in [F2] identifies its zeroth homotopy group with $\operatorname{LC}(|X|,\mathbb Z)$, and the actual map on $K_0$ is the Euler rank. Composing with the weight-zero identification in [F1] gives the first display and the claimed rank equality on every such $X$. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 The rank in step 1.1 is computed on local bounded finite locally free representatives. Those ranks are locally constant, compatible with restrictions, and additive in exact triangles, as in [F2]. Hence this is a natural homomorphism on all perfect classes, including those without a global vector-bundle presentation. On the empty scheme the locally constant-function group is zero and the same identity applies. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Now impose the original separated seminormal finite-type and algebraically closed hypotheses. Apply the natural site comparison and component-section calculation in [F3] to the same weight-zero group. The finite connected components of this noetherian scheme are clopen, so their integer values describe exactly its locally constant functions. These identifications take the map in step 1.1 to the original componentwise rank map and give the second display. Thus every original finite-type assertion and the broader qcqs rank equality hold with their respective precise site conventions. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

## Third-stage graded isomorphism

[Open item](item-lem-third-graded-isomorphism) · level 20


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme of Krull dimension $3$ over a field $k$. Then the actual third-stage projection followed by the graded comparison is an isomorphism
$$p_3:\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z).$$
In particular, this applies to the normal threefolds in Section 6 under the article's standing conventions.

Here $F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ is stage $r$ of the decreasing motivic filtration of the nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum; its third graded spectrum is the cofiber of the transition $F^4_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$. The map $p_3$ is induced by the canonical map from the third stage to this cofiber and the specified graded equivalence. For the weight-three motivic complex $C=\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)$, the group $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ means $H^6(C)$. The symbol $\pi_i$ denotes the $i$th stable homotopy group. No injectivity of the map from the third stage to $K(X)$ is asserted here.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a field $k$, and a Noetherian $k$-scheme $X$ of Krull dimension $3$.

**Goal:** Prove that the actual third-stage projection $p_3$ is an isomorphism.

[F1] A Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Under the choice assumption, [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) supplies the decreasing motivic tower over $k$, and [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) defines the indicated motivic cohomology group.

[F2] For a qcqs $k$-scheme, [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) gives the actual cofiber triangle $F^4_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)[6]$. The natural shift-index identification in [lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index](item-lem-eilenberg-maclane-shift-index) identifies the zeroth homotopy group of this graded spectrum with $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$.

[F3] [lem-high-filtration-vanishing](item-lem-high-filtration-vanishing) states, for a Noetherian scheme of finite dimension $d$ over a field and under the Axiom of Choice, that $\pi_0F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0$ for $i>d$ and $\pi_jF^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0$ for $i\ge d$ and $j<0$.

[F4] [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) gives the homotopy exact sequence of a filtered stage and its cofiber: the image of each map equals the kernel of the next.

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Apply the homotopy exact sequence to the third graded cofiber and use the two stage-four vanishing statements.

1.1 Since $X$ is Noetherian, it is qcqs; therefore the tower and the actual third graded cofiber in [F1] and [F2] apply. Write $G^3$ for that cofiber. The supplied graded equivalence and shift-index identification give a natural isomorphism $\pi_0G^3\cong H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. [F1, F2, given]

1.2 Apply [F4] with stage index $3$ and homotopy degree $0$. The resulting exact segment is
$$\pi_0F^4_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow\pi_0G^3\longrightarrow\pi_{-1}F^4_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X).$$
The middle arrow is the map induced by the canonical third-stage-to-cofiber map. [F4, step 1.1]

2.1 In [F3], take $d=3$ and $i=4$. Since $4>3$, the first group in step 1.2 is zero. Since $4\ge3$ and $-1<0$, the last group is also zero. Exactness therefore makes the middle arrow both injective and surjective. [F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Compose this middle arrow with the isomorphism of step 1.1. By definition this composite is $p_3$, so $p_3$ is an isomorphism. The article's normal threefold case is included because its schemes satisfy the stated Noetherian dimension-three hypotheses; normality and algebraic closedness are not needed for this deduction. [step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Torsion freeness after removing a smooth-locus integral curve

[Open item](item-prop-curve-complement-torsion-free) · level 20

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support). Let $X$ be an affine finite-type threefold over an algebraically closed field $k$, and let $T\subset X$ be a closed integral curve contained in the smooth locus $X_{\mathrm{smooth}}$. Then
$$H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X\setminus T,\mathbb Z)$$
is torsion-free.

A threefold here is a finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension three; no reducedness, irreducibility, normality, or smoothness of $X$ is assumed. An integral curve is a reduced irreducible scheme of dimension one. The smooth locus consists of the points at which $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. A group is torsion-free if $na=0$ for a positive integer $n$ implies $a=0$. The motivic cohomology group is the degree-six cohomology of the weight-three motivic complex, as defined in [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology). The Axiom of Choice is used through the two supported-cohomology suppliers, including their size and comparison constructions.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An affine finite-type threefold $X$ over an algebraically closed field $k$, a closed integral curve $T\subset X_{\mathrm{smooth}}$, the Axiom of Choice, and the size conventions of [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support).

**Goal:** Prove that $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X\setminus T,\mathbb Z)$ is torsion-free.

[F1] [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support) defines the weight-three support spectrum as the fiber of restriction from $X$ to $X\setminus T$, with supported cohomology $H^{a,3}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X,\mathbb Z)=\pi_{-a}M_3(X/(X\setminus T))$. On the qcqs schemes in this statement, [def-motivic-cohomology](item-def-motivic-cohomology) identifies the corresponding ordinary groups with cohomology of the evaluated motivic complexes. [lem-fiber-sequence-homotopy-exactness](item-lem-fiber-sequence-homotopy-exactness) supplies the long exact homotopy sequence of this actual fiber sequence.

[F2] [prop-top-motivic-torsion-free](item-prop-top-motivic-torsion-free) says that $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is torsion-free for an affine finite-type threefold over an algebraically closed field, without extra hypotheses on $X$.

[F3] Under the given field, geometry, choice and size hypotheses, [lem-curve-supported-degree-six-divisible](item-lem-curve-supported-degree-six-divisible) says that the image of the actual support-to-global map in degree six is divisible, and [lem-curve-supported-degree-seven-vanishing](item-lem-curve-supported-degree-seven-vanishing) says that the supported group in degree seven is zero. A group is divisible when multiplication by every positive integer is surjective.

[F4] [lem-divisible-quotient-torsion-free](item-lem-divisible-quotient-torsion-free) says that in a short exact sequence $0\to D\to G\to A\to0$ of abelian groups, if $D$ is divisible and $G$ is torsion-free, then $A$ is torsion-free. Short exact means that the first map is injective, the second is surjective, and the image of the first equals the kernel of the second.

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Apply the support long exact sequence and the divisible-quotient lemma.

1.1 Put $V=X\setminus T$. Since $X$ is noetherian, its open subset $V$ is quasi-compact; both are quasi-separated. The fiber sequence of [F1], followed by its long exact homotopy sequence with the given indexing, yields the exact segment $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\rho}H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(V,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^{7,3}_{\mathrm{mot},T}(X,\mathbb Z).$ The first map is support-to-global and $\rho$ is restriction. [F1, given]

2.1 The hypotheses of both suppliers in [F3] hold for the given $X$, $k$ and $T$, with the stated choice and size conventions. Thus the last group in step 1.1 is zero, and the image $D$ of the first map is divisible. Exactness makes $\rho$ surjective and identifies its kernel with $D$. [F3, step 1.1, given]

3.1 Write $G=H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ and $A=H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(V,\mathbb Z)$. The inclusion of $D$ into $G$ and $\rho$ form a short exact sequence $0\to D\to G\to A\to0$. By [F2], $G$ is torsion-free; by step 2.1, $D$ is divisible. Applying [F4] proves that $A$ is torsion-free, as required. [F2, F4, step 2.1] ∎

## Subgroup generated by smooth closed points

[Open item](item-def-smooth-point-filtration) · level 20

### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the support construction. Let $k$ be a perfect field, meaning that every algebraic extension of $k$ is separable, and let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme of pure finite dimension $d$. Thus $X$ has a finite affine open cover, intersections of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact, and every irreducible component has dimension $d$; dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of distinct irreducible closed subsets. Take $d\geq 0$.

Let $S$ be the set of closed points $x\in X$ at which $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth: each such point has an open neighbourhood smooth over $k$. For each $x\in S$, [def-smooth-point-cycle-map](item-def-smooth-point-cycle-map) gives a homomorphism $\varphi_x:\mathbb Z\to K_0(X)$, with $\varphi_x(1)=[i_*\kappa(x)]$, where $i:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow X$ is the closed immersion and the bracket denotes the class of the perfect residue sheaf. Here $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$ for the nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum of perfect complexes.

The **smooth-point subgroup** is
$$F^d_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X):=\operatorname{im}\left(\bigoplus_{x\in S}\mathbb Z\xrightarrow{\;\oplus\varphi_x\;}F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\right)\subseteq F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\subseteq K_0(X).$$
Here the direct sum consists of integer families with finite support, and its displayed map sends $(n_x)$ to the finite sum $\sum_x\varphi_x(n_x)$. The target $F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of $\pi_0F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to K_0(X)$ as defined in [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration). Equivalently, $F^d_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$ is the subgroup of $K_0(X)$ generated by the classes $[i_*\kappa(x)]$ for $x\in S$. If $S$ is empty, it is zero.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The field, scheme, dimension, choice and size hypotheses in the definition.

**Goal:** Justify the displayed map, its image subgroup, and the equivalent description by generators.

[F1] [def-smooth-point-cycle-map](item-def-smooth-point-cycle-map) constructs each $\varphi_x$ under these hypotheses, identifies its value at $1$ with the residue-sheaf class, and makes it a group homomorphism.

[F2] [lem-smooth-point-filtration](item-lem-smooth-point-filtration) proves that the image of each $\varphi_x$ lies in $F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ for a pure finite-dimensional qcqs scheme over a perfect field, with the stated choice and size assumptions. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) defines that group as a subgroup of $K_0(X)$.

### Justification
1.1 For every $x\in S$, [F1] gives a homomorphism to $K_0(X),$ and [F2] allows its codomain to be restricted to the filtration subgroup. For a finitely supported integer family, the sum of its values is therefore a well-defined element of that subgroup. Finite sums and the homomorphism property of each $\varphi_x$ make the displayed assignment a homomorphism. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Its image is a subgroup of the target: zero is the image of the zero family, and sums and inverses of images are images of the corresponding sums and inverses of families. Every image is a finite integer linear combination of the values $\varphi_x(1)$, and every such combination is the image of a finitely supported family. By [F1] these values are the stated residue-sheaf classes. If $S$ is empty, the direct sum and its image are zero. This establishes the definition and its equivalent generator description. [F1, step 1.1] ∎

## Generic localization detects the point subgroup

[Open item](item-lem-supported-generic-rank-kernel) · level 20

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed universe bounds of the completed comparison suppliers. Let $k$ be a perfect field, $U$ a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension three, and $i:C\hookrightarrow U$ an integral closed curve of codimension two, with generic point $\eta$. No smoothness or normality of $C$ is assumed. Use the actual Elmanto–Morrow filtered nonconnective perfect-complex $K$-theory and write $K_C(U)=\operatorname{fib}(K(U)\to K(U\setminus C))$ and $F_C^jK(U)=\operatorname{fib}(F^jK(U)\to F^jK(U\setminus C))$.

The group $\pi_0K_C(U)$ is canonically the Grothendieck group of perfect complexes on $U$ supported on $C$. Under this identification, the arrow in the supported exact sequence
$$\pi_0F_C^3K(U)\longrightarrow\pi_0K_C(U)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[C]\cong\mathbb Z$$
is generic localization: it sends a supported perfect complex $E$ to $\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{U,\eta}}H^n(E)_\eta$, and the positive cycle $[C]$ corresponds to $1$. Its kernel, equivalently the image of $\pi_0F_C^3K(U)$, is the subgroup generated by the classes of perfect complexes supported at closed points of $C$. Indeed it is generated by the individual residue-sheaf classes $[i_{x*}\kappa(x)]$, where $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow U$ and $x$ ranges over closed points of $C$.

If $U$ is an open subscheme of a finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, these points are closed smooth points of $X$. In particular this applies to a curve contained in the smooth locus in the article's algebraically closed-field setting.

Here integral means reduced and irreducible; a curve is one-dimensional. A perfect complex is a complex locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves. It is supported on a subset when all its cohomology stalks vanish outside that subset. Its Grothendieck group has one generator for each perfect object and the usual distinguished-triangle relations. The length of a finite-length module is the number of simple factors in a composition series. Generic localization is the map induced by restriction to the generic point, expressed through coherent $G$-theory as generic rank; the alternating-length formula specifies the same map on supported perfect objects.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the fixed universe bounds, $k$, $U$, $C$ and the actual supported filtration as in the Statement. For the final assertion, also let $U\subseteq X$ be an open immersion into a finite-type $k$-scheme.

**Goal:** Identify the actual supported sequence and its second arrow, compute its kernel by closed-point classes, and establish the stated smooth-point conclusion.

[F1] [lem-curve-supported-second-stage](item-lem-curve-supported-second-stage) supplies the actual equivalence $\epsilon_2:F_C^2K(U)\simeq K_C(U)$ and the exact sequence after transport along $\epsilon_2$. [lem-smooth-leading-cycle-normalization](item-lem-smooth-leading-cycle-normalization) identifies the transported projection with alternating generic length times the positive supported cycle $[C]$. These suppliers require the stated perfect-field, smoothness, dimension, AC and universe hypotheses.

[F2] [prop-perfect-k-localization-input](item-prop-perfect-k-localization-input) identifies the category-defined supported nonconnective $K$-spectrum with the actual restriction fiber for a qcqs scheme and a quasi-compact open complement. [prop-supported-k-zero-devissage](item-prop-supported-k-zero-devissage) identifies its degree-zero group with $G_0(C)$ and sends the coherent class $[F]$ inversely to the class of $i_*F[0]$. Here $G_0(C)$ is generated by coherent sheaves with short-exact-sequence relations. The ambient scheme must be regular Noetherian and finite-dimensional.

[F3] [lem-curve-generic-rank-localization](item-lem-curve-generic-rank-localization) states, under AC, that for an integral Noetherian one-dimensional scheme the kernel of generic rank on $G_0$ is generated by the residue sheaves of closed points. Under the supported comparison it identifies generic rank with alternating generic length; its localization description is the filtered limit over nonempty opens.

[F4] [lem-koszul-point-support-class](item-lem-koszul-point-support-class) proves under AC that the residue sheaf of a closed smooth point of a finite-type scheme over a perfect field is perfect and supported at that point, using a local Koszul resolution.

### Proof

1.1 A finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated; $U\setminus C$ is quasi-compact because $U$ is Noetherian. Smoothness over the perfect field makes $U$ regular, and its dimension is finite. Thus the hypotheses of [F2] hold. Its localization equivalence identifies the actual fiber $K_C(U)$ with the $K$-spectrum of the full category of perfect complexes supported on $C$. The degree-zero comparison and triangle presentation in the supported dévissage identify its $\pi_0$ with the stated Grothendieck group and canonically with $G_0(C)$. [given, F2]

2.1 The pair $C\subset U$ satisfies all hypotheses of [F1]. Transporting the supported graded exact sequence along the actual augmentation $\epsilon_2$ gives the displayed sequence. By [F1] its second arrow takes $[E]$ to the alternating generic-length coefficient times $[C]$, with positive generator. By [F3], under the specific $G_0(C)$ comparison of step 1.1 this coefficient is generic rank, equivalently localization to the generic point in the stated filtered-limit sense. This identifies the actual arrow, rather than inferring it from an abstract isomorphism of its target with $\mathbb Z$. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F3], the kernel of generic rank on $G_0(C)$ is generated by $[\kappa(x)]$ for closed points $x$ of $C$. Since $C$ is closed in $U$, each such $x$ is closed in $U$. The inverse in [F2] sends $[\kappa(x)]$ to the class of the same residue sheaf, viewed as a perfect complex on $U$ in degree zero. It is supported at $x$; [F4] independently supplies its local perfectness. Consequently the kernel is generated by these point classes. Conversely every perfect complex supported at a closed point has zero stalk at $\eta$, so its alternating generic length is zero. Hence the subgroup generated by all such complexes is exactly the kernel. Exactness in step 2.1 identifies this kernel with the image of $\pi_0F_C^3K(U)$. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1]

4.1 Suppose $U$ is open in a finite-type $k$-scheme $X$. A closed point of the finite-type $k$-scheme $U$ has residue field finite over $k$. Its image in $X$ is therefore a closed point: on an affine neighbourhood its prime has field quotient finite over $k$, hence is maximal. Since $U$ is smooth over $k$, $X$ is smooth over $k$ at each such point by locality of smoothness on the source. Thus all generators in step 3.1 are supported at closed smooth points of $X$. This proves the final assertion and the lemma. [given, step 3.1] ∎

## Local integral chains detect global natural maps into Chern targets

[Open item](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-derived-chain-detection) · level 20


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible universe and site-size bounds of the supplied constructions.

Let $f:P\to Q$ be a map of pointed simplicial sheaves whose normalized integral chain map is a local quasi-isomorphism. For every coefficient complex $D$ with its derived Eilenberg target $K(D,n)$, precomposition gives an equivalence of derived mapping spaces into that target. In particular it is injective on homotopy classes. This applies to $j$ and $j\times j$ of the preceding lemma. Therefore identities of natural Chern maps on $\mathcal K$ or $\mathcal K\times\mathcal K$ may be detected after this local free-class comparison, including all descent morphisms and global cohomology classes.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated universe and site-size bounds. They are inherited from the selected local sheaf and derived-section models in [F2] at steps 1.1–2.1 and from the local free-class comparison in [F1] at step 3.1. The mapping-space argument is conditional on those supplied constructions.

[F1] [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-local-free-test](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-local-free-test) gives local integral homology equivalences. The coefficient targets and local simplicial-sheaf model are those of [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space), concretely the derived version of Asakura–Sato Definition5.1(2).

[F2] The free abelian sheaf/forgetful adjunction and normalized-chain/Dold–Kan adjunction identify maps into $K(D,n)$ with derived maps from normalized free integral chains into $D[n]$. Sheafification of abelian presheaves is exact; its compatible local/derived conventions are those of [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification) and [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites).

### Proof
**Given:** $f$ as stated and any of the actual coefficient complexes. Assume Choice and the universe and site-size bounds in [A1].

**Goal:** Prove map-level detection rather than compare values of Picard/cohomology groups on affine opens.

1.1 Apply normalized free integral chains and then sheafification. Its cohomology sheaves are computed from the local homology groups, so the hypothesis makes the resulting chain map a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of sheaves. This is an equivalence in the derived category, not an assertion that the original spaces are locally weakly equivalent. [F1, F2, A1]

2.1 The derived adjunction in [F2] identifies $\operatorname{Map}(Q,K(D,n))\to\operatorname{Map}(P,K(D,n))$ with the map of derived Hom spaces obtained by precomposing with that chain equivalence. It is an equivalence, hence injective on $\pi_0$. The adjunction and chain map are natural in $P,Q,D$, so this proves an identity in the local sheaf homotopy category. Evaluating a homotopy between fibrant natural maps gives the corresponding homotopy on derived sections over $X$; it retains all gluing data. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Use step 2.1 for $j$ and $j\times j$ by [F1]. A Cartan difference is a map to one such abelian Eilenberg target, so its vanishing on the free-class test forces its vanishing as the global natural map. No generation of $K_0(X)$ by global vector bundles is used. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## The field comparison preserves refined smooth Gysin and the point class

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-smooth-supported-gysin-transport) · level 20

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the existing universe bounds. For a regular closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ of smooth finite-type schemes over a perfect field, the specified field comparison preserves the refined motivic Gysin map and its forget-support map. In particular it takes the actual Spitzweck/classical refined point class to the actual EM positive point class on a smooth point pair. This is sufficient for the supported codimension-three RR application; it asserts no global smooth comparison or new Gysin formalism on singular normal qcqs schemes.

### Statement references

[lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag)

[lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-em-picard-square](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-em-picard-square)

[lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-chern-operation-transport](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-chern-operation-transport)

[thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-field-map-input](item-thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-field-map-input)

### Facts & Assumptions
[A9] Choice is inherited through the current smooth motivic comparison and its classical/cycle model. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F1] [thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-field-map-input](item-thm-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-oriented-field-map-input) supplies the coefficient-independent smooth homotopy-purity equivalence and the orientation/Thom definition of Gysin. [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-field-unit-zigzag), [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-em-picard-square](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-em-picard-square) and [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-chern-operation-transport](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-chern-operation-transport) identify the actual ring and Picard maps and universal Chern classes.

[F2] [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-coordinates](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-coordinates) fixes the positive EM point class by the literal supported reduced cycle $[x]$, whose coordinate is $+1$.

### Proof
**Given:** $i$ as stated, its normal bundle $N$, the specified coefficient comparison on the smooth site, AC and the stated universe bounds.

**Goal:** Identify actual supported Gysin operations, not just their target groups.

1.1 The Thom class of a line bundle is determined by the pointed first-Chern class on its projective completion. The sum/product construction and projective-bundle detection determine the rank-$d$ Thom class from these line classes. Thus an orientation-preserving multiplicative coefficient map preserves the actual Thom class, as well as the Thom isomorphism $a\mapsto\pi^*a\,\mathrm{th}(N)$. Equivalently use the top-Chern definition on the projective completion and its unique refined lift. This uses the actual top class, not Navarro's malformed displayed Thom expansion. [F1, A9]

2.1 Homotopy purity identifies $V/(V\setminus Z)$ with $\mathrm{Th}(N)$ in the motivic category. This is a map of motivic spaces before applying any coefficients, so the coefficient comparison commutes with it. Define refined Gysin by composing the Thom isomorphism from step 1.1 with this purity identification. The resulting square commutes; composing with the coefficient-independent forget-support arrow gives the ordinary Gysin square. The deformation construction in the cited RR source agrees with this construction on smooth regular pairs. For a nonseparated smooth pair, perform this construction on affine opens of the ambient scheme; their closed intersections with $Z$ are affine smooth pairs. Naturality on their open overlaps and Nisnevich descent glue the same purity and Thom maps. Thus the application of the primary purity theorem uses only separated finite-type pairs; descent handles the stated nonseparated scope. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 For a smooth rational point of codimension three, $N$ is a rank-three vector space. Its Thom class is the product of the three normalized Cartier zero-section classes, hence is the positive point class. Units are preserved, so $i_!(1)$ has precisely the same normalization in the two theories. In the supported cycle model these three regular Cartier parameters cut out the reduced point with intersection multiplicity $+1$; the divisor bonding normalization is the $+1$ boundary in Spitzweck Lemma 6.6. In the article application over an algebraically closed field this is exactly the $\delta_x$ of [F2], on its stated pure-threefold neighbourhood. This also agrees with the three-coordinate-hyperplane test in $\mathbb P^3$. No cancellation of a forget-support map or division is used. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Removing normality from the article results

[Open item](item-op-remove-normality) · level 21


### Open problem
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the supplied motivic constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. An affine $k$-scheme here means the spectrum of a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra; its dimension is the supremum of the lengths of chains of distinct irreducible closed subsets. No normality assumption is imposed. A rank-$n$ vector bundle is a locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^n$, and $\mathrm{Vect}_n(X)$ is its set of isomorphism classes. Write $H^{a,b}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ for the supplied integral motivic cohomology and $c_i$ for its motivic Chern classes.

Determine whether the following extensions hold:

1. For every affine surface $X$ over $k$, meaning an affine $k$-scheme of dimension $2$, is $(c_1,c_2):\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)\to H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\times H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ a bijection?
2. For every affine threefold $X$ over $k$, meaning an affine $k$-scheme of dimension $3$, is $(c_1,c_2,c_3):\mathrm{Vect}_3(X)\to H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\times H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\times H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ a bijection?
3. For every such threefold of pure dimension $3$, is $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)=F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$? Here $K_0(X)$ is degree zero of perfect-complex K-theory, $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of degree zero of the third motivic filtration stage in $K_0(X)$, and $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$ is the subgroup generated by the classes of residue sheaves at closed points where $X$ is smooth over $k$. Pure dimension means that every irreducible component has dimension $3$. For threefolds without this purity hypothesis, determine the appropriate formulation and whether the comparison extends.
4. For every affine threefold $X$ over $k$, is $(c_1,c_2):\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)\to H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\times H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ surjective?

The questions include schemes that are not reduced; an affirmative answer in a narrower class alone would not settle the formulations above. The purity qualification in the third question is the domain of the supplied smooth-point filtration definition.

## Third edge homomorphism

[Open item](item-def-third-edge-map) · level 21


### Definition
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a Noetherian $k$-scheme of Krull dimension $3$. Write $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ for the third stage of the decreasing motivic filtration of the nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum of perfect complexes, and $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$. Its third **image-filtration group** is the subgroup
$$F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow K_0(X)\bigr).$$
The arrow is induced by the transition from stage three to stage zero, identified with $K(X)$. Let $p_3$ be the isomorphism from $\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ to $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)=H^6(\mathbb Z(3)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X))$ induced by the canonical map to the third graded cofiber and the specified graded comparison, as in [lem-third-graded-isomorphism](item-lem-third-graded-isomorphism). Here $\pi_0$ denotes the zeroth stable homotopy group, and $H^6$ is degree-six cohomology of the weight-three motivic complex.

The **third edge homomorphism** is the composite
$$\epsilon_3:H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\ p_3^{-1}\ }\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\longrightarrow F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X).$$
The second arrow is the stage-to-$K_0$ homomorphism with its codomain restricted to its image. In particular, $\epsilon_3$ is surjective.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a field $k$, and a Noetherian $k$-scheme $X$ of Krull dimension $3$.

**Goal:** Justify the definition of $\epsilon_3$ and its surjectivity.

[F1] Under these hypotheses, [lem-third-graded-isomorphism](item-lem-third-graded-isomorphism) supplies the actual third-stage projection $p_3$ as an isomorphism with the displayed motivic cohomology group. It does not assert that the stage-to-$K_0$ map is injective.

[F2] Under the Axiom of Choice, [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) supplies the filtration and defines $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ as the image of the stage-to-$K_0$ homomorphism; that homomorphism is surjective onto its image.

### Justification

1.1 The hypotheses in [F1] hold for the given $X$, so $p_3$ has a unique inverse homomorphism from $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ to $\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$. [F1, given]

2.1 By [F2], the second arrow in the displayed composite is a well-defined surjective homomorphism onto the stated image subgroup. Composing it with the inverse from step 1.1 defines $\epsilon_3$. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 For any element of the image subgroup, choose a preimage under the second arrow and apply $p_3$ to it. The resulting motivic cohomology class maps to the chosen element under $\epsilon_3$. Thus $\epsilon_3$ is surjective. No injectivity of the stage-to-$K_0$ map is needed for this conclusion. [F1, F2, step 2.1] ∎


## Distinguishing smooth-point and motivic filtration notation

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the smooth-point filtration definition. Here $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$ for the supplied nonconnective perfect-complex $K$-theory spectrum, and $F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of $\pi_0F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to K_0(X)$. Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the smooth-point construction. Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $X$ be an affine $k$-variety of pure dimension $d>3$: its coordinate algebra is finitely generated and reduced, and every irreducible component has dimension $d$. ## The actual Chern series of a trivial bundle is the unit

[Open item](item-lem-author-b02e51f9da03-trivial-chern) · level 21


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied motivic Chern constructions. For every $m\geq0$, the actual total motivic Chern series of the trivial bundle on a qcqs scheme over a field is $c_t(\mathcal O_X^m)=1$. On a smooth equidimensional finite-type scheme the same identity holds for the ordinary integral Chow Chern series. These statements refer to the actual projective-relation classes and their Whitney formulas. A formal variable $t$ records degree, so $c_t(V)=1+\sum_{i\geq1}c_i(V)t^i$.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated compatible site and universe bounds. These are inherited from the actual motivic Chern and Whitney suppliers when they are applied below; their finite direct-sum and coefficient calculations add no further choice principle.


**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement, AC and the stated compatible site and universe bounds for the actual motivic constructions.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] The completed actual motivic Whitney formula and additive first-Chern orientation hold for these classes; a line has no higher classes and $c_t(0)=1$. [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities), [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-whitney](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-whitney), [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes)

[F2] The ordinary Chow classes have zero positive Chern classes for a trivial line, obey Whitney, and have $c_t(0)=1$. [math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle), [math:lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula)

### Proof

1.1 For the motivic trivial line, tensor-additivity gives $c_1(\mathcal O_X)=c_1(\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal O_X)=2c_1(\mathcal O_X)$. Subtracting in its coefficient group yields zero. Higher line classes vanish, so its total series is 1. The ordinary Chow trivial line has the same unit series by [F2]. [A1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 For $m>0$, apply the respective actual direct-sum Whitney formula to the $m$ trivial line summands. The product is $1^m=1$. For $m=0$ the zero-bundle convention gives the same result. Thus both assertions include all finite stabilizations. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## The quotient cycle map has exactly the smooth-point image

[Open item](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-quotient-image) · level 21


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed size conventions of the supplied point, support and perfect K-theory constructions. Let $T$ be a normal affine scheme of finite type and pure dimension $d\geq1$ over a perfect field. The source cycle map, transported to the actual affine perfect $K_0$, is
$$\operatorname{cyc}_T:\operatorname{CH}^{LW}_0(T)\longrightarrow K_0(T),\qquad [x]\longmapsto[i_*\kappa(x)].$$
It kills every completed Cartier-curve principal-divisor relation and its image is exactly $F^{\dim T}_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(T)$. Its codomain can therefore be restricted to this subgroup, yielding a surjection onto it. This is an image statement, not an assertion of injectivity of the cycle map or an isomorphism of the entire Chow group with that image.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The stated normal affine finite-type pure-dimensional scheme over a perfect field, Choice and size bounds, and the exact quotient definition above.

**Goal:** Identify the actual map and its image, rather than infer descent merely from naming point generators.

[F1] Affine finite type makes $T$ quasi-projective over the field, and normality makes it reduced. Positive pure dimension and the perfect-field hypothesis therefore put $T$ in the source domain. [thm-author-80f982ded420-quotient-cycle-map-input](item-thm-author-80f982ded420-quotient-cycle-map-input) supplies the established quotient map and its values on generators; in particular all allowed principal-divisor relations are killed.

[F2] [lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata) identifies those values with the actual current point classes. [def-smooth-point-filtration](item-def-smooth-point-filtration) identifies their generated subgroup with the stated pure-dimensional smooth-point subgroup.

[F3] [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) supplies the Choice assumption inherited by the point-class and affine perfect comparison in [F2]; the fixed size bounds are those of these supplied constructions.

### Proof
1.1 Apply the supplied comparisons under [F3]. Let $Z$ be the free abelian group on smooth closed points and $R$ the completed Cartier-curve relation subgroup. [F1] asserts a homomorphism on $Z/R$ whose composite with the quotient sends $[x]$ to the classical residue class. By [F2] the affine perfect comparison transports that homomorphism to the current K-group and sends the same generator to $[i_*\kappa(x)]$. Therefore every member of $R$, including each divisor generator, maps to zero under this actual point-class map. This descent is the exact imported established input; it is not a new local reconstruction of the relation theorem. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 The quotient $Z\to Z/R$ is surjective, so composing any homomorphism from $Z/R$ with it does not change its image. The image of the resulting free-point map consists exactly of all finite integer linear combinations of the residue classes. By [F2] this is $F^{\dim T}_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(T)$, and this subgroup lies in the same-weight motivic filtration by the completed definition. Restricting the map's codomain gives the stated surjection. No assertion about its kernel beyond $R$ being killed has been made. [F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Agreement with the existing projective-relation and virtual bundle first classes

[Open item](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-bundle-comparison) · level 21


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied motivic Chern, Picard and flag constructions. For any field $k$ and qcqs $X/k$, the supplied projective-relation first class of an actual bundle $E$ satisfies $c_1(E)=\gamma_X(\det E)$, where $\gamma_X:\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to H^{2,1}(X)$ is the actual EM orientation. The same holds for the existing virtual first class on $K^0_{\rm vb}(X)$. This statement neither assumes nor concludes that $K^0_{\rm vb}(X)\to K_0(\operatorname{Perf}(X))$ is surjective.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated site and universe bounds. These are inherited by the Whitney, projective-relation, flag-detection and virtual-series inputs in [F1]–[F3] when applied in steps 1.1–3.1. The finite rank partition introduces no additional arbitrary choice.

[F1] [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) supplies actual filtered-root Whitney and normalization on lines; [lem-author-79117e1d72ed-additive-c1](item-lem-author-79117e1d72ed-additive-c1) supplies additive natural $\gamma$.

[F2] [lem-determinants-of-short-exact-sequences](item-lem-determinants-of-short-exact-sequences) identifies the determinant of a line-filtered bundle with the tensor product of its line quotients, naturally under pullback.

[F3] The abstract constant-rank detection statement in [lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection](item-lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection) applies to the actual theory of [prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula](item-prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula) over every field, since its projective-bundle contract has that scope. Its finite-clopen motivic restriction property supplies varying ranks; [def-total-chern-class](item-def-total-chern-class) defines their gluing and virtual extension.

### Proof
**Given:** $E$ or a virtual bundle class on a qcqs scheme over an arbitrary field $k$, with AC and the stated compatible size bounds.

**Goal:** Reuse the sound line/filtration argument with justified all-field detection.

1.1 For a constant-rank $E$, take its flag tower in [F3]. Pullback is injective in bidegree(2,1). On the tower, [F1] makes $c_1$ the sum of its line-quotient first classes, and [F2] makes its determinant the tensor product of those lines. Additivity of $\gamma$ identifies these expressions. Naturality and injectivity therefore give $c_1(E)=\gamma_X(\det E)$ on $X$. This uses the abstract detecting PBF statement, not an algebraically closed hypothesis of a separately worded splitting theorem. [A1, F1, F2, F3]

2.1 For varying rank use the finite clopen rank partition and joint restriction isomorphism in [F3]. The same equality holds on every component, including rank-zero components where both classes are zero. It therefore holds globally. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 For a difference $[V]-[W]$ in the presented vector-bundle group, the linear coefficient of its representative-independent series is $c_1(V)-c_1(W)$ by [F3]. The exact-sequence determinant identity in [F2] kills every relation of the presented bundle group, so determinant defines a homomorphism on that group without a locally Noetherian hypothesis. Together with additivity of $\gamma$ in [F1], this identifies the expression as $\gamma(\det V\otimes(\det W)^{-1})$. This proves the claimed virtual comparison without identifying either group with all perfect classes. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 2.1] ∎


## Integral oriented field coefficient comparison with actual Picard and support maps

[Open item](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-integral-field-model) · level 21


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. Fix a perfect field $k$. The classical coefficient theory here is ordinary Voevodsky motivic cohomology with its Bloch cycle model on smooth schemes. On smooth finite-type $k$-schemes and their closed-support restriction diagrams, the integral Spitzweck/classical coefficient theory used by Navarro and the supplied EM theory are related by the following specified natural equivalence: the unit-induced field zigzag $H_{\rm Spi}\leftarrow s^0\mathbf1_k\to s^0KGL_k$, followed by the inverse of the actual structured EM-to-cdh-to-represented comparison. This is multiplicative, unital and preserves the actual Picard first-Chern map. It therefore preserves the universal projective-relation Chern classes in every nonnegative degree. For every $i\geq1$, it preserves the corresponding completed pointed K-space Chern operations and their maps on closed-support fibers. The coefficient $c_0=1$ is preserved separately as the unpointed total-series constant; it supplies no additive-target support-fiber operation. For regular immersions between smooth schemes it also preserves the refined Gysin and forget-support maps; in particular it sends the positive refined point class to the positive EM point class. All statements are integral in every characteristic. No new smooth comparison or Gysin formalism on singular normal qcqs schemes is asserted.

[prop-smooth-motivic-comparison](item-prop-smooth-motivic-comparison), [thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison)
