[F2] [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-chern-operation-transport](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-chern-operation-transport) identifies all universal Chern coefficients and, for $i\geq1$, the completed pointed K-space operations and their support fibers; the unit coefficient is preserved separately as an unpointed constant. [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-smooth-supported-gysin-transport](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-smooth-supported-gysin-transport) identifies the refined smooth Gysin and forget-support maps.

### Proof
**Given:** The fixed perfect field, smooth pairs, actual coefficient models, AC and compatible site and universe bounds in the statement.

**Goal:** Fill the orientation-preserving-map prerequisite, not only identify groups or conventions.

1.1 Apply [F1]. Its zigzag consists of the unit-induced ring maps and canonical structured graded comparisons. EM regular comparison applies because each smooth finite-type scheme over $k$ is regular Noetherian even when $k$ is not finite over its prime field. The Kan-extension argument identifies the actual Picard maps before restriction to $k$. Thus the equivalence preserves their full natural line-bundle maps. [F1, A9]

2.1 Transport Spitzweck's actual Picard map through the unit-induced ring zigzag. The primary input identifies its restriction to the reduced projective line with the unit-adjoint class, after the stated line/quotient and Tate-coordinate convention is matched. The unital maps of the zigzag preserve that class. Apply the Picard-map detector of [F1] with the represented slice coefficients: their negative weights vanish and they satisfy PBF. Thus this transported map is homotopic to the represented Picard map, as a natural map of Picard spaces. Combining it with the EM square of step 1.1 proves the claimed preservation of the actual first Picard operation, including descent data. [F1, A9, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply [F2]. Relation uniqueness identifies the actual universal Chern coefficients. For each $i\geq1$, functorial completion identifies the pointed K-space operations, and taking homotopy fibers of their restriction arrows identifies the supported operations and forget-support squares. In degree zero, the unital coefficient comparison instead preserves the ordinary constant $c_0=1$; no pointed additive-target support operation is constructed from that constant. On smooth regular pairs, the coefficient-independent purity map and matching Thom class identify refined Gysin. Thus the point generator and every stated sign are transported by the specified actual maps, with the positive-index range of the supplier retained. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 This is an integral statement: the field unit zigzag and the primary positive-characteristic specialization use no p-inversion. The construction is confined to the smooth site; the already defined EM operations on a singular qcqs ambient scheme are used via restriction to a smooth neighborhood and their existing support-to-global square. Hence no global normal qcqs claim is narrowed or replaced by a smooth one. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 3.1] ∎

### Convention and source scope
Spitzweck Proposition 11.1 uses the tautological subline $\mathcal O(-1)$ in its line-parametrizing convention. The Picard operation assigns a line its own class. Concretely, $\mathbb P_{\rm lines}(E^\vee)\cong\mathbb P_{\rm quot}(E)$ identifies the dual of the tautological subline with the tautological quotient. Evaluate both Picard maps on that same line, and use the same Tate-coordinate identification for the unit-adjoint reduced class. The argument compares actual maps with these conventions; the symbol $\mathcal O(-1)$ alone neither proves nor refutes compatibility. EM v1 Remark 3.6 states its tower identification with then-in-preparation [7]; the additional BEM v1 constructions above supply the specified structured bridge, while BEM (6.4) is used for no multiplicative assertion.


## The actual perfect K-space operations satisfy total Cartan

[Open item](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-actual-total-cartan) · level 21


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible universe and site-size bounds of the supplied constructions.

For the actual universal perfect K-space Chern operations $C_i:\mathcal K\to K(\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot},2i)$, set $C_0=1$. For every $i\geq1$ the natural maps satisfy, in the local pointed homotopy category,
$$C_i\circ\mu\simeq\sum_{a+b=i}\cup\circ(C_a\times C_b),$$
where $\mu$ is actual K-space addition and the right side uses the actual graded motivic cup product and additive target operation. Consequently, on every noetherian finite-dimensional $X/k$, the actual perfect operations give a natural total-series homomorphism $c_t^{\rm perf}:K_0(X)\to\{1+\sum_{i\geq1}a_it^i:a_i\in H^{2i,i}(X)\}$ under formal series multiplication. This is a coefficientwise Cartan homotopy/identity; no unproved stronger assertion about a chosen coherent E∞ map of total-series objects is made.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated universe and site-size bounds. They are inherited from the universal-operation construction in [F2] at steps 1.1 and 3.1, and the local free-class/derived-chain comparisons in [F3] at step 3.1. The finite coefficient and formal-series arguments introduce no additional choice principle.

[F1] [thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input](item-thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input) supplies the actual Vect/Grass comparison and universal-class detection for the completed non-A¹ EM ring model over base $X$. The theory has explicit zero negative weights in every degree, as in [prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula](item-prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula).

[F2] [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) supplies actual bundle Whitney on all smooth finite Grassmannian pairs over $X$; no smoothness of $X/k$ is needed. [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) constructs the actual stable universal Chern K-space maps from precisely these bundle classes, naturally in coefficients.

[F3] [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-local-free-test](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-local-free-test) gives the block-sum/free-class comparison for actual addition, and [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-derived-chain-detection](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-derived-chain-detection) detects identities in the local homotopy category by its product.

### Proof
**Given:** The actual EM model and K-space operation on the stated site. Assume Choice and the universe and site-size bounds in [A1].

**Goal:** Establish Cartan for these maps on all perfect classes, not just for bundle-representable classes.

1.1 On $\mathrm{Vect}_n\times\mathrm{Vect}_m$, form the Cartan difference of the two universal bundle classes. Pull back to the finite Grassmannian approximations of the two factors. Those schemes are smooth qcqs over $X$ and carry the actual universal bundles. Their completed Whitney identity [F2] makes the difference zero. The faithful comparison in [F1] therefore proves the universal Cartan identity on this product stack, hence a homotopy of its classifying maps into the indicated Eilenberg target. [F1, F2]

2.1 These identities stabilize without a phantom ambiguity. For a fixed Chern weight $i$, [F1] expresses the relevant cohomology in universal variables with their Chern weights. A monomial of total weight $d>i$ has coefficient in weight $i-d<0$, which is zero in every cohomological degree. Thus both the degree-zero and degree-one homotopy groups of the relevant mapping-space systems stabilize once each rank is at least $i$; their potentially contributing variables have indices at most $i$. The Milnor $\lim^1$ of the degree-one groups is therefore zero. Applying the mapping-space inverse limit to the stabilized universal classes gives the identity on stable $BGL\times BGL$, not merely identities on its finite pieces. This uses all-degree negative-weight vanishing, not just vanishing of diagonal Chow groups. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 The actual $C_i$ restrict along $j$ to those stable universal classes by their specified completion construction, and ignore the trivial-rank summand. Addition restricts to block sum by [F3]. Thus the Cartan difference on $\mathcal K\times\mathcal K$ pulls back to zero along $j\times j$. Apply map detection [F3] to conclude that it is zero as the claimed natural map. This identifies the homotopy class of the actual operations, not a new extension selected by equality on affine $K_0$. [F2, F3, step 2.1, A1]

4.1 Evaluate at $X$ and take $\pi_0$. The coefficientwise identities give $c_t^{\rm perf}(x+y)=c_t^{\rm perf}(x)c_t^{\rm perf}(y)$. The operations are pointed for $i>0$, so $c_t^{\rm perf}(0)=1$. The target is an abelian group: the coefficient first degrees are even, multiplication uses finite convolutions, and inverses are defined recursively. Naturality follows from that of the actual operations. This proves the formal total identity for arbitrary perfect classes. [F2, step 3.1] ∎


## Actual perfect Cartan through degree three on all qcqs field-schemes

[Open item](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan) · level 21


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. For every qcqs field-scheme $X$, the actual perfect K-space Chern operations satisfy coefficientwise Cartan through degree three as derived sheaf-map identities. In particular, for $x,y\in K_0^{\rm Perf}(X)$,
$$c_j(x+y)=\sum_{a+b=j}c_a(x)c_b(y)\quad(1\leq j\leq3),\qquad c_0=1.$$
Their constant terms are one and their positive coefficients vanish on zero. Formal inversion is valid through this degree. The same argument proves every fixed finite degree, without asserting a stronger unspecified coherent total-series map.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. Choice and the fixed size bounds are inherited from the projective-bundle, actual-model, Whitney, universal-operation and local-chain premises in [F1]–[F3]. They are used when invoking those constructions in steps 1.1–4.1, in particular for the actual negative coefficients and bounded-weight stabilization in step 2.1.

[F1] [lem-author-32887006bdff-em-p1-model](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-em-p1-model) supplies the actual non-A¹ EM ring spectrum over every qcqs base $X$. [thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input](item-thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input) applies over any qcqs derived base and supplies actual Grass/Vect detection, also on products.

[F2] [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) supplies actual bundle Whitney on all qcqs field-schemes. [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) constructs the specified perfect K-space operations from those actual universal bundle classes. [prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula](item-prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula) supplies its projective-bundle contract under [A1], with its stated zero extension of negative motivic weights. [lem-adjudicate-a8be8a17c858-negative-model-coefficients](item-lem-adjudicate-a8be8a17c858-negative-model-coefficients) supplies vanishing of the actual represented model coefficients in negative weights in every cohomological degree, as required in step 2.1. Both suppliers retain their Choice and size assumptions.

[F3] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-local-chains](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-local-chains) supplies detection on the present site without dimension assumptions.

### Proof
**Given:** $X$ qcqs over a field, the specified actual operations, Choice and the stated size bounds [A1].

**Goal:** Prove the map identity in its full qcqs scope, rather than strengthen the earlier finite-dimensional lemma silently.

1.1 Fix $j\leq3$. Form the Cartan-difference map from $\mathcal K\times\mathcal K$ to $A_j$. Its restriction to $\mathrm{Vect}_n\times\mathrm{Vect}_m$ vanishes on every pair of finite Grassmannian approximations by actual bundle Whitney [F2]. These approximations are smooth qcqs over $X$; no finite-type hypothesis on $X/k$ is needed. The actual universal coordinate comparison in [F1] detects this vanishing on the product stacks. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Stabilize in both ranks. A monomial of total Chern weight $w>j$ has coefficient in negative weight $j-w$, zero in every cohomological degree by [F2]. Thus the mapping-space $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ systems stabilize once both ranks are at least $j$. The inverse-limit sequence has zero $\lim^1\pi_1$, and the vanishing passes to $BGL\times BGL$ without phantom terms. This is the precise bounded-weight consequence of [F1], not an assumed finitarity of motivic cohomology. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 The actual class maps ignore trivial rank and the free-class comparison matches addition with block sum. Hence the difference pulls back to zero along $j\times j$. Apply [F3] to obtain zero as a derived sheaf-map class. Evaluating on $X$ gives the formula on every perfect class, irrespective of global bundle representability. [A1, F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 Pointedness gives $c_j(0)=0$ for $j>0$. All diagonal first degrees are even, so the target coefficient ring is commutative; truncated series with constant term one have unique recursive inverses. Apply Cartan to $x+(-x)=0$ to obtain formal inversion. The same proof works for each fixed finite $j$, but no claim about a separately chosen E∞ total-series enhancement is required. [A1, F2, step 3.1] ∎

Assume AC and the fixed universe conventions. Its concrete candidate, the oriented-ideal group $E(A)$, is already covered by Krishna's established comparison: for a reduced finite-type algebra $A$ of dimension $d\geq2$ over an algebraically closed field,
$$E(A)\cong\operatorname{CH}^{d}_{\mathrm{LW}}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{d}_{\mathrm{sm,ht}}K_0^{\mathrm{proj}}(A).$$
Here the last subgroup is generated by smooth maximal ideals of height $d$, and the second arrow is the actual cycle map. The cited group isomorphisms supply the comparison part for the explicit candidate. This remark neither verifies a determinant-twisted Schlichting comparison nor asserts a new unresolved formulation or a new proof of obstruction compatibility.

## Free-class detection on qcqs perfect K-space models

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-2ec9cc32fdc8-qcqs-free-class-detection) · level 21


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible site-size and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be any field and $X$ any qcqs $k$-scheme. On its smooth qcqs Nisnevich site, let $\mathcal K$ be the specified local replacement of the perfect K-space presheaf, using the stalkwise local homotopy convention consistently. Put $\mathcal B=\operatorname{colim}_n BGL_n$ and let $\underline{\mathbb Z}$ be the sheaf of locally constant integers. The canonical stable free-class map
$$j:\underline{\mathbb Z}\times\mathcal B\longrightarrow\mathcal K$$
is a local integral-chain quasi-isomorphism, as is $j\times j$. It sends $(m,g)$ to the rank-$m$ translate of the reduced stable free-bundle class of $g$, and carries block sum and integer addition to actual K-space addition. The same construction on the rank-zero components gives a local integral-chain quasi-isomorphism from $\mathcal B$ to the rank-zero local K-space.

For any supplied coefficient complex $D$ and its derived Eilenberg target $K(D,n)$, precomposition with either comparison induces an equivalence of derived mapping spaces into that target. Thus identities between the actual natural operations, or between their two-variable Cartan expressions, are detected by these free-class comparisons. Composing an identity of local-model maps with the canonical perfect-space local-replacement unit gives that identity on every global perfect K-space. No claim that global perfect classes are differences of global vector bundles is needed. Here qcqs means quasi-compact and quasi-separated; neither normality, noetherianity, finite type nor finite dimension is assumed.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated compatible size bounds. These are inherited by the actual model, local comparisons and derived mapping constructions in [F1]–[F3] at steps 1.1–3.1.

[F1] [thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-plus-model-input](item-thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-plus-model-input) identifies the canonical local-ring free-class arrow with $\mathbb Z\times BGL(R)\to\mathbb Z\times BGL(R)^+\simeq\Omega^\infty K_{\rm Perf}(R)$, with $K_0(R)=\mathbb Z$, plus acyclicity and the block-sum/direct-sum comparison. Its local-ring statement has no noetherian or dimension hypothesis.

[F2] [lem-adjudicate-10deda40f9da-affine-k-space-sheafification](item-lem-adjudicate-10deda40f9da-affine-k-space-sheafification) supplies the full natural affine comparison for every commutative unital ring, its local sheafification on the smooth qcqs site, and the canonical unit from global perfect K-spaces. [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) specifies that same local model, its rank-reduced universal operations and its actual derived coefficient targets over every qcqs field-scheme. Only local comparison and the unit are used, without asserting ordinary and hypercomplete descent agree.

[F3] The general first assertion of [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-derived-chain-detection](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-derived-chain-detection) applies to every local integral-chain quasi-isomorphism and every derived Eilenberg target. Its additional application to the older noetherian free-class lemma is not used to enlarge that lemma's scope.

### Proof
**Given:** $k,X$, the stated local model and coefficient targets, Choice and compatible site and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Establish the free-class detection needed in qcqs scope using the already supplied unrestricted local-ring and affine comparisons.

1.1 Form $j$ by the actual free-object/core map into K, subtracting the trivial rank of each finite free object, stabilizing, and translating by the locally constant rank. The canonical comparisons in [F1]–[F2] preserve these object maps and direct sum, so this construction gives the stated addition square. At each Nisnevich local stalk its map is precisely [F1]'s componentwise plus arrow. That arrow is an integral homology isomorphism. The identification uses [F2]'s full-space affine comparison on arbitrary rings, including components, rather than a noetherian version of the local free-class lemma. Hence the normalized free integral chain map is a quasi-isomorphism on all stalks, and therefore locally. On the rank-zero component the same argument applies to $BGL(R)\to BGL(R)^+$. [A1, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 Local stalks commute with finite products. On each stalk the normalized free integral chain complexes are nonnegative complexes of free abelian groups. The Eilenberg–Zilber comparison identifies chains on a product with the tensor product up to chain homotopy. Tensoring the two homology equivalences preserves quasi-isomorphisms here: their cones are acyclic bounded-below flat complexes, and the other factors are bounded-below flat complexes. Thus $j\times j$ is also a local integral-chain quasi-isomorphism. This proves precisely the hypothesis required by the general detection statement in [F3]. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply [F3] to the maps verified in steps 1.1–2.1. Precomposition is an equivalence on derived mapping spaces, hence injective on homotopy classes. A difference of two coefficient-valued operations is a map to the same additive Eilenberg target, so zero after precomposition implies zero before it. The construction and adjunction are natural and retain all descent morphisms. Apply derived evaluation and precompose with [F2]'s canonical perfect-space unit to obtain the corresponding identity on global perfect K-spaces. This does not require the unit to be an equivalence or assert hyperdescent of the original perfect-space presheaf. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

## Second Chern class need not be additive on the first piece

[Open item](item-rem-second-chern-nonadditive) · level 22


### Remark
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible universe and site-size bounds of the supplied constructions. The second motivic Chern class need not be a group homomorphism on the first image-filtration group $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. In fact, for virtual vector-bundle classes $x,y$ the Whitney identity gives
$$c_2(x+y)=c_2(x)+c_2(y)+c_1(x)c_1(y).$$
Here $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$ is the degree-zero group of the supplied nonconnective perfect-complex $K$-theory spectrum, and $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of the first filtration stage in it. The classes $c_i$ lie in integral motivic cohomology $H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$, and the product is its cup product. A virtual vector-bundle class is a difference of classes of finite locally free sheaves; its Chern series is the quotient of their total Chern series.

For a concrete example, take an algebraically closed field $k$, $X=\mathbb P^2_k$, $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$ and $x=[L]-[\mathcal O_X]$. The class $x$ belongs to $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$, while $c_2(x)=0$ and $c_2(2x)=c_1(L)^2\ne0$.

### Facts & Assumptions

[A1] The stated Choice, universe and site-size assumptions are inherited from the smooth first-stage comparison in [F1], used in step 1.2; the actual and virtual bundle constructions in [F2] and perfect-K-space constructions in [F5], used in steps 1.1 and 2.1; and the projective-bundle and derived coefficient constructions in [F3]–[F4], used in step 3.1. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, the supplied compatible universe and site-size bounds, an algebraically closed field $k$, and $X=\mathbb P^2_k$ with its quotient-tautological line bundle $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$.

**Goal:** Establish the cross-term identity and the example, using the actual first image filtration and the supplied motivic product.

[F1] The first image filtration is the image of the first stage in perfect-complex $K_0$. For a smooth finite-type scheme over a field, that image is the kernel of the locally constant rank map, via the actual first-stage augmentation. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration), [lem-smooth-leading-cycle-normalization](item-lem-smooth-leading-cycle-normalization)

[F2] Actual Chern series satisfy Whitney's identity and extend multiplicatively to the vector-bundle Grothendieck group. Their degree-two coefficient obeys the displayed cross-term formula. A line bundle has no Chern classes above degree one, and the trivial line has total series $1$. These assertions concern the vector-bundle group; they do not require a general identification of that group with perfect $K_0$. [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities), [lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface](item-lem-virtual-chern-extension-interface), [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes)

[F3] For a rank-three trivial bundle over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, the projective-bundle formula identifies the direct sum of the three coefficient groups with the motivic cohomology of $\mathbb P^2_k$ by $(a_0,a_1,a_2)\mapsto\pi^*a_0+\pi^*a_1h+\pi^*a_2h^2$, where $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. Pullback preserves the unit and products. [prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula](item-prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula)

[F4] For a smooth finite-type scheme, $H^{0,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}$ is isomorphic as an abelian group to its codimension-zero Chow group. For $\operatorname{Spec}k$ that group is $\mathbb Z$, generated by its unique point. [prop-smooth-motivic-comparison](item-prop-smooth-motivic-comparison)

[F5] The actual universal perfect-K-space construction supplies natural pointed operations $c_i:K_0(X)\to H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ for $i\geq1$ on every qcqs field-scheme, retaining the given Chern classes on actual bundle object classes. Its full affine-to-local perfect-K-space comparison includes components and the actual bundle object map. The actual perfect Cartan lemma supplies coefficientwise multiplicativity and inversion through degree two, with $c_0=1$ and $c_i(0)=0$ for $i>0$. Thus $c_{\leq2}(u)=1+c_1(u)t+c_2(u)t^2$ is multiplicative modulo $t^3$ on actual perfect $K_0$, and agrees there with the virtual bundle series through this degree. Neither premise requires global bundle-difference representatives for arbitrary perfect classes. [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space), [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan)

### Proof
1.1 For virtual vector-bundle classes the multiplicative series in [F2] satisfies $c_t(u+v)=c_t(u)c_t(v)$. Comparing coefficients of $t^2$ gives $c_2(u+v)=c_2(u)+c_1(u)c_1(v)+c_2(v)$. Independently, the actual operations in [F5] satisfy the same coefficient identity for every $u,v\in K_0(X)$, by their Cartan formula in degree two. These are the operations on perfect $K_0$ whose restriction to the first image filtration is at issue. [F2, F5, given, A1]

1.2 Projective space is smooth and finite type over $k$. The vector bundles $L$ and $\mathcal O_X$ each have rank one, so the perfect-complex class $x=[L]-[\mathcal O_X]$ has rank zero. Applying [F1] places this actual class in $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. This uses the canonical map sending a vector bundle to its degree-zero perfect complex, not a general vector-bundle-to-perfect $K_0$ isomorphism. [F1, given, A1]

2.1 Put $h=c_1(L)$. By [F2], the actual bundle series are $c_t(L)=1+ht$ and $c_t(\mathcal O_X)=1$. Their virtual quotient is $1+ht$. By [F5], the actual perfect operations have precisely these values on the bundle object classes and are multiplicative with inverses modulo $t^3$. Consequently, on the perfect class $x=[L]-[\mathcal O_X]$ of step 1.2, they give $c_{\leq2}(x)=(1+ht)\cdot1^{-1}=1+ht\pmod{t^3}$. Thus the actual values are $c_1(x)=h$ and $c_2(x)=0$. Apply the perfect-class identity from step 1.1 with both arguments equal to $x$ to obtain $c_2(2x)=h^2$. This proves compatibility for the displayed virtual representatives using the supplied operation itself. [F2, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, A1]

3.1 By [F4], the underlying abelian group $H^{0,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}(\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathbb Z)$ is nonzero. Its ring unit is therefore nonzero: a unital ring whose unit is zero is the zero ring. In [F3], the element with this unit in the third summand and zero in the others maps to $h^2$. Since the displayed projective-bundle map is injective, $h^2\ne0$. Thus $c_2(2x)\ne2c_2(x)$, proving the example and the claimed failure of additivity. [F3, F4, step 2.1, A1] ∎


## Rational third-edge comparison

[Open item](item-prop-rational-motivic-degeneration) · level 22

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme of Krull dimension $3$ over a field $k$. Let $F^q_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ denote stage $q$ of the Elmanto–Morrow motivic filtration of nonconnective $K$-theory and put
$$F^q_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_0F^q_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to K_0(X)\bigr).$$
The associated motivic spectral sequence degenerates after tensoring its terms and differentials with $\mathbb Q$. Moreover its actual third edge homomorphism induces an isomorphism
$$\epsilon_3\otimes\mathbb Q:\ H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q.$$
Here $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is degree-six cohomology of the weight-three motivic complex; $\epsilon_3$ is the inverse of the actual third-stage projection followed by the stage-to-$K_0$ map restricted to its image. Rational degeneration means that every differential on every page from $E_2$ onward becomes zero after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$.

In particular, this applies to the normal affine threefolds over algebraically closed fields in Proposition 6.2 of the article. It also applies to $X\setminus T$ under Proposition 6.1's hypotheses: $X$ is an affine finite-type threefold over an algebraically closed field and $T$ is a closed integral curve contained in its smooth locus. No normality assumption is needed for this rational comparison on the complement.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Choice, a Noetherian dimension-three scheme $X$ over a field $k$, and the actual motivic tower and third edge map described above.

**Goal:** Prove rational degeneration and that the rationalization of the actual edge map is an isomorphism, including the two article applications.

[F1] [thm-author-14463ef2f4e5-finite-valuative-dimension](item-thm-author-14463ef2f4e5-finite-valuative-dimension) gives finite valuative dimension for a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme under Choice. Such a scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The structure map over $k$ factors through the prime field, which is $\mathbb Q$ in characteristic zero and $\mathbb F_p$ in characteristic $p$.

[F2] Under the qcqs, prime-field and finite-valuative-dimension hypotheses, [prop-rational-weight-splitting-input](item-prop-rational-weight-splitting-input) supplies an equivalence of the actual rationalized augmented tower with a direct-sum tail tower and supplies degeneration of its spectral sequence. This is an imported splitting; its construction is not reconstructed here. [lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-image-filtration](item-lem-author-9f61e4df2141-split-image-filtration) states that every tail inclusion has a retraction and identifies the successive image quotients with the corresponding graded homotopy groups.

[F3] [lem-third-graded-isomorphism](item-lem-third-graded-isomorphism) identifies the actual third-stage-to-cofiber map, followed by the specified graded comparison, with an isomorphism $p_3:\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. [def-third-edge-map](item-def-third-edge-map) defines $\epsilon_3$ as $p_3^{-1}$ followed by the actual map to the image subgroup. [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) supplies the actual graded and spectral-sequence identifications.

[F4] [def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions) makes affine schemes in the article finite type over the base field. Over an algebraically closed field, [math:lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset) says that a nonempty open subset of an irreducible classical variety has the same dimension. Passing to the reduced structure does not change the underlying topological space or its chain dimension.

### Proof

1.1 The given Noetherian scheme is qcqs and has finite valuative dimension by [F1]. Its map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ also makes it a scheme over the appropriate prime field. Thus the rational filtered splitting in [F2] applies. Its stated spectral-sequence consequence, with the actual page identification of [F3], proves rational degeneration. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Let $A=\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$, $B=K_0(X)$, and let $u:A\to B$ be the stage-to-$K$ homomorphism. The augmented tower equivalence in [F2] identifies the rationalized stage-three map with a tail inclusion. That inclusion has a retraction, so $u\otimes\mathbb Q$ is injective: rationalization of spectra induces tensoring of homotopy groups with $\mathbb Q$. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By definition, $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)=\operatorname{im}u$. The rational numbers are flat over $\mathbb Z$, so tensoring the exact sequence $0\to\ker u\to A\to\operatorname{im}u\to0$ with $\mathbb Q$ remains exact. Step 2.1 makes $(\ker u)\otimes\mathbb Q=0$; hence $A\otimes\mathbb Q\to F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$ is an isomorphism. This uses the actual image subgroup, not merely an abstract group isomorphic to it. [F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 By [F3], $p_3$ is an isomorphism and $\epsilon_3$ is its inverse followed by $u$ with codomain restricted to $\operatorname{im}u$. Tensoring this composite with $\mathbb Q$ and applying step 3.1 proves the displayed edge isomorphism. [F3, step 3.1]

5.1 An affine finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian. For the first article application its dimension is three by hypothesis, so steps 1.1 through 4.1 apply. For the complement, $U=X\setminus T$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian threefold and is Noetherian of dimension at most three. Choose an irreducible component of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ of dimension three. The closed integral curve $T$ has dimension one and cannot contain that component, so its intersection with $U$ is a nonempty open subset. By [F4], this intersection has dimension three; its chains are also chains in $U$. Consequently $\dim U=3$. It is a scheme over the same field, and steps 1.1 through 4.1 apply to it without normality. [F4, given, step 4.1] ∎

## Stable triviality forces vanishing of the actual Chern coefficients

[Open item](item-lem-author-b02e51f9da03-whitney-vanishing) · level 22


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied motivic Chern constructions. If $E$ is stably trivial on a qcqs scheme over a field, all its positive motivic Chern classes vanish. If the scheme is smooth and equidimensional of finite type, all its positive ordinary integral Chow Chern classes vanish too. In either theory, this follows by applying the actual Whitney formula to a stable trivialization, without assuming that Chern classes of actual bundles depend only on an unspecified K-zero class.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated compatible site and universe bounds. These are inherited from the actual motivic Chern and Whitney suppliers when they are applied below; their finite direct-sum and coefficient calculations add no further choice principle.


**Given:** The data and hypotheses in the statement, AC and the stated compatible site and universe bounds for the actual motivic constructions.

**Goal:** Establish the stated conclusion.

[F1] There is an actual stable isomorphism $E\oplus\mathcal O_X^N\cong\mathcal O_X^{r+N}$. [def-stably-free-bundles](item-def-stably-free-bundles)

[F2] In each of the stated theories trivial bundles have the unit Chern series. [lem-author-b02e51f9da03-trivial-chern](item-lem-author-b02e51f9da03-trivial-chern)

[F3] The actual motivic and Chow direct-sum Whitney formulas hold, and Chern classes are invariant under bundle isomorphism. [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities), [lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-whitney](item-lem-author-4f94f7982b0d-actual-whitney), [math:lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula), [math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle)

### Proof

1.1 Apply the actual direct-sum formula to the isomorphism in [F1]. Isomorphism invariance and [F2] give $c_t(E)\cdot1=c_t(E)c_t(\mathcal O_X^N)=c_t(\mathcal O_X^{r+N})=1$. This argument applies independently to both the motivic and the ordinary Chow operations under their stated hypotheses. [A1, F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Equality of formal series is equality of coefficients. Hence $c_i(E)=0$ for every $i\geq1$ in each applicable coefficient group. No cancellation of bundles and no comparison inferred from equality of groups has entered this deduction. [A1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎


## Dimension-specific point images and a precise lower-component obstruction

[Open item](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope) · level 22


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed size conventions of the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be a perfect field. For a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $d\geq1$, define the top-dimensional point image by
$$F^{d}_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X):=(i_d)_*F^{d}_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X_d),$$
where $(i_d)_*$ is the exact clopen zero-extension map justified above. This definition has no pure-dimensional hypothesis on $X$; its piece $X_d$ is pure. Its generators are precisely the residue classes of smooth closed points on the dimension-$d$ components. Then
$$\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{cyc}^{\mathrm{Kr}}_X)=F^d_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)\subseteq F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X).$$
For each positive dimension $e$, the analogous zero-extended image of $\operatorname{CH}^{LW}_0(X_e)$ is contained in $F^e_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. The subgroup generated by all geometric smooth closed points of $X$ is the direct sum of these dimension-specific point images, together with the free residue-point subgroup on $X_0$ in weight zero. It need not be contained in $F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The Axiom of Choice and the fixed size conventions of the cited constructions are inherited through [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products). They discharge that supplier’s local-realization premise at its first application below. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

**Given:** The stated normal affine finite-type scheme over a perfect field, the Axiom of Choice and the fixed size conventions of the cited constructions, together with the clopen dimension strata and their established cycle maps, all with AC.

**Goal:** Give the strongest componentwise statement and exclude the falsely broadened fixed-weight assertion.

[F1] [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-quotients](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-quotients) identifies Krishna's source quotient with that on $X_d$. [lem-author-80f982ded420-quotient-image](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-quotient-image) gives its pure image and generator normalization.

[F2] [lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata) and [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) give the actual clopen K-class/image-filtration decompositions.

[F3] [lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-zero-projection-rank](item-lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-zero-projection-rank) gives $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(k)=0$ since rank $K_0(k)=\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ is identity; [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) gives nesting and pullback naturality.

### Proof
1.1 Use the supplied realization under [A1]. Each nonempty $X_e$ is a normal affine finite-type scheme of pure dimension $e$ over the same perfect field, so the corrected pure quotient-image lemma applies whenever $e>0$. Under [F1], the source point map on $X$ has exactly the same generator values as the map on $X_d$ followed by clopen zero extension. Thus its image is the displayed top-dimensional point image by the quotient-image argument. [F2] puts it inside $F^d_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ because it lies in the dimension-$d$ piece there and is zero in every other component. Repeating with $e$ gives the same-weight containments for every positive-dimensional stratum. The displayed definition is legitimate because [F2] supplies the exact zero-extension map and its injective coordinate inclusion. [A1, F1, F2]

1.2 Smooth closed points partition by the finitely many strata, so their generated subgroup splits by [F2] as the direct sum of the component generated subgroups. A normal zero-dimensional affine finite-type scheme over the perfect field is a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions; its residue classes generate its $K_0$ with weight-zero rank generators. This last point description uses the free point group, not Krishna's $d\geq1$ definition on a zero-dimensional scheme. Thus no convention for a nonexistent positive-codimension curve is being imposed on $X_0$. [F2, algebra]

2.1 For a concrete failure of the all-points fixed-weight extension, let $X=\mathbb A_k^3\amalg\operatorname{Spec}k$ over algebraically closed $k$. It is normal affine of dimension three. Its isolated component point $p$ is geometrically smooth, and its class restricts to $1\in K_0(k)=\mathbb Z$. Every class of $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ restricts to $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(k)\subseteq F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(k)=0$ by [F3]. Therefore $[p]\notin F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. This proves the obstruction to using all lower-dimensional smooth points at weight three, without asserting a defect in an implicit pure-threefold source convention. [F2, F3] ∎


## Canonical first motivic class on every perfect K zero class

[Open item](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-all-perfect-factorization) · level 22


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site-size and universe bounds of the specified perfect K-theory, derived-section and weight-one constructions. For every field $k$ and qcqs $X/k$, the actual first EM layer defines a natural homomorphism $c_1^{\rm perf}:K_0(X)\to H^{2,1}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)$ as follows. Let $r(\alpha)$ be the locally constant Euler rank, and let $s(r)$ be the virtual trivial-bundle class of that rank, formed on its finite clopen rank partition. Let $\widetilde\alpha$ be the unique element of $\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^1K(X)$ mapping to $\alpha-s(r(\alpha))$. Set $c_1^{\rm perf}(\alpha)=\pi_0q_1(\widetilde\alpha)$, using the actual weight-one identification. Then $c_1^{\rm perf}(\alpha)=\gamma_X(\det_X\alpha)$ for every perfect class. It agrees with the existing first class on actual and virtual vector-bundle classes under their canonical map to perfect K zero.

The size data consist of universes containing the schemes and perfect-category enhancements in use, the chosen small Nisnevich sites used for derived sections of units, and a suitably small skeleton of the qcqs schemes over the prime field in those universes for the big-site low-layer comparisons. All these categories and their sheaves are interpreted in a sufficiently large ambient universe. These are the supplied size conventions; the assertion retains every field and every qcqs scheme.

[def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface)

[def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites)

[lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site)

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). The compatible site and universe data are those of [def-derived-sections-on-sites](item-def-derived-sections-on-sites), [lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site](item-lem-author-dcdf962edbda-qcqs-site) and [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface), with the weight-one site bounds of [prop-motivic-weight-one](item-prop-motivic-weight-one). These premises are used through the supplied rank-zero and Picard comparisons in [F1], and through the perfect determinant and weight-one identification in [F2], at steps 1.1–3.1. The finite clopen rank-section construction itself uses only finite data.

[F1] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage) supplies the rank and unique lift. [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection) identifies the actual q₁ map with determinant on that rank-zero space.

[F2] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-perfect-determinant](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-perfect-determinant) supplies the homomorphism $\det_X$ on all perfect classes. [prop-motivic-weight-one](item-prop-motivic-weight-one) supplies the natural isomorphism $\gamma_X$. [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-bundle-comparison](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-bundle-comparison) matches actual/virtual bundle first classes.

### Proof
**Given:** A field $k$, a qcqs $k$-scheme $X$, Choice, the stated site-size and universe bounds, and $\alpha\in K_0(X)$ in the supplied perfect model.

**Goal:** Justify the definition on all classes and prove the formula.

1.1 The rank function has finite image on qcqs $X$. For each clopen rank stratum, extension of its trivial line by zero is a finite locally free sheaf (rank1 there, rank0 elsewhere). Integer combinations of these classes define $s(r)$, including negative ranks. Refining partitions leaves the class unchanged by direct sums on clopen components. Thus $s$ is a natural additive section of rank. Its determinant is the trivial line: each component trivial bundle has trivial determinant there and in rank zero elsewhere, with the canonical gluing. [F1, F2, construct, A1]

2.1 The difference $\alpha-s(r(\alpha))$ has rank zero. By [F1] it has the unique stated first-stage lift, so the displayed definition uses no representative of $\alpha$ and no global vector-bundle presentation. All constituent maps are natural and additive, hence so is $c_1^{\rm perf}$. [F1, step 1.1, A1]

3.1 By [F1], the projected rank-zero lift equals $\gamma_X(\det_X(\alpha-s(r(\alpha))))$. By the trivial determinant from step 1.1 and [F2], this is $\gamma_X(\det_X\alpha)$. On actual or virtual bundle classes, the latter expression equals their existing first coefficient by [F2]. Thus the comparison concerns the actual EM projection and original orientation, not a new map defined by the desired determinant equality alone. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, A1] ∎


## Actual supported Chern operation and its smooth comparison

[Open item](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-chern-map) · level 22


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the motivic and perfect K-theory constructions. Let $k$ be any field, let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme, and let $i\geq1$. The actual EM Chern classes admit natural pointed K-space operations
$$C_i:\Omega^\infty K(X)\longrightarrow\Omega^\infty\bigl(H\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}(X)[2i]\bigr),$$
where $H\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}(X)$ is the Eilenberg–Mac Lane spectrum of the supplied weight-$i$ cochain complex. Their global values on bundles are the supplied projective-relation classes. For affine $X$, their values on the specified perfect $K_0(X)$ agree with the supplied virtual-series classes. These assertions require no normality, noetherianity or dimension bound.

Let $x\in X$ be a closed point and put $U=X\setminus\{x\}$. Write $K(X/U)=\operatorname{fib}(K(X)\to K(U))$ and $M_i(X/U)=\operatorname{fib}(H\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}(X)\to H\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}(U))$. On non-quasi-compact opens use exactly the inverse-limit extensions over quasi-compact opens in the supplied support convention. Taking fibers of the pointed operations gives operations of pointed sets
$$c_{i,x}^{\rm fib}:\pi_0K(X/U)\longrightarrow H^{2i,i}_x(X),\qquad H^{2i,i}_x(X)=\pi_0\bigl(M_i(X/U)[2i]\bigr).$$
They commute with open restriction and forgetting support. If $U$ is quasi-compact, localization identifies $K(X/U)$ with the category-defined supported perfect K-spectrum $K_x(X)$; the resulting operation is denoted $c_{i,x}:K_{0,x}(X)\to H^{2i,i}_x(X)$. Under this hypothesis, restriction to every quasi-compact open neighbourhood of $x$ is an excision identification for both support theories. For a non-quasi-compact complement, only the declared fiber construction is used here, without claiming that localization comparison. Higher Chern operations are not asserted additive.

For the classical comparison assume additionally that $k$ is perfect and $x$ has a smooth affine finite-type open neighbourhood $V\subseteq X$. Restriction of the fiber operation to $(V,x)$ is the classical integral motivic universal operation used in supported Riemann–Roch, through the actual multiplicative coefficient comparison preserving the original Picard orientation. When $U$ is quasi-compact this is also its identification by support excision. Use the size-bounded site of smooth qcqs schemes of finite presentation over $V$, with all $V$-morphisms and Zariski covers; its objects and relevant quasi-compact opens are smooth finite-type $k$-schemes. In the article's application, $k$ is algebraically closed in arbitrary characteristic, $X$ is a normal affine finite-type threefold, and $x$ is a smooth closed point on a three-dimensional component; one can choose $V$ of pure dimension three. The pointed construction is only for $i\geq1$; $c_0=1$ remains an unpointed global constant.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. These are inherited by the actual EM spectrum and orientation models, the sheaf K-space construction, the smooth coefficient comparison, the bundle and virtual Chern constructions, and the support/localization constructions below. These premises are used in steps 1.1–4.1; no additional choice principle is asserted.

[F1] [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) gives the positive-index formal universal-Chern/K-space construction and its map-level coefficient and restriction naturality. It includes the full affine K-space comparison, the canonical unit from actual perfect K-values into the local model, and the inverse-limit extension on open complements. [lem-author-32887006bdff-em-p1-model](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-em-p1-model) and [lem-author-32887006bdff-actual-orientation](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-actual-orientation) supply its actual EM ring model and Picard orientation over the qcqs base $X$. A comparison of only $K_1$ or only target groups is not substituted for this input.

[F2] [lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-chern-operation-transport](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-chern-operation-transport) supplies the actual smooth square of pointed universal Chern maps and its support fibers. [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-integral-field-model](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-integral-field-model) supplies the integral multiplicative, orientation-preserving coefficient comparison on smooth finite-type pairs over a perfect field. [prop-smooth-motivic-comparison](item-prop-smooth-motivic-comparison) fixes the ordinary Voevodsky/Bloch classical theory. These are used only under the additional comparison hypotheses in the Statement.

[F3] [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes), [def-total-chern-class](item-def-total-chern-class) and [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) specify the projective relation, normalization and actual virtual bundle coefficients. [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge) identifies the specified affine perfect $K_0$ with the bundle group, by the same object classes, over every commutative unital ring.

[F4] [lem-affine-bundle-module-interface](item-lem-affine-bundle-module-interface) identifies affine bundles with finite projective modules, preserving sums. The module assertion of [lem-finite-projective-complements](item-lem-finite-projective-complements) gives a finite projective complement over every ring. Only that assertion, not its separately locally noetherian Grothendieck-group clause, is used below; the affine object-class bridge supplies the bundle difference.

[F5] [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support) fixes the unshifted support spectrum $M_i(X/U)$, its $[2i]$ shift, and the actual inverse-limit extension on non-quasi-compact opens. In particular $\pi_0(M_i(X/U)[2i])=H^{2i,i}_x(X)$. [prop-perfect-k-localization-input](item-prop-perfect-k-localization-input) supplies the category-to-fiber comparison and K-theory open descent/excision when the complement and neighbourhood are quasi-compact.

[F6] [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) supplies derived Nisnevich descent for the actual EM complexes on all qcqs schemes over the prime field and, by restriction, over $k$. Hence a cover by two quasi-compact opens has a homotopy-cartesian restriction square. [lem-open-excision-for-support-fibers](item-lem-open-excision-for-support-fibers) turns that square into motivic support excision; it is not inferred merely from the existence of a fiber.


**Given:** The qcqs field-scheme $X$, the positive integer $i$, the closed point when supports are used, and [A1]. For the localization/excision assertions assume the complement is quasi-compact. For the classical comparison assume the perfect field and smooth affine finite-type neighbourhood $V$ in the Statement.

**Goal:** Construct the actual operations and their support, restriction and classical comparison maps with the stated hypotheses.

### Proof
1.1 Fix $i\geq1$. Use the EM P¹-ring model of [F1] on the size-bounded smooth qcqs site over $X$, which includes the identity of $X$ and its quasi-compact opens. The universal bundle classes are the projective-relation classes of [F3]; their stability under $E\mapsto E\oplus\mathcal O$ follows from actual Whitney. Apply [F1] to obtain the pointed maps on the local perfect K-space model, and compose on derived sections with its canonical unit from the actual K-values. This gives the displayed maps $C_i$ and their actual restriction arrows; the target is the shifted Eilenberg spectrum in the Statement. Their values on bundles are the original classes. The full affine comparison and local-replacement unit, rather than an assertion of unbounded K-hyperdescent or global bundle representation, are the specified inputs. [A1, F1, F3, construct]

2.1 On affine $X$, [F3] represents each perfect class as $[P]-[Q]$ for actual bundles. Apply [F4] to obtain a finite projective complement $Q^{\prime}$ with $Q\oplus Q^{\prime}\cong\mathcal O_X^N$. The same class is $[P\oplus Q^{\prime}]-[\mathcal O_X^N]$. The completed universal construction in [F1] projects away from trivial rank, so its Chern value is that of the actual bundle $P\oplus Q^{\prime}$. The actual Whitney identity gives $c_t(Q)c_t(Q^{\prime})=c_t(\mathcal O_X^N)=1$ and thus $c_t(P\oplus Q^{\prime})=c_t(P)c_t(Q)^{-1}$. Its positive coefficients are precisely the prescribed virtual-series values. Varying ranks are handled on the finite clopen rank strata as in [F3]; no global bundle-difference representation on nonaffine schemes is used. [A1, F1, F3, F4, step 1.1]

2.2 If $U$ is not quasi-compact, take the inverse limits of the natural operations over its quasi-compact open subsets, exactly as prescribed in [F1] and [F5]. These subsets are qcqs by quasi-separatedness of $X$. Since $\Omega^\infty$ preserves limits, the resulting source and target spaces are those of the declared extensions. Apply these natural pointed maps to the restriction arrow from $X$ to $U$ and take homotopy fibers over zero. The target is $\Omega^\infty(M_i(X/U)[2i])$, whose $\pi_0$ is $H^{2i,i}_x(X)$ by [F5]. Taking $\pi_0$ defines $c_{i,x}^{\rm fib}$. The natural fiber projections give the support-to-global square; compatible restrictions give open naturality. If $U$ is quasi-compact, [F5] also identifies the source with $K_x(X)$ and its support-forgetting map. This yields the asserted $c_{i,x}$ on the category-defined group. No additive spectrum map for the individual higher Chern operations is asserted. [A1, F1, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 Assume $U$ quasi-compact and let $W\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open containing $x$. Then $X=U\cup W$, and $U\cap W=W\setminus\{x\}$ is quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness. The K-localization/open-descent supplier in [F5] and the actual derived motivic descent in [F6] therefore apply to the same four qcqs opens. The conditional excision lemma of [F6] identifies the support fibers on $X$ and $W$; for K-theory these are also the category-defined support spectra by [F5]. Naturality of step 2.2 gives the commuting squares of supported Chern operations under these excision equivalences, compatible with forgetting support. [A1, F5, F6, step 2.2]

4.1 Under the additional classical-comparison hypotheses, every object of the stated smooth finite-presentation qcqs site over $V$ is smooth finite type over the perfect field $k$. The same holds for its quasi-compact opens, including $V\setminus\{x\}$, since $V$ is noetherian. Thus [F2] applies naturally to the coefficient restriction diagram on $(V,x)$. It preserves products and the actual Picard first class, so the supplied operation-transport square identifies the projective-relation universal classes, their completed pointed K-space maps, and their support fibers. By step 2.2 this is the restriction of the constructed operation; when $U$ is quasi-compact, step 3.1 makes it the asserted excision identification. In the article specialization, algebraic closedness implies perfectness, finite type over a field makes $X$ noetherian and $U$ quasi-compact, and the smooth locus near the stated point has an affine finite-type neighbourhood of pure dimension three. Hence the article's $i=3$ application satisfies all these hypotheses without narrowing the general qcqs construction. The same actual Picard operation is compared throughout; the name of a tautological line alone introduces no extra sign. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎

The ordinary total-series constant is $c_0=1$. It is unpointed and is not asserted to give an additive-target support-fiber operation. The supported target in step 2.2 is the fiber of $\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}[2i]$ under restriction; its zeroth homotopy is $H^{2i,i}_x(X)$ in the declared cohomological convention.

## The actual supported third edge sends the positive point class to its residue object

[Open item](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-actual-edge) · level 22


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the motivic and support constructions. Let $k$ be algebraically closed of arbitrary characteristic, let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension three, and let $x$ be a smooth closed point. Let $i:\operatorname{Spec}k(x)\hookrightarrow X$ be the closed immersion. Write $u_x=[i_*k(x)]\in K_{0,x}(X)$ and let $\delta_x\in H^{6,3}_x(X,\mathbb Z)$ be the positive fundamental point-cycle class. Put $F^3_xK(X)=\operatorname{fib}(F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X\setminus\{x\}))$, and define $K_x(X)$ by the analogous restriction fiber of $K$. For this pair, the actual stage augmentation $a_{3,x}:F^3_xK(X)\to K_x(X)$ is an equivalence and its stage-to-layer map induces an isomorphism $p_{3,x}:\pi_0F^3_xK(X)\to H^{6,3}_x(X,\mathbb Z)$. The supported edge $\epsilon_{3,x}=\pi_0a_{3,x}\circ p_{3,x}^{-1}$ satisfies $\epsilon_{3,x}(\delta_x)=u_x$. It is the inverse of the actual inverse-augmentation leading projection, not an independent group identification.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] [thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-supported-slice-positive-cycle-input](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-supported-slice-positive-cycle-input) is explicitly a codimension-$q$ theorem. For a smooth affine neighbourhood $V$, integral support $\{x\}$ and $q=3$, its leading map is stage augmentation inverse followed by slice projection, with coefficient $K_0^x(V)\to G_0(x)\to K_0(k(x))\xrightarrow{\dim}\mathbb Z$.

[F2] [thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-augmented-slice-comparison) and [lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-augmented-filtered-support-transport](item-lem-author-16f30f6b95cb-augmented-filtered-support-transport) identify the actual EM augmented tower and its support projections with that classical tower on smooth pairs. [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-coordinates](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-coordinates) fixes both current coordinates and their excision equivalences. For arbitrary $k$, the tower bridge uses the regular-Noetherian comparison of EM Theorem 6.1(2)/Remark 6.3 and the stated slice identification of Remark 3.6; that identification is explicitly attributed in v1 to then-in-preparation [7], whose proof is not reconstructed here.

[F3] [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) is the inherited assumption used by the positive-coordinate supplier and by the perfect-K and motivic constructions in [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration). The fixed size bounds are those of these constructions; the edge notation agrees with [def-third-edge-map](item-def-third-edge-map).

[F4] [lem-smooth-point-motivic-purity](item-lem-smooth-point-motivic-purity) gives $H^{a,j}_x(Y,\mathbb Z)=0$ for every integer $a$ and $0\leq j<3$ for each pure-three-dimensional pair used here, including $Y=X$ and the smooth affine neighbourhood $Y=V$. [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) supplies the actual natural graded triangles. [lem-filtered-support-exactness](item-lem-filtered-support-exactness) identifies their restriction fibers as the supported graded triangles. [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support) fixes the actual support model and $\pi_n\operatorname{gr}^j_xK=H^{2j-n,j}_x$. These assertions use the same Choice and compatible size premises as [F3].


**Given:** The stated finite-type pure threefold, smooth closed point, algebraically closed and hence perfect field, Axiom of Choice, and fixed site and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Identify the actual supported augmentation and edge on X before transporting the local positive generator.

### Proof
1.1 The finite-type schemes and their open complements are noetherian and qcqs, so [F4] applies to the actual restricted tower on $X$. For $j=0,1,2$ and every $n\in\mathbb Z$, it gives $\pi_n\operatorname{gr}^j_xK(X)=H^{2j-n,j}_x(X,\mathbb Z)=0$. A spectrum with all homotopy groups zero is zero. Thus the three supported graded triangles make $F^3_xK(X)\to F^2_xK(X)\to F^1_xK(X)\to F^0_xK(X)$ equivalences. Stage zero is $K_x(X)$ by the actual stage-zero identifications on $X$ and its complement. Their composite is exactly $a_{3,x}$, so this augmentation is an equivalence on the possibly singular ambient X. [F3, F4, given]

2.1 Choose the smooth affine pure-three-dimensional finite-type neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ from [F2]. The same argument as step 1.1 gives the actual stage-three augmentation equivalence on $V$. The local ring at $x$ is regular of dimension three, so its point support is integral of codimension three; $V$ is quasi-projective over the perfect field. Apply [F1] at $q=3$ and transport through the actual augmented comparison in [F2]. Its resulting inverse-augmentation leading map $\psi_{x,V}:K_{0,x}(V)\to H^{6,3}_x(V)$ is an isomorphism taking the positive residue class to the positive point cycle. Its domain, projection and sign are the specified actual maps. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Restriction from $X$ to $V$ commutes with augmentations and stage-to-layer maps by the actual natural triangles and support construction in [F4]. The K-support and motivic-support restrictions are equivalences by [F2]. Because both stage-three augmentations are equivalences by steps 1.1 and 2.1, their commuting square also makes the stage-three support restriction an equivalence. Consequently the leading map $\psi_{x,X}=p_{3,x}(\pi_0a_{3,x})^{-1}$ is identified by the actual support restrictions with $\psi_{x,V}$. It is therefore an isomorphism taking $u_x$ to $\delta_x$, with the generators transported by [F2]. This establishes the global supported normalization without inferring stage excision merely from K-theory excision. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Since $a_{3,x}$ is an equivalence and $\psi_{x,X}$ is an isomorphism, the equality $p_{3,x}=\psi_{x,X}\pi_0a_{3,x}$ makes $p_{3,x}$ an isomorphism. Inverting this equality gives $\epsilon_{3,x}=\pi_0a_{3,x}\,p_{3,x}^{-1}=\psi_{x,X}^{-1}$ and hence $\epsilon_{3,x}(\delta_x)=u_x$. These are the actual augmented tower maps, consistent with the supported version of the global edge notation in [F3]. [F3, step 1.1, step 3.1] ∎

The Statement is unchanged. Lower-weight point purity supplies the actual stage-three augmentation equivalence on X; the local slice normalization is then transported through the resulting commuting restriction diagrams. The two direct consumers were inspected and use precisely this same edge and generator. Existing source-version qualifications in [F2], including EM v1 Remark 3.6, remain binding. No fresh reconstruction or independent acceptance of the imported slice or purity inputs is asserted.

## External actual supported Riemann–Roch in codimension three

[Open item](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-rr) · level 22


### Statement
For a regular closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ of codimension $d$ between finite-dimensional noetherian schemes, every integer $q>0$, every nonnegative integer $r$ and every class $a\in K_r(Z)$ in ordinary algebraic K-theory, the actual supported integral motivic Chern operation of Navarro §2.2 satisfies the following identity in $H^{2q-r}_{\mathrm M,Z}(V,\mathbb Z(q))$:
$$c^Z_{q,r}(\bar i(a))=\bar i\bigl(P_q^d(\operatorname{rk}(a),c_{1,r}(a),\ldots;c_1(N),\ldots)\bigr).$$
The refined K pushforward and refined motivic Gysin are the specified actual maps. For the EM application assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds. In our application $V$ is smooth affine over the perfect field, $Z=x$, $q=d=3$, $r=0$, so the polynomial has no positive Chern or normal variables and is $P^3_3(\operatorname{rk}(a))$. Refined K pushforward of1 is the positive residue-sheaf class; refined motivic pushforward of1 is the fundamental point class, with divisor normalization and composition as in the source. Forget-support maps commute with the universal Chern maps by §2.2, and ordinary K→KH is compatible with those maps; on the regular pair it is an equivalence.

### External input
Import the supported identity of Theorem3.1, with its actual operations and positive Chern-index range. The numerical specialization of the universal polynomial belongs to the downstream coefficient helper, which uses this input and its projective-space calculation; that calculation is not a premise of this item. The proof does not use the source’s defective Key formula, printed Thom expansion or unequal-rank stabilization sentence. The main supported RR theorem is an established input, not claimed reconstructed here. No counterexample to it follows from the separate background-display findings.


### Exact impact of the retained background errors
The deformation argument in Theorem3.1 uses the correctly printed general excess formula2′ of Theorem2.3, with its top excess Chern factor; this is the applicable version of the malformed Key formula. The argument uses the actual Thom top class $c_d(H)$ and its uniquely refined support class, not the inhomogeneous polynomial expansion in §2.6. Finally our closed support is a smooth point, so its normal bundle is a three-dimensional vector space, and its pullback along the deformation is trivial. The needed zero-section normalization is therefore the trivial-bundle case of Theorem2.7: compose the three Cartier zero sections and apply the correctly stated divisor normalization and functoriality. The false general unequal-free-rank stabilization criterion is not needed for that case. Thus the exact inputs to this restricted deformation/RR application are specified without reproducing any of those three false printed steps. The deeper Kondo–Yasuda/Jouanolou universal computations remain explicit external inputs, not locally reconstructed proofs.

### Exact EM application
[lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-smooth-supported-gysin-transport](item-lem-adjudicate-6e70d30b9793-smooth-supported-gysin-transport) identifies the refined smooth Gysin map and positive point class under the specified integral coefficient comparison. The inherited Choice premise, [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), belongs to this EM/smooth-model application; Navarro’s general theorem retains its stated hypotheses. The first and higher Chern maps are identified before taking support fibers. All background-source qualifications above remain in force.


## Coefficientwise perfect Cartan on every qcqs field-scheme

[Open item](item-lem-adjudicate-2ec9cc32fdc8-qcqs-perfect-cartan) · level 22


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible site-size and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be any field and $X$ any qcqs $k$-scheme. For the specified actual universal operations $C_i:\mathcal K\to K(D_i,2i)$ on the local perfect K-space, put $C_0=1$, where $D_i=\mathbb Z(i)_{\rm mot}$. For every $i\geq1$, their homotopy classes satisfy the coefficientwise Cartan identity
$$C_i\circ\mu\simeq\sum_{a+b=i}\cup\circ(C_a\times C_b),$$
where $\mu$ is K-space addition and the sum and cup products are those of the supplied actual motivic targets. After composing with the canonical map from the global perfect K-space and taking components, the series
$$c_t^{\rm perf}(x)=1+\sum_{i\geq1}c_i(x)t^i$$
is a natural group homomorphism from $K_0(X)=\pi_0K_{\rm Perf}(X)$ to multiplicative formal series with coefficient of $t^i$ in $H^{2i,i}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)$. This asserts coefficientwise homotopies and formal-series identities, without claiming a chosen coherent map of total-series objects. The scope includes nonnoetherian and nonseparated qcqs schemes, with no dimension bound.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the compatible size bounds in the Statement. They are used through the actual universal, coefficient and local comparison constructions in [F1]–[F4] at steps 1.1–4.1; finite coefficient algebra adds no further choice principle.

For the supplied EM model it proves stabilization of mapping homotopy degrees zero and one at each fixed target weight, using all-degree negative-weight vanishing. Its current proof explicitly covers arbitrary qcqs field bases.

[F3] [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) supplies Whitney for actual bundles on every qcqs field-scheme, including each finite Grassmannian product over $X$. ### Proof
**Given:** $k,X$, the specified actual Chern operations and coefficient model, Choice and the stated size bounds.

**Goal:** Prove Cartan on all perfect classes in the full qcqs scope.

1.1 Fix $i\geq1$. On $BGL_n\times BGL_m$, subtract the proposed Cartan expression from the class of the universal direct sum, as a map to the additive target $K(D_i,2i)$. Pull back to each product of finite Grassmannians over $X$. These schemes are smooth qcqs over $X$, hence qcqs over $k$, and their universal bundles have precisely the projective-relation classes of [F1]–[F3]. Actual Whitney in [F3] makes the difference zero there. The actual universal-coordinate detection of [F2] therefore makes it zero on the product of classifying stacks. No smoothness of $X$ over $k$ is used. [A1, F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Pass to the stable classifying stacks using [F2]. For fixed target weight $i$, a monomial of Chern weight $w>i$ has coefficient in weight $i-w<0$ and is zero in every cohomological degree. The supplier's explicit finite-basis and rank-stabilization calculation therefore gives eventually isomorphic mapping-space $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ systems. The associated $\lim^1\pi_1$ is zero, as proved in that supplier. Consequently the coefficientwise identity of step 1.1 holds on stable $BGL\times BGL$, with no undetected inverse-limit class. This calculation imposes no noetherian or dimension hypothesis. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F1] the actual $C_i$ pull back along the comparison $j$ of [F4] to these stable universal classes and vanish on trivial-rank classes. By [F4], addition pulls back along $j\times j$ to block sum with rank translation. Thus the Cartan difference on $\mathcal K\times\mathcal K$ pulls back to zero by step 2.1, for every pair of locally constant ranks. Apply the two-variable detection in [F4] to conclude that the Cartan difference itself is zero. This is an identity of the specified natural local-model maps. [A1, F1, F4, step 2.1]

4.1 Evaluate the identity of step 3.1 on derived sections over $X$ and compose with the canonical perfect-space unit in [F1] and [F4]. This unit preserves addition because local replacement preserves finite products and is natural. Taking components yields $c_t^{\rm perf}(x+y)=c_t^{\rm perf}(x)c_t^{\rm perf}(y)$ for arbitrary perfect classes. Positive operations are pointed, so the value at zero is one. Formal multiplication uses finite convolutions and formal inversion is recursive; the coefficient ring is commutative because the cohomological degrees $2i$ are even. Thus these series form an abelian group and the claimed natural homomorphism follows. No assertion of global bundle generation, convergence or polynomiality for arbitrary perfect classes enters the argument. [A1, F1, F3, F4, step 3.1] ∎

## A nontrivial rank-two bundle with trivial Chern classes on a smooth complex affine fourfold

[Open item](item-cex-stably-trivial-fourfold-bundle) · level 23


### Statement refuted
Trivial Chern classes force every rank-two algebraic vector bundle on every smooth complex affine variety to be trivial. In particular, this proposed criterion would assert that a rank-two bundle with all positive integral Chow Chern classes zero on a smooth complex affine fourfold is isomorphic to the trivial rank-two bundle.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated compatible site and universe bounds. These premises are inherited by the affine perfect-class and actual motivic Whitney/trivialization suppliers in [F2]–[F5], applied in steps 2.1–4.1. They grant no new source-existence or nontriviality proof.


**Given:** AC, the fixed compatible site and universe bounds of the supplied perfect K-theory and motivic Chern constructions, and the exact imported existence input below.

**Goal:** Exhibit the stated smooth complex affine fourfold counterexample and verify vanishing using the actual Chern operations.

[F1] The exact imported Mohan Kumar existence supplies a smooth complex affine fourfold X and rank-two bundle E which is nontrivial but stably trivial. [thm-author-b02e51f9da03-mohan-kumar-existence-input](item-thm-author-b02e51f9da03-mohan-kumar-existence-input)

[F2] The actual right-invertible kernel-matrix construction and matrix-completion criterion supply an algebraic obstruction to trivialization. [lem-author-b02e51f9da03-matrix-kernel](item-lem-author-b02e51f9da03-matrix-kernel), [lem-author-b02e51f9da03-matrix-completion](item-lem-author-b02e51f9da03-matrix-completion)

[F3] The stable isomorphism fixes the perfect K-zero class and determinant line. [lem-author-b02e51f9da03-stable-invariants](item-lem-author-b02e51f9da03-stable-invariants)

[F4] The trivial-bundle series and actual motivic/Chow Whitney identities give zero positive Chern coefficients for every stable trivial bundle. [lem-author-b02e51f9da03-trivial-chern](item-lem-author-b02e51f9da03-trivial-chern), [lem-author-b02e51f9da03-whitney-vanishing](item-lem-author-b02e51f9da03-whitney-vanishing)

[F5] The ordinary Chow Chern classes are the quotient-projective-bundle classes on a smooth scheme; the article\'s motivic classes are the actual projective-relation classes. [math:def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle), [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes)

### Counterexample

1.1 By [F1], choose one smooth complex affine fourfold X and nontrivial rank-two E with an actual stable isomorphism $E\oplus\mathcal O_X^N\cong\mathcal O_X^{2+N}$ for some $N\geq1$. This is an existence witness supplied by the explicitly imported established construction, rather than a newly specified system of equations. Its base field is exactly $\mathbb C$, its algebraic dimension is four, and it is affine. [A1, F1]

2.1 For $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, [F2] constructs a right-invertible matrix $q:A^{2+N}\to A^N$ with E as its kernel bundle. The imported nontriviality means exactly that this q has no completion to an invertible matrix: a completion would give a global frame of the kernel. Thus the bundle is nontrivial as an algebraic bundle even though its finite free stabilization is trivial. The no-completion assertion follows from the imported existence and local equivalence; no independent calculation of matrix entries is claimed. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F3], this actual stable isomorphism gives $[E]=2[\mathcal O_X]$ in perfect spectral $K_0(X)$ and $\det E\cong\mathcal O_X$. Neither equality cancels a bundle summand; E remains nontrivial by step 2.1. [A1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Apply [F4] independently to the ordinary Chow Chern operation and to the actual motivic operation fixed in [F5]. The stable isomorphism gives $c_t(E)c_t(\mathcal O_X^N)=c_t(\mathcal O_X^{2+N})$, so both trivial-bundle series being 1 implies $c_t(E)=1$. Every coefficient $c_i(E)$ for $i\geq1$ is therefore zero in ordinary integral Chow groups, and likewise for the article\'s motivic Chern classes. This deduction uses the actual Whitney identity, not an identification of maps from their targets alone. [A1, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1]

5.1 The pair (X,E) consequently satisfies all the smooth complex affine fourfold and rank-two hypotheses of the proposed criterion and has all its positive Chern classes zero, while $E\not\cong\mathcal O_X^2$. It refutes that criterion and preserves the article\'s stronger stable-triviality assertion. [A1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.1] ∎
