## Levine–Weibel cycle image with pure-dimensional and component conventions

[Open item](item-rem-levine-weibel-cycle-image) · level 23


### Remark
Assume AC and the completed size conventions. In the article's pure-dimensional normal affine finite-type threefold setting over an algebraically closed field,
$$\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{cyc}_X:\operatorname{CH}^{LW}_0(X)\to K_0(X)\bigr)=F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X).$$
The map sends $[x]$ to the actual perfect residue-sheaf class $[i_*\kappa(x)]=\varphi_x(1)$ and kills the specified Cartier-curve principal-divisor relations. Thus it is a surjection onto this image subgroup; no injectivity or identification of the whole Chow group with its image is asserted. The pure-dimensional interpretation is explicit in the source Definition6.5, so it does not require treating the customary word threefold/variety as an original-paper error.

For a normal affine finite-type scheme of dimension three over the same field with lower-dimensional clopen components, put $X_3$ for the union of its three-dimensional components. The exact source dimension-three convention gives the stronger, unambiguous componentwise formula
$$\operatorname{CH}^{3}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(X)\cong\operatorname{CH}^{LW}_0(X_3),\qquad\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{cyc}^{\mathrm{Kr}}_X)=F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)=(i_3)_*F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X_3)\subseteq F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X).$$
Here $F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}$ is the zero-extended top-dimensional point image defined and justified in the local prerequisite. Lower-dimensional strata have their own same-dimension Levine–Weibel point images (and a free weight-zero point group in dimension zero). The subgroup generated by all geometrically smooth closed points across these strata is their direct sum; it is not in general a subgroup of weight three. The explicit $\mathbb A^3\amalg\operatorname{Spec}k$ counterexample prevents that overbroad generated interpretation. None of these clarifications edits the completed pure-dimensional definitions.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The field and finite-type scheme hypotheses just stated, the actual point-map normalization and the completed definitions. These finite-type hypotheses agree with the article’s affine convention on printed p. 3.

**Goal:** Establish the source remark's image claim, its quotient-map premise, and the strongest correct nonpure componentwise form.

[F1] [thm-author-80f982ded420-quotient-cycle-map-input](item-thm-author-80f982ded420-quotient-cycle-map-input) supplies the source-backed quotient map, actual point values and relation-vanishing.

[F2] [lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata), [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) and [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-quotients](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-quotients) supply actual class/model and component identifications.

[F3] [lem-author-80f982ded420-quotient-image](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-quotient-image) proves the image equality on pure pieces; [lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope) proves the top-dimensional formula and the lower-component obstruction.

### Proof
1.1 In the pure-dimensional threefold case, affineness and finite type give quasi-projectivity and normality gives reducedness; the algebraically closed field is perfect. Thus apply [F1] with $d=3$. By [F2] its generator $[\kappa(x)]$ is the current class $\varphi_x(1)$, and its relation subgroup is the completed Levine–Weibel one. Since the quotient map from the free point group is surjective, the cycle map has the same image as the free point-class homomorphism. By [F3] that image is precisely $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$, proving the first displayed equality with its actual factorization. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 In the dimension-only nonpure normal case, [F2] identifies Krishna's top-dimensional quotient with the pure $X_3$ quotient, and identifies the actual K-map with zero extension from that piece. The clopen scheme $X_3$ remains affine and finite type over the same field, so apply step 1.1 to $X_3$ and the filtered product result in [F2] to obtain the second display. The dimension-specific direct-sum statement and its counterexample are exactly [F3]. Thus both the source pure theorem and its precise broader componentwise formulation are established, without adding a false fixed-weight assertion about smaller components or inferring a published defect from a conventional purity assumption. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## First Chern class factors through determinant

[Open item](item-prop-first-chern-determinant) · level 23


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site-size and universe bounds required by the supplied perfect K-theory, derived-section and weight-one constructions. Let $k$ be any field and $X$ any qcqs $k$-scheme. For the specified perfect-complex spectral $K_0(X)$, the first motivic Chern class is the actual rank-reduced first-layer map constructed by rank reduction, and it factors naturally as
$$K_0(X)\xrightarrow{\det_X}\operatorname{Pic}(X)\xrightarrow{\gamma_X\,\sim}H^{2,1}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z).$$
The first arrow is the extended perfect-complex determinant and the second is the actual EM weight-one orientation. For a line-filtered bundle its determinant is the tensor product of the line factors and the first classes add. On actual and virtual vector-bundle classes this agrees with their supplied projective-relation and total-series first coefficients. No global equality of vector-bundle K zero with perfect K zero is assumed.

### Proof
**Given:** $k,X$ and perfect class as stated.

## Third edge isomorphism

[Open item](item-prop-third-edge-isomorphism) · level 23

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $X$ a normal affine threefold over $k$, where threefold means a finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension three. Then the third edge homomorphism
$$\epsilon_3:H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$$
is an isomorphism. Moreover, the actual stage-to-$K$ homomorphism $\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to K_0(X)$ is injective.

Here $K(X)$ is the nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum of perfect complexes, $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$, and $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ is the third stage of its decreasing motivic filtration. The group $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of the stage-to-$K_0$ homomorphism. The group $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is degree-six cohomology of the weight-three motivic complex. The map $\epsilon_3$ is the inverse of the actual third-stage-to-graded isomorphism $p_3$ followed by the stage-to-$K_0$ homomorphism with codomain restricted to its image. A group is torsion-free if no nonzero element is killed by a nonzero integer.

### Statement references

[def-third-edge-map](item-def-third-edge-map)

[lem-third-graded-isomorphism](item-lem-third-graded-isomorphism)

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, an algebraically closed field $k$, and a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension three.

**Goal:** Prove that the specified third edge map is an isomorphism and that the actual third-stage map to $K_0(X)$ is injective.

[F1] A finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian. Under the Axiom of Choice, [lem-third-graded-isomorphism](item-lem-third-graded-isomorphism) supplies the actual isomorphism $p_3:\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. By [def-third-edge-map](item-def-third-edge-map), the stated edge map is $p_3^{-1}$ followed by the stage map restricted to its image, and is surjective. The choice assumption used by these suppliers is as in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice).

[F2] For an affine finite-type threefold over an algebraically closed field, [prop-top-motivic-torsion-free](item-prop-top-motivic-torsion-free) states that $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is torsion-free.

[F3] Under the Axiom of Choice, [prop-rational-motivic-degeneration](item-prop-rational-motivic-degeneration) states that the rationalization of the actual third edge map is an isomorphism for a Noetherian dimension-three scheme over a field.

[F4] [lem-rational-injection-detection](item-lem-rational-injection-detection) states that a homomorphism with torsion-free domain is injective if its rationalization is injective.

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Detect the kernel of the edge map after rationalization, then use its relation to the actual third-stage map.

1.1 The given finite-type scheme $X$ is Noetherian and has dimension three. Thus the hypotheses of [F1], [F2], and [F3] hold. In particular, the domain of $\epsilon_3$ is torsion-free, and $\epsilon_3\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ is an isomorphism, hence injective. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 Apply [F4] to $\epsilon_3$. Step 1.1 shows that its domain is torsion-free and its rationalization is injective, so $\epsilon_3$ is injective. It is surjective by [F1], and therefore is an isomorphism. [F1, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Let $u:\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to K_0(X)$ be the actual stage-to-$K_0$ homomorphism and let $v$ be the same map with codomain restricted to its image. By [F1], $v=\epsilon_3\circ p_3$. Both factors are isomorphisms by [F1] and step 2.1, so $v$ is injective. The inclusion of its image into $K_0(X)$ is injective; consequently $u$ is injective. This proves both assertions. [F1, step 2.1] ∎

## An integral P³ test fixes the supported RR coefficient as positive two

[Open item](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-rr-coefficient) · level 23


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible site-size and universe bounds of the supplied motivic and perfect K-theory constructions. For the RR polynomial of codimension $d=3$ and class index $q=3$, $P^3_3(n)=2n$ for every integer rank $n$. In particular the supported third Chern class of the positive point K-generator is twice the positive motivic point generator. The coefficient is integral and the same in every characteristic.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and fix compatible universes and small scheme sites as in [def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification](item-def-scheme-sites-and-sheafification). These are the foundational assumptions of the projective-bundle, smooth-comparison, point-purity, virtual-Chern and actual perfect K-space suppliers in [F1]–[F3], used in steps 1.1–3.1. The finite Koszul resolution and integral formal-series arithmetic require no additional choice.

[F1] [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-rr](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-rr) gives the actual supported formula, and [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-chern-map](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-chern-map) identifies the actual supported Chern operation and its compatibility with forgetting support through the smooth comparison. When $q=d=3$, every positive Chern/normal variable disappears and only rank remains.

[F2] By [prop-smooth-motivic-comparison](item-prop-smooth-motivic-comparison), $H^{2j,j}(k)=CH^j(k)=0$ for $j>0$ and $H^{0,0}(k)=\mathbb Z$. The projective-space formula of [prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula](item-prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula) gives the diagonal ring on $\mathbb P^3_k$ with hyperplane $h=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ and $H^{6,3}=\mathbb Z h^3$. The triple coordinate-hyperplane point has positive fundamental class $h^3$ by normalized divisor Gysin and its functoriality, included in [F1]. [lem-smooth-point-motivic-purity](item-lem-smooth-point-motivic-purity) gives $H^{6,3}_x(\mathbb P^3)=\mathbb Z\delta_x$ and forgetting support sends $\delta_x$ to $h^3$, hence is injective.

[F3] [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-actual-total-cartan](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-actual-total-cartan) supplies the actual perfect total-series homomorphism on every noetherian finite-dimensional scheme, hence on the nonaffine scheme $\mathbb P^3_k$. Its bundle values are the original projective-relation classes. Thus the virtual bundle rules of [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) and [def-total-chern-class](item-def-total-chern-class) compute these actual perfect operations on the explicit Koszul class and on all its integer multiples. No global bundle-representation assertion for arbitrary qcqs schemes is used.

### Proof
**Given:** [A1], any algebraically closed $k$, a coordinate point $x\in\mathbb P^3_k$, and integer $n$.

**Goal:** Determine the universal integer polynomial value without a sign convention guess or division.

1.1 The three coordinate linear sections cut out $x$ regularly. Their Koszul resolution gives $[k(x)]=1-3[\mathcal O(-1)]+3[\mathcal O(-2)]-[\mathcal O(-3)]$ in actual perfect $K_0(\mathbb P^3)$. The actual perfect total Chern operation on this explicit Koszul class is computed by [F3] from the line-bundle values in [F2], giving $(1-2ht)^3/((1-ht)^3(1-3ht))$. [A1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 Expand only through degree3 in the integral formal-series ring. The numerator is $1-6ht+12h^2t^2-8h^3t^3$; the denominator is $1-6ht+12h^2t^2-10h^3t^3$ modulo $t^4$. Thus their quotient is $1+2h^3t^3$ modulo $t^4$, with first two coefficients zero. For $n$ times this perfect class, the actual total Cartan identity of [F3] gives the $n$th power of this series, whose degree-three coefficient is $2nh^3$, including negative $n$ by formal inversion. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply supported RR [F1] to $a=n\in K_0(k)=\mathbb Z$ and forget support. Its right side is $P^3_3(n)h^3$, while step 2.1 gives $2nh^3$. Since $h^3$ freely generates $H^{6,3}(\mathbb P^3)$, their equality gives $P^3_3(n)=2n$. The injective support-forgetting map in [F2] also fixes its supported sign. This test determines the universal polynomial value for every regular codimension-three point pair. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 2.1] ∎


## Line bundles and first motivic Chern class

[Open item](item-thm-line-bundle-first-chern-classification) · level 24

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site-size and universe bounds required for the weight-one comparison, Nisnevich cohomology and perfect-complex determinant below. Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme. The first motivic Chern class gives a natural group isomorphism
$$c_1:\operatorname{Pic}(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z).$$
Consequently two line bundles on $X$ are isomorphic exactly when their first motivic Chern classes agree, and every class in the displayed motivic cohomology group is the first class of a line bundle.

A line bundle is a Zariski locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of rank one; $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of its isomorphism classes under tensor product. The group $H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is degree-two cohomology of the supplied weight-one motivic complex. The map $c_1$ is the supplied first motivic Chern class on an actual line bundle. Its inverse first applies the inverse of the weight-one comparison to obtain a class in $H^1_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,\mathbb G_m)$ and then takes the line bundle descended from the corresponding frame torsor. Here $\mathbb G_m$ is the sheaf of invertible regular functions on the small Nisnevich site.

### Statement references
[prop-motivic-weight-one](item-prop-motivic-weight-one)

[prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant)

[lem-nisnevich-line-bundle-torsors](item-lem-nisnevich-line-bundle-torsors)

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $k$, a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme $X$, the Axiom of Choice and the site-size and universe bounds in the cited suppliers.

**Goal:** Prove that the actual first motivic Chern class is the stated natural bijective group homomorphism, with the specified inverse.

[F1] The natural weight-one comparison induces an isomorphism $H^1_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,\mathbb G_m)\to H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ under Choice and its stated site-size bounds. [prop-motivic-weight-one](item-prop-motivic-weight-one)

[F2] Under Choice and its specified small-site and universe bounds, the frame-torsor construction identifies $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ with $H^1_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,\mathbb G_m)$ as a group; descent from frames gives the inverse. [lem-nisnevich-line-bundle-torsors](item-lem-nisnevich-line-bundle-torsors)

[F3] For every qcqs scheme over a field, under the stated Choice and universe bounds, the actual first motivic Chern class on a bundle agrees with the composite of its determinant and the weight-one orientation $\gamma_X:\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. This orientation is the isomorphism obtained from the weight-one comparison and the Picard identification. [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant)

[F4] The determinant of a bundle agrees with its exterior determinant. In rank one the top exterior power is the bundle itself, canonically. [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-perfect-determinant](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-perfect-determinant)

[F5] The Axiom of Choice is assumed as required by the cited cohomological and determinant constructions. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Identify the first Chern class with a composite of the frame-torsor and weight-one isomorphisms.

1.1 By [F2], a line bundle class maps to the class of its frame torsor, and this defines a group isomorphism from $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ to $H^1_{\mathrm{Nis}}(X,\mathbb G_m)$. Compose it with the isomorphism of [F1]. The resulting map $\gamma_X$ is a group isomorphism, with inverse given by the two inverse constructions in reverse order. [F1, F2, F5]

2.1 Let $L$ be a line bundle. Its determinant is canonically $L$ by [F4]. Applying the actual bundle-class comparison in [F3] therefore gives $c_1(L)=\gamma_X([L])$. Thus the map of step 1.1 is precisely the stated first Chern class, including its orientation. [F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Since $c_1=\gamma_X$, it is a natural group isomorphism. Its injectivity says that equal first classes give the same Picard class, hence isomorphic line bundles; its surjectivity gives a line bundle representing each motivic class. The inverse is the one described in the statement by steps 1.1 and 2.1. Naturality follows from the naturality of the two supplied comparison maps. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

## First projection is first Chern class

[Open item](item-lem-first-projection-chern) · level 24


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe size bounds required by the specified motivic and weight-one comparisons. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X$ be a normal quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme. For the motivic filtration of perfect-complex $K$-theory, the first-stage augmentation identifies its zeroth homotopy group with its image in $K_0(X)$. Transporting the actual first-stage projection along this identification gives
$$p_1=c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}\vert_{F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)}:F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\longrightarrow H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z).$$
In fact the image identification and equality hold for every quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme over any field, under the same foundational assumptions. If additionally $X$ is of finite type over the algebraically closed field $k$ and $U\subseteq X$ is its smooth locus, restriction to $U$ carries this equality to the smooth first-stage normalization. In this additional case the restriction map on the target is injective under the natural weight-one identifications with Picard groups.

Here quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated means that the intersection of two affine open subsets is quasi-compact. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Finite type means here that $X$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. The smooth locus consists of the points where $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. The group $K_0(X)$ is the zeroth homotopy group of the specified nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum of perfect complexes, and $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of the first filtration stage in it. Write $a_X:\pi_0F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ for the stage-to-image map and $\ell_X:\pi_0F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ for the actual stage projection. Thus $p_1=\ell_Xa_X^{-1}$; on normal qcqs schemes over the algebraically closed field this is the existing transported projection. The broader arbitrary-field assertion uses this same explicit transport. The first class $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}$ is the rank-reduced actual first-layer class; equivalently it is the determinant line followed by the natural weight-one orientation. The Picard group is the group of isomorphism classes of locally free rank-one sheaves under tensor product. Choice asserts that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the small Nisnevich sites and ambient universes used by the cited comparisons.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** A field $k$, a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme $X$, Choice and the stated size bounds. For the smooth-locus assertions additionally assume that $k$ is algebraically closed and $X$ is normal and finite type, and let $U$ be its smooth locus.

**Goal:** Identify the first stage with its image, prove the first-Chern equality in full qcqs scope, and retain the finite-type smooth-restriction assertions.

[F1] The first-stage projection is induced by the actual map to the weight-one graded cofiber, and the filtration, graded maps and augmentations are natural under restriction. For a normal qcqs scheme over an algebraically closed field, the current image-domain convention transports precisely this map along the stage-to-image isomorphism ([def-filtration-projections](item-def-filtration-projections)).

[F2] On every quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme over a field, the actual first stage maps injectively onto the kernel of the locally constant Euler rank on perfect $K_0$ ([lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage)). This also supplies the first-stage image identification over an arbitrary field, without normality.

[F3] For a perfect class $x$, the first Chern class is defined by subtracting the virtual trivial-bundle class $s(r(x))$ with its locally constant Euler rank, taking the unique first-stage lift, and applying the actual weight-one projection. It equals the perfect determinant followed by the natural weight-one orientation and agrees with the existing first class on actual and virtual bundle classes ([lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-all-perfect-factorization](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-all-perfect-factorization), [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant)).

[F4] Under Choice and the stated size bounds, the weight-one orientation is a natural isomorphism $\gamma_Y:\operatorname{Pic}(Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(Y,\mathbb Z)$ for a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $Y$ over a field ([prop-motivic-weight-one](item-prop-motivic-weight-one)).

[F5] If $k$ is algebraically closed and $X$ is normal and finite type over $k$, its smooth locus $U$ is open and dense and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Pic}(U)$ is injective ([lem-normal-smooth-locus-restriction](item-lem-normal-smooth-locus-restriction)).

[F6] For a smooth finite-type scheme over a field, the actual first-stage degree-zero projection is the first Chern class, identified with determinant through the smooth weight-one normalization ([lem-smooth-leading-cycle-normalization](item-lem-smooth-leading-cycle-normalization)). Only this degree-zero first-stage assertion is used here.

[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice ([math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)) and the fixed site-size and universe bounds. They are carried through the filtration construction in [F1] in steps 1.1 and 3.1, the perfect-class construction in [F3] in steps 2.1 and 3.1, and the weight-one comparison in [F4] in step 4.1. Choice also supplies the hypotheses of [F5] in steps 3.1 and 4.1 and of [F6] in step 3.1. No new choice of global bundle representatives is made.

### Proof
1.1 By [F2], the augmentation from the actual first stage is injective on $\pi_0$ and its image is exactly the rank-zero subgroup of $K_0(X)$. Consequently its corestriction $a_X$ is an isomorphism onto $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. Transport the actual projection $\ell_X$ of [F1] along $a_X^{-1}$. On the normal qcqs schemes in the current image convention of [F1], its augmentation and projection are these same maps, so the transported homomorphisms agree. This justifies the stated $p_1$ throughout the qcqs field-scheme scope. [F1, F2, A1, given]

2.1 Let $x\in F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. By step 1.1 it has rank zero and unique first-stage lift $\widetilde x=a_X^{-1}(x)$. The trivial-bundle rank section in [F3] therefore gives $s(r(x))=s(0)=0$. Thus the unique lift used in [F3] to define $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}(x)$ is precisely $\widetilde x$, and $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}(x)=\ell_X(\widetilde x)=p_1(x)$. This argument uses only that $X$ is qcqs over a field, with [A1], and proves the asserted broader equality. [F2, F3, A1, step 1.1]

3.1 Now impose the additional normal finite-type and algebraically closed hypotheses. By [F5], $U$ is open; since $X$ is noetherian and finite type over $k$, $U$ is also finite type and is smooth over $k$. Restriction commutes with the stage augmentations and projections by [F1]. The unique lift in step 1.1 therefore restricts to the unique lift of the restricted class, by [F2]. The first Chern class is natural by [F3], so the restriction square with horizontal maps $p_1-c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}$ commutes. The lower map is zero by the actual smooth normalization in [F6], with the same orientation. This proves the claimed smooth restriction. [F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, A1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Under these additional hypotheses, the naturality in [F4] identifies $H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\to H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(U,\mathbb Z)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Pic}(U)$ after applying the two isomorphisms $\gamma_X$ and $\gamma_U$. The latter restriction is injective by [F5], so the target restriction is injective. Together with the general equality in step 2.1 and the smooth compatibility in step 3.1, this proves all assertions. [F4, F5, A1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Rank and determinant on the second piece

[Open item](item-lem-second-piece-rank-determinant) · level 24


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds required by the low-weight and perfect K-theory constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X$ be a normal quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme. For every $\alpha\in F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$, the composites
$$F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\longrightarrow K_0(X)\xrightarrow{p_0}H^{0,0}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z),\qquad F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\longrightarrow F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\xrightarrow{p_1}H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$$
vanish. Consequently $\alpha$ has rank zero and $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}(\alpha)=0$. If in addition $\alpha=[V]-[W]$ for vector bundles $V,W$ on $X$, then $V$ and $W$ have equal rank at every point and their determinant line bundles are isomorphic. In particular these assertions hold on normal finite-type $k$-schemes.

Here $K_0(X)$ is the zeroth homotopy group of nonconnective K-theory of perfect complexes, and $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of the $j$th motivic filtration stage in it. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite-rank vector bundles; its rank is the locally constant Euler characteristic of its derived fibers. A vector bundle is a finite locally free sheaf, and its determinant is its top exterior power on each constant-rank locus. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means intersections of quasi-compact open subsets are quasi-compact. Finite type over $k$ means a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras.

The map $p_0$ is the actual zeroth stage-to-graded projection, using $F^0_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=K(X)$. The first-stage augmentation identifies $\pi_0F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ injectively with $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ on every qcqs field-scheme. The map $p_1$ here is the actual first stage-to-graded projection transported through this identification. Thus its construction applies throughout the stated qcqs scope and agrees with the existing finite-type projection convention. The first Chern class is the actual rank-reduced first-layer class, equivalently the perfect determinant followed by the actual weight-one Picard isomorphism. Choice means every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds specify the sites and ambient universes of the cited constructions.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The field $k$, scheme $X$, Choice, site and universe bounds, and $\alpha\in F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ as stated.

**Goal:** Prove both projection composites vanish, then deduce rank zero and vanishing first Chern class, with the stated consequences for any bundle-difference representation.

[F1] The decreasing motivic filtration has compatible stage maps to $K(X)$, with stage zero identified with $K(X)$, and nested image groups. For each stage, exactness makes the kernel of its stage-to-graded map on $\pi_0$ the image of the next stage. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence)

[F2] On every qcqs scheme over a field, the actual weight-zero map is the locally constant Euler rank on perfect $K_0$. The first-stage augmentation is injective on $\pi_0$ and identifies its image with the rank-zero subgroup of $K_0$. [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage)

[F3] On the qcqs Nisnevich site over a field, the actual map from the rank-zero K-space to the weight-one Picard stack is the perfect-complex determinant map. On components it retains global determinant line classes, including on nonaffine schemes. [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection)

[F4] Under Choice and the stated bounds, on every qcqs field-scheme one has $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}=\gamma_X\det_X$, with $\gamma_X:\operatorname{Pic}(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ the actual weight-one orientation. This class agrees with the actual bundle and virtual-bundle first Chern classes. In particular, on a bundle difference its determinant is the Picard class of $\det V\otimes(\det W)^{-1}$. The Picard group consists of isomorphism classes of line bundles under tensor product. [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant)

[F5] The assumed Choice and size bounds are used when invoking the filtration and perfect rank/Picard constructions; choosing a single lift of a given image element below does not itself require arbitrary-index choice. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)



**Proof technique:** Transport only the first-stage map through the full-qcqs rank-fiber identification, apply consecutive stage exactness, and then use the actual determinant comparison.

### Proof
1.1 Invoke the filtration and rank/Picard constructions under [F5]. By [F2], the first-stage augmentation is an isomorphism onto its image group, so composing its inverse with the actual first stage-to-graded map defines $p_1$ on $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. This uses the injective first-stage augmentation on the stated qcqs scheme, without applying a finite-type comparison outside its hypotheses. Whenever the finite-type projection convention applies, both definitions use the inverse of the same augmentation and the same stage map, so they agree. [F1, F2, F3, F5, given]

2.1 Choose a lift $a\in\pi_0F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ of $\alpha$, which exists by the image-group definition. Let $b$ be its image in $\pi_0F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ and let $c$ be the image of $b$ in $\pi_0F^0_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=K_0(X)$. Compatible augmentations give $c=\alpha$. The element $b$ is the unique first-stage representative of $\alpha$ by [F2]. [F1, F2, step 1.1, given]

3.1 The first stage-to-graded map sends $b$ to zero because it comes from stage two. The zeroth stage-to-graded map sends $c$ to zero because it comes from stage one. These are exactly the adjacent-stage kernels in [F1]. By the transport in step 1.1 and the augmentation compatibility in step 2.1, this proves $p_1(\alpha)=0$ and $p_0(\alpha)=0$, hence both displayed composites vanish. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 By [F2], $p_0(\alpha)=0$ says that $\alpha$ has pointwise Euler rank zero. By [F3] the value of the actual first-layer map on its unique first-stage representative $b$ is $\gamma_X(\det_X\alpha)$, which is $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}(\alpha)$ by [F4]. Step 3.1 makes that value zero. Thus the rank and first-Chern conclusions hold for arbitrary perfect classes in the second image group. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 If $\alpha=[V]-[W]$, additivity of Euler rank and step 4.1 give equal ranks of $V$ and $W$ at every point. By [F4], $\gamma_X([\det V\otimes(\det W)^{-1}])=c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}(\alpha)=0$. Injectivity of $\gamma_X$ makes this Picard class zero, equivalently $\det V\cong\det W$. Normal finite-type schemes over $k$ are qcqs, so the original finite-type special case is included. This proves every assertion. [F4, step 4.1, given] ∎

The article's original normal qcqs scope is retained, including nonseparated schemes. No global bundle-difference representation or resolution property is assumed. The final assertion applies only when a representation is supplied. The original article's blanket representation premise remains a source proof defect; the rank and determinant conclusions do not require it. This proof uses the actual full-qcqs rank and Picard interfaces instead of extending the finite-type smooth-locus comparison by assertion. Their underlying constructions are used as supplier premises, without new acceptance or audit claims.

## Second Chern additivity on the second piece

[Open item](item-lem-second-chern-additive) · level 24


### Statement
Assume AC and the fixed site/universe bounds. Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $X$ a normal qcqs $k$-scheme. For perfect-complex $K_0$ the actual global operation restricts to a homomorphism
$$c_2:F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\longrightarrow H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z).$$
For every bundle difference $[V]-[W]$ in this piece, $c_2([V]-[W])=c_2(V)-c_2(W)$. There is no finite-type, noetherian, finite-dimensional or global bundle-representation hypothesis. In fact the same conclusion holds on every qcqs scheme over any field with these operations and conventions.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. Choice and the fixed size bounds are inherited from the actual first-layer comparison in [F2] at step 1.1 and the perfect Cartan and inversion operations in [F1] at steps 2.1–3.1.

**Given:** The stated scheme, conventions, and the second image subgroup $H$.

**Goal:** Prove the claim for actual perfect classes, including those without global bundle-difference representatives.

[F1] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan) supplies actual perfect Cartan through degree three on all qcqs field-schemes, with zero normalization and formal inversion.

[F2] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) defines the nested image subgroups. [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) makes the composite from the second stage to the first layer zero. [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection) and [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant) identify this layer on the rank-zero fiber with the actual first Chern class, naturally and in full qcqs scope.

### Proof
1.1 For $x\in H$ choose a second-stage representative and map it to the first stage. Its first-layer value is zero by the consecutive fiber sequence in [F2], and its augmentation is $x$. The actual first-layer identification in [F2] gives $c_1(x)=0$. The same holds for every element of $H$, an additive subgroup by definition. [A1, F2, given]

2.1 For $x,y\in H$, the degree-two identity in [F1] gives $c_2(x+y)=c_2(x)+c_1(x)c_1(y)+c_2(y)=c_2(x)+c_2(y)$. Pointedness gives $c_2(0)=0$; taking $y=-x$ gives inverse preservation. Thus this restriction is a homomorphism. [A1, F1, step 1.1]

3.1 If $[V]-[W]\in H$, additivity of the first class in [F2] gives $c_1(V)=c_1(W)$. Cartan and inversion in [F1] give $c_2([V]-[W])=c_2(V)-c_1(V)c_1(W)+c_1(W)^2-c_2(W)$, which is the stated formula. This proves the special bundle formula without assuming all perfect classes have that form. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Reduced bundle class identities

[Open item](item-lem-reduced-bundle-class-identities) · level 24


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe bounds required by the rank-fiber, determinant-fiber and Chern-class comparisons. Let $k$ be any field and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme. For a vector bundle $V$ of constant rank $n\geq 0$, put
$$\delta(V)=[V]-[\det V]-(n-1)1\in K_0(X).$$
Then $\delta(V)\in F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. If $V$ and $W$ have the same constant rank and isomorphic determinant line bundles, then
$$[V]-[W]=\delta(V)-\delta(W).$$
If $V=L_1\oplus L_2$ for line bundles $L_1,L_2$, then
$$([L_1]-1)([L_2]-1)=[\det V]+1-[V].$$
For every $V$ as above, its virtual second Chern class satisfies $c_2(\delta(V))=c_2(V)$. Finally, if $L$ is a line bundle, then
$$\delta(V\oplus L)=\delta(V)-([L]-1)([\det V]-1).$$

A vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module; a line bundle has rank one. The determinant $\det V$ is $\bigwedge^n V$, with $\det 0=\mathcal O_X$. Quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means that intersections of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. In particular, these assertions apply to all normal qcqs schemes over an algebraically closed field, including the finite-type case. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Here $K_0(X)$ is the zeroth group of nonconnective K-theory of perfect complexes; a vector bundle gives a class in it, $1=[\mathcal O_X]$, and its product is induced by tensor product. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of vector bundles. The group $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of the $j$th motivic filtration stage in $K_0(X)$. The virtual Chern class in the displayed formula is the second coefficient of the representative-independent total Chern series on the vector-bundle Grothendieck group, evaluated on the indicated virtual bundle expression; no identification of that group with all of perfect-complex $K_0(X)$ is assumed. Choice asserts that every family of nonempty sets admits a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and ambient universes of the cited comparisons.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $k$, $X$, Choice, the stated size bounds, and the vector bundles and line bundles occurring in the assertions.

**Goal:** Prove the second-filtration membership, both ring identities, the equal-rank comparison, and the virtual second-Chern identity.

[F1] The zeroth filtration stage is $K(X)$ and the image groups are the images of the stage augmentations. On qcqs field-schemes, put $S=\Omega^\infty F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K$ and $T=\Omega^\infty F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K$. The actual first projection $d:S\to B\mathbb G_m$ is determinant, and $T$ is its homotopy fiber over the trivial line. Thus a first-stage point together with a trivialization of its determinant gives a second-stage lift. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) [lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber](item-lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber)

[F2] For every qcqs scheme over a field, the actual first-stage augmentation identifies $\pi_0F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ injectively with the kernel of Euler rank on perfect $K_0(X)$. Hence every rank-zero perfect class has a unique first-stage class lifting it. [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage)

[F3] The first perfect Chern class of a virtual bundle is the image of its determinant under the weight-one orientation; this agrees with the first coefficient of its virtual bundle Chern series. [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant)

[F4] The total Chern series is multiplicative for direct sums and virtual differences. For a line bundle $M$, $c_t(M)=1+c_1(M)t$, and $c_1(V)=c_1(\det V)$. The latter follows from [F3], while the line and virtual-series formulas are supplied by [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities).

[F5] The Axiom of Choice is among the hypotheses of the cited filtration and Chern comparisons. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Lift the rank-zero class through the actual determinant fiber, then compute in the bundle Grothendieck ring and its virtual Chern series.

1.1 The rank of $\delta(V)$ is $n-1-(n-1)=0$, including $n=0$. By [F2], it has a unique first-stage class $s\in\pi_0S(X)$ lifting it. Its virtual determinant is $\det V\otimes(\det V)^{-1}\otimes(\det\mathcal O_X)^{-(n-1)}\cong\mathcal O_X$, since the determinant of a virtual trivial bundle is trivial. By [F1], the image of $s$ under the actual determinant map is therefore the trivial line class. Represent $s$ by a point of $S(X)$ and choose a trivialization of its determinant; this is a path of its image to the basepoint of $B\mathbb G_m(X)$. The point and path define a point of the actual fiber $T(X)$ whose underlying perfect class is $\delta(V)$. By the image-group definition in [F1], this proves $\delta(V)\in F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. These suppliers apply throughout the stated qcqs scope under the assumed Choice and size bounds. [given, F1, F2, F5]

1.2 If $V$ and $W$ have the same rank and isomorphic determinants, subtracting their definitions of $\delta$ cancels the determinant and trivial-bundle terms. This gives $\delta(V)-\delta(W)=[V]-[W]$. [given, construct]

1.3 For $V=L_1\oplus L_2$, its determinant is $L_1\otimes L_2$. Distributivity in $K_0(X)$ and the direct-sum relation give $([L_1]-1)([L_2]-1)=[L_1\otimes L_2]-[L_1]-[L_2]+1=[\det V]+1-[V].$ This calculation is performed on actual bundle classes and their images in perfect-complex $K_0$. [given, construct]

1.4 Write $a=c_1(V)=c_1(\det V)$. By [F4], the total series of $\delta(V)$ is $c_t(V)(1+at)^{-1}$: the trivial-bundle factor has total class $1$, even when its coefficient in the virtual expression is negative. Through degree two, $c_t(V)(1+at)^{-1}=(1+at+c_2(V)t^2+\cdots)(1-at+a^2t^2+\cdots).$ The coefficient of $t^2$ is $c_2(V)-a^2+a^2=c_2(V)$. This proves the stated virtual identity without requiring a Chern-series operation on arbitrary perfect classes. [F3, F4, construct]

2.1 For $D=\det V$, the determinant of $V\oplus L$ is $D\otimes L$. Therefore $\begin{aligned} \delta(V\oplus L)-\delta(V) &=[L]-[D\otimes L]+[D]-1\\ &=-([L]-1)([D]-1). \end{aligned}$ The equality uses distributivity and the tensor-product interpretation of multiplication. Together with steps 1.1 through 1.4 this proves all assertions. [given, construct, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4] ∎


## Unique divisibility of the smooth-point subgroup

[Open item](item-prop-smooth-cycle-unique-divisibility) · level 24

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the smooth-point construction. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $X$ a normal, pure-dimensional affine $k$-scheme of finite type and dimension $3$. The smooth-point subgroup $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$, generated by the perfect residue-sheaf classes of smooth closed points, is uniquely divisible: multiplication by every positive integer is an isomorphism. In particular multiplication by $2$ is an isomorphism.

More generally, if normal affine $X$ has dimension $3$ but has lower-dimensional components, let $X_3$ be the union of its three-dimensional components. Its zero-extended subgroup $F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)=(i_3)_*F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X_3)$ is uniquely divisible. This assertion does not include smooth points on lower-dimensional components in fixed weight $3$.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The field and scheme hypotheses, choice and size conventions in the statement.

**Goal:** Prove unique divisibility in the pure case and for the stated zero-extended subgroup, including the multiplier $2$.

[F1] [thm-author-b87d598e83f3-krishna-cycle-input](item-thm-author-b87d598e83f3-krishna-cycle-input) gives unique divisibility of the Levine–Weibel group and a kernel killed by $2$ for its actual cycle map on a reduced pure affine threefold over $k$.

[F2] [rem-levine-weibel-cycle-image](item-rem-levine-weibel-cycle-image) identifies the actual cycle-map image with the smooth-point subgroup, using the residue-sheaf point classes. [def-smooth-point-filtration](item-def-smooth-point-filtration) defines the latter for pure schemes.

[F3] [lem-author-b87d598e83f3-cycle-image-roots](item-lem-author-b87d598e83f3-cycle-image-roots) gives unique divisibility of an image when its domain is uniquely divisible and its kernel is torsion.

[F4] [lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope) supplies the pure top-dimensional stratum and the zero-extended subgroup; [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) makes zero extension an injective coordinate inclusion. [lem-author-b87d598e83f3-isomorphism-transfers-roots](item-lem-author-b87d598e83f3-isomorphism-transfers-roots) transports unique divisibility across an isomorphism.

### Proof
1.1 A normal finite-type affine scheme is reduced, so the pure $X$ satisfies [F1]. The kernel killed by $2$ is torsion. Applying [F3] to the cycle map yields unique divisibility of its image. By [F2] that image is exactly $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$ with the stated point-class normalization. Thus multiplication by every positive integer, in particular $2$, is an isomorphism on that subgroup. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 In the dimension-only case, [F4] makes $X_3$ a pure normal affine threefold and identifies zero extension with an injective coordinate inclusion. Step 1.1 applies to $X_3$; its zero-extension map is an isomorphism onto the subgroup defined in the statement. The transport result in [F4] therefore gives unique divisibility there. The definition selects top-dimensional components, so it makes no fixed-weight assertion about points on smaller components. [F4, step 1.1] ∎

## Supported RR and the actual support-to-global application

[Open item](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-rr-and-global-square) · level 24


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the motivic and support constructions. Let $k$ be algebraically closed of arbitrary characteristic, let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension three, and let $x$ be a smooth closed point, with closed immersion $i:\operatorname{Spec}k(x)\hookrightarrow X$. Write $u_x=[i_*k(x)]$ for the positive supported residue class and $\delta_x$ for the positive fundamental point-cycle class. For this pair, $c_{3,x}(nu_x)=2n\delta_x$ and $\epsilon_{3,x}c_{3,x}(nu_x)=2nu_x$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$. If, in addition, $X$ is normal and affine, write $\iota_K:K_{0,x}(X)\to K_0(X)$ and $\iota_H:H^{6,3}_x(X,\mathbb Z)\to H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ for forgetting support. For every $z\in K_{0,x}(X)$ and $b\in H^{6,3}_x(X,\mathbb Z)$, both squares with support-to-global commute:
$$c_3(\iota_Kz)=\iota_Hc_{3,x}(z),\qquad \epsilon_3(\iota_Hb)=\iota_K\epsilon_{3,x}(b),$$
where the second equality is viewed in $K_0(X)$ via the image-filtration inclusion. Thus the global composite equals twice the residue-sheaf class on every such point generator, whether or not support-to-global is injective. The same supported formulas and global equalities hold for a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension three with lower-dimensional components, provided $x$ lies on a three-dimensional component: compute on the pure clopen union $X_3$ of those components and extend the point class by zero.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-rr](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-rr) supplies the actual supported RR formula and its refined-pushforward normalizations; [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-rr-coefficient](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-rr-coefficient) identifies the rank value as $2n$. The RR input's residue-object normalization sends $n$ to $nu_x$ in K theory. Its fundamental-cycle normalization, with divisor normalization and composition, sends $1$ to the positive motivic point class $\delta_x$; the coefficient helper checks the positive sign by its integral projective-space test. [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-coordinates](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-coordinates) defines these same generators through the residue object and the actual supported-cycle model. The compatibility with refined Gysin is supplied by the RR input, rather than inferred from an abstract purity isomorphism.

[F2] [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-chern-map](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-chern-map) supplies the actual Chern support/global square. [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-actual-edge](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-actual-edge) supplies the actual supported edge and positive normalization.

[F3] [lem-third-graded-isomorphism](item-lem-third-graded-isomorphism) and [def-third-edge-map](item-def-third-edge-map) supply the global $p_3$ isomorphism and edge. Support fibers of the augmented tower preserve the stage-to-layer and stage-to-zero maps.

[F4] [lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata) supplies the pure normal affine clopen union $X_3$ and the actual zero extension of its residue classes. [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) gives product decompositions of the augmented stages; their graded cofibers give the corresponding motivic decomposition. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) supplies the inherited Choice premise of the point-coordinate, coefficient and edge constructions.

[F5] For the potentially nonaffine punctured open, [prop-perfect-k-localization-input](item-prop-perfect-k-localization-input) supplies K-localization on qcqs schemes with quasi-compact open complement. [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) supplies derived Nisnevich motivic sheaves at every nonnegative weight, and [lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-clopen-derived-descent](item-lem-author-ab0a6fc202cb-clopen-derived-descent) gives their finite-clopen products, including value zero on the empty scheme. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) identifies stage zero with K, and [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) supplies the natural stage-to-layer triangles on qcqs schemes. These inputs are invoked under the Choice and size premises of the statement.


**Given:** The finite-type pure threefold, smooth closed point, field, Choice and size hypotheses above; also normality and affineness for the global assertion. For the final extension use the stated normal affine threefold and a smooth closed point on its three-dimensional clopen part.

**Goal:** Compute supported operations and identify the exact global maps used by the pending consumer.

### Proof
1.1 The positive-coordinate supplier in [F1], under the assumptions in [F4], supplies a smooth affine pure three-dimensional neighbourhood $V$ of the closed point $x$. Its point immersion is regular of codimension three, so apply [F1] to $x\hookrightarrow V$ with $q=d=3$, $r=0$ and $a=n$. Using [F1] and excision gives $c_{3,x}(nu_x)=2n\delta_x$. Apply the generator equality in [F2] to obtain $\epsilon_{3,x}c_{3,x}(nu_x)=2nu_x$. This proves additivity of this supported $c_3$ as well; no general additivity of higher Chern operations is assumed. [F1, F2, F4]

1.2 The first global square is the one constructed in [F2]. For the edge square, the support-to-global maps of $F^3K$, its graded cofiber, and $K$ commute with the actual projection and augmentation. Since both supported and global $p_3$ are isomorphisms, their inverses commute on $\pi_0$ as well. Compose with stage augmentation to get precisely the edge equality of the statement. In particular $\iota_Ku_x=[i_*k(x)]$ lies in the third image filtration. [F2, F3]

1.3 For the nonpure case, [F4] gives $X=X_3\amalg Y$ with $x\in X_3$. Put $U=X\setminus\{x\}$ and $U_3=X_3\setminus\{x\}$, so $U=U_3\amalg Y$. All these schemes and opens are Noetherian, hence qcqs; $U_3$ need not be affine. Extension by zero from either clopen piece is exact on perfect complexes and identifies its perfect category with the supported category on that piece. The K-localization sequence in [F5] for $U_3\subseteq U$ is split by zero extension from $U_3$. Consequently actual restrictions give $K(U)\simeq K(U_3)\times K(Y)$. The derived sheaf and clopen descent in [F5] give the corresponding product of motivic complexes in each nonnegative weight. [F4, F5]

2.1 Starting at stage zero, the K-product of step 1.3 and the natural triangles of [F5] inductively give $F^jK(U)\simeq F^jK(U_3)\times F^jK(Y)$ for every $j\geq0$: the stage-$j$ and layer-$j$ product equivalences imply the stage-$(j+1)$ equivalence by taking fibers. These are restriction maps, compatible with transitions, graded comparisons and augmentations. Together with the products on $X$ in [F4], they identify restriction from $X$ to $U$ with the product of restriction from $X_3$ to $U_3$ and the identity on $Y$. Taking fibers therefore identifies the supported augmented towers at $x$ on $X$ and $X_3$; applying the same argument to the motivic-complex restrictions identifies their supported complexes. This supplies the claimed support identifications on the possibly nonaffine open. [F4, F5, step 1.3]

3.1 These restrictions preserve the residue objects and fundamental point classes. Apply steps 1.1–1.2 on the pure normal affine threefold $X_3$. The supported Chern operations and their support-to-global squares transport along step 2.1 by [F2]. Globally, the Chern operations are pointed and natural for restriction, so a zero-extended point class has zero Chern coordinate on $Y$. For the edge, the global $p_3$ maps on $X$ and $X_3$ are isomorphisms by [F3]. Given a motivic class with coordinates $(b_3,0)$, the stage class with coordinates $(p_{3,X_3}^{-1}b_3,0)$ maps to it by naturality of the stage projections and the product decompositions. Uniqueness of the inverse of $p_{3,X}$ identifies this as its inverse image; no isomorphism assertion on $Y$ is needed. Augmentation also preserves these coordinates. Thus both global squares and the supported identities extend from $X_3$ to $X$ exactly as stated. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1]

4.1 Apply the two squares to $z=nu_x$ and its supported Chern image. In the pure case steps 1.1–1.2, and in the nonpure case step 3.1, give $\epsilon_3c_3(n[i_*k(x)])=\iota_K\epsilon_{3,x}c_{3,x}(nu_x)=2n[i_*k(x)]$. This applies a support-forgetting map to a supported equality and never cancels one, so it remains valid when the global point class vanishes. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 3.1] ∎

## First-class matching and explicit perfect Chern arithmetic

[Open item](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-first-class-and-coefficients) · level 24


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible site-size and universe bounds required by the supplied perfect K-theory, motivic and derived-section constructions. Let $k$ be any field and $X$ any qcqs $k$-scheme. The first operation $C_1$ of the specified actual universal perfect Chern construction induces exactly the completed perfect first class $c_1^{\rm perf}$ on $K_0(X)=\pi_0K_{\rm Perf}(X)$. The total operations satisfy Cartan in this qcqs scope. Their second coefficient therefore satisfies, for all perfect classes $x,y\in K_0(X)$,
$$c_2(x+y)=c_2(x)+c_1^{\rm perf}(x)c_1^{\rm perf}(y)+c_2(y).$$
It also satisfies $c_2(-y)=(c_1^{\rm perf}(y))^2-c_2(y)$. If the first classes of $x,y$ agree, then $c_2(x-y)=c_2(x)-c_2(y)$. The total operations restrict to the existing virtual bundle series under the canonical map $K^0_{\rm vb}(X)\to K_0(X)$, without presuming surjectivity. In particular every assertion applies on normal qcqs schemes in the original article's scope, with no noetherian, finite-type or dimension restriction. Here $K^0_{\rm vb}(X)$ is the group on finite locally free bundles modulo exact-sequence relations, and the $i$th coefficient lies in $H^{2i,i}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)$.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the compatible site-size and universe bounds in the Statement. They are inherited through the actual qcqs comparisons and Chern construction in [F1]–[F2] at step 1.1 and their consequences at steps 2.1–3.1. The formal finite-coefficient algebra adds no additional choice assumption.

[F1] [lem-adjudicate-2ec9cc32fdc8-qcqs-perfect-cartan](item-lem-adjudicate-2ec9cc32fdc8-qcqs-perfect-cartan) supplies the actual coefficientwise Cartan identities and the induced total-series homomorphism on every qcqs field-scheme. [lem-adjudicate-2ec9cc32fdc8-qcqs-free-class-detection](item-lem-adjudicate-2ec9cc32fdc8-qcqs-free-class-detection) supplies detection from the actual local free-class arrow and passage to global perfect K-spaces through the canonical unit.

[F2] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection) and [thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-determinant-one-type-input](item-thm-author-16f30f6b95cb-lowweight-determinant-one-type-input) identify the actual rank-zero first-layer map with the extended perfect determinant/Picard stack map, retaining line-frame-torsor descent and true/enhanced cofiber coherence. [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant) identifies the completed perfect first class on every qcqs field-scheme with this determinant followed by the original EM orientation, and agrees with the actual bundle first class. [thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input](item-thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input) supplies universal-class detection and fixed-weight stabilization, including mapping homotopy degrees zero and one, over every qcqs base.

[F3] [def-total-chern-class](item-def-total-chern-class) and [lem-third-order-chern-inversion](item-lem-third-order-chern-inversion) supply the existing virtual bundle normalization and the formal multiplication/inversion formulas. Only the formal-series arithmetic is needed here; arbitrary perfect classes need not be globally bundle-representable.

### Proof
**Given:** $k,X$, the specified actual perfect operations and classes, Choice and the compatible site and universe bounds in the Statement.

**Goal:** Match the actual first operation globally in qcqs scope before using it in the Cartan cross term.

1.1 Compare $C_1$ with the extended determinant followed by the actual EM Picard orientation of [F2], as maps on the same local perfect K-space. On a finite Grassmannian over $X$, their restrictions to the universal quotient bundle agree by the actual-bundle comparison in [F2]; that Grassmannian is qcqs over $k$. The determinant map here is the already supplied stack map with its automorphism and gluing data. Universal-class detection and fixed-weight stabilization in [F2], applied at weight one, identify the two stable $BGL$ maps, without an inverse-limit ambiguity. Both maps are zero on trivial-rank classes, so their pullbacks along the entire free-class arrow agree. The qcqs detection in [F1] identifies the maps on the local model; its canonical perfect-space unit then gives equality on every global perfect class. By the completed determinant factorization in [F2], this is exactly $c_1^{\rm perf}$. This comparison never uses equality of affine Picard groups to infer equality of global maps. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Compare coefficients of $t^2$ in the actual total Cartan identity of [F1], using step 1.1 for its first coefficient. This gives the stated formula for $c_2(x+y)$. The formal inverse identity of [F3] applies to the same total-series homomorphism and gives $c_2(-y)=c_1^{\rm perf}(y)^2-c_2(y)$. Multiplication for $x-y$ therefore gives $c_2(x-y)=c_2(x)-c_1^{\rm perf}(x)c_1^{\rm perf}(y)+c_1^{\rm perf}(y)^2-c_2(y)$. If the first classes agree, the two quadratic terms cancel. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 On every actual bundle the specified universal operation is its original projective-relation class, as retained by [F1]. Therefore the total homomorphism on perfect $K_0$ and the virtual bundle homomorphism of [F3], composed with the canonical bundle-to-perfect homomorphism, agree on all bundle generators. They agree on the entire bundle presentation and its image. This proves every asserted restriction and arithmetic formula on the stated qcqs schemes, including normal ones, without assuming that image is all of perfect $K_0$. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎
