## Actual second-stage comparison on every qcqs field-scheme

[Open item](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-second-fiber) · level 24


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. For every qcqs field-scheme, put $S=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^1K$, $B=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{gr}^1K\simeq B\mathbb G_m$ and $T=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^2K$. The actual second-layer map and second Chern map satisfy
$$Q_2\simeq-C_2i_K:T\longrightarrow A_2$$
as derived sheaf maps on the small Zariski site. This is a new full-scope statement proved below; no enlargement of a completed finite-type projection contract is implicit.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. Choice and the fixed size bounds are inherited from [F1]–[F3] in steps 1.1–3.1, including perfect Cartan in step 2.1 and the actual coefficient and derived-chain detection constructions in step 3.1.

[F1] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection), [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage) and [prop-motivic-weight-one](item-prop-motivic-weight-one) identify the actual rank fiber, determinant $d:S\to B$, and pointed section $\kappa(L)=[L]-1$, with an actual homotopy $d\kappa\simeq\mathrm{id}$ on all qcqs schemes.

[F2] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) makes $T$ the actual homotopy fiber. [prop-filtration-product-projection](item-prop-filtration-product-projection) supplies the stage product/projection square on all qcqs schemes. [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant) fixes the actual positive first-Chern convention.

[F3] [lem-flag-tower-line-quotients](item-lem-flag-tower-line-quotients) and [lem-adjudicate-6cf37231df39-arbitrary-field-flag-detection](item-lem-adjudicate-6cf37231df39-arbitrary-field-flag-detection) give line-quotient filtrations and integral motivic cohomology detection over every qcqs field-scheme. The latter uses prime-field restriction, the printed projective-bundle formula applied to dual bundles, and finite-clopen descent. [thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input](item-thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input) supplies actual universal detection and bounded-weight stabilization. [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-local-chains](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-local-chains) and [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan) supply full-scope derived-chain detection and perfect Cartan under [A1].

### Proof
**Given:** The actual maps on the qcqs site and their restrictions to any $X$.

**Goal:** Identify operations on the genuine determinant-trivial homotopy fiber, including all descent data.

1.1 The map $T\times B\to S$, $(t,b)\mapsto i(t)+\kappa(b)$, is an equivalence over $B$: translation by $\kappa(b)$ identifies the zero fiber with the fiber over each generalized point $b$, using the specified homotopy $d\kappa\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Its inverse gives a natural pointed retraction $r:S\to T$, underlying $s\mapsto s-\kappa(d(s))$ with that nullhomotopy; $ri\simeq\mathrm{id}$. No additivity of $\kappa$ is required. The section makes $\pi_1S(Y)\to\pi_1B(Y)$ surjective on every qcqs $Y$, so $\pi_0T(Y)\to\pi_0S(Y)$ is injective. The discrete rank target also makes $\pi_0S(Y)\to K_0(Y)$ injective. [A1, F1, F2]

1.2 For a rank-$n$ bundle $V$, $r([V]-n)$ has underlying class $\delta(V)=[V]-[\det V]-(n-1)$. Pull back to a detecting flag tower and let its line quotients be $L_s$. Put $D_s=\bigotimes_{i\leq s}L_i$ and $R_s=\sum_{i\leq s}[L_i]-[D_s]-(s-1)$. Exact flag sequences give this equality without splitting, and
$$R_1=0,\qquad R_s=R_{s-1}-([L_s]-1)([D_{s-1}]-1).$$
The latter product is the augmentation of the actual stage product of the line lifts $\kappa(L_s),\kappa(D_{s-1})$. Injectivity in step 1.1 identifies these equal K-classes with their unique second-stage classes. The actual product square in [F2] and induction give
$$Q_2r([V]-n)=-\sum_{i<s}c_1(L_i)c_1(L_s)=-c_2(V).$$
Rank zero/one give zero, and finite clopen decomposition handles varying ranks. Detection in [F3] descends the identity. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

2.1 Put $a=c_1(V)=c_1(\det V)$. Full-scope Cartan in [F3] gives $c_t(\delta(V))=c_t(V)(1+at)^{-1}$ through degree two. Its second coefficient is $c_2(V)-a^2+a^2=c_2(V)$. Thus $(Q_2+C_2i_K)r$ vanishes on every actual universal bundle on finite Grassmannians over $X$. [A1, F3, step 1.2]

3.1 The particular difference $(Q_2+C_2i_K)r$ is built from the natural actual stage maps, Chern operations, determinant and line-class section of [F1]–[F3]. Form these same constructions first on the smooth big Zariski site over $X$, where the universal-operation and coefficient constructions in [F3] are defined. This gives a specific big-site difference map; it is not an extension of an arbitrary small-site map. Apply the actual coefficient adjunction and Grass/Vect detection there, then stabilize to $BGL$. In weight two the actual negative-coefficient vanishing supplied in [F3] eliminates every coefficient of monomial weight greater than two in all degrees. Therefore both mapping $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ stabilize at rank at least two, and $\lim^1\pi_1=0$. The resulting big-site homotopy restricts along the open immersions to the small Zariski site and shows that the difference vanishes after its actual rank-zero free-class map $j_0:BGL\to S$. By the first helper's derived-chain detection it vanishes on $S$. Restrict along $i$ and use $ri\simeq\mathrm{id}$ to prove the displayed map identity on $T$. This extends the comparison by a retraction before using plus detection; it never asserts preservation of an arbitrary homotopy fiber by a homology equivalence. [A1, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎


## Factor two in the supported third Chern map

[Open item](item-prop-smooth-point-third-chern-factor) · level 25


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the motivic and support constructions. Let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension three over an algebraically closed field $k$ of arbitrary characteristic, and let $x$ be a smooth closed point, with closed immersion $i:\operatorname{Spec}k(x)\hookrightarrow X$. With the actual support operations constructed above,
$$K_{0,x}(X)\xrightarrow{c_{3,x}}H^{6,3}_{\rm mot,x}(X,\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{3,x}}K_{0,x}(X)$$
is multiplication by $2$. More precisely, $c_{3,x}([i_*k(x)])=2\delta_x$ and $\epsilon_{3,x}(\delta_x)=[i_*k(x)]$, where $\delta_x$ is the positive fundamental motivic point class. These maps commute with support-to-global maps into the current global Chern class and third edge. Consequently the global composite $\epsilon_3c_3$ is multiplication by $2$ on each residue-sheaf point generator of the third image filtration. This conclusion also holds on a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension three that has lower-dimensional components, for every smooth closed point on a three-dimensional component: its supported groups are those on the pure clopen union $X_3$ of the three-dimensional components, and its global point class is extended by zero.

### Facts & Assumptions
[F1] [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-coordinates](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-coordinates) fixes the positive supported generators; [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-chern-map](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-supported-chern-map) supplies actual Chern support compatibility.

[F2] [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-rr-coefficient](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-positive-rr-coefficient) fixes the supported RR integer and sign; [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-actual-edge](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-actual-edge) supplies the actual supported edge and its normalization.

[F3] [lem-author-d026a7b99ace-rr-and-global-square](item-lem-author-d026a7b99ace-rr-and-global-square) gives the calculation on all integer multiples and the two actual support-to-global squares.

[F4] [lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata) and [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) give the pure clopen union $X_3$, its zero-extended point classes and the augmented product decompositions. The supported and global extension in [F3] uses these actual decompositions. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) is the inherited assumption used by the point-coordinate and edge suppliers.

### Proof
**Given:** The stated field, normal affine finite-type pure threefold, smooth closed point, Choice and size hypotheses; or the stated nonpure extension with $x$ on its three-dimensional clopen part.

**Goal:** Prove the precise factor and its global application.

1.1 Apply [F1] under the stated Choice premise in [F4]. In the pure case every supported K-zero class is $nu_x$ for a unique integer $n$. By [F2]–[F3], $c_{3,x}(nu_x)=2n\delta_x$ and $\epsilon_{3,x}(\delta_x)=u_x$, so their composite is $nu_x\mapsto2nu_x$. This also fixes the two requested generator formulas with their positive signs. [F1, F2, F3, F4]

2.1 Apply the commutative support-to-global squares in [F3]. The image of $u_x$ is the actual perfect residue-sheaf class in $K_0(X)$ and belongs to its third image filtration. Thus the global composite on that generator is twice the same class, even if its global image is zero. For a nonpure normal affine $X$ as stated, use [F4] and the extension in [F3]: the pure calculation on $X_3$ gives the same supported formula, and the global class is zero on the complementary clopen factors. Pointed Chern operations, the natural edge, and the augmented product decompositions transfer the same identity to $X$. Thus every smooth-point generator on a three-dimensional component has the asserted factor, with no purity restriction on the global normal affine scheme. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1] ∎


## Murthy splitting input in rank three

[Open item](item-prop-murthy-k-theoretic-splitting) · level 25

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the size conventions of the cited perfect K-theory and smooth-point constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a normal affine $k$-scheme of finite type and dimension $3$. Let $E$ be a rank-three vector bundle on $X$, and put
$$\beta(E)=[\mathcal O_X]-[E]+[\Lambda^2E]-[\det E]\in K_0(X).$$
If $\beta(E)=0$ in $K_0(X)$, then $E\cong\mathcal O_X\oplus E'$ for a rank-two vector bundle $E'$.

In particular, this applies when $\beta(E)$ is trivial in $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$ for pure-dimensional $X$. If $X$ also has lower-dimensional components, the corresponding hypothesis may instead be stated using the zero-extended top-dimensional subgroup $F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)$; it does not include all smooth points on those lower-dimensional components.

Here a vector bundle is a finite locally free sheaf, and rank three means locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^3$. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. The group $K_0(X)$ is the degree-zero perfect K-theory group in [def-rank-three-euler-k-class](item-def-rank-three-euler-k-class). The pure smooth-point subgroup in [def-smooth-point-filtration](item-def-smooth-point-filtration) is generated by the classes of residue sheaves at smooth closed points. Its top-dimensional zero extension for a nonpure normal scheme is specified in [lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope).

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The field, scheme, bundle, choice and size hypotheses in the statement, and $\beta(E)=0$ in $K_0(X)$.

**Goal:** Construct a decomposition of $E$ into a trivial line and a rank-two bundle, and establish the stated subgroup implications.

[F1] [lem-affine-bundle-module-interface](item-lem-affine-bundle-module-interface) identifies vector bundles on $X$ with finite projective $A$-modules, compatibly with rank, direct sums and duals. [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge) identifies the projective-module Grothendieck group with the specified perfect $K_0(X)$ and sends a bounded finite-projective resolution to its alternating class.

[F2] For $P=\Gamma(X,E)$, [lem-author-394a5b71198d-exterior-dual-interface](item-lem-author-394a5b71198d-exterior-dual-interface) identifies $C^K_3(P)=\sum_{i=0}^3(-1)^i[\Lambda^iP^*]$, where $P^*=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)$, with the dual exterior class in perfect $K_0(X)$. It also proves that this class and $\beta(E)$ vanish simultaneously.

[F3] [prop-smooth-cycle-unique-divisibility](item-prop-smooth-cycle-unique-divisibility) gives unique divisibility, in particular absence of $2$-torsion, for the pure smooth-point subgroup and for its zero-extended top-dimensional counterpart. [lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope) identifies the latter's generators as the residue classes of smooth closed points on the three-dimensional components.

[F4] [thm-author-394a5b71198d-murthy-module-splitting-input](item-thm-author-394a5b71198d-murthy-module-splitting-input) imports Murthy's criterion: for a reduced affine algebra of dimension $n\geq2$ over an algebraically closed field, if the subgroup of projective $K_0$ generated by residue-field classes of height-$n$ smooth closed points has no $(n-1)!$ torsion, then a rank-$n$ finite projective module splits off a free rank-one summand when its exterior-dual class vanishes. Its external-input section and reference give the precise source and reading limits.

### Proof

1.1 A finite-type algebra over a field is noetherian, and normality makes $A$ reduced. By [F1], $P=\Gamma(X,E)$ is finite projective of constant rank $3$, and $E$ is its associated bundle. The affine K-zero comparison in [F1] is an isomorphism. [F1, given]

2.1 Let $G\subset K_0^{\mathrm{proj}}(A)$ be the subgroup in [F4] for $n=3$. A height-three smooth closed point lies on a three-dimensional component, and conversely a smooth closed point on a three-dimensional component has height three. Over the perfect field $k$, these are the point classes in [F3]. Their residue modules admit finite projective resolutions: at such a point the local ring is regular, while the residue module is supported only there; the associated perfect residue sheaf has the same class as the alternating resolution by [F1]. Hence the comparison in [F1] identifies $G$ with $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$ in the pure case and with $F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)$ in the general normal case. By [F3], multiplication by $2$ is injective on that image, and therefore on $G$. Thus $G$ has no $(3-1)!=2$ torsion. [F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F2], $\beta(E)=0$ implies that the image of $C^K_3(P)$ in perfect $K_0(X)$ is zero. The comparison is injective by [F1], so $C^K_3(P)=0$ in projective $K_0(A)$. The reducedness, dimension, field, rank and factorial-torsion hypotheses of [F4] now hold. It follows that $P\cong A\oplus Q$ for a finite projective module $Q$ of rank two. Applying the affine equivalence gives $E\cong\mathcal O_X\oplus\widetilde Q$, where $\widetilde Q$ is a rank-two vector bundle. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 The pure smooth-point subgroup and the zero-extended top-dimensional subgroup are subgroups of $K_0(X)$ by their definitions. Thus an element trivial in either subgroup is zero in $K_0(X)$, and step 3.1 applies. The stated nonpure convention follows from [F3]. This proves the splitting implication and its subgroup formulations. [F3, step 3.1] ∎

## Apply the actual perfect Cartan identity to the second image

[Open item](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-second-subgroup) · level 25


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix the site and universe bounds of the supplied perfect K-theory, motivic filtration and Chern-operation constructions. Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $X$ be a normal quasi-compact quasi-separated (qcqs) $k$-scheme. The actual second motivic Chern operation restricts to a group homomorphism
$$c_2:H=F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\longrightarrow H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z).$$
In particular $c_2(0)=0$ and $c_2(-x)=-c_2(x)$ for $x\in H$. Whenever $[V]-[W]\in H$ for vector bundles $V,W$ on $X$, one has $c_2([V]-[W])=c_2(V)-c_2(W)$, with their original bundle Chern coefficients.

Here $K_0(X)$ is the zeroth homotopy group of nonconnective K-theory of perfect complexes, and $H$ is the image of the second filtration stage in that group. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves; a vector bundle is a finite locally free sheaf. Normality means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means that intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact. No finite-type, noetherian, dimension or global bundle-representation hypothesis is required.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The Axiom of Choice, as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice), and the fixed site and universe bounds are inherited by the supplied perfect-category realizations, motivic constructions and local integral-chain comparisons. They are used when invoking those suppliers in steps 1.1–3.1; choosing a lift of one image element is not itself an arbitrary-index choice argument.

[F1] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan) supplies coefficientwise Cartan for the actual perfect operations on every qcqs field-scheme through degree three, with zero normalization and formal inversion. Write $C_1$ for its first operation until it is matched with the perfect first-layer class; its second operation is the specified $c_2$.

[F2] [lem-second-piece-rank-determinant](item-lem-second-piece-rank-determinant) supplies rank zero and $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}(x)=0$ for every $x\in H$ in precisely this normal qcqs scope. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) defines $H$ as an additive image subgroup.

[F3] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection) identifies the actual first-layer map on the rank-zero K-space $S$ with the perfect determinant/Picard map, including its global descent data. [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant) identifies its oriented class with $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}$ and matches the original bundle first classes. [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) constructs the actual $C_i$ from those original stable universal bundle classes: their restriction to the stable free-class map is the original classifying map, including the determinant-torsor normalization in weight one. Thus on actual bundles their coefficients are the original ones.

[F4] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-local-chains](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-local-chains) supplies, on the small Zariski site of every qcqs field-scheme, detection of derived sheaf-map classes into the actual Eilenberg targets by precomposition with the rank-zero free-class map $j_0:BGL\to S$. This is a local integral-chain comparison, with no dimension or global bundle-generation hypothesis.


**Given:** $k,X,H$, Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds as stated.

**Goal:** Establish additivity for arbitrary second-image perfect classes and retain the conditional bundle-difference formula.

### Proof
1.1 Restrict $C_1$ to $S$ and compare it with the actual first-layer determinant/Picard map, with target identified with the weight-one Eilenberg target by its specified positive orientation. After precomposition with $j_0$, both maps are the oriented determinant-torsor map of the stable universal bundle by [F3], including its automorphism and gluing maps. The derived-map detection in [F4] identifies these maps on $S$. Evaluation on $X$ therefore identifies $C_1(x)$ with $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}(x)$ for every rank-zero perfect class $x$; this is an equality of actual map classes, rather than a deduction from local Picard-group agreement. [A1, F1, F3, F4]

2.1 Every $x\in H$ has rank zero and $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}(x)=0$ by [F2]. Step 1.1 consequently gives $C_1(x)=0$ for every such $x$. This uses the full-qcqs supplier and no global bundle representative. [A1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 For $x,y\in H$, [F1] gives $c_2(x+y)=c_2(x)+C_1(x)C_1(y)+c_2(y)$. The cross term vanishes by step 2.1. Pointedness gives $c_2(0)=0$; since $H$ is a subgroup, applying additivity to $x+(-x)$ yields $c_2(-x)=-c_2(x)$. Thus the restriction is a group homomorphism. [A1, F1, F2, step 2.1]

4.1 Suppose $[V]-[W]\in H$. Additivity of $c_1^{\mathrm{perf}}$ and its bundle agreement in [F3], together with [F2], give $c_1(V)=c_1(W)$. On bundle classes the coefficients in [F1] are the original ones by [F3]. Degree-two inversion gives $c_2(-[W])=c_1(W)^2-c_2(W)$, and Cartan therefore gives $c_2([V]-[W])=c_2(V)-c_1(V)c_1(W)+c_1(W)^2-c_2(W)$. The equal first classes cancel the quadratic terms, proving the stated formula. Only this conditional assertion uses the supplied bundle-difference representation. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 3.1] ∎

This restores the normal qcqs scope of the supplied article's p. 3 conventions and p. 11 Lemma 5.3. The actual full-scope Cartan, first-layer and local-chain suppliers are used with their stated hypotheses; their deep constructions are not reconstructed or independently judged here. The earlier total-Cartan supplier's noetherian finite-dimensional consequence is not extended by assertion. The original article's blanket bundle-representation premise remains a source proof defect, distinct from this perfect-class proof and its conditional bundle formula.

## The reduced universal bundle calculation identifies the second projection

[Open item](item-lem-author-e216acade157-bundle-calculation) · level 25


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible site-size and universe bounds required by the supplied perfect K-theory, motivic and derived-section constructions. For a vector bundle $V$ of locally constant rank $n$ on a noetherian finite-dimensional field-scheme $Y$, let $v=[V]-n\in\pi_0S(Y)$ and $\widetilde\delta(V)=r(v)\in\pi_0T(Y)$. Its underlying perfect class is $\delta(V)=[V]-[\det V]-(n-1)$. For the actual second stage projection $Q:T\to A=\Omega^\infty(\mathbb Z(2)_{\rm mot}[4])$ and actual second Chern map $C_2:\Omega^\infty K\to A$,
$$Q(\widetilde\delta(V))=-c_2(V)=-c_2(\delta(V)).$$
The assertion holds for actual universal bundles on finite Grassmannians over $Y$, naturally under their transition maps.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the compatible site-size and universe bounds in the Statement. They are inherited through the determinant-fiber, first-Chern and flag constructions in [F1]–[F2] at steps 1.1–2.1 and the actual perfect Cartan comparison in [F3] at step 3.1.

[F1] [lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber](item-lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber) supplies the determinant retraction $r:S\to T$ for $S=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^1K$ and $T=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^2K$, and injectivity of $\pi_0T\to K_0$. [prop-filtration-product-projection](item-prop-filtration-product-projection) supplies the actual stage product and its projection square on every qcqs field-scheme; only this stage-level assertion is used, without the additional hypotheses of its image-group square. The line lift $\kappa(L)$ has first projection $c_1(L)$ by that section and [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant).

[F2] [lem-flag-tower-line-quotients](item-lem-flag-tower-line-quotients) gives a flag pullback with a filtration by line quotients; [lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection](item-lem-flag-tower-cohomology-detection) detects equality in every motivic bidegree on this tower. It does not assert that the filtration splits globally. [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) identifies its Chern roots.

[F3] [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-actual-total-cartan](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-actual-total-cartan) supplies actual perfect Cartan in this noetherian finite-dimensional scope. [lem-reduced-bundle-class-identities](item-lem-reduced-bundle-class-identities) supplies the reduced-class ring identities on every qcqs scheme over any field under Choice and its size bounds. On each constant-rank component of the flag tower, apply those identities to partial direct sums of the line quotients. The exact flag sequences identify the final direct-sum class with the pulled-back bundle class. A noetherian scheme is qcqs, and these finite projective-bundle towers and finite Grassmannians remain noetherian and finite-dimensional. The calculation below spells out both the ring expansion and its actual stage lifts.

### Proof
**Given:** $Y,V$ as stated, with the actual maps and finite clopen rank decomposition.

**Goal:** Compute both actual operations on the reduced determinant-trivial class.

1.1 The expression for $\delta(V)$ follows from the formula for $r$. It has rank zero and its determinant is canonically trivial. Under [A1], construct the detecting flag tower in [F2] on each constant-rank clopen stratum. On one such tower put $l_s=[L_s]$, $D_s=\bigotimes_{i\leq s}L_i$ and $R_s=\sum_{i\leq s}l_i-[D_s]-(s-1)$. Exact flag sequences give these perfect $K_0$ class equalities without globally split sequences. For $s\geq2$, the line-product identity in [F3], or direct distributivity, gives $([L_s]-1)([D_{s-1}]-1)=[D_s]-[L_s]-[D_{s-1}]+1$, hence $R_s=R_{s-1}-([L_s]-1)([D_{s-1}]-1)$ and $R_1=0$. Define $\widetilde R_s=r(\sum_{i\leq s}\kappa(L_i))$. Its argument has underlying class $\sum_{i\leq s}l_i-s$ and determinant $D_s$, so $\widetilde R_s$ has underlying class $R_s$. Let $P_s$ be the actual second-stage product of $\kappa(L_s)$ and $\kappa(D_{s-1})$. Its underlying class is the product in the recursion. Injectivity of the second-stage augmentation in [F1] gives $\widetilde R_1=0$ and $\widetilde R_s=\widetilde R_{s-1}-P_s$. At $s=n$ the same injectivity identifies $\widetilde R_n$ with the pullback of $\widetilde\delta(V)$. This comparison uses no additivity of $r$. [F1, F2, F3, A1, algebra]

2.1 Write $x_i=c_1(L_i)$. The multiplicative projection square and additivity of the actual second-stage map give by induction $Q(\widetilde\delta(V))=-\sum_{s=2}^n x_s\Big(\sum_{i<s}x_i\Big)=-\sum_{i<j}x_ix_j=-c_2(V).$ For rank two this is exactly $([L_1]-1)([L_2]-1)=-\delta(V)$; the displayed recursion is the full rank induction. Additivity of line $c_1$ identifies $c_1(D_{s-1})$ with the indicated sum. Rank zero and rank one give zero. Detection in [F2] descends the equality; finite clopen reduction handles varying rank. [F1, F2, step 1.1, A1]

3.1 Put $a=c_1(V)=c_1(\det V)$. Actual perfect Cartan gives $c_t(\delta(V))=c_t(V)(1+at)^{-1},$ since a trivial virtual rank has Chern series one. Its $t^2$ coefficient is $c_2(V)-a^2+a^2=c_2(V)$. This uses actual perfect Cartan, not a global bundle presentation of arbitrary classes. All constructions commute with pullback, so they apply to the actual universal bundles on each finite Grassmannian. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, A1] ∎


## The perfect image filtration has the stated second projection and kernel

[Open item](item-lem-author-e216acade157-perfect-image-formula) · level 25


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed compatible site and universe size bounds for the specified motivic filtration, perfect K-theory and Chern constructions. Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $k$-scheme. The actual second-stage projection transports uniquely to the second image subgroup, giving a homomorphism
$$p_2:F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\longrightarrow H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z),\qquad p_2(\alpha)=-c_2(\alpha).$$
Its kernel is
$$\ker(p_2)=F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X).$$
Here $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$ is the K-theory of perfect complexes, and $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of $\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^jK(X)\to K_0(X)$, including for $j=3$. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite-rank locally free sheaves. The target is degree-four cohomology of the specified weight-two integral motivic complex, and $c_2$ is the actual perfect second Chern operation. Transport means that composing $p_2$ with the second-stage augmentation gives the actual stage projection.

In particular, this preserves the original normal qcqs scope over an algebraically closed field. The formula and kernel require no finite-type, noetherian, dimension or global bundle-representation hypothesis; they assert no injectivity of the third-stage augmentation. Here qcqs means quasi-compact quasi-separated, normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain, Choice asserts that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function, and the size bounds fix the sites and ambient universes of the constructions.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the compatible size bounds in the Statement. These are inherited from the specified filtration, section and Chern constructions in [F1]–[F4], used at steps 1.1–3.1. No separate choice of a family of representatives is made.

[F1] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-second-fiber](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-second-fiber) gives the actual homotopy $Q_2\simeq-C_2i_K$ on the small Zariski site of every qcqs field-scheme. It evaluates on derived sections over $X$, and $i_K$ is the augmentation into its perfect K-space.

[F2] [lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber](item-lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber) supplies the actual pointed section $\kappa:B\to S$ of $d:S\to B$, with $S=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^1K$, $B=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{gr}^1K$ and fiber $T=\Omega^\infty\operatorname{Fil}^2K$. It also identifies the first stage with the rank fiber over a discrete target. Its argument applies after derived sections on every qcqs field-scheme. Only the pointed section and the resulting injections on $\pi_0$ are needed; the section need not be additive.

[F3] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) defines the compatible augmentations and their image subgroups. [def-filtration-projections](item-def-filtration-projections) defines the actual stage map $Q_{2,*}:\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^2K(X)\to H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ on every qcqs field-scheme, using the graded cofiber of this same tower. [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) gives exactness at the middle term of $\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^3K(X)\to\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^2K(X)\xrightarrow{Q_{2,*}}H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$.

[F4] [lem-second-chern-additive](item-lem-second-chern-additive) supplies the additive restriction of the actual $c_2$ to this second image subgroup on every qcqs scheme over a field, with the same assumptions. Its perfect-class argument does not require a global bundle-difference representative.

### Proof
**Given:** $k,X$, Choice and the size bounds in the Statement, with the specified actual tower and perfect Chern operations.

**Goal:** Transport the actual second-layer map and identify its sign and third-image kernel throughout the stated qcqs scope.

1.1 Evaluate the pointed section in [F2] on derived sections over $X$. It makes $\pi_1S(X)\to\pi_1B(X)$ surjective. The homotopy-fiber exact sequence therefore makes $\pi_0T(X)\to\pi_0S(X)$ injective. The rank target is discrete, so the rank-fiber sequence also makes $\pi_0S(X)\to K_0(X)$ injective. Their composite is the second-stage augmentation by [F3]. Its corestriction $q_2:\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^2K(X)\to F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is consequently injective and, by the image definition, surjective. Define $p_2=Q_{2,*}q_2^{-1}$. This is a homomorphism and is the unique one with $p_2q_2=Q_{2,*}$ because $q_2$ is onto. [A1, F2, F3]

2.1 For $\alpha\in F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$, take its unique stage representative $\widetilde\alpha=q_2^{-1}(\alpha)$. Evaluation of the derived-map identity in [F1] on this representative gives $p_2(\alpha)=Q_{2,*}(\widetilde\alpha)=-c_2(\alpha)$. The operation is the same actual perfect operation as in [F4], so its additive interpretation agrees with that supplier. This applies to every perfect class in the image, including classes without global bundle-difference representatives. [A1, F1, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Write $r:\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^3K(X)\to\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^2K(X)$ for the transition. Exactness in [F3] gives $\ker Q_{2,*}=\operatorname{im}r$. Thus the isomorphism $q_2$ in step 1.1 gives $\ker p_2=q_2(\operatorname{im}r)$. Compatibility of augmentations identifies the image of this composite in $K_0(X)$ with the image of the third-stage augmentation, which is exactly $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. This proves the kernel formula without third-stage injectivity. [A1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

## The first two perfect Chern classes vanish on the third image piece in full scope

[Open item](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-lower-vanishing) · level 25


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. For every qcqs $k$-scheme $X$ over any field, every $\alpha\in F^3_{\rm mot}K_0(X)$ has rank zero and $c_1(\alpha)=c_2(\alpha)=0$. This uses actual stage maps and needs neither normality nor an image-stage isomorphism.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. Choice and the fixed size bounds are inherited from the first-layer comparison in [F2] at step 1.1 and the actual second-fiber comparison in [F3] at step 2.1.

[F1] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) defines nested image groups. [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) gives the consecutive stage-to-layer fiber sequences.

[F2] [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-global-picard-projection) and [prop-first-chern-determinant](item-prop-first-chern-determinant) identify the actual first layer with determinant/first Chern on the rank-zero space for all qcqs field-schemes.

[F3] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-second-fiber](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-second-fiber) identifies the actual second layer with minus the actual second Chern operation in the same scope.

### Proof
**Given:** $X,\alpha$ and a third-stage representative $a\in\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^3K(X)$, which exists by the image definition.

**Goal:** Prove lower-class vanishing without transporting projections through a finite-type image-stage identification.

1.1 Send $a$ to the second, first and zeroth stages. Their common augmentation is $\alpha$. Consecutive stage-to-layer composites are null by their fiber sequences. In particular its rank is zero, and the actual first-layer map of the first-stage representative is zero. By [F2] this gives $c_1(\alpha)=0$. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Its second-stage representative is in the image of the third stage, so its actual second-layer value is zero. By [F3] that value is $-c_2(\alpha)$. Thus $c_2(\alpha)=0$. No injectivity of any stage augmentation or representation of $\alpha$ by global bundles has been used. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## The second-stage projection is minus the actual second Chern map on its homotopy fiber

[Open item](item-lem-author-e216acade157-actual-fiber-comparison) · level 26


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the compatible site-size and universe bounds required by the supplied perfect K-theory, motivic and derived-section constructions. On the small Nisnevich site of every noetherian finite-dimensional field-scheme $X$, the actual natural maps from the second-stage space satisfy
$$Q\simeq-C_2\circ i_K:T\longrightarrow A,$$
where $i_K$ is its augmentation into the perfect K-space. This is an equality of homotopy classes of derived sheaf maps, hence induces the equality on derived sections, not merely on bundle classes or affine $\pi_0$ groups.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] The Axiom of Choice is as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice). The foundation bounds and Choice in the unchanged Statement are inherited by the supplied filtration, model, detecting flag towers and local comparisons. They are assumed when these constructions are used in steps 1.1–7.1; no foundational necessity assertion is made.

[F1] [lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber](item-lem-author-e216acade157-split-determinant-fiber) constructs the actual natural determinant map $d:S\to B$, its pointed line-class section $\kappa:B\to S$, the homotopy $d\kappa\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and retraction $r:S\to T$ with $ri\simeq\mathrm{id}$ on qcqs schemes. Here $B\simeq B\mathbb G_m$ and $i:T\to S$. [lem-author-e216acade157-bundle-calculation](item-lem-author-e216acade157-bundle-calculation) computes $Q(r([V]-n))=-c_2(V)=-c_2(\delta(V))$, where $\delta(V)=[V]-[\det V]-(n-1)$, for actual bundles on noetherian finite-dimensional schemes, including the finite Grassmannians used below.

[F2] [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-local-free-test](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-local-free-test) supplies the actual local plus comparison, and [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-derived-chain-detection](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-derived-chain-detection) supplies the derived free-chain adjunction and detection of map classes into the abelian target $A$.

[F3] [thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input](item-thm-author-3cde9692a7e9-universal-grass-input) supplies the map-induced Grass/Vect cohomology comparison and finite Grassmannian basis. [lem-author-32887006bdff-em-p1-model](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-em-p1-model) and [lem-author-32887006bdff-actual-orientation](item-lem-author-32887006bdff-actual-orientation) identify its actual oriented non-A¹ model over $X$; the model has the supplied projective bundle maps, consistent with [prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula](item-prop-motivic-projective-bundle-formula). [lem-adjudicate-a8be8a17c858-negative-model-coefficients](item-lem-adjudicate-a8be8a17c858-negative-model-coefficients) proves all-degree negative-weight coefficient vanishing for this represented model. A formal zero convention for negative complexes alone is not used to establish that vanishing.

[F4] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) gives the actual functorial stages and augmentation on qcqs schemes. [thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input](item-thm-author-74a9c17e63f1-source-multiplicative-input) supplies their natural actual graded equivalence $\gamma_2:\operatorname{gr}^2F_{\rm mot}K\simeq\mathbb Z(2)_{\rm mot}[4]$, restricted from the prime field. Thus $Q$ is $\Omega^\infty$ of the stage-to-cofiber map followed by this same $\gamma_2$, naturally under restriction. No boundedness or convergence assertion is used. [lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage](item-lem-author-ec13f1db88a5-rank-zero-stage) identifies $S$ as the actual rank fiber. [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) constructs $C_2$ functorially from the specified stable bundle maps, including on the smooth big site and under restriction. The spectrum model in [F3] has actual level $A=\Omega^\infty(\mathbb Z(2)_{\rm mot}[4])$ there. The evaluation/shift and coefficient adjunctions in [thm-author-32887006bdff-p1-spectrum-input](item-thm-author-32887006bdff-p1-spectrum-input) identify maps into this level with its weight-two cohomology. [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) supplies derived Nisnevich descent for the coefficient functor. The actual rank and determinant fibers in [F1] are already Nisnevich sheaf objects, with the given natural maps and homotopies.


**Given:** $X$, Choice, the stated size bounds, and these actual natural operations and coefficient models.

**Goal:** Establish a compatible big-site comparison before using small-site chain detection.

### Proof
1.1 On the smooth big Zariski site $\mathrm{Sm}_X$, evaluate the functorial stages and maps of [F4]. Construct $r$ by the fiber-product inverse of $T\times B\to S$, $(t,b)\mapsto i(t)+\kappa(b)$, using the specified homotopy in [F1]. Together with the actual $Q$ and the functorial universal $C_2$, this defines $D_{\rm big}=(Q+C_2i_K)r:S\to A$. Its restriction to small-site objects is the specified difference $D$, because every constituent, including the determinant-fiber path, is the same natural construction. Smooth qcqs objects over the noetherian finite-dimensional $X$ have finite presentation and remain noetherian finite-dimensional. Thus all bundle calculations used on this site meet [F1]'s hypotheses. [A1, F1, F4]

2.1 The rank-zero test is the pointed zero class. For positive ranks the reduced bundle-class construction defines $j_0:BGL=\operatorname{colim}_n BGL_n\to S$ on this big site, with $BGL_n=\mathrm{Vect}_n$ after Zariski descent. The composite $D_{\rm big}j_0$ on $\mathrm{Vect}_n$ is a map into the actual spectrum level in [F4], so the adjunction identifies its class with a weight-two cohomology class of that stack. This applies to this particular constructed map; it is no claim that arbitrary small-site maps extend to motivic stacks. For pointed classes, forgetting the basepoint is injective here: the chosen trivial-bundle basepoint splits the coefficient-valued suspension spectrum of $\mathrm{Vect}_{n,+}$ into its unit and reduced summands, as also recorded in Asakura–Sato Proposition 5.2. Thus a zero class in the displayed unreduced cohomology also gives a zero pointed map class. [A1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

2.2 At a Nisnevich local ring $R$, the small-site map $j_0$ is the actual rank-zero plus map $BGL(R)\to BGL(R)^+$. Projectives over $R$ are free, and the rank target is discrete by [F4]. The component-zero local comparison in [F2] therefore makes $j_0$ an integral-chain equivalence. This uses the actual plus model of this rank fiber; it does not claim that an arbitrary homotopy fiber preserves a homology equivalence. [A1, F2, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Pull this class back along $G(n,N)\to\mathrm{Vect}_n$, where $G(n,N)$ carries the actual universal rank-$n$ quotient. By derived Yoneda this pullback is the value on that universal bundle as an element of its full cohomology group. Its image under $rj_0$ has underlying class $\delta(V)$, and [F1] gives $Q(r([V]-n))+C_2(\delta(V))=0$. These Grassmannians are smooth qcqs over $X$ and remain noetherian finite-dimensional. Their cohomology classes therefore vanish by the bundle calculation, including the bundle descent data. [A1, F1, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Apply [F3] on the big site over the qcqs base $X$. Its actual model is homotopy commutative, linearly oriented and satisfies PBF; use the unit coring in Corollary 4.4.7. In mapping homotopy degree $u=0,1$, a Chern monomial of weight $w$ has coefficient $\mathcal E_X^{4-2w-u,2-w}(X)$, which vanishes for $w>2$ by the actual negative-coefficient lemma. The finite basis on $G(n,N)$ is indexed by $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j\leq N-n$ and weight $w=\sum_jj\alpha_j$. Every potentially nonzero monomial has $|\alpha|\leq2$, so ambient ranges $N-n\geq2$ include them all, and the transition maps preserve them. This holds for both mapping degrees. Hence the finite-approximation tower has zero $\lim^1\pi_1$; the map-induced Grass/Vect comparison detects the class in step 2.1 from the zero restrictions in step 3.1. It follows that $D_{\rm big}j_0$ is zero on each $\mathrm{Vect}_n$. [A1, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 Stabilization $V\mapsto V\oplus\mathcal O$ preserves $[V]-n$, its determinant, and the specified universal Chern maps with their natural identifications. Thus these restrictions are restrictions of a single stable map. In the coefficient formula of step 4.1, variables newly introduced after rank two have weight greater than two. Both mapping $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ therefore stabilize for $n\geq2$. The Milnor exact sequence for the mapping-spectrum inverse limit has $\lim^1\pi_1=0$. Its map to $\lim\pi_0$ is consequently injective, and the zero rank restrictions imply $D_{\rm big}j_0\simeq0$ on stable $BGL$. This separately controls the rank limit, rather than choosing incompatible nullhomotopies at each rank. [A1, F3, F4, step 4.1]

6.1 Represent the homotopy in step 5.1 in the local simplicial-sheaf model with fibrant derived coefficient target. It is then a homotopy of presheaf maps. Restrict it along the inclusion of qcqs étale $X$-schemes into $\mathrm{Sm}_X$, and apply the supplied derived Nisnevich sheafification. At finite rank the restricted bundle stack is the small-site $\mathrm{Vect}_n$: both assign to an étale test scheme its groupoid of rank-$n$ bundles and their isomorphisms. Use the canonical map from the presheaf colimit of these restricted finite-rank stacks to the restriction of the big-site stable $BGL$, and precompose the restricted homotopy with it. After Nisnevich sheafification its source is exactly the small-site stable $BGL$, since sheafification preserves this colimit. The target remains the actual $A$ by its derived Nisnevich descent in [F4]; the rank and determinant fibers, retraction, augmentation and stage map are the same natural constructions by [F1] and [F4]. On each finite-rank stack the precomposed map is exactly the reduced bundle-class map followed by $D$, since its constituents were restricted from step 1.1. The resulting homotopy is therefore precisely $Dj_0\simeq0$. This uses restriction of the particular constructed big-site homotopy; it requires neither an equivalence of sites nor commutation of restriction with a sheaf colimit. [A1, F1, F4, step 1.1, step 5.1]

7.1 The derived free-chain adjunction of [F2] makes precomposition with this $j_0$ injective on homotopy classes of maps into $A$. Steps 6.1 and 2.2 imply $D\simeq0$ on $S$. Restrict along $i:T\to S$ and use $ri\simeq\mathrm{id}$ from [F1] to obtain $Q+C_2i_K\simeq0$. Evaluation on derived sections proves the asserted equality, retaining all gluing morphisms. No global bundle-difference presentation of a perfect class is used. [A1, F1, F2, step 6.1, step 2.2] ∎

No serving or library content was changed, and no independent judgment or render pass is claimed.


## The low-dimensional quotient follows from the stage sequence

[Open item](item-lem-author-e216acade157-low-dimensional-quotient) · level 26


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $X$ a normal finite-type $k$-scheme. If $d=\dim X\leq3$, the actual projection induces an isomorphism
$$F^2_{\rm mot}K_0(X)/F^3_{\rm mot}K_0(X)\xrightarrow{\ \overline p_2\ }H^{4,2}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z),\qquad\overline p_2=-\overline c_2.$$
If $d\leq2$, the third image subgroup itself is zero.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. Choice and the existing size bounds are inherited from the stage-vanishing and stage-to-image premises in [F2] at steps 1.1–2.1 and the perfect-image comparison in [F3] at step 2.1.

[F1] [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) gives the exact sequence ending in $H^{4,2}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)\to\pi_{-1}\operatorname{Fil}^3K(X)$.

[F2] [lem-high-filtration-vanishing](item-lem-high-filtration-vanishing) says $\pi_j\operatorname{Fil}^iK=0$ for $j<0$ and $i\geq d$, and $\pi_0\operatorname{Fil}^iK=0$ for $i>d$. [def-filtration-projections](item-def-filtration-projections) identifies the second stage with its image under the present normal hypotheses.

[F3] [lem-author-e216acade157-perfect-image-formula](item-lem-author-e216acade157-perfect-image-formula) identifies the actual transported map with $-c_2$ and its kernel with the third image subgroup under the stated Choice and site/universe size hypotheses.

### Proof
**Given:** $X$ in the stated normal finite-type algebraically closed scope, of dimension at most three, with Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds as in [A1].

**Goal:** Obtain the quotient without a later surjectivity consumer.

1.1 Since $3\geq d$, [F2] makes the final obstruction group $\pi_{-1}\operatorname{Fil}^3K(X)$ zero. Exactness of [F1] makes the second-stage projection surjective. Transfer this assertion to $F^2$ using its stage-image isomorphism in [F2]. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Its kernel is $F^3$ and its value is $-c_2$ by [F3]. The first isomorphism theorem proves the displayed quotient identification with that exact sign. If $d\leq2$, then $3>d$ and [F2] makes the third stage's $\pi_0$, hence its image subgroup, zero. No later second-Chern-surjectivity proposition is used. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## Degree-three coefficient algebra on the lower-Chern kernel

[Open item](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-coefficient-algebra) · level 26


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds of the supplied constructions. On every qcqs field-scheme $X$, the actual third Chern operation is additive on any subgroup of perfect $K_0(X)$ where $c_1=c_2=0$. In particular it is additive on $F^3_{\rm mot}K_0(X)$; it sends zero to zero and $-x$ to $-c_3(x)$ there.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. Choice and the fixed size bounds are inherited from perfect Cartan in [F1] at steps 1.1–2.1 and lower-class vanishing in [F2] at step 2.1. The subsequent coefficient arithmetic is finite algebra.

[F1] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-cartan) supplies the coefficientwise identity through degree three for every perfect class in this scope, with even first degrees and the actual motivic cup product.

[F2] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-lower-vanishing](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-lower-vanishing) gives $c_1=c_2=0$ on $F^3$. [lem-third-order-chern-inversion](item-lem-third-order-chern-inversion) records the formal inverse coefficient identity; its algebra also follows directly from [F1].

### Proof
**Given:** A subgroup $G\subseteq K_0(X)$ with the stated vanishing, and $x,y\in G$.

**Goal:** Derive the homomorphism assertion purely after the actual full-scope operation identities are available.

1.1 Extract the third coefficient in [F1]: $c_3(x+y)=c_3(x)+c_2(x)c_1(y)+c_1(x)c_2(y)+c_3(y).$ The two middle terms vanish by the hypothesis on $G$. Hence $c_3(x+y)=c_3(x)+c_3(y)$. [A1, F1, given]

2.1 The pointed operation gives $c_3(0)=0$. Applying step 1.1 to $x+(-x)=0$ gives $c_3(-x)=-c_3(x)$. Equivalently the formal inverse has third coefficient $-c_3+2c_1c_2-c_1^3$, which reduces to $-c_3$ on $G$. Apply [F2] with $G=F^3$, a subgroup by the image definition. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1] ∎


## Second projection is minus second Chern class

[Open item](item-prop-second-projection-chern) · level 27


### Statement
Assume AC and the fixed site/universe bounds. Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $X$ a normal qcqs $k$-scheme. For perfect-complex $K$-theory, the actual second-stage projection transports uniquely to its image subgroup, and
$$p_2:F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\longrightarrow H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z),\qquad p_2(\alpha)=-c_2(\alpha).$$
Its kernel is $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. No finite-type or global bundle-representation hypothesis is imposed on this equality or kernel assertion. If, additionally, $X$ is finite type and $\dim X\leq3$, it induces $F^2/F^3\cong H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ with this sign.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The normal qcqs scheme and the actual motivic stages and perfect operations.

**Goal:** Preserve the original scope, actual map, sign, kernel, and the existing finite-type low-dimensional supplement.

[F1] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-second-fiber](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-actual-second-fiber) identifies the actual second-layer map with minus the actual second Chern map as derived sheaf maps on every qcqs field-scheme. Its determinant-fiber retraction also proves injectivity of the second-stage augmentation on $\pi_0$, without finite-type assumptions.

[F2] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) defines image groups and their compatible augmentations. [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) supplies exactness of the consecutive stage sequence. [lem-second-chern-additive](item-lem-second-chern-additive) gives additivity in this full scope.

[F3] [lem-author-e216acade157-low-dimensional-quotient](item-lem-author-e216acade157-low-dimensional-quotient) gives the quotient isomorphism for normal finite-type schemes of dimension at most three.

[F4] [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) states the Choice assumption inherited from the actual filtration, section and Chern-operation constructions in [F1]–[F3].

### Proof
1.1 By [F1] the second-stage augmentation is injective on $\pi_0$, hence identifies that group with its image $F^2$. Transport the actual layer map by this isomorphism to define $p_2$. Evaluating the actual map identity of [F1] on the unique lift of any $\alpha\in F^2$ gives $p_2(\alpha)=-c_2(\alpha)$; it includes non-bundle-representable perfect classes. Additivity is also consistent with [F2]. [F1, F2, F4]

2.1 Exactness of the third-to-second stage sequence in [F2] says that the layer value of the lift is zero precisely when it comes from a third-stage class. Augmenting to $K_0$ identifies these classes exactly with the third image subgroup. Conversely any third-stage representative has zero second-layer value. Injectivity at stage two from step 1.1 therefore gives $\ker(p_2)=F^3$; no injectivity at stage three is assumed. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Under the additional finite-type and dimension assumptions apply [F3]. It gives surjectivity of this same actual projection, and steps 1.1–2.1 identify its sign and kernel. Thus the quotient supplement is retained without narrowing the normal qcqs equality. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎


## Third Chern additivity on the third piece

[Open item](item-lem-third-chern-additive) · level 27


### Statement
Assume AC and the fixed site/universe bounds. Let $k$ be the standing algebraically closed field and let $X$ be any normal qcqs $k$-scheme. For the specified perfect-complex K-theory and actual motivic Chern operations,
$$c_3:F^3_{\rm mot}K_0(X)\longrightarrow H^{6,3}_{\rm mot}(X,\mathbb Z)$$
is a homomorphism. No finite-type, noetherian, finite-dimensional, reduced-presentation or global bundle-resolution hypothesis is added. In fact the proof supplies the same assertion on every qcqs scheme over any field.

### Facts & Assumptions
[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice as formulated in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and the stated size bounds. Choice and the fixed size bounds are inherited from lower-class vanishing in [F2] at step 1.1 and the actual coefficient calculation in [F3] at step 2.1.

[F1] [def-article-conventions](item-def-article-conventions) fixes the original normal qcqs scope; [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) defines the third image subgroup in this scope.

[F2] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-lower-vanishing](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-lower-vanishing) proves $c_1=c_2=0$ for every class in that subgroup using actual stage maps in full scope.

[F3] [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-coefficient-algebra](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-coefficient-algebra) proves the actual degree-three coefficient calculation after the full-scope Cartan construction.

### Proof
**Given:** The normal qcqs scheme in the statement and $x,y\in F^3_{\rm mot}K_0(X)$.

**Goal:** Preserve the article's full scope and show homomorphy for actual perfect classes.

1.1 Apply [F2] to $x,y$. Their first and second perfect Chern classes vanish, with no image-stage injectivity or finite-type hypothesis. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Apply [F3] to this subgroup. The degree-three Cartan cross terms vanish by step 1.1, yielding $c_3(x+y)=c_3(x)+c_3(y)$ and preservation of zero and negatives. Thus the displayed map is a homomorphism in the exact original scope. [A1, F3, step 1.1] ∎


## Second Chern surjectivity in dimensions two and three

[Open item](item-lem-second-chern-surjective-low-dimension) · level 28


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe size bounds required by the motivic filtration and its low-stage comparison. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X$ be a normal finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension $2$ or $3$. Then both homomorphisms
$$p_2,c_2:F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\longrightarrow H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$$
are surjective. The obstruction group $\pi_{-1}F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ in the stage exact sequence is zero. In particular, these conclusions apply to the normal affine surfaces and threefolds in the article's main theorems.

Here normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain, finite type means that $X$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras, and Krull dimension is the supremum of the lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets. An algebraically closed field is a field in which every nonconstant polynomial in one variable has a root. Choice means that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the small sites and ambient universes used for derived sections.

The spectrum $K(X)$ is the specified nonconnective K-theory spectrum of perfect complexes, and $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$. A perfect complex is a complex locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite-rank locally free sheaves. The decreasing motivic tower has stages $F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ mapping compatibly to $K(X)$; $F^r_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of the induced map on $\pi_0$. The target is degree-four cohomology of the weight-two motivic complex on $X$. The map $p_2$ is the homomorphism induced on that image by the actual second-stage graded projection, and $c_2$ is the actual second Chern operation on perfect K-theory restricted to this image. Their existence and the identity $p_2=-c_2$ under these hypotheses are supplied by the second-projection proposition.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An algebraically closed field $k$, a normal finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $d\in\{2,3\}$, Choice, and the stated site and universe size bounds.

**Goal:** Prove the stated obstruction-group vanishing and the surjectivity of the actual $p_2$ and $c_2$.

[F1] The actual weight-two graded triangle is $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to\mathbb Z(2)_{\mathrm{mot}}(X)[4]$, whose degree-zero homotopy group is $H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. Its associated stage sequence is exact. [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence)

[F2] Under the given field, normality, finite-type, Choice and size hypotheses, the canonical map $\pi_0F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is an isomorphism. [lem-low-filtration-homotopy](item-lem-low-filtration-homotopy)

[F3] For a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme of dimension $d$ over a field, Choice gives $\pi_jF^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0$ when $i\geq d$ and $j<0$. [lem-high-filtration-vanishing](item-lem-high-filtration-vanishing)

[F4] Under the given normal finite-type and choice hypotheses, the actual second-stage projection descends to $p_2$ on the image filtration, and $p_2(\alpha)=-c_2(\alpha)$ for every $\alpha$ in that image. [prop-second-projection-chern](item-prop-second-projection-chern)

[F5] [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) states the Choice assumption used in the stage-vanishing and low-stage comparisons in [F2]–[F3].

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Apply the exact sequence of the second graded stage, then transfer the resulting surjection to the image filtration.

1.1 A finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian. Since $3\geq d$ and $-1<0$, [F3] gives $\pi_{-1}F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)=0$. This is vanishing of the stage group itself. [F3, F5, given]

2.1 The exact sequence in [F1] contains the actual maps $\pi_0F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\to\pi_{-1}F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$. The last group is zero by step 1.1, so exactness makes the first map surjective. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F2], every element of $F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ has a unique stage representative. By [F4], $p_2$ applied to that image is the graded projection of the representative. Thus the surjection in step 2.1 is exactly $p_2$ after the isomorphism of [F2], proving $p_2$ surjective. [F2, F4, step 2.1]

4.1 For any target class $a$, step 3.1 supplies $\alpha$ with $p_2(\alpha)=-a$. The identity in [F4] then gives $c_2(\alpha)=a$. Hence $c_2$ is also surjective, and all stated assertions follow. [F4, step 1.1, step 3.1] ∎


## Rank-three representatives with two zero Chern classes

[Open item](item-lem-third-piece-representatives) · level 28


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe size bounds required by the completed filtration and Chern comparisons. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X$ be a normal affine $k$-scheme of finite type and dimension three. Every $\alpha\in F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ can be written
$$\alpha=[P]-[\mathcal O_X^3]$$
for a rank-three vector bundle $P$ with $c_1(P)=0$, $c_2(P)=0$, and $\det P\cong\mathcal O_X$.

A vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module, and rank three means that it is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^3$. Its determinant is the line bundle $\bigwedge^3P$. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; finite type means that the affine coordinate ring is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Dimension is the supremum of lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. Here $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$ for the specified nonconnective K-theory spectrum of perfect complexes, and $[P]$ denotes the class of $P$ concentrated in degree zero. The subgroup $F^i_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of the zeroth homotopy group of the $i$th motivic filtration stage in $K_0(X)$. The bundle Chern classes $c_i(P)$ lie in $H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ and are the classes defined by the supplied motivic projective-bundle relation. Choice asserts that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and ambient universes of the cited comparisons.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $k$, $X$, $\alpha$, Choice, and the site and universe bounds as stated.

**Goal:** Construct a rank-three representative and prove the two Chern-class vanishings and determinant triviality.

[F1] The motivic image filtration is decreasing: $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\subseteq F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration)

[F2] Every class in the second image piece has pointwise rank zero and first perfect Chern class zero. If it is a difference of two bundle classes, the two bundles have isomorphic determinants. [lem-second-piece-rank-determinant](item-lem-second-piece-rank-determinant)

[F3] Under Choice as in [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) and suitable universes, every pointwise rank-zero perfect K-zero class on a nonempty affine finite-type field-scheme of dimension three has the form $[P]-[\mathcal O_X^3]$ with $P$ of constant rank three. [lem-critical-rank-representatives](item-lem-critical-rank-representatives)

[F4] On the second image piece, the actual second projection $p_2$ is minus the actual perfect second Chern operation, and its kernel is the third image piece. No injectivity of the third stage into K-zero is required. [prop-second-projection-chern](item-prop-second-projection-chern)

[F5] For a bundle difference $[V]-[W]$ in the second image piece, the actual perfect operation satisfies $c_2([V]-[W])=c_2(V)-c_2(W)$. [lem-second-chern-additive](item-lem-second-chern-additive)

[F6] The total bundle Chern class is multiplicative on direct sums, and a line bundle has no Chern classes above degree one. [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Represent the rank-zero class at the critical rank, then apply the actual filtration projections and bundle comparison.

1.1 Since $X$ has dimension three it is nonempty. By [F1], $\alpha$ lies in the second image piece, so [F2] gives pointwise rank zero. Applying [F3] yields a rank-three vector bundle $P$ with $\alpha=[P]-[\mathcal O_X^3]$. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 The bundle-difference assertion of [F2], applied to the expression in step 1.1, gives $\det P\cong\det(\mathcal O_X^3)$. The standard basis trivializes the latter determinant, so $\det P\cong\mathcal O_X$. The first perfect Chern class of $\alpha$ is zero by [F2]; its bundle-difference comparison in the same supplied contract, together with the first-class normalization for the trivial determinant, gives $c_1(P)=0$. Equivalently, the determinant comparison identifies $c_1(P)$ with the image of the trivial line under the weight-one orientation. [F2, step 1.1]

2.2 Since $\alpha$ belongs to the third image piece, [F4] gives $p_2(\alpha)=0$, hence $c_2(\alpha)=0$. By [F5] and step 1.1, $c_2(\alpha)=c_2(P)-c_2(\mathcal O_X^3)$. The latter trivial bundle is a direct sum of three trivial lines. Its total Chern class is $1$: the first class of the trivial line is zero by the determinant normalization in [F2], its higher classes vanish by [F6], and [F6] multiplies the three total classes. Thus $c_2(\mathcal O_X^3)=0$, and consequently $c_2(P)=0$. [F2, F4, F5, F6, step 1.1]

3.1 Steps 1.1 through 2.2 prove all the stated assertions. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎


## Chern classes of the alternating exterior class

[Open item](item-lem-exterior-square-chern-calculation) · level 28

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the fixed site and universe bounds required by the cited motivic filtration and Chern constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X$ be a normal affine threefold over $k$, and let $E$ be a rank-three vector bundle on $X$. Put
$$\beta(E)=[\mathcal O_X]-[E]+[\Lambda^2E]-[\det E]\in K_0(X).$$
Then $\beta(E)$ has rank zero and its actual motivic Chern classes satisfy
$$c_1(\beta(E))=0,\qquad c_2(\beta(E))=0,\qquad c_3(\beta(E))=-2c_3(E).$$
Consequently $\beta(E)\in F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. On the flag space supplied by the splitting principle, if $\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3$ are the first Chern classes of the successive line quotients of the pulled-back $E$, the corresponding line roots of $\Lambda^2E$ are $\ell_1+\ell_2$, $\ell_1+\ell_3$ and $\ell_2+\ell_3$.

Here a vector bundle is a finite locally free sheaf, its rank is the local rank, $\Lambda^2E$ is its second exterior power, and $\det E=\Lambda^3E$. The group $K_0(X)$ is the zeroth homotopy group of the K-theory spectrum of perfect complexes; a bundle is regarded as a complex in degree zero. The integral motivic Chern class $c_i$ lies in $H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. The group $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of the $j$th motivic filtration stage in $K_0(X)$. A normal scheme has integrally closed local domains, and a threefold here has dimension three. A line root means the first Chern class of a line-bundle quotient in the indicated locally split flag filtration; it does not require the pulled-back bundle to split as a direct sum.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The field, scheme, bundle, Choice and site and universe bounds in the statement.

**Goal:** Compute the rank and first three actual Chern classes of $\beta(E)$, identify the exterior-square roots, and prove membership in the third image filtration.

[F1] [def-rank-three-euler-k-class](item-def-rank-three-euler-k-class) defines $\beta(E)$ and its four bundle terms. [thm-motivic-splitting-principle](item-thm-motivic-splitting-principle) supplies, under Choice, a flag map $q:Y\to X$ with locally split line quotients $L_i$ and injective pullback on integral motivic cohomology in every bidegree.

[F2] [lem-exterior-square-root-formula](item-lem-exterior-square-root-formula) gives the locally split filtration of $\Lambda^2q^*E$ with quotients $L_i\otimes L_j$ for $i<j$, and identifies $\det q^*E$ with $L_1\otimes L_2\otimes L_3$. [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) gives the filtered product formula and $c_1(L\otimes M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M)$.

[F3] On noetherian finite-dimensional field-schemes, [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-actual-total-cartan](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-actual-total-cartan) gives a natural multiplicative total Chern series for actual perfect $K_0$ classes. [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) identifies its restriction to bundle classes with the supplied universal bundle Chern classes. [lem-third-order-chern-inversion](item-lem-third-order-chern-inversion) gives the formal inverse through degree three.

[F4] For the stated normal finite-type scheme, [lem-zero-projection-rank](item-lem-zero-projection-rank) identifies $p_0$ with rank; [lem-first-projection-chern](item-lem-first-projection-chern) identifies $p_1$ on $F^1$ with $c_1$; and [prop-second-projection-chern](item-prop-second-projection-chern) identifies $p_2$ on $F^2$ with $-c_2$ and its kernel with $F^3$. The low-stage projections and stage-to-image isomorphisms are those of [def-filtration-projections](item-def-filtration-projections). [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) identifies the kernel of a transported stage projection with the next image filtration. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) states the Choice assumption.

### Proof

1.1 A rank-three bundle has exterior-square rank three and determinant rank one, as can be checked on a local basis. Thus the alternating rank of the four terms of $\beta(E)$ is $1-3+3-1=0$ at every point. The scheme is affine of finite type over a field and hence noetherian, finite-dimensional and quasi-compact quasi-separated; normality gives the seminormality required in [F4]. [given, F1, F4]

1.2 Apply [F1] to $E$. Write $x_i=c_1(L_i)$ and set $s=x_1+x_2+x_3$, $e_2=x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3$, and $e_3=x_1x_2x_3$ in the even-degree motivic cohomology ring of $Y$. By [F2], the exterior-square line roots are $x_1+x_2$, $x_1+x_3$, and $x_2+x_3$, while the determinant line has first class $s$. Moreover $c_t(q^*E)=1+st+e_2t^2+e_3t^3.$ The equality is the Whitney formula for the flag filtration, not an assertion that the flag splits globally. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 The actual perfect Chern series is natural and multiplicative under addition by [F3]. Its values on the four bundle terms are their bundle Chern series, so [F2] and [F3] give, through degree three, $q^*c_t(\beta(E))=\frac{\prod_{i<j}(1+(x_i+x_j)t)}{(1+st)(1+st+e_2t^2+e_3t^3)}.$ The numerator is $1+2st+(s^2+e_2)t^2+(se_2-e_3)t^3$, while the denominator is $1+2st+(s^2+e_2)t^2+(se_2+e_3)t^3$ modulo $t^4$. Their constant coefficients are one. Formal inversion therefore yields $q^*c_t(\beta(E))=1-2e_3t^3\pmod{t^4}.$ These polynomial identities hold integrally, including in characteristic two; no division by two is used. [F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 By step 1.2, $e_3=q^*c_3(E)$. Comparing coefficients in step 2.1 gives zero pullbacks of $c_1(\beta)$ and $c_2(\beta)$ and of $c_3(\beta)+2c_3(E)$. The injectivity in [F1], separately in bidegrees $(2,1)$, $(4,2)$ and $(6,3)$, proves the three stated identities on $X$. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1]

4.1 By step 1.1 and [F4], $p_0(\beta)=0$. Stage exactness and the low-stage identification in [F4] put $\beta$ in $F^1$. By step 3.1 and the first-projection identity, $p_1(\beta)=0$; the same exactness puts it in $F^2$. Finally $p_2(\beta)=-c_2(\beta)=0$, so the kernel statement in [F4] puts $\beta$ in $F^3$. This is membership in the image filtration and does not assert that the third stage itself maps injectively to $K_0$. Together with steps 1.1 through 3.1, this proves all assertions. [F4, step 1.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Prescribing two surface Chern classes

[Open item](item-lem-surface-chern-prescription) · level 29


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site-size and universe bounds required by the cited motivic and perfect K-theory constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension two. For every pair $a_1$ in $H^{2,1}_{mot}(X, Z)$ and $a_2$ in $H^{4,2}_{mot}(X, Z)$, there is a rank-two vector bundle $W$ on $X$ with $c_1(W)=a_1$ and $c_2(W)=a_2$.

More precisely, one may choose a line bundle $L$ with $c_1(L)=a_1$ and a rank-two bundle $V$ with trivial determinant such that $[V]-[O_X^2]$ lies in the second motivic image filtration and has second Chern class $a_2$. Then $V$ direct-summed with $L$ is isomorphic to $W$ direct-summed with $O_X$, and the resulting $W$ has the prescribed classes. The virtual class $[V]-[O_X^2]+[L]-[O_X]$ also has first and second Chern classes $a_1$ and $a_2$.

A vector bundle is a finite locally free sheaf, its rank is the number of copies of the structure sheaf in a local trivialization, and a line bundle is a rank-one vector bundle. Its determinant is its top exterior power. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; finite type over $k$ means a finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets. The groups $H^{2i,i}_{mot}(X, Z)$ are the indicated cohomology groups of the integral weight-$i$ motivic complexes. The group $K_0(X)$ is the zeroth homotopy group of nonconnective K-theory of perfect complexes; a perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of vector bundles. The second motivic image filtration $F^2_{mot}K_0(X)$ is the image in $K_0(X)$ of the zeroth homotopy group of the second stage of the motivic K-theory tower. Brackets denote the class of a bundle in $K_0(X)$, and $c_i$ on virtual classes denotes the actual perfect K-theory Chern operation.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An algebraically closed field $k$, a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension two, the two prescribed motivic cohomology classes, Choice, and the stated site-size and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Construct $L$, $V$ and $W$ with the stated properties and calculate both actual and virtual Chern classes.

[F1] Under these Choice and size hypotheses, first Chern class identifies line bundles with $H^{2,1}_{mot}(X, Z)$. [thm-line-bundle-first-chern-classification](item-thm-line-bundle-first-chern-classification)

[F2] For a normal finite-type scheme of dimension two over an algebraically closed field, with the stated Choice and size hypotheses, the actual second Chern operation maps $F^2_{mot}K_0(X)$ onto $H^{4,2}_{mot}(X, Z)$. [lem-second-chern-surjective-low-dimension](item-lem-second-chern-surjective-low-dimension)

[F3] On such a normal finite-type scheme, every class in the second image filtration has pointwise rank zero and first perfect Chern class zero. If it is represented by a difference of bundles, their determinants are isomorphic. [lem-second-piece-rank-determinant](item-lem-second-piece-rank-determinant)

[F4] On a nonempty affine finite-type scheme of dimension two over a field, Choice and suitable universes allow every pointwise rank-zero perfect $K_0$ class to be written $[V]-[O_X^2]$ with $V$ a rank-two bundle. [lem-critical-rank-representatives](item-lem-critical-rank-representatives)

[F5] Under Choice, a rank-three bundle on a nonempty noetherian affine scheme of dimension two splits as a rank-two bundle plus a trivial line. [thm-serre-affine-splitting](item-thm-serre-affine-splitting)

[F6] Actual perfect Chern operations satisfy the total Cartan identity on noetherian finite-dimensional schemes over a field, and the universal operation restricts to the supplied actual bundle classes. Bundle Chern classes obey Whitney's formula, a line has no Chern classes above degree one, and trivial bundles have total Chern class one. [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-actual-total-cartan](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-actual-total-cartan) [thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space](item-thm-author-d026a7b99ace-universal-chern-space) [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities)

[F7] The Axiom of Choice is assumed for the cited constructions and affine splitting. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Choose the two classes separately, represent the second by a critical-rank bundle, and split one trivial line from the resulting rank-three bundle.

1.1 The dimension hypothesis makes $X$ nonempty. It is noetherian because it is finite type over a field. By [F1], choose a line bundle $L$ with $c_1(L)=a_1$. By [F2], choose a class $alpha$ in $F^2_{mot}K_0(X)$ with $c_2(alpha)=a_2$. [F1, F2, F7, given, choose]

2.1 The class $alpha$ has pointwise rank zero by [F3]. Applying [F4], write $alpha=[V]-[O_X^2]$ for a rank-two bundle $V$. The determinant assertion of [F3] gives an isomorphism from the determinant of $V$ to the determinant of $O_X^2$, which is the trivial line. Also $c_1(alpha)=0$ by [F3]. [F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 The actual perfect total Cartan identity and bundle restriction in [F6] give $c_t(alpha)c_t(O_X^2)=c_t(V)$. Since the total class of $O_X^2$ is one, $c_1(V)=c_1(alpha)=0$ and $c_2(V)=c_2(alpha)=a_2$. Here $c_t$ denotes the formal total Chern series with constant term one; the equalities are its coefficients in degrees one and two. [F6, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Put $beta=alpha+[L]-[O_X]$. By [F6], the total class of $[L]-[O_X]$ is $1+a_1t$. Multiplying by the total class of $alpha$, whose first coefficient vanishes, gives $c_1(beta)=a_1$ and $c_2(beta)=a_2+0$; the cross term is $c_1(alpha)a_1=0$. This establishes the virtual-class assertion. [F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 The bundle $V$ direct-summed with $L$ has constant rank three. Apply [F5] to obtain an isomorphism $V$ direct-summed with $L$ isomorphic to $W$ direct-summed with $O_X$, where $W$ has rank two. Whitney's formula and the trivial-line normalization in [F6] give $c_i(W)=c_i(V\oplus L)$ for $i=1,2$. The first class of the latter is $0+a_1$; its second is $a_2+0a_1+0$, using step 3.1 and the vanishing of the second class of a line. Hence $c_1(W)=a_1$ and $c_2(W)=a_2$, as required. [F5, F6, step 1.1, step 3.1] ∎


## Curve-and-point support reduction

[Open item](item-lem-bertini-support-reduction) · level 29

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe bounds of the completed filtration, representative and K-theory suppliers. Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension three.
