For every $\alpha\in F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ there are a rank-three vector bundle $P$ with $\det P\cong\mathcal O_X$ and $c_1(P)=c_2(P)=0$, a functional $s:P\to\mathcal O_X$, and, on $U=X\setminus S$ for its zero locus $S$, a functional $t:Q|_U\to\mathcal O_U$ for $Q=\ker s$, with the following properties.

The class is $\alpha=[P]-[\mathcal O_X^3]$. The zero scheme $S$ is a finite set of smooth closed points, and $Q|_U$ is a rank-two vector bundle. The zero scheme $Y$ of $t$ is a finite disjoint union of smooth geometrically integral curves, one on each three-dimensional clopen integral component of $X$; it is empty on the lower-dimensional components. It is contained in the smooth locus of $X$. For integral $X$, $Y$ is a single curve. Put $C$ for the reduced closure of $Y$ in $X$, $T=C\cup S$, and $V=X\setminus T$. Then $C\setminus Y\subseteq S$, $C$ is smooth away from $C\setminus Y$, and $T$ lies in the smooth locus of $X$. On $V$ there are short exact sequences
$$0\to Q|_V\to P|_V\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal O_V\to0,\qquad 0\to\mathcal O_V\to Q|_V\xrightarrow{t}\mathcal O_V\to0.$$
Consequently $\alpha|_V=0$ in $K_0(V)$, and $\alpha$ is in the image of the actual support-to-global map $K_{0,T}(X)=\pi_0K_T(X)\to K_0(X)$.

A vector bundle is a finite locally free sheaf; its determinant is its top exterior power. A functional is a morphism to the structure sheaf, with zero scheme defined locally by its coefficients. A curve here is a finite-type scheme of pure dimension one, and geometrically integral means integral after every field extension. The smooth locus consists of points at which the structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. The reduced closure is the smallest reduced closed subscheme with the given underlying closed set. The group $K_0$ is zeroth homotopy of the specified nonconnective perfect-complex K-spectrum; $K_T(X)$ is the supported spectrum in the localization supplier. The motivic filtration piece is the image of the third stage in that $K_0$. Choice means that every family of nonempty sets admits a choice function.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The field, scheme, class, Choice and size bounds in the statement.

**Goal:** Construct the componentwise curve-and-point support and prove the two exact sequences and the actual supported lift.

[F1] [lem-third-piece-representatives](item-lem-third-piece-representatives) gives a rank-three representative with the stated Chern vanishings and trivial determinant, under the stated Choice and size assumptions.

[F2] [lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata) decomposes $X$ into finitely many clopen integral components. [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) identifies restriction on the actual filtration images and $K_0$ with the product over those components. [lem-high-filtration-vanishing](item-lem-high-filtration-vanishing) gives $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0=0$ on each component of dimension less than three.

[F3] [prop-swan-bertini-point-section](item-prop-swan-bertini-point-section) supplies a functional with finite smooth zero scheme and a rank-two kernel bundle off that scheme. [lem-normal-smooth-locus-restriction](item-lem-normal-smooth-locus-restriction) makes the nonsmooth locus on each normal three-dimensional component closed of codimension at least two. [prop-bertini-curve-section](item-prop-bertini-curve-section) supplies, for this fixed avoidance locus, a smooth geometrically integral codimension-two zero curve on each such component. These suppliers assume Choice.

[F4] [lem-determinants-of-short-exact-sequences](item-lem-determinants-of-short-exact-sequences) gives the determinant isomorphism for a short exact sequence of bundles. [lem-trivial-determinant-rank-two-kernel](item-lem-trivial-determinant-rank-two-kernel) identifies the kernel of a surjective functional on a rank-two bundle of trivial determinant with $\mathcal O$.

[F5] [def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface](item-def-nonconnective-k-spectrum-interface) gives the classes of bundles in perfect $K_0$ and their additivity in short exact sequences. [prop-perfect-k-localization-input](item-prop-perfect-k-localization-input) gives the fiber sequence $K_T(X)\to K(X)\to K(V)$ when $X$ is qcqs and $V$ is quasi-compact open. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) records the inherited Choice assumption.

### Proof
1.1 By [F1], choose a representative $P_0$ of $\alpha$ with the stated rank, determinant and Chern properties. By [F2], each lower-dimensional clopen component has zero third filtration image, so $\alpha$ restricts to zero there. Replace $P_0$ on all such components by $\mathcal O^3$, leaving it unchanged on the three-dimensional components. Gluing over the finite disjoint clopen partition gives a rank-three bundle $P$. The componentwise $K_0$ decomposition in [F2] shows that $[P]-[\mathcal O_X^3]=\alpha$. Its determinant and the two Chern vanishings hold componentwise, hence globally. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Apply the point-section supplier [F3] to the restriction of $P$ on the union of three-dimensional components. On each lower-dimensional component use the first-coordinate projection $\mathcal O^3\to\mathcal O$. These maps glue to $s$. Its zero scheme $S$ is finite, lies in the smooth locus, and has no points on lower-dimensional components. On $U=X\setminus S$, [F3] gives the exact sequence $0\to Q|_U\to P|_U\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal O_U\to0$ with rank-two kernel; on lower-dimensional components this kernel is the displayed trivial rank-two summand. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 On each three-dimensional component, prescribe the closed nonsmooth locus in $U$ as the avoidance set. It has codimension at least two by [F3]. The curve supplier [F3] gives a functional on the actual restricted kernel whose zero scheme is a smooth geometrically integral codimension-two curve avoiding that set. On each lower-dimensional component use a coordinate projection from the trivial rank-two kernel; it has empty zero scheme. Glue these finitely many functionals to $t$ on $U$. Thus $Y$ is precisely the stated finite disjoint union of curves and lies in the smooth locus. The construction uses the avoidance set fixed before choosing the functional. [F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 The zero scheme $Y$ is closed in the open subset $U$. Its reduced closure $C$ in $X$ therefore satisfies $C\cap U=Y$ as reduced schemes: $Y$ is smooth and hence reduced. Thus $C\setminus Y\subseteq X\setminus U=S$. Since $Y$ is smooth and every point of $S$ is in the smooth locus of $X$, both $C$ and $T=C\cup S$ have the asserted location properties; the possible nonsmooth points of $C$ are contained in $C\setminus Y$. This also applies to the empty boundary. [F3, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 On $V=X\setminus(C\cup S)$ both functionals are pointwise nonzero. A functional on a finite locally free module is surjective wherever one of its coefficients is a unit, so the sequence for $s$ restricts to the first displayed sequence and $t|_V$ is surjective. By [F4], $\det Q|_V\otimes\det\mathcal O_V\cong\det P|_V\cong\mathcal O_V$. The rank-two kernel result in [F4] identifies the kernel of $t|_V$ with $\mathcal O_V$, giving the second sequence. [F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1]

6.1 Additivity of bundle classes in perfect $K_0$ gives $[Q|_V]=2[\mathcal O_V]$ and then $[P|_V]=3[\mathcal O_V]$, so $\alpha|_V=0$. The finite-type affine scheme $X$ is Noetherian and qcqs; its open subset $V$ is quasi-compact. Applying the actual localization fiber sequence in [F5], exactness on zeroth homotopy identifies the kernel of $K_0(X)\to K_0(V)$ with the image of $K_{0,T}(X)\to K_0(X)$. Therefore $\alpha$ has the claimed supported lift. The lift is an existence statement and is not asserted to be canonical. [F5, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

### Source/application note
The article's integral-curve construction is applied separately on the finitely many three-dimensional clopen integral components. The resulting finite union is sufficient for the subsequent localization argument. Lower-dimensional components contribute no third image-filtration class by the named stage-vanishing supplier and are given trivial representatives and nowhere-zero functionals. No globally irreducible curve is asserted for a disconnected fixed pair.

## Motivic Chern classification on normal affine surfaces

[Open item](item-thm-normal-surface-classification) · level 30

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site-size and universe bounds required for the specified motivic and perfect K-theory constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension two. The map
$$ (c_1,c_2):\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)\longrightarrow H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\times H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z) $$
is a bijection. Under the first-Chern-class identification of $H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ with the Picard group, its first component is the determinant. Thus rank-two bundles are classified by their determinant and second motivic Chern class.

A vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module; rank two means that it is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^2$. The set $\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)$ consists of its isomorphism classes. A line bundle is a rank-one vector bundle, the determinant of a rank-two bundle is its second exterior power, and the Picard group is the group of line-bundle isomorphism classes under tensor product. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Krull dimension is the supremum of the lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets. The displayed motivic groups are cohomology groups of the indicated integral weight-one and weight-two motivic complexes, and $c_i$ are the specified motivic Chern classes. Choice means that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and ambient universes used by the supplied constructions.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The field $k$, scheme $X$, Choice and site-size and universe bounds in the statement.

**Goal:** Prove that the displayed map is well-defined and bijective, and identify its first component with the determinant.

[F1] A bundle has a well-defined isomorphism class and a class in $K_0(X)$, the zeroth homotopy group of the nonconnective K-theory spectrum of perfect complexes. On an affine scheme the latter agrees with the vector-bundle Grothendieck group. [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

[F2] The motivic image filtration $F^iK_0(X)$ is the image of the zeroth homotopy group of stage $i$ in $K_0(X)$; stage zero is $K(X)$. For $i=0,1,2$, the actual stage-to-image maps are isomorphisms under the stated normal finite-type hypotheses. The exact sequence of consecutive stages implies $\ker p_0=F^1K_0(X)$ and $\ker p_1=F^2K_0(X)$ for the transported graded projections. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) [def-filtration-projections](item-def-filtration-projections) [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence)

[F3] For the stated $X$, $p_0$ is the locally constant rank and $p_1$ on $F^1K_0(X)$ is the actual perfect first Chern class. Normality implies seminormality, as an element of the fraction field whose square and cube belong to a normal domain is integral and therefore belongs to it. [lem-zero-projection-rank](item-lem-zero-projection-rank) [lem-first-projection-chern](item-lem-first-projection-chern)

[F4] The actual perfect Chern operations restrict to bundle Chern classes. When two perfect classes have equal first Chern classes, the second Chern class of their difference is the difference of their second Chern classes. [lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-first-class-and-coefficients](item-lem-author-3cde9692a7e9-first-class-and-coefficients)

[F5] On $F^2K_0(X)$, $p_2=-c_2$ and its kernel is $F^3K_0(X)$. For a noetherian two-dimensional scheme over a field, the zeroth homotopy group of stage three vanishes; hence its image $F^3K_0(X)$ vanishes. [prop-second-projection-chern](item-prop-second-projection-chern) [lem-high-filtration-vanishing](item-lem-high-filtration-vanishing) [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration)

[F6] Every pair in the displayed target is realized by a rank-two bundle on $X$. [lem-surface-chern-prescription](item-lem-surface-chern-prescription)

[F7] Two rank-two bundles on this nonempty affine surface are isomorphic exactly when their classes in the specified perfect $K_0(X)$ agree. The first Chern class identifies the Picard group with $H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ and sends the determinant to the first Chern class of the bundle. [thm-critical-rank-cancellation](item-thm-critical-rank-cancellation) [thm-line-bundle-first-chern-classification](item-thm-line-bundle-first-chern-classification) [lem-first-projection-chern](item-lem-first-projection-chern)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Compare the difference of two bundle classes successively with the first three filtration stages, and use the separate prescription theorem for surjectivity.

1.1 The given finite-type scheme is noetherian and, because its dimension is two, nonempty. Chern classes are invariant under bundle isomorphism, so the displayed assignment is well-defined on $\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)$. The target groups and bundle classes use the constructions and assumptions in [F1]–[F4]. [F1, F4, given]

1.2 Let rank-two bundles $E$ and $F$ have equal first and second Chern classes, and put $x=[E]-[F]\in K_0(X)$. Both bundles have rank two at every point, so $p_0(x)=0$ by [F3]. Exactness in [F2] therefore gives $x\in F^1K_0(X)$. [F1, F2, F3, given, construct]

2.1 The first Chern class of $x$ is $c_1(E)-c_1(F)=0$, since the actual first operation is additive and restricts to the bundle operation. Thus [F3] gives $p_1(x)=0$, and [F2] gives $x\in F^2K_0(X)$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2]

3.1 By the equal-first-class difference formula in [F4], $c_2(x)=c_2(E)-c_2(F)=0$. Hence [F5] gives $x\in F^3K_0(X)=0$. Therefore $[E]=[F]$, and [F7] gives $E\cong F$. The displayed map is injective. [F4, F5, F7, step 2.1]

4.1 For an arbitrary pair in the target, [F6] supplies a rank-two bundle with exactly those two Chern classes, so the map is surjective. Finally, [F7] identifies the first component with the determinant under the Picard isomorphism. Together with step 3.1 this proves the bijection and the stated classification. [F6, F7, step 3.1] ∎

## Removing isolated points from the support

[Open item](item-lem-point-correction-localization) · level 30

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe bounds of the cited filtration and support constructions. Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension three, and let $\alpha\in F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. Choose $P,S,C,T$ as in [lem-bertini-support-reduction](item-lem-bertini-support-reduction): $\alpha=[P]-[\mathcal O_X^3]$, $S$ is a finite set of smooth closed points on the three-dimensional components, $C$ is the reduced closure of the componentwise curve constructed there, $T=C\cup S$, and $\alpha$ restricts to zero on $X\setminus T$. Put $D=S\setminus C=\{y_1,\ldots,y_r\}$, allowing $D=\varnothing$.

The square of open immersions
$$\begin{matrix}X\setminus T&\longrightarrow&X\setminus C\\\downarrow&&\downarrow\\X\setminus D&\longrightarrow&X\end{matrix}$$
is cartesian and cocartesian. The actual localization and restriction maps form a commutative diagram with exact rows
$$\begin{matrix} \bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathbb Z&\xrightarrow{f}&K_0(X)&\longrightarrow&K_0(X\setminus D)\\ \Vert&&\downarrow i&&\downarrow\\ \bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathbb Z&\xrightarrow{g}&K_0(X\setminus C)&\xrightarrow{j}&K_0(X\setminus T). \end{matrix}$$
The two copies of the direct sum identify with the respective supported $K_0$ groups by actual restriction and point dévissage; the $i$th basis vector maps under $f$ to $[\kappa(y_i)]$. Moreover, for both pairs the actual map from the third supported filtration stage to supported $K$ induces an isomorphism on $\pi_0$.

There is $a\in\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z$ with $i(\alpha)=g(a)$. Thus $\beta=\alpha-f(a)$ restricts to zero in $K_0(X\setminus C)$, and $f(a)$ belongs to the zero-extended top-dimensional smooth-point subgroup $F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)\subseteq F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. Consequently $\beta$ belongs to the kernel of the natural restriction $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\to F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X\setminus C)$. If $X$ is pure three-dimensional, the top-dimensional subgroup is the smooth-point subgroup $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$ of [def-smooth-point-filtration](item-def-smooth-point-filtration).

Here $K_0$ is zeroth homotopy of nonconnective perfect-complex $K$-theory, and $K(A/B)$ is the fiber of restriction $K(A)\to K(B)$. Its supported third stage is the corresponding fiber at stage $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K$. The image filtration $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0$ is the image of that stage in $K_0$. The top-dimensional smooth-point subgroup is generated by the residue-sheaf classes of smooth closed points on the three-dimensional clopen components, extended by zero to $X$. No point on a lower-dimensional component is included merely because it is smooth.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The field, scheme, class, support data, Choice and size bounds in the statement. A finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian, so all its open subsets are quasi-compact; an algebraically closed field is perfect.

**Goal:** Establish the actual finite-support localization diagram, the supported third-stage comparison, and the correction without assuming either support-to-global map injective.

[F1] [lem-bertini-support-reduction](item-lem-bertini-support-reduction) supplies the stated data, including $T=C\cup S$, the location of $S$ on three-dimensional components, and $\alpha|_{X\setminus T}=0$. Its componentwise construction applies to disconnected $X$ and uses Choice.

[F2] [prop-perfect-k-localization-input](item-prop-perfect-k-localization-input) gives natural localization, Mayer–Vietoris and supported open excision for these qcqs schemes and opens. [prop-smooth-point-excision-purity](item-prop-smooth-point-excision-purity) identifies the actual supported $K_0$ at each smooth closed point with $\mathbb Z$, with positive generator the supported residue-sheaf class and with its stated global image.

[F3] [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration), [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support), [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) and [lem-filtered-support-exactness](item-lem-filtered-support-exactness) give the natural supported tower, stage-zero $K$, and its graded restriction fibers. [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) supplies the derived Nisnevich sheaves underlying each motivic graded term, hence their Zariski descent. [lem-smooth-point-motivic-purity](item-lem-smooth-point-motivic-purity) makes every homotopy group of each supported graded term of weight $0,1,2$ vanish at a smooth point of a pure three-dimensional scheme.

[F4] [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) gives the actual stagewise finite clopen product decomposition. [lem-smooth-point-filtration](item-lem-smooth-point-filtration) gives the point-supported stage-three surjection in the pure case. [lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope) identifies the zero-extended top-dimensional point subgroup and its containment in the third image filtration; [def-smooth-point-filtration](item-def-smooth-point-filtration) gives the pure-dimensional convention. The filtration is natural for restriction by [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration).

### Proof
1.1 Since $D=S\setminus C$ and $T=C\cup S=C\cup D$, the upper-left open is $(X\setminus C)\cap(X\setminus D)$ and the other two opens cover $X$. Intersections of open immersions are their fiber products, and morphisms out of the two covering opens that agree on their intersection glue uniquely. Therefore the displayed scheme square is cartesian and cocartesian. All four opens are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. [F1, given]

2.1 Apply localization to $D\subset X$ and to the same closed set $D\subset X\setminus C$. It is closed in the latter because $D$ is a finite set of closed points and is disjoint from $C$. Open excision identifies the two supported spectra by actual restriction, compatibly with their maps to the ambient spectra. Their long exact homotopy sequences give the two exact rows and the commutative square of maps. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 For disjoint finite closed subsets $A,B\subset X$, the cover $X=(X\setminus A)\cup(X\setminus B)$ and Mayer–Vietoris identify the support spectrum for $A\cup B$ with the product of the support spectra for $A$ and $B$: take the fiber over $K(X\setminus(A\cup B))$ of the cartesian restriction square and use the universal property of the pullback. The two factors map to the union-support spectrum by the corresponding maps of support fibers. Iterating, including the empty case, identifies $K_D(X)$ with the finite product of the one-point support spectra. By point dévissage each zeroth group is $\mathbb Z$, and the inverse generator maps to the residue-sheaf class. Open excision gives the same identification on $X\setminus C$ and preserves these generators. This proves the displayed diagram and its generator normalization. [F2, step 2.1]

4.1 Each motivic stage has Zariski Mayer–Vietoris on the opens used here. Indeed, stage zero has it by [F2]. If stage $q$ has it, compare its Mayer–Vietoris square with the square of the weight-$q$ graded spectrum. The latter is cartesian by derived Zariski descent in [F3]; taking fibers in the natural graded triangle shows that the stage-$(q+1)$ square is cartesian. Induction gives the assertion through stage three. The same finite-support pullback argument as in step 3.1 therefore splits the supported stage and its stage-to-$K$ map into the corresponding one-point maps. [F2, F3, step 3.1]

5.1 Let $y\in D$. It lies on a three-dimensional clopen component, and the union $X_3$ of those components is pure three-dimensional. The stagewise clopen product equivalence identifies the support tower at $y$ on $X$ with that on $X_3$: the other component contributes the fiber of an identity map. On $X_3$, [F3] makes the supported graded spectra in weights $0,1,2$ contractible, since all their homotopy groups vanish. The supported graded triangles therefore make the transitions from stage three to stage zero equivalences. Stage zero is supported $K$. Thus the actual one-point stage-three map is an equivalence. By step 4.1, so is the map for the finite set $D$ on $X$; the analogous map on $X\setminus C$ follows by stagewise open excision from its Mayer–Vietoris square. Taking $\pi_0$ proves the two stated isomorphisms. [F3, F4, step 4.1]

6.1 By [F1], $j(i(\alpha))=\alpha|_{X\setminus T}=0$. Exactness of the lower row gives an element $a$ with $i(\alpha)=g(a)$. Commutativity gives $i(f(a))=g(a)$, hence $i(\beta)=0$. By step 3.1, $f(a)$ is a finite integral combination of residue classes at points of $D$; every such point is smooth and lies on a three-dimensional component. Therefore [F4] puts $f(a)$ in $F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)$ and hence in $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. Since this is a subgroup, $\beta$ lies in it too. Natural restriction of the image filtration then makes its vanishing in ambient $K_0(X\setminus C)$ exactly the asserted kernel condition. For pure $X$, [F4] identifies the point subgroup with $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}$. No injectivity of $f$ or $g$ is used. [F1, F4, step 3.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Independent determinant and second-Chern prescription

[Open item](item-cor-surface-determinant-prescription) · level 31

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site-size and universe bounds required for the motivic and perfect K-theory constructions in [thm-normal-surface-classification](item-thm-normal-surface-classification). Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $X$ a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension two. Then
$$E\longmapsto (\det E,c_2(E))$$
induces a bijection from $\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)$ to $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\times H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. Thus two rank-two bundles with the same determinant and second motivic Chern class are isomorphic, and every pair of such invariants occurs.

A vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module; rank two means locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^2$. The set $\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)$ consists of their isomorphism classes. A line bundle is a rank-one vector bundle, $\det E=\bigwedge^2 E$, and $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ is the group of line-bundle isomorphism classes under tensor product. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets. The displayed motivic group and $c_2$ are the integral weight-two motivic cohomology group and the second motivic Chern class used in the supplier. Choice means that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and ambient universes used in those constructions.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $k$, $X$, Choice and the site-size and universe bounds in the statement.

**Goal:** Prove that determinant and the second motivic Chern class give the stated bijection.

[F1] Under these hypotheses, the map $(c_1,c_2)$ from $\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)$ to $H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\times H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is bijective. The same supplier identifies $\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ with $H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ by first Chern class and identifies $c_1(E)$ with the image of $\det E$. [thm-normal-surface-classification](item-thm-normal-surface-classification)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Transport the first coordinate of the supplied classification along the Picard isomorphism.

1.1 Let $\gamma:\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ be the isomorphism in [F1]. For every rank-two bundle $E$, [F1] gives $\gamma([\det E])=c_1(E)$. Consequently the map in the statement is the composite of the bijection $(c_1,c_2)$ with $(\gamma^{-1},\mathrm{id})$. In particular it is well-defined on isomorphism classes. [F1, given]

2.1 Both maps in this composite are bijections, so their composite is a bijection. Its injectivity gives uniqueness up to isomorphism, and its surjectivity gives a bundle for every prescribed pair. This proves the stated classification and independent prescription. [F1, step 1.1] ∎

## Lifting the corrected class to the curve-supported third stage

[Open item](item-lem-lift-curve-supported-filtration) · level 31

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe bounds of the cited filtration and support constructions. Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension three, and let $C$ be the reduced closed curve constructed in [lem-bertini-support-reduction](item-lem-bertini-support-reduction). Thus $C$ lies in the smooth locus $W=X_{\mathrm{smooth}}$ and, on each three-dimensional clopen integral component of $X$, its intersection is a closed integral curve; it is empty on the lower-dimensional components. Put $U=X\setminus C$ and $V=W\setminus C$.

If $\beta\in F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ restricts to zero in $K_0(U)$, then its unique representative $b\in\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ lifts to some
$$\widetilde b\in\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X/U).$$
Restriction induces an isomorphism
$$\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X/U)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(W/V),$$
compatible with support-to-global maps. In particular this applies to the corrected class of [lem-point-correction-localization](item-lem-point-correction-localization). The support lift need not be unique.

Here an integral curve is a reduced irreducible scheme of dimension one, and the smooth locus is the open set where $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. The spectrum $K$ is nonconnective perfect-complex $K$-theory; $K_0=\pi_0K$. The image-filtration group $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0$ is the image of $\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K\to K_0$. For an open complement $A\setminus B$, the supported third stage $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(A/(A\setminus B))$ means the homotopy fiber of the actual restriction of third stages, with its map to the stage on $A$. A homotopy-cartesian square is a square whose upper-left object is equivalent to the homotopy pullback of the other three objects.

### Facts & Assumptions
**Given:** The field, scheme, curve, class, Choice and size assumptions in the statement.

**Goal:** Lift the actual third-stage representative of $\beta$ to the curve-support fiber and identify that fiber on the smooth locus.

[F1] [lem-bertini-support-reduction](item-lem-bertini-support-reduction) supplies the componentwise curve and its containment in $W$; [lem-point-correction-localization](item-lem-point-correction-localization) supplies a corrected class satisfying the stated kernel condition. The components form a finite clopen partition because $X$ is normal and Noetherian, as used in the former supplier.

[F2] [prop-third-edge-isomorphism](item-prop-third-edge-isomorphism) gives injectivity of $\pi_0F^3K(X)\to K_0(X)$. The definition of the image filtration in [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) gives a representative for every element of $F^3K_0(X)$.

[F3] [rem-third-edge-curve-complement](item-rem-third-edge-curve-complement) gives injectivity of $\pi_0F^3K(X_e\setminus C_e)\to K_0(X_e\setminus C_e)$ for each three-dimensional affine component $X_e$ and its closed integral curve $C_e\subset(X_e)_{\mathrm{smooth}}$. [lem-high-filtration-vanishing](item-lem-high-filtration-vanishing) gives $\pi_0F^3K(X_e)=0$ on each component of dimension less than three. [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) identifies the actual stage and $K$ maps on a finite clopen union with their componentwise products.

[F4] [lem-filtered-support-exactness](item-lem-filtered-support-exactness) gives the long exact homotopy sequence of the actual stagewise support fiber. [def-cohomology-with-support](item-def-cohomology-with-support) identifies the displayed quotient notation with that fiber. [lem-open-excision-for-support-fibers](item-lem-open-excision-for-support-fibers) gives support excision, compatible with support-to-global maps, provided the relevant restriction square is homotopy cartesian.

[F5] [prop-perfect-k-localization-input](item-prop-perfect-k-localization-input) gives Zariski Mayer–Vietoris for $K$ on quasi-compact opens. [prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence](item-prop-motivic-graded-spectral-sequence) gives the natural fiber triangles $F^{r+1}K\to F^rK\to\mathbb Z(r)_{\mathrm{mot}}[2r]$, and [lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes](item-lem-author-b747b28c359f-elmanto-morrow-complexes) gives Nisnevich descent, hence Zariski descent, for the graded terms.

### Proof
1.1 By [F1], write $X$ as the finite disjoint union of its clopen integral components $X_e$. On every three-dimensional component, $C_e=C\cap X_e$ is the reduced closure of an integral curve, hence is a closed integral curve; it lies in the smooth locus. On every lower-dimensional component $C_e$ is empty. The opens $U$ and $W$, and their intersections with the components, are quasi-compact: $X$ is finite type over a field and therefore Noetherian. [F1, given]

1.2 For a three-dimensional component, [F3] makes the actual stage-to-$K_0$ map on $X_e\setminus C_e$ injective. For a lower-dimensional component, its complement is all of $X_e$ and its third-stage zeroth group is zero by [F3], so the same map is injective. The finite clopen product equivalences in [F3], applied to $U=\coprod_e(X_e\setminus C_e)$ and compatible with the stage-to-$K$ maps, therefore show that
$$\pi_0F^3K(U)\longrightarrow K_0(U)$$
is injective. [F3, step 1.1]

2.1 By [F2], $\beta$ has a representative $b\in\pi_0F^3K(X)$, and that representative is unique. Naturality of the stage-to-$K$ maps sends the restriction of $b$ to the restriction of $\beta$, which is zero in $K_0(U)$. Step 1.2 therefore makes $b|_U=0$ in $\pi_0F^3K(U)$. The exact sequence in [F4] supplies $\widetilde b\in\pi_0F^3K(X/U)$ mapping to $b$. Exactness does not assert that this lift is unique. [F2, F4, given, step 1.2]

2.2 The opens $U$ and $W$ cover $X$ because $C\subset W$, and their intersection is $V$. The restriction square for stage zero $K$ is homotopy cartesian by [F5]. The corresponding square for each graded term is homotopy cartesian by its Zariski descent. If the stage-$r$ square is homotopy cartesian, the natural triangle in [F5] identifies the stage-$(r+1)$ square as its fiber over the graded-term square; fibers preserve homotopy-cartesian squares. Induction for $r=0,1,2$ proves that the stage-three square for this cover is homotopy cartesian. All opens involved are qcqs by step 1.1. [F5, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply the spectrum form of open excision in [F4] to $C\subset W\subset X$ and the stage-three square of step 2.2. It gives the actual restriction equivalence $F^3K(X/U)\simeq F^3K(W/V)$ and its compatibility with support-to-global maps. Taking $\pi_0$ gives the displayed isomorphism. Applying step 2.1 to the corrected class supplied by [F1] proves the final assertion. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Smooth points generate the third motivic piece

[Open item](item-thm-smooth-point-generation) · level 32

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe size bounds required by the cited motivic filtration, support, and comparison constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $X$ a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension three. Then
$$F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)=F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X).$$

More generally, if $X$ is normal affine of finite type and dimension three but is not assumed pure-dimensional, the same equality holds with $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$ replaced by the zero-extended subgroup $F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)$ generated by smooth closed points on its three-dimensional components.

Here normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; affine finite type means $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a finitely generated $k$-algebra $A$. Dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of distinct irreducible closed subsets, and pure dimension three means that every irreducible component has dimension three. A point is smooth if $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth in a neighbourhood of it. The group $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$ is the zeroth homotopy group of nonconnective $K$-theory of perfect complexes, where a perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves. The motivic image piece $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of $\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to K_0(X)$. For pure $X$, $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$ is the subgroup generated by the perfect residue-sheaf classes $[\kappa(x)]$ at smooth closed points. In the nonpure case the top-dimensional subgroup uses only points on three-dimensional components, with classes extended by zero along the clopen component inclusions. Choice means that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and universes of the cited constructions.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $k$ and $X$ as in the general statement, the Axiom of Choice, and the stated size bounds.

**Goal:** Show that the third motivic image piece is precisely the top-dimensional smooth-point subgroup, and recover the pure-dimensional assertion.

[F1] [lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata) gives a finite disjoint clopen decomposition of $X$ into integral components and identifies zero extension of their point classes. [lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-dimension-weight-scope) defines the top-dimensional point subgroup and proves its inclusion in $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. In the pure case it is the subgroup of [def-smooth-point-filtration](item-def-smooth-point-filtration).

[F2] For any $\alpha$ in the third image piece, [lem-bertini-support-reduction](item-lem-bertini-support-reduction) constructs the componentwise curve-and-point support: the reduced closed curve $C$ lies in the smooth locus $W$; on each three-dimensional integral component its intersection is an integral closed curve, and on lower-dimensional components it is empty. [lem-point-correction-localization](item-lem-point-correction-localization) gives a top-dimensional smooth-point class $p$ such that $\beta=\alpha-p$ remains in the third image piece and restricts to zero in $K_0(X\setminus C)$.

[F3] [lem-lift-curve-supported-filtration](item-lem-lift-curve-supported-filtration) gives an actual third-stage support lift of the stage representative of $\beta$ and an actual restriction equivalence between the support fibers on $(X,X\setminus C)$ and $(W,W\setminus C)$, compatible with the maps to the global stages. The image-piece convention is that of [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration).

[F4] On a smooth pure three-dimensional finite-type scheme over the perfect field $k$, for an integral closed curve of codimension two, [lem-supported-generic-rank-kernel](item-lem-supported-generic-rank-kernel) identifies the image of the actual supported third stage in supported $K_0$ with the subgroup generated by residue-sheaf classes of closed points of that curve. The maps are the actual stage and support maps, with the normalization specified in that supplier.

[F5] [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) supplies finite clopen product decompositions of the actual stages and their maps. [lem-open-excision-for-support-fibers](item-lem-open-excision-for-support-fibers) identifies support fibers under restriction to an open neighbourhood of the support, compatibly with support-to-global maps. [lem-koszul-point-support-class](item-lem-koszul-point-support-class) supplies the perfect residue-sheaf classes at smooth closed points. The cited suppliers use the stated Choice and size hypotheses; an algebraically closed field is perfect. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Reduce to componentwise curve support, lift to the actual supported third stage, and apply the generic-rank kernel calculation.

1.1 By [F1], $X$ is a finite disjoint union of clopen integral components. The top-dimensional smooth-point subgroup is contained in $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$. It remains to prove the reverse inclusion. Let $\alpha$ be an arbitrary element of that image piece. [F1, given]

2.1 Apply [F2] to $\alpha$. It supplies a closed subset $C\subset W=X_{\mathrm{smooth}}$ and a class $p\in F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)$ such that $\beta=\alpha-p$ lies in $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ and restricts to zero in $K_0(X\setminus C)$. For every three-dimensional component $X_e$, $C_e=C\cap X_e$ is an integral closed curve in $X_e$ contained in $W_e=W\cap X_e$; on every lower-dimensional component $C$ is empty. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F3], a representative of $\beta$ in $\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ lifts to an element of the actual support group $\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X/(X\setminus C))$. Restrict this lift to $W$ using the support equivalence in [F3]. Its image in $\pi_0K(W/(W\setminus C))$, followed by the support-to-global map and the compatible comparison back on $X$, represents $\beta$. This uses the maps of support fibers, rather than identifying unrelated groups merely by isomorphism. [F3, step 2.1]

4.1 The finite clopen decomposition in [F1] restricts to $W$ and to its complement of $C$. Taking fibers of the componentwise stage and $K$ maps in [F5] decomposes both supported groups into the corresponding finite products. A component with empty support contributes the fiber of an identity map and hence zero on $\pi_0$. For each remaining component, $W_e$ is smooth of pure dimension three and $C_e\subset W_e$ is an integral closed curve of codimension two. Applying [F4] to the component of the lifted element shows that its supported $K_0$ image is a finite integer combination of the residue-sheaf classes at closed points of $C_e$. [F1, F4, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 Each such point is closed and smooth in $X_e$, hence in $X$: closedness follows because a closed point of the finite-type $k$-scheme $W_e$ has finite residue field over $k$, and smoothness is local on the source. By [F5], excision for a neighbourhood of each point identifies its supported class on $W_e$ with its supported class on $X_e$, compatibly with support-to-global maps; [F1] identifies subsequent clopen zero extension with the point class on $X$. Thus the image on $X$ of the combination in step 4.1 is a top-dimensional smooth-point class. Compatibility in step 3.1 shows that this image is $\beta$. Consequently $\alpha=p+\beta$ is in $F^3_{\mathrm{sm,top}}K_0(X)$. [F1, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1]

6.1 Since $\alpha$ was arbitrary, step 5.1 and the inclusion in step 1.1 prove the general equality. If $X$ is pure three-dimensional, all its components are three-dimensional, so [F1] identifies the top-dimensional subgroup with $F^3_{\mathrm{sm}}K_0(X)$. This proves the article assertion. [F1, step 1.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Third Chern isomorphism

[Open item](item-cor-third-chern-isomorphism) · level 33


### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe size bounds required by the cited motivic filtration and support constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, of arbitrary characteristic, and let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension three. Then the composite
$$F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\xrightarrow{\ c_3\ }H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\ \epsilon_3\ }F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$$
is multiplication by $2$, and $c_3$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups.

Here normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; affine finite type means $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a finitely generated $k$-algebra $A$; and Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of distinct irreducible closed subsets. A perfect complex is a complex locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves. Write $K(X)$ for the nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum of perfect complexes and $K_0(X)=\pi_0K(X)$. The group $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image of $\pi_0F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)\to K_0(X)$, where $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K(X)$ is the third stage of the motivic filtration. The group $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is degree-six cohomology of the weight-three motivic complex, and $c_3$ is the actual third Chern operation on perfect $K$-classes. The edge map $\epsilon_3$ is the inverse of the actual third-stage-to-graded isomorphism followed by the stage-to-$K_0$ map with codomain restricted to its image. The Axiom of Choice says that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and universes used by the constructions.

### Statement references

[def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration)

[def-third-edge-map](item-def-third-edge-map)

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The field, scheme, choice and size hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Prove the displayed composite is multiplication by $2$ and that $c_3$ is an isomorphism.

[F1] [thm-smooth-point-generation](item-thm-smooth-point-generation) identifies $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ with the subgroup generated by classes of smooth closed points on the three-dimensional components, extended by zero. In the pure-dimensional case this is the subgroup generated by all smooth closed points. A point is smooth when $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth in a neighbourhood of it; its generator is the class of its perfect residue sheaf.

[F2] [lem-third-chern-additive](item-lem-third-chern-additive) says that the actual $c_3$ is a group homomorphism on the third image piece. [def-third-edge-map](item-def-third-edge-map) defines $\epsilon_3$ as a group homomorphism.

[F3] Apply [prop-smooth-point-third-chern-factor](item-prop-smooth-point-third-chern-factor) on the pure threefold $X_3$, the union of the three-dimensional clopen components of $X$. For every smooth closed point $x\in X_3$, it identifies the positive supported residue class $u_x$ and positive motivic point class $\delta_x$ and proves $c_{3,x}(u_x)=2\delta_x$ and $\epsilon_{3,x}(\delta_x)=u_x$. Both operations commute with support-to-global maps on $X_3$. No point on a lower-dimensional component is used.

[F4] [prop-smooth-cycle-unique-divisibility](item-prop-smooth-cycle-unique-divisibility) says that the top-dimensional smooth-point subgroup is uniquely divisible: multiplication by each positive integer is an isomorphism. [prop-third-edge-isomorphism](item-prop-third-edge-isomorphism) says that the specified $\epsilon_3$ is an isomorphism for the given normal affine finite-type threefold. The cited constructions use the stated choice and size conventions; [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) states the choice assumption.

[F5] [lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-normal-point-strata) makes $X_3$ a pure normal affine finite-type threefold and identifies zero extension of its residue classes. [lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products](item-lem-author-80f982ded420-clopen-filtered-products) gives the actual clopen product decompositions of the augmented stages and their image subgroups. Its graded triangles give the corresponding product decomposition of motivic cohomology. The actual Chern operations and the edge map commute with these restrictions; the former are pointed and the latter is defined from the natural stage-to-graded and augmentation maps in [def-third-edge-map](item-def-third-edge-map). Thus an identity for a zero-extended top-dimensional point class can be checked on $X_3$ and its clopen complement.

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Compute on smooth-point generators and use the edge isomorphism and unique divisibility.

1.1 Set $G=F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ and $H=H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. By [F1], $G$ is generated by the residue-sheaf classes of smooth closed points on the three-dimensional components, with the stated zero extensions. By [F2], $c_3:G\to H$ and $\epsilon_3:H\to G$ are homomorphisms. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Let $g_x$ be one of these generators, so $x\in X_3$. On the pure threefold $X_3$, [F3] gives $u_x\mapsto2\delta_x\mapsto2u_x$ in the supported groups, and the support-to-global squares give $\epsilon_3c_3(g_x|_{X_3})=2g_x|_{X_3}$. On the clopen complement the class is zero; pointedness of $c_3$ and additivity of the edge make its composite zero there. By the product decompositions and naturality in [F5], these componentwise equalities give $\epsilon_3c_3(g_x)=2g_x$ on $X$. This remains true if $g_x$ vanishes globally. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 Every element of $G$ is a finite integer linear combination of these generators. Since the composite is a homomorphism, step 2.1 shows that $\epsilon_3c_3=2\operatorname{id}_G$ on all of $G$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 By [F4] and the equality of groups in [F1], multiplication by $2$ is an automorphism of $G$, and $\epsilon_3$ is an isomorphism from $H$ to $G$. Thus $c_3=\epsilon_3^{-1}\circ(2\operatorname{id}_G)$ is a composite of isomorphisms. Together with step 3.1 this proves both assertions. [F1, F4, step 3.1, algebra] ∎


## Prescribing three Chern classes successively

[Open item](item-lem-threefold-chern-prescription) · level 34

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe size bounds required by the cited motivic filtration and Chern-class constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $X$ a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension three. Given classes $a_i\in H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ for $i=1,2,3$, there is a rank-three vector bundle $E$ with $c_i(E)=a_i$ for all three indices.

More precisely, choose a line bundle $L$ with $c_1(L)=a_1$, set $\alpha_1=[L]-1$, choose $\alpha_2\in F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ with $c_2(\alpha_2)=a_2$, put $b_3=c_3(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)$, and choose $\alpha_3\in F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ with $c_3(\alpha_3)=a_3-b_3$. Then $\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3=[E]-3$ for a rank-three bundle $E$, and its first three Chern classes are the prescribed classes. The sum lies in $F^1_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$.

Here a vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module, its rank is its local free rank, and a line bundle is a rank-one vector bundle. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains; affine finite type means $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a finitely generated $k$-algebra $A$. Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. An algebraically closed field is one in which every nonconstant one-variable polynomial has a root. A perfect complex is a complex locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of vector bundles; $K_0(X)$ is the zeroth homotopy group of its nonconnective K-theory spectrum. A bundle gives the class of its degree-zero complex, $1=[\mathcal O_X]$, and an integer denotes that multiple of $1$. The subgroup $F^j_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image in $K_0(X)$ of the $j$th stage of the supplied motivic filtration. The group $H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is degree-$2i$ cohomology of the weight-$i$ motivic complex; $c_i$ is the actual motivic Chern operation, agreeing on bundle classes with the bundle Chern class. Choice asserts that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and ambient universes used by the suppliers.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The field, scheme, choice and size hypotheses above and the three target classes.

**Goal:** Carry out the stated successive choices and obtain a rank-three bundle with the specified classes.

[F1] The first Chern class gives an isomorphism from the Picard group of line bundles to $H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. [thm-line-bundle-first-chern-classification](item-thm-line-bundle-first-chern-classification)

[F2] Under the given normal finite-type hypotheses, $c_2$ is surjective from $F^2_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ to $H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. [lem-second-chern-surjective-low-dimension](item-lem-second-chern-surjective-low-dimension)

[F3] For the given normal affine finite-type threefold, $c_3$ is an isomorphism from $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ to $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. [cor-third-chern-isomorphism](item-cor-third-chern-isomorphism)

[F4] Every class in $F^2$ has pointwise rank zero and first Chern class zero. Every class in $F^3$ has rank zero and first and second Chern classes zero. [lem-second-piece-rank-determinant](item-lem-second-piece-rank-determinant) [lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-lower-vanishing](item-lem-author-9b6cb358ddc9-lower-vanishing)

[F5] On this nonempty affine finite-type threefold, each pointwise rank-zero perfect $K_0$ class is $[V]-3$ for a rank-three bundle $V$. The affine bridge identifies bundle and perfect $K_0$ classes compatibly. [lem-critical-rank-representatives](item-lem-critical-rank-representatives) [lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge](item-lem-affine-perfect-k-zero-bridge)

[F6] The bundle total Chern series is multiplicative under direct sums, a line has no Chern classes above degree one, and the virtual series of a difference is the quotient of the bundle series. A trivial bundle has total class $1$. [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities)

[F7] The image filtration is decreasing, and the kernel of the zeroth stage projection is $F^1$. On this normal affine finite-type scheme the zeroth projection is pointwise rank. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) [lem-zero-projection-rank](item-lem-zero-projection-rank)

[F8] The Axiom of Choice and the indicated site and universe bounds are the assumptions used in the cited constructions. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Choose the classes in successive filtration pieces, represent the higher pieces by rank-three bundles, and calculate using Whitney multiplication.

1.1 By [F1], choose $L$ with $c_1(L)=a_1$ and put $\alpha_1=[L]-1$. Its pointwise rank is zero, so [F7] places it in $F^1$. By [F2], choose $\alpha_2\in F^2$ with $c_2(\alpha_2)=a_2$. Put $b_3=c_3(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)$. By [F3], choose $\alpha_3\in F^3$ with $c_3(\alpha_3)=a_3-b_3$. These choices use the hypotheses and bounds in [F8]. [F1, F2, F3, F7, F8, given, choose]

2.1 By [F4], $\alpha_2$ and $\alpha_3$ have pointwise rank zero. The dimension assumption makes $X$ nonempty, so [F5] gives rank-three bundles $E_2,E_3$ with $\alpha_i=[E_i]-3$ for $i=2,3$. Since the trivial bundle has total Chern class $1$, [F6] identifies $c_j(E_i)$ with $c_j(\alpha_i)$ for these virtual classes. In particular $c_1(E_2)=0$, $c_2(E_2)=a_2$, $c_1(E_3)=c_2(E_3)=0$, and $c_3(E_3)=a_3-b_3$. [F4, F5, F6, step 1.1]

3.1 Let $V=E_3\oplus E_2\oplus L$, a rank-seven bundle. In $K_0(X)$, $\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3=[V]-7$. By [F6] and step 2.1, the total class of $E_3$ through degree three is $1+c_3(E_3)t^3$, and that of $E_2\oplus L$ begins $1+a_1t+a_2t^2+b_3t^3$. The latter equality follows because $\alpha_1+\alpha_2=[E_2\oplus L]-4$ and trivial summands do not change total Chern classes. Multiplying these series through degree three gives $c_1(V)=a_1$, $c_2(V)=a_2$, and $c_3(V)=b_3+c_3(E_3)=a_3$. [F5, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The class $[V]-7$ has pointwise rank zero. Applying [F5] gives a rank-three bundle $E$ with $[E]-3=[V]-7=\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3$. The affine bridge and the representative-independent virtual Chern series in [F5] and [F6] imply $c_j(E)=c_j(V)=a_j$ for $j=1,2,3$, since trivial bundles have total class $1$. Finally, $\alpha_1\in F^1$ by step 1.1 and $F^3\subseteq F^2\subseteq F^1$ by [F7]; hence their sum lies in $F^1$. This proves the construction. [F5, F6, F7, step 1.1, step 3.1] ∎

### Source notation
The article first identifies the sum with $[E_3\oplus E_2\oplus L]-7$. Its final two occurrences use $E_1\oplus E_2\oplus L$, although the preceding rank-three bundle is called $E_3$. The calculation above retains the defined $E_3$.

## Third Chern vanishing and a trivial summand

[Open item](item-cor-rank-three-zero-chern-splitting) · level 34

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe size bounds required by the cited motivic filtration, support and Chern constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a normal affine $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension three, and let $E$ be a rank-three vector bundle on $X$. Then
$$c_3(E)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E\cong E'\oplus\mathcal O_X$$
for some rank-two vector bundle $E'$ on $X$.

Here algebraically closed means that every nonconstant polynomial over $k$ has a root in $k$; finite type means that $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra; normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; and Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of distinct irreducible closed subsets. A vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module, and rank $r$ means locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^r$. The class $c_3(E)$ is the third integral motivic Chern class in $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$, the degree-six cohomology of the weight-three motivic complex. The Axiom of Choice says that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and universes used by the cited constructions.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $k$, $X$ and $E$ as in the statement, the Axiom of Choice and the stated site and universe bounds.

**Goal:** Prove both implications of the displayed equivalence.

[F1] [def-rank-three-euler-k-class](item-def-rank-three-euler-k-class) defines the alternating exterior class
$$\beta(E)=[\mathcal O_X]-[E]+[\Lambda^2E]-[\det E]\in K_0(X),$$
where $\det E=\Lambda^3E$ and $K_0(X)$ is the degree-zero K-theory group of perfect complexes. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free sheaves.

[F2] Under the given hypotheses, [lem-exterior-square-chern-calculation](item-lem-exterior-square-chern-calculation) proves that $\beta(E)$ lies in $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ and that $c_3(\beta(E))=-2c_3(E)$. The group $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ is the image in $K_0(X)$ of the degree-zero homotopy group of the third motivic filtration stage.

[F3] Under the same hypotheses, [cor-third-chern-isomorphism](item-cor-third-chern-isomorphism) says that the actual third Chern operation on perfect K-classes restricts to an isomorphism $c_3:F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)\to H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. In particular this restriction is injective.

[F4] [prop-murthy-k-theoretic-splitting](item-prop-murthy-k-theoretic-splitting) says that, under the given hypotheses, $\beta(E)=0$ in $K_0(X)$ implies $E\cong E'\oplus\mathcal O_X$ for a rank-two bundle $E'$.

[F5] [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes) defines the total Chern polynomial $c_t(V)=\sum_i c_i(V)t^i$ of a bundle $V$ and sets $c_i(V)=0$ for $i$ greater than its rank. [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) gives $c_t(V\oplus W)=c_t(V)c_t(W)$; in particular a trivial line has total Chern polynomial $1$. [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice) states the Choice assumption used by these constructions.

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Apply the third-Chern isomorphism to the alternating exterior class, then use the splitting criterion; the converse follows from Whitney and rank vanishing.

1.1 Suppose $c_3(E)=0$. By [F2], $\beta(E)$ belongs to the third motivic image piece and $c_3(\beta(E))=-2c_3(E)=0$. [given, F2]

2.1 The restricted third Chern operation in [F3] is injective. Since $\beta(E)$ lies in its domain and maps to zero, $\beta(E)=0$ in $F^3_{\mathrm{mot}}K_0(X)$ and hence in its ambient group $K_0(X)$. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply [F4] to this vanishing. All its field, normality, finite-type, dimension, rank, Choice and size hypotheses are those given here. It yields a rank-two bundle $E'$ and an isomorphism $E\cong E'\oplus\mathcal O_X$. [given, F4, step 2.1]

4.1 Conversely, suppose $E\cong E'\oplus\mathcal O_X$ with $E'$ of rank two. By [F5], $c_t(E)=c_t(E')c_t(\mathcal O_X)=c_t(E')$. The coefficient of $t^3$ on the right is zero because $E'$ has rank two. Thus $c_3(E)=0$. [given, F5, step 3.1]

5.1 Steps 1.1–4.1 prove both implications and hence the stated equivalence. [step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎



## Motivic Chern classification on normal affine threefolds

[Open item](item-thm-normal-threefold-classification) · level 35

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe size bounds required by the cited motivic filtration and Chern-class constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic and let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension three. Then
$$ (c_1,c_2,c_3):\mathrm{Vect}_3(X)\longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^{3}H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z) $$
is a bijection.

A vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module; $\mathrm{Vect}_3(X)$ is the set of isomorphism classes of bundles of constant rank three. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain; affine finite type means $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a finitely generated $k$-algebra $A$. Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. An algebraically closed field is a field in which every nonconstant one-variable polynomial has a root. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of vector bundles, and $K_0(X)$ is the zeroth homotopy group of its nonconnective $K$-theory spectrum. The class of a bundle $E$, viewed as a complex in degree zero, is denoted $[E]$. The group $H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is degree-$2i$ cohomology of the weight-$i$ motivic complex, and $c_i$ is the specified motivic Chern operation, evaluated on bundle classes. Choice asserts that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and ambient universes used by the suppliers.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The field, scheme, choice and size hypotheses in the statement.

**Goal:** Prove that the displayed map is injective and surjective.

[F1] The motivic image filtration $F^jK_0(X)$ is the image of the $j$th filtration stage in $K_0(X)$ and is decreasing. Its actual zeroth and first projections have respective kernels $F^1K_0(X)$ and $F^2K_0(X)$. The zeroth projection is pointwise rank, and the first projection on $F^1$ is the actual first Chern class. The kernel assertions use the descended projections and the stage exact sequence. [def-motivic-filtration](item-def-motivic-filtration) [lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence](item-lem-filtered-stage-exact-sequence) [lem-zero-projection-rank](item-lem-zero-projection-rank) [lem-first-projection-chern](item-lem-first-projection-chern)

[F2] On $F^2K_0(X)$, the actual second projection is $-c_2$ and has kernel $F^3K_0(X)$. [prop-second-projection-chern](item-prop-second-projection-chern)

[F3] The bundle total Chern series is multiplicative under direct sum. On the affine scheme $X$, its representative-independent virtual extension assigns $c_t([E]-[F])=c_t(E)c_t(F)^{-1}$; it agrees with the actual Chern operations on these classes. [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities) [def-vector-bundle-classes](item-def-vector-bundle-classes)

[F4] The actual third Chern class is an isomorphism from $F^3K_0(X)$ to $H^{6,3}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$. [cor-third-chern-isomorphism](item-cor-third-chern-isomorphism)

[F5] Every triple in the displayed target occurs as the first three Chern classes of a rank-three bundle. [lem-threefold-chern-prescription](item-lem-threefold-chern-prescription)

[F6] For bundles of constant rank at least the dimension on a nonempty affine finite-type scheme over an algebraically closed field, equality of their perfect $K_0$ classes is equivalent to isomorphism. The supplier assumes Choice and its stated universes. [thm-critical-rank-cancellation](item-thm-critical-rank-cancellation) [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

### Proof

1.1 Let $E$ and $F$ be rank-three bundles with $c_i(E)=c_i(F)$ for $i=1,2,3$, and put $\alpha=[E]-[F]\in K_0(X)$. By [F3], the coefficients through degree three of $c_t(\alpha)=c_t(E)c_t(F)^{-1}$ vanish: the two bundle series agree through degree three, so their quotient is $1$ modulo $t^4$. Thus $c_1(\alpha)=c_2(\alpha)=c_3(\alpha)=0$. Both bundles have rank three at every point, so $\alpha$ has pointwise rank zero. [F3, given, algebra]

2.1 The zeroth projection of $\alpha$ is zero by its rank, and [F1] therefore puts $\alpha$ in $F^1K_0(X)$. Its first projection is $c_1(\alpha)=0$; the first kernel assertion in [F1] consequently puts $\alpha$ in $F^2K_0(X)$. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F2], the second projection of $\alpha$ is $-c_2(\alpha)=0$, so $\alpha\in F^3K_0(X)$. The third Chern class is injective on this group by [F4], and $c_3(\alpha)=0$ by step 1.1. Hence $\alpha=0$ in $K_0(X)$. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Since $X$ has dimension three it is nonempty. The bundles $E$ and $F$ have constant rank three, equal to $\dim X$, and step 3.1 gives $[E]=[F]$. Applying [F6] yields $E\cong F$. Thus the displayed map is injective on isomorphism classes. [F6, step 3.1]

5.1 Given any triple in the target, [F5] provides a rank-three bundle having exactly those three classes. This proves surjectivity. Together with step 4.1, the displayed map is a bijection. [F5, step 4.1] ∎

## Rank-two bundles with prescribed first two classes

[Open item](item-cor-rank-two-threefold-existence) · level 36

### Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the site and universe size bounds required by the cited motivic filtration, support and Chern-class constructions. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic and let $X$ be a normal affine finite-type $k$-scheme of Krull dimension three. Then the map
$$ (c_1,c_2):\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)\longrightarrow H^{2,1}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)\times H^{4,2}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z) $$
is surjective.

Here an algebraically closed field is a field in which every nonconstant polynomial in one variable has a root. Affine and finite type mean $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a finitely generated $k$-algebra $A$; normal means every local ring is an integrally closed domain; and Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. A vector bundle is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $\mathrm{Vect}_2(X)$ is the set of isomorphism classes of bundles locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X^2$. The group $H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is degree-$2i$ cohomology of the weight-$i$ integral motivic complex, and $c_i$ is the corresponding motivic Chern-class operation on bundles. Choice says every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the size bounds fix the sites and universes used by the suppliers.

### Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $k$ and $X$ as in the statement, the Axiom of Choice, the stated size bounds, and a pair $(a_1,a_2)$ in the displayed target.

**Goal:** Produce a rank-two bundle $E'$ with $c_i(E')=a_i$ for $i=1,2$.

[F1] Under these field, scheme, Choice and size hypotheses, every triple in $\prod_{i=1}^3 H^{2i,i}_{\mathrm{mot}}(X,\mathbb Z)$ is the first three Chern classes of a rank-three bundle. [thm-normal-threefold-classification](item-thm-normal-threefold-classification) [math:def-axiom-of-choice](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-axiom-of-choice)

[F2] Under the same hypotheses, a rank-three bundle with third Chern class zero is isomorphic to $E'\oplus\mathcal O_X$ for some rank-two bundle $E'$. [cor-rank-three-zero-chern-splitting](item-cor-rank-three-zero-chern-splitting)

[F3] Chern classes are invariant under bundle isomorphism, vanish above the rank, and have $c_0=1$. The total Chern polynomial satisfies $c_t(V\oplus W)=c_t(V)c_t(W)$, and first Chern classes of line bundles are additive under tensor product. [def-motivic-chern-classes](item-def-motivic-chern-classes) [prop-chern-whitney-identities](item-prop-chern-whitney-identities)

### Proof

**Proof technique:** Prescribe a zero third class, split off a trivial line, and compare Chern polynomials.

1.1 Apply [F1] to $(a_1,a_2,0)$. There is a rank-three bundle $E$ with $c_1(E)=a_1$, $c_2(E)=a_2$, and $c_3(E)=0$. The field, dimension, normality, finite-type, Choice and size hypotheses required by [F1] are precisely those given. [F1, given]

2.1 Apply [F2] to $E$. Its hypotheses hold by the statement and step 1.1, so $E\cong E'\oplus\mathcal O_X$ for a rank-two bundle $E'$. [F2, given, step 1.1]

3.1 By the line-bundle tensor identity in [F3], $c_1(\mathcal O_X)=2c_1(\mathcal O_X)$ because $\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_X$. Cancellation in the cohomology group gives $c_1(\mathcal O_X)=0$. Its higher Chern classes vanish by rank, and $c_0=1$; hence $c_t(\mathcal O_X)=1$. [F3, algebra, step 2.1]

4.1 Using the isomorphism from step 2.1 and the Whitney identity, $c_t(E)=c_t(E')c_t(\mathcal O_X)=c_t(E')$. Comparing coefficients of $t$ and $t^2$ and using step 1.1 gives $c_1(E')=a_1$ and $c_2(E')=a_2$. Thus every target pair has a preimage, proving surjectivity. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎
